articleTitle: Shifted-Beam Array Coil for Highly Focal Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) using an array of vertically arranged, counter-propagating coils to achieve extremely high focality. The proposed design significantly reduces unwanted field spread and the activated brain volume, creating an E-field peak with a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of approximately 1 cm on the cortical surface. The focality is superior compared to all established designs, and in particular all physically realizable figure-8 coils. Such high level of focusing is a notable improvement over current designs and enables even more precise stimulation of the cerebral cortex.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Feeding Structure for Exciting Metal Casing as an Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In IoT applications, the platform excitation by low-profile feeding element have been proposed to improve the bandwidth of overall systems. However, further miniaturization of the feeding element is required. This paper presents a small and low-profile feeding structure of the parasitic meandered inverted-L element. The proposed antenna can excite the metal casing and its size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12.2\ \text{mm} \times 6.0\ \text{mm} \times 1.7\ \text{mm}$</tex>. The simulation results show that its radiation efficiency is 75 % at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Homogenization and Extreme Fresnel Drag in Spatiotemporally Modulated Wire Medium
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this presentation we will discuss the homogenization of a spatiotemporally modulated loaded-wire medium. We will derive the effective permittivity of the various wave solutions that are propagating in this system, and in particular we will focus on extraordinary waves that emerge and propagate at frequencies below the so called “plasma frequency” of the wire medium, already with weak and slow modulation. These waves will give rise to an extreme Fresnel drag effect that is usually associated with fast moving medium.

articleTitle: Direction Finding for BPSK with In-band Interference Based on Amplitude Comparison Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel amplitude comparison method for direction finding (DF) aiming to Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) with cyclostationarity analysis is proposed to overcome the in-band interference problem in this paper. By using the cyclostationary characteristic, the ratio information of amplitude can be accurately extracted without being interfered by the aliasing spectrum and the direction of desired signal can also be effectively estimated. The experimental systems, with antennas working at 2.44GHz and 5.8GHz respectively, are constructed to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna at Millimeter Wave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the design of an antenna based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW). The structure consists of slot antenna designed to operate at Ka band frequency. The effect of introducing slots and diameter of vias have been extensively studied. The basic structure is designed on a substrate with dielectric constant of 2.2 and with a thickness of 0.508mm with loss tangent of 0.0009. The design consists of a SIW antenna fed with a microstrip to SIW transition. Multiple slots and different diameter of vias effects have been studied and analyzed using CST. Signal power reduces at mm wave frequencies as compared to lower frequency bands due to smaller effective aperture size of single element antenna. Therefore, in order to compensate these losses, the mm wave communication systems are required to have high gain antenna. A high gain and efficiency and low losses are major considerations which can be achieved by the proposed design. The proposed antenna geometry has a bandwidth of 2GHz with a gain of 7.9 dB at 26GHz and efficiency of 95%.

articleTitle: Deionized Water Insulator Loaded Brain-Implanted UWB Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a novel configuration of an insulator for human-head implanted UWB antenna. The insulator is 3D printed with a biocompatible material and is filled with a deionized water of high dielectric constant and low loss tangent. The proposed compact antenna shows an average gain of −20 dBi in the boresight region for the target frequency of 3–5 GHz band, high enough for the wireless biotelemetry communications.

articleTitle: Static and Dynamic Beamforming with Huygens' Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Most antenna applications require certain control of the radiation characteristics, such as the direction of the beam, the directivity and the sidelobe level. It may also be desirable to steer the beam dynamically. Although control of the far-field region of antennas has been traditionally achieved by antenna arrays, the feeding networks of such arrays result in bulky designs and increase power losses. A promising alternative is the use of metasurfaces that transform the fields of a simple source to aperture fields corresponding to prescribed radiation patterns. In this paper, different ways are presented to obtain both static and dynamic beamforming with Huygens' metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Reconfigurable SIW-Based Leaky-Wave Antenna Loaded with Inclined Slot
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel reconfigurable antenna. The proposed design is a low-profile leaky-wave antenna (LWA) based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). Embedding inclined switches at the backside of the antenna leads to the variation of the propagation constant and main-lobe pointing angle. The proposed design's key novelties are the electronic beam-scanning using one switch per cell, small gain variations, and miniaturizing the antenna by integrating the bias circuitry into the ground plane. The center frequency was chosen as 29 GHz to accommodate 5G wireless networks. The width, length, and thickness of the antenna are 24 mm, 95 mm, and 0.127 mm, respectively. Sweeping the switches' bias voltages leads to an 18° scanning range of the main beam with a peak realized gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12+0.2\ \text{dBi}$</tex> and sidelobe level (SLL) of −9 dB at 29 GHz. The compactness, high gain, low SLL, and electronic beam-steering capability of the proposed reconfigurable antenna make it a suitable candidate for 5G miniaturized applications.

articleTitle: An Integral-Equation-Based Method for Efficient and Accurate Solutions of Scattering Problems with Highly Nonuniform Discretizations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a full-wave electromagnetic solver for analyzing multiscale scattering problems with highly nonuniform discretizations. The developed solver employs an elegant combination of potential integral equations (PIEs) with the magnetic-field integral equation (MFIE) to improve the iterative convergence properties of matrix equations obtained via method of moments, especially derived from highly nonuniform discretizations for which PIEs suffer from ill conditioning. A mixed-form multilevel fast multipole algorithm with incomplete tree structures is employed to efficiently and accurately solve the obtained matrix equations. The solver circumvents the well-known low-frequency problem originating from the breakdown of the conventional surface formulations and the standard MLFMA for highly nonuniform discretizations. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed solver are demonstrated on canonical but challenging scattering problems.

articleTitle: Unified Approach to Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An algebraic link between transition matrix and impedance matrix is utilized in this work to unify characteristic mode decomposition originally proposed by Garbacz with a framework proposed later on by Harrington and Mautz. The resulting formulation is unique to all method of moments formulations, valid for all linear and lossless materials, and has many favorable properties. The unified prescription is applicable to surface equivalence, body-of-revolution, or volumetric method of moments formulations. The unification paves a way to establish characteristic modes as a standalone technique in time-harmonic domain being independent of method of moment paradigm, i.e., to utilize - for example - finite element method instead.

articleTitle: An Efficient ESM with Focus Stacking Technique for 3D Radiation Source Localization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient emission source microscopy (ESM) with focus stacking technique is presented to localize active sources of radiation in three-dimension (3D) volume space rather than on two-dimension (2D) plane, e.g., a PCB. Due to providing limited information about the components contributing to far-field radiation, the utilization of near-field scanning is often difficult to localize the sources of radiation from complex and large systems with multiple sources. Based on 2D synthetic aperture radar (SAR), the existing emission source microscopy (ESM) is only suitable to localize the EMI source on 2D plane, e.g., a PCB. In order to localize the radiation sources in 3D space, an efficient radiation source location technique based on ESM with focus stacking technique is proposed. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed method can distinguish between multiple radiating sources in 3D space.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Cylindrical MEFSS for 360° Azimuthal Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Miniaturized element frequency selective surfaces (MEFSSs) are periodic structures composed of sub-wavelength metallic and/or dielectric scatterers. These surfaces can realize higher-order filter responses by utilizing their non-resonant behavior. Reconfigurable MEFSSs have the potential of achieving wideband responses, while maintaining a compact design, by loading the unit cells with tunable element(s). The potential reconfigurability of MEFSSs opens up the possibility of realizing adaptive beamforming systems from them. In this paper, a reconfigurable MEFSS is presented with a binary mode of operation. The MEFSS is placed in a cylindrical arrangement and shown to implement fine resolution azimuthal beam steering, in steps of 9.2 degrees, while being compact compared to previous proposed solutions using conventional frequency selective surfaces (FSSs).

articleTitle: Wideband Substrate-Integrated-Coaxial-Line-Fed Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna with End-Fire Radiation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an end-fire magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna fed by substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL). End-fire radiation is obtained by combining a horizontally-oriented quarter-wave shorted patch and a loaded dipole array. An SICL direct-feeding scheme is applied to provide a simple and wideband excitation of the ME-dipole antenna. Experimental results verify that the proposed antenna exhibits a wide impedance bandwidth of 77%, a stable gain of around 5.5 dBi, and a compact lateral size of 0. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$32\lambda_{0}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Predicting MRI RF Exposure for Passive Implantable Medical Devices Using a Mesh-based Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this study, a mesh-based fast prediction method, using a convolutional neural network (CNN) was proposed to estimate the radio-frequency (RF) exposure for passive implantable medical devices (PIMDs) during magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The mesh file from the FDTD grid was used as input for the CNN. The RF exposure, in terms of peak-spatial 10 gram (g) averaged specific absorption rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(_{\text{ps}}\text{SAR}_{10\mathrm{g}})}$</tex>, was used as the output of the CNN. This method is implemented and validated with 576 generic orthopedic PIMDs. Among the 576 PIMDs, 403 were randomly selected and used as the training set for the CNN, while 173 were used to examine the validity of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{_{\text{ps}}\text{SAR}_{10\mathrm{g}}}$</tex> predicted by the CNN. The results show that the correlation between the estimation and the target <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{_{\text{ps}}\text{SAR}_{10\mathrm{g}}}$</tex> was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\sim 0.9}$</tex> and that the mean absolute percentage error was ~4% at 1.5 T and 3 T.

articleTitle: Correction of the Excitation Coefficients of Ku-band Phased Arrays With a Rotatable Polarization Plane
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method of correcting the excitation coefficients of a Ku-band phased array with a rotatable polarization plane. By optimizing both the amplitudes and phases of the excitation coefficients, the cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) is improved from 8.2 dB to 54.8 dB when controlling the main-beam direction to 30° and the polarization angle to −45° at 14.25 GHz.

articleTitle: Research on Open Resonator at 35 GHz for Plasma Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an open resonator at 35 GHz for plasma diagnosis. The resonator combines the closed cavity with the antenna. According to the hole coupling theory, the resonant mode in the cavity can be converted into the propagation mode of the antenna. After the plasma is loaded, the reflection coefficient of the antenna will be affected, thereby disturbing the resonance mode in the cavity. In view of the phenomenon, a measurement for the plasma electron density (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N_{e}$</tex>) based on resonance theory will be realized.

articleTitle: A Highly Miniaturized 3D Antenna in Package for UHF RFID Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) and sensing technologies are spreading out, modern systems require wireless and real-time data transfer between devices. RFID technology is one of the most used technologies for this information exchange. For compact devices, antenna in package (AiP) concept presents an advantage in this scenario because the antenna does not need any additional space while the package protects the electronic components and sensors from the environment. In this paper, an AiP is designed and miniaturized by employing volumetric folding and dielectric loading techniques. Firstly, a dipole in free space is analyzed by folding it into a cuboid shape. Later, a free space is replaced with the dielectric as AiP body material to achieve the required miniaturization for the RFID band. The proposed AiP resonates at 891 MHz with a ka of 0.27 and exhibits a decent efficiency of 34<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering from Composite Objects using a Multi-trace Surface Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The multi-trace domain-decomposition surface integral equation (MT-DD-SIE) originally proposed to analyze electromagnetic scattering from dielectric composite objects is extended to efficiently account for perfect electrically conducting (PEC) bodies. This extension uses a special form of Robin transmission conditions (RTCs) on the surfaces of the PEC bodies to “couple them to the dielectric bodies. Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG)-based discretization of these RTCs, which are the only governing equations on PEC surfaces, yields a well-conditioned matrix block. Therefore, PEC bodies are accounted for within the MT-DD-SIE solver without negatively affecting the convergence of the iterative solution. The accuracy and the efficiency of this approach are demonstrated by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Wideband CPW-PS Feed for Millimeter Wave Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A simple double U-shaped magneto-electric dipole antenna (MEA) with a wide bandwidth is presented. The antenna feed employs a coplanar waveguide (CPW) to parallel strip (PS) transition to obtain balanced feed. Full-wave simulations show fractional IBW <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert \leq-10\text{dB})}$</tex> of 64.18% with realized gain being 6.44 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 1.65\ \text{dBi}}$</tex> for 21.07 to 40.98 GHz. It exhibits stable radiation pattern with total efficiency of 88 -99 % and low broadside cross-polarization levels. The antenna profile and footprint measure <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.24}\lambda_{0}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.87}\lambda_{0}^{2}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{f}_{0}=31.025}$</tex> GHz.

articleTitle: Partial Arc Sampling Receiving Scheme for Demultiplexing of Orbital Angular Momentum Vortex Beam
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Due to the divergence of the orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam, the OAM demultiplexing needs a considerable aperture size to acquire the OAM field information, which brings the challenges to implementation of the receiving end. To tackle this issue, we develop a partial arc sampling receiving (PASR) scheme for demultiplexing of the vortex beams by using the augmented dynamic mode decomposition (A-DMD) approach. Simulation benchmarks are provided to demonstrate the validity of the proposed novel demultiplexing method.

articleTitle: E-band Wide-Angle Multi-Beam Shaped Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm-wave) E-band multi-beam transmitarray with a wide beam coverage is developed in this paper. The transmitarray has a three-dimensional (3D) elliptical cylindrical shape. This aperture shape and phase compensation are jointly designed according to the desired maximum beam direction, leading to different focal lengths for different beams. This way, the proposed transmitarray can achieve a larger beam scanning range with a low scanning loss compared to many other reported designs. A transmitarray prototype is simulated, fabricated and measured at 70.5 GHz, which can provide a continuous beam coverage between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 43^{\circ}$</tex> with a 2.7-dB gain drop at the maximum radiation angle.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of 2-D Fabry-Perot Cavity Antennas with Uniform Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The radiation characteristics of 2-D circular uniform Fabry-Perot cavity (FPC) antennas are investigated, providing theoretical references for general 2-D FPC antenna design. Based on the radial leaky wave theory and the transverse equivalent network (TEN) model, the gain and the aperture efficiency of the circular FPC antenna are calculated. The optimum radiation efficiency that maximizes the broadside gain is found. The bandwidth is also discussed.

articleTitle: Diagonalization of the Hamiltonian for EM Fields in Absorbing/Dispersive/Inhomogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We numerically study a one-dimensional energy-conserving explicit model, in which classical electromagnetic fields interact with coarse-grained matter oscillators, to recover the physics of EM propagation in absorbing/dispersive/inhomogeneous dielectric media. Based on the Hamiltonian mechanics framework, we derive a generalized Hermitian eigenvalue problem and extract a countably finite/complete set of eigenmodes using the finite-difference method. The present approach provides a platform to perform the canonical quantization with mode decomposition in the presence of absorbing/dispersive/inhomogeneous dielectric media.

articleTitle: A high-speed railway channel measurement scheme based on 5G signal
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The fifth-generation (5G) communication facilitates the development of smart transportation and the analysis of wireless channel's characteristics becomes crucial, whlie traditional measurement scheme has the difficulty of setting up the transmitter. This paper focuses on the high-speed railway (HSR) wireless channel measurement scheme based on 5G downlink standard signal, which is the current network signal. The Demodulation Reference Signal (DM-RS) in the Physical Downlink Shared Channel (PDSCH) were used to calculate the Channel Impulse Response (CIR), then extracted the time delay according to CIR. The validity and accuracy of the scheme can be verified by comparing the calculated time delay value with the preset value. The paper's work is helpful for futural radio channel measurement and channel characteristics extraction.

articleTitle: Guided and Leaky Mode Radiation Characteristics of Solid Dielectric Pyramidal Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Even though solid dielectric horn antennas have gains comparable to metallic horn of the same size, a complete analytical analysis is not seen in literature. In this paper, the radiation equations especially for the leaky mode of a solid dielectric horn antenna have been deduced, compared with numerical results and also verified by comparison with reported measured results.

articleTitle: A Compact Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact omnidirectional antenna with circular polarization (CP) is presented, which is a small loop antenna loaded with 1/10 wavelength vertical stub. The loop consists of four bent dipoles acts as idea magnetic dipole, which generates horizonal electric component. While the loaded stub is placed in middle of dipole arm, vertical component with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{90}^{\circ}$</tex> phase difference is obtained, hence, circular polarized radiation is achieved. Antenna radiator is fed by a balanced parallel stripline. The prototype at 2.4GHz band is etched on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{30}\mathbf{mm}\times \boldsymbol{30}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> FR4 substrate, and is fabricated and measured, comparisons between simulation and measurement are presented. Measured results show that, at 2.45GHz, measured peak gain is -0.43dB and polarization rejection ratio is 14.21dB. The proposed loop antenna is suitable for applications like wireless measurement detection and IoT applications.

articleTitle: Advances in Antenna Diagnostic Techniques through Post-Processing of Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper gives an overview of advanced source reconstruction techniques employing Plane Wave Spectrum formulation. Applications in the topics of spherical near-field measurements, RLSA antenna diagnostics and radio-telescope surface characterization are introduced. This shows the potential and versatility of this very efficient holography technique.

articleTitle: A Low-RCS and Low-ECC Transparent Meta-Radomes Based on a Conductive Nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we employ the optical nanocircuit theorem to build an invisible nanocomposite with unprecedentedly high relative optical transparency (~96.4 %) and electric conductivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sim 12.6\Omega/\text{sq})$</tex>. With this material platform, we experimentally demonstrate a new optically-transparent, low-RCS metasurface radome that can not only protect a transparent patch antenna integrated with a solar cell ground plane, but also enable wideband RCS reduction (20.5 dB at 14 GHz), gain enhancement (5.1 dB), and excellent isolation for antenna array applications.

articleTitle: Online EM Teaching: E-XAM tool for Students' Self-Evaluation and Final Assessment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel tool for supporting and simplifying electromagnetic (EM) teaching activities related to students' self-evaluation and final examination. The proposed approach has been experimentally validated within the Bachelor course “Electromagnetic Fields” and was recently applied to all courses provided by the ELEDIA Research Center teaching staff.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Tolerance Analysis of Antennas /Radomes with Mesh/Element Strip Grouping
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a strip grouping method is proposed to facilitate the tolerance analysis of antennas/radomes using Monte Carlo method. Antenna array elements or antenna/radome discretized meshes are grouped into less categories to reduce the number of independent random variables. In this way, the power pattern variation interval can be better predicted using less calculations. Results of an array antenna with excitation errors and a spherical radome with thickness errors validate the effective ness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Spectral smoothness of embedded element patterns in the SKA-LOW prototype station AAVS2: preliminary results
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Highly preliminary results are presented for the spectral smoothness (frequency dependence) of the embedded element patterns (EEPs) of the SKA-LOW prototype system AAVS2. Mutual coupling in this tightly coupled quasi-random array results in variation in these, and results are shown for two EEPs, extracted from a much larger dataset. Some suggestions are outlined for further work.

articleTitle: Low-SCS Phased Array Based on Optimized RLC Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel method to reduce scattering cross section (SCS) of a phased array antenna is proposed in this paper. The optimum load impedance for antenna element with zero backward scattering is theoretically analyzed and fitted by a simple RLC circuit according to minimum mean square error criterion. Afterwards the RLC circuit is implemented by strip lines with open- and short-circuited shunt stubs, as well as an impedance transformer. A 1×32 E-plane linear array is constructed, and simulated results show the proposed array achieves generally 6dB SCS reduction compared to its conventional counterpart.

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband E-plane Crossover and Its Application on Multi-beam Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm-wave) multi-beam antenna array fed by a wideband <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> E-plane butler matrix is presented. The butler matrix consists of 3-dB coupler, phase shifter and crossover based on the gap waveguide (GWG) structure. It employs a novel crossover structure, which is formed by two symmetrical septum polarizers to realize broadband and high isolation. The slow-wave horn antenna is implemented as the radiation antenna element. The simulated reflection and isolation coefficients are better than −11 dB over the operating bandwidth from 95-110 GHz. At the center frequency of 102.5 GHz, the simulated four beams point toward −44°, −14°, +14°and +44°.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Planar Ultra-wideband Modular Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a planar ultra-wideband modular antenna (PUMA) array is designed and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7\times 7$</tex> prototype is fabricated, based on which experimental research is conducted. Active reflection coefficients of the center unit have been obtained by accounting for mutual coupling effects from 24 co-polarized and 16 cross-polarized neighboring units in the centered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 5$</tex> array. Measured results agree well with simulated ones of the infinite array, which demonstrates the effectiveness of using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 5$</tex> -array test to verify the performance of large array. It also indicates that all the mutual coupling over −25 dB should be completely taken into account.

articleTitle: Numerical Evaluation of Impacts of Dust and Water Vapor on Indoor Channel Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: At 5G and beyond frequencies, the existence of scatterers such as dust or water vapor in the propagation medium can cause significant attenuation of radio signals, and needs to be considered properly during the characterization of wireless communications links. In this paper, a three-dimensional radio wave propagation model, based on a split-step parabolic equation method, is applied to evaluate the impacts of those scatterers on indoor channel characteristics. The Maxwell Garnett equation is utilized for the effective medium approximations. The simulated received power in a factory geometry at 4.9 GHz with the presence of dust and water vapor in the propagation medium is compared. The effect of environmental visibility is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Acoustically Driven VLF Antennas with High Data Rates
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Conventional antennas are fundamentally difficult to operate at the very low frequency (VLF) band with a portable size. Here, we demonstrate an acoustically driven portable antenna based on the piezoelectric lead zirconate titanate (PZT) ceramic, which can efficiently transmit and receive electromagnetic wave at 26.2 kHz with a size of 10cm. This VLF antenna was designed and modeled by the finite element method, and communication distance is 1 km with the power of 1.25 W. By using a binary amplitude shift keying modulation technique, we achieve a data rate up to 400 bit/s.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Antenna Array for Imageless Contraband Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a novel approach to contraband detection using sparse Fourier domain sampling with a dynamic antenna array. A 38-GHz two-element antenna array is dynamically rotated to generate a ring-shaped filter in the Fourier transform domain of a scene, or the spatial frequency domain, where unique responses from contraband are identified, without image reconstruction. Objects with sharp edges generate sharp yet broadband spatial frequency responses that can be identified with only a subset of the spatial frequency information. In contrast to other millimeter-wave contraband detection approaches, the presented system does not depend on a fully reconstructed image nor has the ability to form one. In the presented technique, only a subset of all available spatial frequency samples are measured by the two-element dynamic antenna array with the objective to identify the strong broadband spatial frequency responses associated with sharp edges. Conducted measurements include a fabricated knife prop as contraband concealed under clothing, along with a control scenario. Measurement results demonstrate the ability to recognize a metal object, and furthermore indicate the ability to identify the shape of the target based on the responses from the knife edge as well as the angled tip that are visible in both simulation and measurement.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Compact Circular Patch Antenna with Monopole-like Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Excitation of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>mode in planar circular patch antenna exhibit monopole-like radiation pattern and yet have a low-profile in terms of the vertical height of the antenna. Such an antenna is useful for smart IoT/wireless sensor network applications. The design of a narrow-band antenna operating in the 2.4GHz ISM band that is also compact in the lateral dimension and made with a single layer of substrate is presented in this paper. Due to the resonant nature of the radiating element, low-loss substrate such as RO5880 is needed to achieve higher realized gain. The measured antenna performance in terms of both the reflection coefficient and the radiation pattern are presented. Since no air layers are used in the design, conventional printed circuit board fabrication is possible to realize the antenna and hence can be easily integrated with the sensor electronics as demanded by the application.

articleTitle: Transmission Properties Analysis of Huygens' Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The transmission properties of the Huygens' metasurface are analyzed. The relation between the transmission phase shift and transmission amplitude is obtained by modeling the electric surface admittance and magnetic surface impedance. This analysis shows that the transmission phase shift coverages are 53.58° and 89.72° for −1-dB and −3-dB transmission amplitude when either electric or magnetic surface current exists. In contrast, if both electric and magnetic surface currents exist, the Huygens' metasurface can maintain above −1-dB and −3-dB transmission amplitude with 360° phase shift coverage, when the absolute value difference between the normalized electric surface admittance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> and magnetic surface impedance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex>, i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert y-z\vert$</tex>, are less than 0.9 and 1.6, respectively.

articleTitle: A Phase-controlled Beam-Steered $2\times 2$ Patch Antenna Array With a Partially Reflecting Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a gain-enhanced phase-controlled beam-steered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> microstrip patch antenna array with a partially reflecting surface (PRS) superstrate is investigated for X-band applications. The gain of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> patch antenna array is enhanced by 2.92 dB in broadside direction using the PRS superstrate. The beam-steering of the pattern is also investigated for the configuration in both the E and H-planes by varying the phase of the input signal.

articleTitle: Coupling Effects in an L-band Reflector Antenna with Dual-polarization Stacked Patch Feed Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Reflector based antennas with dual linear polarizations are of interest for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) Earth observation missions. In the development of such antennas mutual coupling within the feed and with the reflector may impact the performance. This contribution presents the impact of mutual coupling on the reflection coefficients, the accepted power, and the individual radiation patterns in an L-band offset-fed reflector antenna. Significant impact of mutual coupling is observed over the frequency range of a typical L-band SAR chirp.

articleTitle: ENG-TL based Two-Element Diversity Antenna with Metasurface Shielding for High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a new and compact two-element diversity antenna based on an epsilon negative (ENG) transmission line (TL) operating at 4.87 GHz. The intended single antenna offers a miniaturized size of 24 × 24 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and circular polarization (CP) radiation due to the orthogonallv aligned ENG-TL based radiators. The antenna provides higher isolation ranging from 27–64 dB for the complete operating band due to the placement of a split-ring resonator (SRR) based metasurface wall between the single radiator antennas, which act like an effective electromagnetic shield between the two antennas. The diversity antenna provides an axial ratio less than 3 dB for θ = ± 65° and ϕ = 0° to 360° at 4.87 GHz. The antenna provides a maximum gain of antenna 2 dBi with excellent directional radiation Performance.

articleTitle: Differentially Fed Linear Antenna Array with Wideband Common-mode Absorption
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Novel differentially fed linear antenna array with wideband common-mode (CM) absorption is proposed. In the proposed antenna array, four radiation patches with stepped widths, common ground plane and the differential corporate-fed network are implemented from the top layer to the bottom layer, respectively. Four T-shaped slots are etched on the ground plane to realize aperture coupling. Furthermore, four absorptive stubs are added at the symmetric plane of the differential corporatefed network to achieve wideband CM absorption. The simulated and measured results demonstrate that the proposed antenna array can achieve the broadened -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 4.74 GHz to 5.02 GHz (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dd11</inf>< -10 dB), in which the flat differential-mode realized gain is kept around 13.4 dBi. Meanwhile, the measured CM reflection coefficient S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cc11</inf> is kept less than -10 dB from 3.15 GHz to 6.2 GHz with 65.2% fractional bandwidth, indicating the good CM absorption performance.

articleTitle: Wideband Compact Stripline Antenna for 5GB/6G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Recent communication systems are utilizing space diversity as a mean to increase the system capacity. Accordingly, the need for wideband and compact antennas has experienced a remarkable growth to support these new systems. In this article, a wideband antenna is proposed based on stripline technology. The proposed antenna is compact to enable the utilization of this structure as building block in 2D array configuration for beamforming networks. The proposed design covers bandwidth above 20%, with a matching level below 19 dB. The proposed design achieves a stable gain of 6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\text{dB}\pm 1}$</tex> over the operation bandwidth.

articleTitle: Scattering Reduction Metasurfaces Using Circular Inter-Digitated Self-Phased Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a circular inter-digitated (CID) self-phased (SP) element to design scattering reduction metasurfaces. Unlike using different building blocks to form checker-board patterns as in conventional approaches, we propose using only a single element to realize a reduction surface. The metasurface achieves scattering reduction by phase cancellation among elements. We use a constituent material in the dielectric layer supporting the element to obtain phase tuning capability. As the constituent material permittivity changes, the resonance wavelength of the element also changes, which results in a phase change. The proposed element design consists of a dual-circular ring, incorporating a meandered slot line, or an inter-digitated line, in between. The element can achieve polarization independent phase control with 300 degrees of tunable phase and less than 2 dB loss. We synthesize a prototype scattering reduction surface to verify the proposed element design. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed metasurface structure significantly reduces the broadside scattering by more than 10 dB at 12.8 GHz for a normally incident plane wave.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Unconventional Feasible Sources for Smart Electromagnetic Enviornments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents an innovative methodology for synthesizing unconventional “feasible” sources enabling the profitable exploitation of the complex scattering phenomena in smart electromagnetic environments (SEEs) for achieving the desired electromagnetic field distribution within a user-defined region-of-interest. Towards this goal, the design of all-dielectric field manipulating devices (FMDs) is formulated according to the inverse source (IS) theory and is solved as a global optimization problem. An illustrative numerical example is shown to assess the effectiveness and the potentialities of the proposed design strategy.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Surpershape UWB Microstrip Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized Supershape antenna is presented for ultra-wideband (UWB) application. This microstrip-fed antenna is designed on the Isola IS680 AG-348 substrate with a dielectric constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Er \approx 3. 5)$</tex> and a dielectric loss tangent <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(tano \approx 0.0029)$</tex> by an appropriate choice of the Superformula parameters. The ground plane is designed on the bottom of the substrate with a slot and diagonal edges for bandwidth enhancement. The resulting antenna has a diameter of about 16.14 mm leading to a 46.75% and 11 % reduction in size when compared with the regular circular patch and a previously designed antenna with a similar configuration respectively. Simulations performed with HFSS and measurement results show that the antenna has a return loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{11}(dB)\vert$</tex> greater than 10dB across the FCC designated band.

articleTitle: Low Cross-Polarized Patch Antenna With Lossy Material
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A method to suppress cross-polarization by using lossy material is proposed in this paper. Absorbing material with a large dielectric loss tangent angle is used at the four corners where the cross polarization is generated. Simulated results show that the proposed structure can obtain a cross-polarization of −39.2 dB without affecting other radiation performance. It proves that the lossy material could be another alternative means of suppressing cross-polarization.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Aperture-Shared Antenna Array with Low Blockage Effect
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarized aperture-shared antenna array with low blockage effect is proposed. The proposed dual-band array consists a low-band (LB) element and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> high-band (HB) antenna array. The LB element is located at the center of the HB array which is shielded under the LB element radiator. In the normal case, strong blockage effect from the LB on HB elements would exists. By adding split ring resonators (SRRs) along the LB radiator, the LB element scattering in the high-band can be suppressed. As a result, the blockage effect of the low scattering LB element on the HB array is indistinct. The proposed blockage reduction method is suitable for multi-band aperture-shared antenna array.

articleTitle: Implementation of Discrete Exterior Calculus in Solving the $\mathbf{A}-\Phi$ Formulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The discrete exterior calculus (DEC) is the discrete version of exterior calculus in differential geometry, which can be used in defining differential forms and solving differential equations such as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}-\Phi$</tex> equations in electromagnetics. Compared with the E-H formulation, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}-\Phi$</tex> formulation is immune to low-frequency breakdown, which makes it ideal for broadband and multi-scale analysis. In this paper, the implementation of DEC in solving the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}-\Phi$</tex> equations is addressed. Technical implementation details as well as numerical examples are provided. The proposed algorithm can be used as a stable fast solver for problems with quasi-static frequencies to optical frequencies with arbitrary meshes.

articleTitle: Deriving Maxwell's Equations from First Principles of Relativistic Charge Invariance and Space-Time Relations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper introduces a simple, rigorous approach to derive Maxwell's equations from first principles, based on an invariant form of the Gauss' law using only basic space-time transformation relations of special relativity. More advanced concepts of relativistic mechanics, such as transformation of mass, momentum and force, are not necessary in this development, resulting in a simple theory. The new derivation is of fundamental theoretical significance in electromagnetic theory, making Maxwell's equations less mysterious to comprehend, and would fill an educational need to introduce the modern theory of special relativity to derive electromagnetic theory from the first principles. The approach would be suitable for a senior (even junior) undergraduate or an introductory graduate engineering student, depending on the level of depth and rigor.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Quiet Zone of Tapered Chambers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Tapered chambers are mainly used to achieve an anechoic environment or free-space-simulated environment at frequencies below 700 MHz, where traditional rectangular chambers are not economically feasible. In this paper, the performance of the quiet zone of a tapered range is analyzed from 100 MHz to 1 GHz. The analysis shows that based on the phase distribution, the tapered chamber is a far field measurement. The analysis also shows that the performance is strongly dependent on the absorber surrounding the range antenna.

articleTitle: Study on Homogenization Methods of Stacked Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The effective dielectric constant (EDC) theory for stacked rectangular dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) is investigated. First, the classical static capacitance models (SCMs) are revisited. It is found that these models might have been abused, e.g., controversial models were applied in similar structures. Accordingly, the accuracy of these EDC methods is questionable though they are widely used. To solve this problem, numerical experiments are conducted for validation. Novel homogenization methods are then introduced based on the effective medium theory as improvements. All the above methods are compared through a set of DRA samples where the resonant mode and stacking order are taken into account. The practicability of each method is then discussed based on error analysis. It is found that the effective medium theory outperforms the prevalent SCMs.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Hollow Dielectric Resonator Antenna for GPS Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a dual-band hollow rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) fed by a single coaxial probe, which is designed to operate at the L5 and L1 bands for Global Positioning System (GPS) applications. The dimensions of the dielectric resonator are designed so that each one of its fundamental modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TE}_{\delta 11}^{x}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TE}_{1\delta 1}^{y}$</tex> resonates at the L5 and L1 bands, respectively. However, the higher-mode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TE}_{\delta 21}^{x}$</tex> may appear at the upper band and, thus, disturbing the radiation characteristics of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TE}_{\delta 11}^{x}$</tex> mode. To overcome this situation, an air gap is introduced into the DRA to shift this mode away from the L1 band. Also, the reflection coefficient and radiation patterns are simulated and the results show the efficiency of the proposed model.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized End-fire Antenna Planar Array with Wide-angle Scanning Performance for Base-Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an end-fire antenna planar array with operational bands from 24 to 28 GHz for millimeter-wave base-station applications is presented, which is structured by arranging the single-arm stepped ridge antenna elements into an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> planar array. The element is constituted by two metallic arms, one of which is a single-arm stepped ridge structure and the other is a ground structure. Moreover, the slot is added in the ground arm structure for improving the port isolations between adjacent elements. The simulated results show that the antenna element has an impedance bandwidth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11} < - 15\ \text{dB}$</tex> from 24 GHz to 28 GHz. And the radiation beams of antenna array can scan with ± 60° in the H-plane and ±40° in the E-plane. The proposed antenna array is suitable for base station applications.

articleTitle: A Self-Filtering Horn Antenna Based on Multipolar All-Dielectric Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we describe the design of a self-filtering horn antenna based on the innovative features of multipolar all-dielectric metasurfaces. We first analyze the scattering response of a dielectric core-shell meta-atom with a strong permittivity contrast and we show how such a geometry allows a fine control of the spectral positions of the dipolar and quadrupolar Mie resonances. Then, we describe how it is possible engineering the electric and magnetic surface currents flowing on the metasurface for achieving a band-pass filtering response. Finally, we show how such high-Q filters are suitable for the integration in an horn antenna and, thus, for the implementation of an ultra-selective filtenna. A realistic design based on commercial materials is proposed and checked with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: A W-band, Microfabricated, Tiled Phased Array Realized by Bricked Tapered Slot Antenna Element
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a microfabricated W-band tapered slot antenna (TSA) integrated with a rectangular micro-coaxial line (RμCL) to substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) transition is proposed. To integrate the vertical end-fire TSA array with the horizontally planar feed network in W-band, the transition from an SIW to an RμCL is designed. Then, a linear TSA array is built and achieves a bandwidth from 85 to 100 GHz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S_{11} < -10\ \text{dB})$</tex>, which can be expanded to a two-dimensional scanning array. The linear array prototype is then fabricated and measured. The measured results show good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Compact Waveguide Surface End-launcher Suitable for Wearable Body Area Network Terminals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact end-launcher with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\times 30$</tex> mm terminal form factor enabling body area network (BAN) communication through a waveguide surface is proposed. It targets Bluetooth communication at 2.4 GHz for on-body communication. The wireless power transmission is studied in both planar and curved scenarios.

articleTitle: Low-loss and low profile metamateriallens antenna for 5G millimeter wave
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel wideband, low loss and full phase adjustable metamaterial unit is proposed in this paper. The simple structure can reduce the simulation time and the antenna production cost. The metamaterial unit consists of only two fork elements on both surfaces of a piece of thin dielectric substrate. Its transmission phase coverage is over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$360^{\circ}$</tex>, reflection coefficient is better than - 10dB and transmission coefficient is better than -0.5dB. A lens antenna with capability of beam scanning for 5G millimeter-wave application is designed based on this unit. The lens can fully cover 5G spectrum from 24.25 to 27.5GHz, the peak gain of which can achieve 20.45dBi at 26GHz with 9dB higher than the feed antenna. The simulated results show that a scanning coverage of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> in the horizontal plane can be realized by adding equal phase difference to the four ports of the feed antenna array.

articleTitle: Indoor Propagation Loss Model for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer Based in Multicommodity Flow Problems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) is a widely studied topic, mainly to enable low power consumption applications, as in several cases of Internet of Things applications. Therefore, Thus, the objective of this work is to develop a propagation loss model based on the modeling of multicommodity flow problems, MCF. The proposed model is focused on indoor applications, considering the optimization needs of information transmission and Energy for SWIPT applications. the frequencies analyzed were 3 GHz and 3.5 GHz. The proposed model showed higher adherence to the measured values than the indoor propagation picocell model.

Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: A Compact Ultra-Wideband Antenna and Its Application in MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact ultra-wideband antenna is proposed for portable UWB MIMO systems. The parasitic branches are loaded on the back of the dielectric substrate, and the feeding lines are curving, so the bandwidth of the antenna is improved. A metal U-shaped branch is loaded on the top of the MIMO antenna, and a U-shaped slot is etched on the bottom ground, so the isolation between the two ports is improved. The proposed antenna exhibits a bandwidth covering the entire UWB band (3.1-10.6 GHz) with high isolation better than 19 dB, a gain of 4-8dBi, efficiency of 62-77%, and guaranteed value of envelope correlation coefficient(ECC) ⩽ 0.01.

articleTitle: Implantable Antenna Design Using Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Medical implanted sensors coupled with antennas are sought in order to wirelessly transmit crucial health info and operate in a complex environment. Such antennas need to operate in a lossy environment, be robust when embedded in various body types, do not interact with the device electronics, and have very small physical sizes. To satisfy conflicting requirements multiple geometrical parameters should be tuned. While physical insight is always needed, optimization is the key factor for a successful design. Towards this goal, unconventional design techniques like evolutionary algorithms can be used. In this paper, we apply the improved grey wolf optimizer (IGWO) for implantable antenna design.

articleTitle: Enhanced Microwave Heating Uniformity using Reconfigurable Fresnel Zone Plate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Microwave heating is adapted in diverse industrial applications, but achieving heating uniformity remains elusive. Conventional microwave heating methods are problematic in terms of accurate analysis and the design process is heavily dependent on trial and errors. In this paper, we propose a method of beam steering using a 2.45 GHz reconfigurable Fresnel zone plate antenna. The devised topology is placed inside a chamber with an absorber. Studies indicate that the uniformity of the electric field increases by more than three times, underlining the fact that microwave heating uniformity can be significantly enhanced using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimum Gain Conditions for 1-D Unidirectional Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The optimization of the radiating performance for finite-length 1-D unidirectional leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) is first treated in the general case, i.e., assuming that the phase and attenuation constants can be varied freely. In this general case, an approximate analytical formula is derived to calculate the gain from the beamwidth, improving the accuracy of previous existing formulas. When a particular class of 1-D LWAs is considered, design equations are required to relate the geometrical parameters to the relevant LWA wavenumber. Leaky rectangular waveguides and other LWAs based on partially reflecting sheets (PRS) are two important classes of LWAs for which approximate expressions are available. Design procedures for optimizing the gain are given here for general 1-D LWAs, including leaky rectangular waveguides and other PRS-based LWAs.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reflectarray Adopting Quasi-Self-Complementary Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband reflectarray adopting quasi-self-complementary elements is presented. The unit cell contains an inverted L-shape patch and an inverted L-shape slot embedded within a rectangular patch, forming a quasi-self-complementary configuration. The element can achieve a linear phase span of 370°, leading to a broadband behavior. Simulations reveal that adopting the proposed element, the reflectarray antenna can achieve a 39% bandwidth for 1-dB gain drop as well as a 67% aperture efficiency at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Multi Branch Dual Band Rectifier for RF Energy Harvesting Efficiency Improvement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The RF energy harvester has promising application in making the IoT nodes self-sufficient in wireless sensor network. However, current state of the art lacks RF-DC conversion efficiency at lower incident power and output DC voltage level. In this paper, two multi-branch power combining architecture is proposed. The voltage combining or voltage multiplier configuration provides higher output DC voltage. However, it has less efficiency at lower incident power level. In comparison, the current combining configuration provides significantly higher efficiency at lower incident power level. The proposed architecture has the capability to improve the efficiency up to 30% at -20 dBm input power level and DC output voltage up to 8.5V.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Antenna Modeling Using Constrained Domains with Adaptive Lateral Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Surrogate modeling allows for reducing high costs associated with electromagnetic (EM)-driven design of antenna structures. Yet, the applicability of conventional surrogates is severely limited by the curse of dimensionality and high nonlinearity of antenna characteristics. Recently, a nested kriging technique has been proposed for mitigating these obstacles by constraining the model domain to the parameter space region comprising high-quality designs. This work proposes an enhancement of nested kriging with the lateral dimensions of surrogate domain varying across the design space. This enables further reduction of training data acquisition cost without compromising the model predictive power.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Electric Field Distribution in Metal Cabinet with Built-in RFID Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the influence of different working positions for the 922 MHz high-frequency radio frequency identification (RFID) antennas on the statistical characteristics of the electric field distribution in a metal cabinet. It shows that when RFID antennas are placed in the center of the opposite both walls of the cabinet, the probability density function (PDF) of the higher electric field level can achieve the most effective layout. When objects consist of different dielectric constants in the metal cabinet, the level of the electric field is inversely proportional to the corresponding relative permittivity of the dielectric constants.

articleTitle: Compact Planar Design of 2-D Butler Matrix for Passive Beamforming of $2\times 2$ Patch Array in D-Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact planar design of 2-D Butler matrix steering the beam of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> patch antenna array for D-band frequencies. The stripline Butler matrix feeding network is beneath the microstrip patch array with a similar size. The full-wave simulation results show an operating band wider than 125GHz - 150GHz for the butler matrix, and demonstrate the four beams of antenna array with 8.5dBi gain.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Leaky Wave Antenna based on ISGW
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with circular polarization (CP) and broadside radiation based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW) technology is proposed. A unique periodic structure, i.e. microstrip line with a periodic set of radiating stubs attached and series U-shape slot, is used to scan continuously from backward to forward and thus to form CP. The proposed LWA provides beam scanning from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-29^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12^{\circ}$</tex> over the frequency range of 21.5-27.5 GHz. Return loss less than -10 dB, and axial ratio less than 3 dB are achieved in 21 - 27.5 GHz (26.8%), and 21.16 - 26.05 GHz (20.7%), respectively. The average radiation efficiency is 87.8%.

articleTitle: Shaped-Beam Reflectarray Antenna Optimized at Multiple Frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In previous research, only the center frequency was optimized when designing a reflectarray antenna that radiates a shaped beam. In this study, we designed a shaped beam reflectarray antenna by optimizing the center frequency as well as multiple frequencies, in addition to using the conventional design method.

articleTitle: Wireless Propagation and Focusing into the Human Body with Wearable Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Wireless networking with implanted medical devices is hindered by inefficient transmission of radio-frequency waves in the vicinity of the human body. In this paper, we propose a wearable metamaterial structure that guides wireless propagation along the surface of the body and focuses the electromagnetic field deep in the body. This structure, operating in 2.4-2.5 GHz band, consists of a spoof surface plasmonic waveguide and a phased concentric rings connected through a tapered matching section. Simulations and measurements show that the structure provides nearly 20 dB enhancement in transmission efficiency between an implanted device (4 cm depth) and a distant (18 cm along the surface) external device.

articleTitle: Integrated Loop Antenna for Smartwatch
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A loop antenna integrated into the frame of the watch case for Bluetooth and 5G communication is proposed in this work. The structure of the antenna is a thin metal layer attached to the outer surface of a cylindrical substrate frame. The system ground plane is a circular metal patch inside the frame wall, holding a gap to the antenna. The proposed antenna can cover the ISM 2.45 GHz band (2400–2480 MHz) for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi applications and sub-6GHz FR1-N78 band (3400–3600 MHz) for 5G communication while working in the vicinity of body material.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering reduction using sparse metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The present work exploits a simulation-based design procedure to reduce the scattering of a metallic cylinder in desired directions using conformal sparse metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf Solution of E-Polarized Plane Wave Diffraction by a Dielectric Slit in a Thick Screen
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The study of the scattering and the radiation problems constituted of a dielectric slit in a thick conducting screen is of great importance in antenna systems, periodic structure, screens and propagation problems. In this paper, we formulate the problem and illustrate the solution's procedure through the Wiener-Hopf method.

articleTitle: Printed SIW Horn and Aperture Design for Surface-Wave Control and Power Routing by Genetic Algorithm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work a new design approach, using genetic algorithm optimization, is proposed to control surface waves (SWs) launched from a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) planar horn antenna. In particular, by using genetic algorithm optimization in CST Microwave Studio, simple and printed inclusions, defined by sub-wavelength microstrip patches and positioned near the SIW horn aperture, were optimized for power routing of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> SW mode at K-band frequencies. Also, the new structure demonstrated improved matching and reduced back-radiation as well as SW field culmination along the principal axis of propagation. Results are also compared with and without the sub-wavelength patches. Such an SIW-SWL and technique for SW control can be useful for new planar antennas, novel planar circuits for SW powering routing, and holographic beam forming systems.

articleTitle: A Narrowband Harmonic Tag Using a Microstrip Ring Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a narrow-band harmonic tag using a microstrip antenna based on a ring resonator structure. The tag uses a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.5$</tex> GHz ring antenna with a capacitive coupling to a microstrip feed line. The 2.5 GHz signal is input to a diode to generate harmonics, with the first harmonic at 5 GHz retransmitted via a microstrip dipole antenna. The ring radius and the capacitive coupling gap between the feedline and the ring antenna were tuned to achieve a measured fractional bandwidth of 0.98% at 2.5 GHz and 1.3% at 5 GHz.

articleTitle: Feasible study of MACKEY II type R with Enhanced Robustness on metal
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this study, a meta-surface-inspired antenna chip, developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), that is sufficiently robust to a metal object and MACKEY II type R with enhanced robustness against metal is proposed. Moreover, the antenna width was optimized to obtain a wider operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Flush-Surface Antenna for the 5G mmW Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a flush-surface antenna (FSA) for a 5G mmW band that is invisible view. An invisible FSA is realized by fixing a microstrip antenna (MSA) on a flexible substrate to a chassis or product body and painting them both. The antenna's performance can be maximized by optimally designing only the radiating element, including paints and other peripheral components, and shielding it from the feeding line using a flexible substrate on the connector. The fabricated 28-GHz FSA has an excellent return loss and a measured radiation pattern that correlates with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Folded Transmitarray Antenna Using Full-Space Chiral Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a bidirectional dual-circularly polarized folded transmitarray antenna (FTA) using full-space chiral metasurfaces (MSs). A receiver-transmitter based meta-atom is applied to inspire chiral characteristic. By assembling two MSs into face-to-face configuration, each MS acts as a phase modulator to collimate the radiation while simultaneously acts as a polarization-selective reflector for the other MS. Thus, bidirectional radiation beams with different polarizations are achieved. The proposed FTA is then numerically simulated and experimentally verified. The measured results show maximum aperture efficiencies of 34.7% and 31.6%, 3-dB gain bandwidths of 14.4% and 16.4% for two FTAs. Furthermore, the axial ratios are below 3 dB within the entire operating band.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Charging of Smartphone up to 6 Feet From Transmitter Antenna at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present wireless power transfer system capable of continuously charging smartphone while moving around in the room. The system comprises of rectangular patch antenna array with 1 W power radiating at 2.45 GHz, and receiver with rectenna and power management circuit providing 4.2 to 5.3 V DC output suitable to charging smartphone up to 6 feet away from transmitter while moving around the space.

articleTitle: Non-Uniform Gratings that Produce Preselected Anomalous Reflections
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a wire-impedance solution for an array of loaded wires above a ground plane that produces a preselected field when illuminated by a known plane wave. The preselected field consists of plane waves that are determined from a set of parameters, which salsify a periodicity condition. The solution determines both the wire impedances and the locations of the wires directly from the parameters of the preselected field. The preselected plane-wave parameters within one period determine how many different types of wires are needed. The number of degrees of freedom available for the grating design is increased by the number of different wires employed. We examine the ramifications of the solution when the preselected plane waves are tilted away from the generic directions observed in standard grating theory.

articleTitle: A Wideband Slot Pair Array Based on SIDL Technology for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel linearly polarized substrate-integrated double line (SIDL) slot array is presented in this paper. By introducing differential-mode (DM) excitation, the SIDL slot pair can obtain a low cross-polarization level and wide bandwidth.
