Additionally, the parallel-series feed network based on hybrid microstrip and SIDL structure is adopted to halve the length of the SIDL, the bandwidth is further increased. As a proof-of-concept, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> slot pair array is designed and measured. The measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> is below-10 dB from 23.3 GHz to 28.1 GHz (18.7 %), which agrees well with the simulation prediction. A peak gain of 23.2 dBi in the operating frequency band is obtained at 27 GHz in the measurements. Furthermore, the beam scanning ability is also verified via simulation for multi-beam applications.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Differentially-Fed Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on SRR
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized differentially fed circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna based on split-ring resonator (SRR) for WIFI applications is proposed. Capacitive gaps and metallic screws are used to construct the SRR structure. The CP antenna with a compact size is implemented by the two crossed dual-capacitor SRRs. Composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) loaded differential Wilkinson power divider is proposed to realize an integrated design and a relatively pure CP radiation. Owing to the novel SRR structure, a compact size of 0.24 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}\times 0.24\lambda_{0}\times 0.04\lambda_{0}(}$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}}$</tex> is the free space wavelength at 2.4 GHz) is achieved. The measured -10 dB impedance and 3 dB AR bandwidth are 16.25% and 3.3%, respectively. The measured peak gain and efficiency are 5.5 dBic and 81.3%, respectively.

articleTitle: Tolerance Analysis of Continuous and Discrete Apertures Through a Novel Probabilistic Interval Arithmetic Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a probabilistic interval analysis method for the tolerance analysis of discrete and continuous apertures. Given the knowledge of the interval tolerances, and starting from inclusive pattern bounds obtained using state-of-art interval analysis tools, a novel methodology is here introduced that allows to compute, in closed-form, the probability distribution of the random pattern occurrences within the interval bounds. A numerical example is reported showing the advantage of the proposed approach with respect to the state-of-art interval analysis methods.

articleTitle: Circular Horn Antenna with Ring and Coaxial Grooves for Dual Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new dual-band horn consisting of a tapered section, coaxial grooves section, and a ring projection installed between both sections in order to achieve rotationally symmetric beam, low cross-polarization components, and compact size over a wide frequency range. The effective design procedure for this antenna that optimizes two sections individually is described. As a design example, we present a compact horn antenna with low cross-polar level less than −30 dB at both center frequencies 7.8 GHz and 26 GHz of specified two bands.

articleTitle: A Metasurface Design for Enhancing In-Body Signal Transmission in Biomedical Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a metasurface for improving signal penetration inside biological medium and reducing the reflection at the air-tissue interface for microwave imaging applications. We started from the design of a common bow-tie antenna working at 2.56 GHz and then we developed a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{5\times 5}$</tex> metasurface to be interposed between the antenna and the tissue. The numerical simulation demonstrated that the transmission coefficient in presence of the designed metasurface is 6.8 dB higher than the isolated bow-tie case. Moreover, the combination of compactness and easy fabrication makes this design appropriate for future integration in portable systems.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assisted Array Synthesis Under Mutual Coupling and Platform Effects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An efficient machine learning assisted array synthesis (MLAAS) method is proposed for practical array designs under mutual coupling and platform effects. By introducing machine learning methods, the impact of the electromagnetic environment on the antenna element is learned and utilized to build surrogate models for active element patterns and S- parameters. Compared with conventional methods, the proposed MLAAS is able to achieve great prediction accuracy based on limited numbers of full-wave simulations. Moreover, the algorithm is able to deal with array design problems with variable element numbers, which is validated using a practical antenna array design task.

articleTitle: A Passive Phased-Array Antenna Module
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{4\times 4}$</tex> passive phased-array antenna module is presented. The antenna array incorporates slot-coupled patch antennas with left-handed circularly-polarized (LHCP) radiation. The phase shifter employed in the system operates based on the principle of loaded-transmission line phase shifters. The proposed phase shifter has compact size, and low insertion loss and it covers full range of phase tuning. The simulation results show peak gain of 16.8 dBic and radiation efficiency of 73% at boresight at the frequency of 29 GHz.

articleTitle: A Folded Waveguide Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a folded waveguide reflectarray antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a horn as the feed, a top reflector and a bottom reflector. Unlike other presented folded reflectarray antennas whose bottom layers are printed structures, waveguide-based polarization converter is designed as the bottom layer to twist the polarization. Besides, benefit from the folded design concept, the proposed reflectarray antenna has a compact structure and planar top surface. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna achieves 18.0 dBi peak gain at the operating bandwidth from 10.9 GHz to 11.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Branch Dual-band Monopole Based MIMO Antenna for 5G mm-wave Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An eight element dual-band MIMO antenna operating at n257 and n260 band frequencies for 5G operation in smart phones is delineated in this article. To reserve an apposite space for the other antennas, the elements are positioned symmetrically alongside the longer edges of the smartphone, with 4 antenna elements on each side. The individual antenna element is a dual-branch monopole with a vertical orientation and is fed by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\Omega$</tex> micro-strip line. With the center frequencies at 28 GHz, and 38 GHz a −10 dB impedance matching bandwidth of 2.5 GHz and 3 GHz are observed, respectively. A maximum gain of 8 dBi is observed at the lower band resonant mode frequency and a maximum gain of 5 dBi is observed at the upper band resonant mode frequency for the single antenna element.

articleTitle: Multiport broadband 5G MIMO antenna with very high isolation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new unidirectional radiating structure with 4 independent radiation patterns, with an isolation of more than 24 dB, and with a bandwidth of 20 %, oriented for use in 5G indoor MIMO base stations. The element can be used as a building block for arrays with a number of antennas of 4x4 or more. The radiating elements are triangular cavities derived from a square cavity with the TMz 11 mode. The 4-port antenna has a very low profile, with a height of 5 mm and the dimensions of the ground plane are less than one wavelength.

articleTitle: Non-invasive Aqueous Glucose Monitoring using Microwave Sensor with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a microwave dipole sensor is used with machine learning algorithms to build a non-invasive CGM system. Preliminary, the sensor is used on aqueous (water-glucose) solutions with different glucose concentrations to check the sensitivity of the sensor to those different glucose concentrations. Machine learning is used to extract the appropriate features from the signals coming from the aqueous solutions and then to build the regression model using those extracted features to be able to predict the actual glucose levels. Using more than 19 regression models, the results showed a good accuracy with Root Mean Square Error <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{(RMSE)=6.7}$</tex> by Matern 5/2 Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) algorithm. More data is needed to improve the accuracy of the prediction.

articleTitle: Surface Equivalence Theory for 5G MIMO Metasuraface Lens Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper applies the concept of surface equivalence theorem to design metasurface lens (metalens) antennas for 5G MIMO applications. Fictitious surface electric and magnetic currents are implemented through non periodic metasurfaces to create the required field discontinuity for radiation in the desired direction. The method has the advantage of customizing the wave front based on the generated electric and magnetic fields generated by the feeding antenna. As an example, a metalens is designed for three dual-polarized stack patch antennas for the operation at the 5G sub-6GHz band of 3.1-3.6 GHz. The designed six-port MIMO antenna provides three beams at 0 and +/−12 degrees with vertical and horizontal polarizations, with the maximum realized gain of 21 dBi and the aperture efficiency of over 33%.

articleTitle: Multi-frequencies Full-wave Simulations of Wave Propagation in Vegetation for Remote Sensing of Soil Moisture
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A two-step hybrid method combining both the analytical and numerical solutions is used to perform full-wave simulations of a wheat field at three different frequencies. First, the full-wave simulations of one single plant is performed using the HFSS and the multiple scattering within a single wheat plant is characterized using the T-matrix of vector cylindrical waves. Second, the scatterings among different plants are considered using the Foldy-Lax equations of multiple scattering theory (MST) and the extracted T-matrix. The transmission of microwaves through wheat field at the L-, S- and C-bands are calculated using the hybrid method. Results show that the full-wave based transmission is much larger than those obtained from the radiative transfer equations (RTE) model. Moreover, the attenuation caused by the vegetation layer would saturate as frequency increases and the full-wave transmission has a weaker frequency dependence than those of the RTE.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis of MIMO Base Station Antenna Arrays With Different Column Spacings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: One of the most important goals of multiple-input multiple-output systems is to achieve large channel capacity. Nevertheless, channel capacity decreases when antenna correlation increases, which can be characterized by correlation coefficient. Therefore, antenna engineers pay great attention to correlation coefficient, however, there are very few literatures on the study of correlation coefficient analysis of multi-port MIMO antenna array with feeding networks. This paper analyzes correlation coefficients of three 4×4 MIMO base station antenna arrays with different column spacings, which includes four-way power splitters. Some useful characteristics are summarized in this paper and can be used as the reference of research on correlation of MIMO antenna array with feeding networks.

articleTitle: High Gain Low Profile CTS Antenna Array for Satcom Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wide band continuous transverse stub array is presented in printed circuit board (PCB) technology. The array of slots is fed by a multi-layer corporate network. A pillbox beam former illuminates the corporate network and generates the required phase front. Numerical results show a reflection coefficient lower than −10 dB in the K/Ka-band (more than 50% bandwidth). Beam scanning is achieved along the slots of the array (H-plane). The maximum realized gain is 21 dBi at 29 GHz. The estimated efficiency is higher than 45% in the band.

articleTitle: Location and Identification of Linear and Nonlinear Targets in 3D using PI-DORT and Time of Flight
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses combining PI-DORT with time-of-flight measurement to realize location and identification of linear and nonlinear targets in three dimensions (3D). DORT (a French acronym for “Decomposition of the Time Reversal Operator”) is used to identify multiple targets in bistatic detection with pulse inversion (PI) being employed to distinguish nonlinear scatterers from linear scatterers. The resulting technique, PI-DORT, is then combined with time-of-flight (ToF) to allow for 3D target location in complex, multi-target environments containing both linear and nonlinear targets. The result is an approach combining PI-DORT and time-of-flight measurements to identify and locate targets in 3D.

articleTitle: Primary Surface Transition Modules for Metasurface Designs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The notion of 0-D circuit has been extensively and successfully developed and has been proven to be a powerful tool in the design, innovation, and discovery of new functionalities in circuits. This paper thus extends and applies the mathematical machinery and tools of circuit theory to the 2-D surface transition structures. To achieve this, we first find patch and mesh sheets as primary surface transition modules, then adopt the surface susceptibility and surface porosity as characteristic parameters. At last, we design an example space filter using the proposed framework.

articleTitle: The Permanent Magnet Based Reluctance Modulated VLF Transmitter: An Equivalent Circuit Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) analysis of a VLF /ULF transmitter based on reluctance modulation of the medium surrounding a permanent magnet is presented in this paper. To investigate the structure, the transmitter's MEC is interpreted in two ways, the most straightforward and the comprehensive. According to the MEC analysis, the nonlinear properties of the surrounding magnetic material are essential in modulation effectiveness. Using MEC analysis, the aim is to optimize the architecture by releasing the maximum available energy from the permanent magnet for modulation.

articleTitle: Broadband and Wide Angular Stable Inductive Grid-Based Linear to Circular Transmission Type Polarizer for Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a broadband transmissive type linear-circular polarizer with wide angular stability is demonstrated. It shows a 3 dB Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth of 21.05 GHz (from 20.17 - 41.22 GHz) with 68.58 % fractional bandwidth (FBW) covering K and Ka-bands. The angular stability of the converter is examined, and it possesses a stable AR response up to 50° (for ϕ = 0°) and 40° (for ϕ = 90°). The design is compact with the periodicity of 0.107λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> x 0.141λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the free-space wavelength corresponding to the lowest frequency over the broadband. Authors' strongly believed that the proposed design has broadband 3 dB AR, better angular stability, and compactness made it suitable for countervailing the effect of Faraday rotation in satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Design of Series- fed Patch Array with Modified Binomial Coefficients for MIMO Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a collocated antenna configuration having three transmitter and five receiver arrays for automotive MIMO Radar application. The individual antenna arrays consist of a seven-element series fed array with the feed provided at the edge. We introduce a modified-binomial coefficient-based excitation scheme to achieve improved side-lobe level (SLL) in series-fed patch arrays with edge feeding. The proposed MIMO configuration exhibits low SLL less than 16 dB and a wide field-of-view (FoV) of about 80° in the azimuth plane, along with satisfactory angular resolution (5.82°) and low cross-polar level (30 dB), rendering it extremely suitable for automotive medium-range radar (MRR) application.

articleTitle: Compact, Small, Chip-Inductor-Loaded Wi-Fi 6E Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact chip-inductor-loaded monopole antenna for 2.4/5/6 GHz WLAN operation with new 6 GHz (5925–7125 MHz) band is presented. The antenna occupies a small size of 4 mm x 16 mm only, easily fitted in the bezel above the notebook display. The design consists of a symmetrical, two-branched monopole with two shorting inductors for generating the 5 and new 6 GHz WLAN bands. With further loading the chip inductor at the end of the monopole branch and connecting it to a tuning portion, the lower-band resonant mode in the 2.4 GHz band can be obtained. Good radiation characteristics are achieved too. The proposed design is promising for Wi-Fi 6E notebook antennas with new 6 GHz band.

articleTitle: UWB Antipodal Antenna With Parasitic Patch and Elliptical Cylindrical Dielectric For Concealed Object Detection with Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a high gain Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Antipodal Antenna (AA) with four paddle shaped stubs, an elliptical parasitic patch and a elliptical cylindrical dielectric enclosure utilizing a systematic approach, for microwave imaging of concealed metal objects. Initially the paddle shaped stubs are designed and their performance are optimized. Then, the elliptical patch is added to improve the high frequency performance. Lastly an elliptical cylindrical dielectric was introduced to further enhance the antenna performance. The proposed antenna provides simulated return loss of < 10 dB over 1.3 - 14 GHz with a simulated peak gain of 13.2 dBi at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact and Wideband $4\times 4$ Butler Matrix for Millimeter-wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and wideband (24 GHz-27.5 GHz) switched beam antenna array consists of a 4-dipole antennas fed by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> Butler matrix is presented. The Butler matrix is designed on a multilayer structure based on elliptically shaped <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{45^{\mathrm{o}}}$</tex> phase shifters and 3 dB hybrid couplers to improve the impedance bandwidth and eliminate crossover. A broadband printed-dipole antenna is designed and developed to an array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda/2}$</tex> (at 26 GHz) inter-element spacing to fully utilize the beam-switching capability. Simulated radiation patterns of the integrated planar array with the proposed Butler matrix showed 4 output beams for different input port excitation with an average 8dBi radiation gain in the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Using a 2-Bit Programmable Metasurface for Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have attracted significant interest as an enabling technology for future sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication networks. Programmable metasurfaces are a relatively low-cost and lowcomplexity architecture for realizing dynamic RIS arrays. This paper presents the design and simulation of a 128 element programmable metasurface antenna in a reflectarray configuration operating at 6 GHz with direct phase and frequency modulating capability for index modulation. This metasurface is a functional demonstration prototype and tile building block for larger RIS arrays. Specifically, we present full-wave simulation results of a meta-atom with 2-bit quantized phase shifts with an average reflection amplitude loss of 0.34 dB over all coding states. To the best of our knowledge, our 2-bit meta-atom design achieves lower reflection amplitude loss at the design frequency and is electrically thinner than existing designs. Additionally, we present full-wave simulation results of our 128 element RIS finite array performing beam steering and phase modulation.

articleTitle: On the Importance of the Love's Condition for Inverse Equivalent-Source Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The importance of the Love's condition for inverse equivalent-source approaches for metasurface design is clarified and formalized herein. A review of important concepts is provided to show that the enforcement of Love's condition is necessary to obtain Maxwellian fields which are then used to obtain the metasurface parameters. We clarify that this enforcement is not only necessary for reflectionless metasurfaces, but also necessary to obtain a desired reflection all the while maintaining the correct field transformation.

articleTitle: Sequential Deep Learning for In-Home Activity Monitoring Using mm-Wave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a stand-alone mm-wave radar system coupled with deep learning algorithms as the basis of an autonomous in-home free-living, physical activity recognition system. Using the mm-wave radar system, human spectrograms (time-varying micro-doppler patterns) are used to train deep Gated Recurrent Networks (GRU) to identify physical activities performed by a subject in his living environment. An overall model accuracy of 93% was achieved to classify five in-home physical activities. The system enables free-living human activity monitoring and gait cycle identification.

articleTitle: 2.75-Bit Reflecting Unit Cell Design for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a phase-shifting unit cell for a reconfigurable intelligent surface capable of exhibiting 8 discrete phase states at 5G mid-band. An individually addressable unit cell embedded with 3 PIN diodes has been designed to provide enhanced phase resolution with a minimal number of active components. A particle swarm optimisation algorithm has been employed in order to maximise the phase state separation whilst minimising reflection loss and unit cell periodicity. Simulations are performed with extracted PIN diode and capacitor Sparameters for a realistic estimation of the fabricated device performance, with a resulting simulated average reflection loss of 1 dB and equivalent phase resolution of 2.75-bits.

articleTitle: Liquid-Metal-Tuned Patch Element for Flexible and Reconfigurable Reflectarrays/Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible and reconfigurable reflecting element based on liquid metal encapsulated in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The proposed unit cell provides precise reflection phase tuning of over 360° by pneumatically extending or retracting liquid metal in channels spiraling outward from a square patch. The flexible materials are well suited to realize deployable or conformal reflecting surfaces for devices such as reflectarrays or reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs). To demonstrate use of the reflecting element, a curved <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$12\ \text{element} \times 12\ \text{element}$</tex> array operating at 8.425 GHz is designed and verified using full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Chamber-Decay Time in a mm-Wave Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present results of a novel mm-wave reverberation chamber, where we discuss the role of the chamber quality factor and chamber decay time, or time constant, for mm-wave applications. For the first time, we analyze the uncertainty due to antenna positioning for these metrics in such a chamber, where we show that the quality factor computed in the frequency domain has a higher uncertainty due to antenna positioning than its time domain counterpart. We describe that the the chamber decay time and quality factor are lower for mm-wave chambers as compared to lower-frequency (sub-6 GHz) chambers, but that they can still function as ideal candidates for metrics revolving around losses.

articleTitle: High Gain Antenna Using Dielectric Slabs and Electromagnetic Band Gap Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a unique design perspective to reduce the size of the feeding network of a linear antenna array. The proposed technique provides a generalization of using either electric or magnetic excitations, with dielectric or magnetic rectangular slabs. This technique has a significant impact on reducing the complexity of the feeding network. The realized structure has a low profile, low cost, and compact size features.

articleTitle: A 3–9 GHz UWB High-Gain Conformal End-Fire Vivaldi Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel conformal Vivaldi antenna array with two elements is designed to achieve 3–9 GHz ultra-wideband (UWB) high-gain end-fire radiation. By employing a flexible printed circuit and two Vivaldi antenna elements, this conformal antenna array has a wide bandwidth and low cross-polarization levels. In addition, a feeding network provides a co-phase equal amplitude excitation of the array to create the required high-gain end-fire radiation within the operating band. Simulated reflection coefficient illustrates that an impedance bandwidth of 102.5 % is obtained from 3.06 GHz to 9.5 GHz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathbf{S}_{11}\vert < \boldsymbol{-10}$</tex> dB. Within the operating band, the range of realized gain is 8.81-15.18 dBi, and stable end-fire radiation patterns are maintained.

articleTitle: A Compact Low-Cost and Lightweight 3-D Printed Horn Antenna for UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a 3-D printed compact and lightweight horn antenna suitable for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The antenna has dimensions of 7.8 cm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(0.13\lambda_{0})\times 3.7\text{cm}(0.06\lambda_{0})\times 4.5}$</tex> cm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(0.08\lambda_{0})}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}}$</tex> refers to the lowest operating frequency. The weight of the antenna is only 23 gm. The horn geometry is constructed by nickel spray coating on a 3-D printed PLA (Polylactic Acid) supporting structure. This makes the antenna extremely lightweight and low-cost. The antenna covers a bandwidth of 0.5-3.5 GHz. Although the gain of the antenna crosses 0 dB after 2.4 GHz, it is quite significant (~5 dB) at around 3.5 GHz. A prototype of the antenna was fabricated and tested which showed good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Enhanced Joint Inversion of Multiphysics Data with Nonconforming Discretization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Join inversion has been playing an important role in integrating multiphysics data to reduce inversion uncertainties and improve resolution. In this paper, we propose a deep learning enhanced (DLE) joint inversion framework which enforces structural similarity by a deep neural network (DNN) and considers nonconforming discretizations of different physical models due to the resolution capability of different measuring data. The framework enables the DNN to fuse and extract the information from separate inversion workflows in the model domain and improves the joint inversion result iteratively. Interpolation can be performed due to the model domain fusion to deal with the nonconforming discretizations. Numerical examples demonstrate the inverted models by our DLE method have more accurate property values and better structural features compared to traditional separate inversions.

articleTitle: An IC-Enabled Metasurface Producing OAM and Pencil Beams
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The capabilities of a multifunctional metasurface design are explored in this work. The metasurface's meta-atoms are equipped with a programmable integrated circuit. The programable integrated circuit loads the meta-atom at four locations to control the reflection coefficient. With this ability a complex reflection pattern is generated. The generated reflected pattern consists of a pencil beam and a second beam which has an orbital angular momentum. The presented design operates in the vicinity of 4.1 GHz and has the potential to be incorporated in future metasurface-aided wireless telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Biconical Antenna: A Wideband Benchmark Antenna for IEEE P2816
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present here the exact expressions and numerical results for a general angle biconical antenna, which serves as a benchmark geometry for the ongoing P2816: IEEE Recommended Practice for Computational Electromagnetics Applied to Modeling and Simulation of Antennas.

articleTitle: Dual-Components Magnetic Probe for Electromagnetic Interference Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-components magnetic probe which can measure the magnetic fields <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{x}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{y}$</tex> at the same time is proposed. The dual-components probe saves lots of scanning time when one need to measure both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{x}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{y}$</tex> in electromagnetic interference measurement. Its working frequency ranges from 20MHz to 6GHz. The probe is designed based on a four-layered printed circuit board. The simulation and measurement results show that the sensitivity of the fabricated probe is high, and even higher than the commercial single component magnetic probe.

articleTitle: In-Package Integrated Dielectric Lens Paired with a MIMO mm-Wave Radar for Corridor Gait Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a first-of-its-kind corridor/hallway gait monitoring system. A dielectric hyperbolic lens antenna is designed and integrated in the housing package of a commercially available low-cost MIMO FMCW radar to provide long-range detection and sharpen the wide beam of the printed circuit board radar antennas. Measurement results show that the proposed system achieves approximately 14 dB gain improvements compared to the stand-alone radar module. Additionally, we validate the improved system functionality through capturing the spatiotemporal gait values accurately (e.g., speed, step points, step count, step time, step length, and cadence) in a highly reflective hallway.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Flexible Circularly Polarized Implantable Antenna for Biotelemetry Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Flexible implantable antennas have got much attention in the field of biotelemetry applications. So, a circularly polarized compact size wideband implantable antenna for the applications of biomedical telemetry is presented in this research work. The proposed design is being operated in ISM (industrial scientific, and medical) band at 5.8 GHz for medical applications. The antenna consists of the discrete ground circular patch and a CPW (coplanar waveguide) fed radiating patch printed on a Polyimide substrate. The overall size of the design is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\times 3\times 0.15\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The antenna covers the bandwidth from 3.4 GHz to 7 GHz (3.6 GHz). The design is being simulated inside human tissues like skin, fat, and muscle. The antenna gives circularly polarized behaviour at 5.8 GHz. This proposed design is well-suited for medical implantable applications.

articleTitle: Microwave Planar Sensor Antenna for Glucose Sensing in Aqueous Solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Microwave sensing is a vastly growing sensory method that allows to reduce sensing limits in biomedical applications. In this paper, a coupled complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) design is introduced that exploits the mutual coupling between CSRRs, thereby creating a highly sensitive region for capacitive changes. An ultra-wideband binomial slot antenna is employed to feed the coupled-CSRRs with an improved excitation signal. This technique requires phase measurement only at the single frequency of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">res</inf>= 2.77 GHz. As a result, glucose content in water within the range of 0 – 500 mg/dL are detectable with the sensitivity better than 30 mg/dL.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Circularly Polarized Millimeter-Wave Antenna using 3D Additive Manufacturing Dielectric Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a novel single-layer printed feed used with a low-cost 3D printed polarizer. The feed is made on a single substrate layer. The proposed antenna gain is 15 dBi, and the overlapped impedance-axial ratio bandwidth is 20 %.

articleTitle: Multiband 4-Port DGS MIMO Antenna with DR Isolating Element for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A multiband 4 port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna design functioning in 2.4/5GHz and 5G applications is analyzed. The size of proposed MIMO antenna is 45x45 mm2, where the dielectric resonator (DR) material having a height of 6 mm has been deployed as an isolating element to reduce the mutual coupling among the antenna elements. The 4-port DGS MIMO antenna functions in the 2.4 (2.4-2.6) GHz, 5G New Radio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{n}77/78/79(3.3-5.0)$</tex> GHz and 5 (5.15-5.75) GHz with enhanced isolation of above 20dB among the antenna elements. Furthermore, from the design analysis and results explicitly explained in the manuscript, it is confirmed that the proposed 4 port DGS MIMO antenna is considerable for wireless applications.

articleTitle: RFID Tag Analysis Using an Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze one of the most common UHF RFID tag antenna structures, a T-matched dipole. We for the first time derive the closed-form solutions for the resonant frequencies of tag sensitivity and backscatter responses as functions of tag equivalent circuit parameters. We apply our general analysis to a 70 mm x 14 mm T-matched RFID tag with Monza R6 and show a good agreement between the model, the measurements, and the derived formulas.

articleTitle: Flat Panel Interlaced Shared Aperture Antenna Array for LEO Ka-band High Throughput Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact, single layer shared aperture antenna array capable of serving LEO satellite communication. The shared aperture array presented here uses a triangular lattice to reduce grating lobes while allowing close tessellation of the receive and transmit elements. The array provides beamforming of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-40^{\circ} < \theta < +40^{\circ}$</tex> in all azimuth directions. Quadrature feeding is utilized in both the receive and transmit antenna elements to enable reconfigurable circular polarization. This work demonstrates a method to serve LEO satellite communication from a compact, single layer antenna array ideal for integration in vehicles, UAVs and backpacks.

articleTitle: Polarization-Insensitive Circular Reflectarray for Satellite Applications in Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A polarization-insensitive circular refiectarray antenna (RA) for long-distance wireless communications is investigated. By combining patches, dipoles, and rings, a polarization-insensitive unit cell is achieved. With a phase variation of around 314° between 30 GHz and 32 GHz, a circular reflectarray with a radius of 400 mm is built. Simulation results indicate a maximum realized gain of 27.6 dB at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Dynamic Dual-Reflector Antennas for High-Resolution Real-Time SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents two novel dual-reflector antennas that can generate a synthetic array of phase centers for high frame-rate, high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. The antennas consist of a main reflector and a sub-reflector which physically move to shift the phase center of a single transceiver. Digital beamforming is then used to generate a pencil beam with a Half Power Beamwidth (HPBW) less than 0.3° and side-lobe levels below −15 dB for a scanning angle of ±10° in both azimuth and elevation. The estimated array formation time (i.e. inverse of frame-rate) is a fraction of a second. The antennas are designed for a SAR system operating at 240 GHz. Physical optics (PO) is used to model the far-field characteristics. The analytical models are corroborated using the ANSYS HFSS Integral Equation solver.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction in Dual Differential-Fed $2\times 1$ Phased Array with Polarization and Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Mutual coupling reduction in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 1$</tex> phased array with six polarization states and two sets of radiation is presented in this paper. Implementing different power and phase at four differential-fed pairs results in six polarization states with the mainlobe at broadside, including 0°, 90°, ±45° linear polarization (LP), right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP). An end-fire radiation pattern can also be achieved for one more degree of freedom. Moreover, an electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure is applied at the patch level to improve the mutual coupling between four differential-fed pairs. A minimum improvement of 11dB in the mutual coupling between the pairs along the X-axis across the frequency band of 9.3-9.5 GHz is achieved for the proposed multiport system. The peak realized gain for the broadside main-beam and end-fire main-beam at 9.4 GHz are 10 dBi and 6.6 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Bow-tie Slot Antenna Loaded with Superstrate Layers for 5G/6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) based bow-tie slot antenna loaded with superstrate layers is designed for 5G/6G applications. Three layers of cylindrical shaped superstrate material are cascaded forming dielectric lens shape. These layers cover the antenna slot and used to improve both the antenna gain and bandwidth. To implement these layers, a perforation technique is provided to achieve the equivalent effective dielectric constant surrounding the cylindrical shaped layers. The antenna gain is enhanced by 1.6 dBi through loading the antenna with the lens structure, while the operating bandwidth is almost doubled to be in the range 30.5-39.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for 5G Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper outlines the design, fabrication, and characterization of a 5.8 GHz reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) suitable for 5G wireless communication applications. The proposed RIS can be deployed as a dynamically reconfigurable relay to steer the base station (BS) signal to desired directions, thereby eliminating shadow regions or improving the SNR at the receiver (user). The RIS prototype consists of a 16×10 array of patch antennas integrated with radio-frequency (RF) PIN diodes and uses a control circuit to realize the beam-steering functionality. The design features a planar, single layer topology that is compatible with future millimeter wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) RISs. The beamforming capability is evaluated with field tests.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of 90°-Bend in NRD Guide Using DBS Algorithm and 2D-FVFEM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An optimal design approach based on the mosaic-like structure concept for NRD guide devices is proposed in this paper. In order to achieve efficient design with high transmission efficiency, and minimum computational effort, we employ recently proposed two-dimensional full-vectorial finite element method (2D-FVFEM) for numerical simulations. Non-linear direct binary search algorithm is implemented as an optimization problem to obtain the optimal NRD guide device at operating frequency 60GHz. In order to prove the significance of the proposed optimization approach we designed an NRD 90°-bend guide and it achieves more than 99% transmission efficiency. The analysis of numerical results by 2D-FVFEM are also verified by 3D-FVFEM.

articleTitle: Analysis of Optimized Subarray Configuration for Cross Polarization Reduction for Phased Array Antennas used in Weather Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a dual linearly polarized, high isolation, optimized cross-polarization, phased array patch an-tenna that operates in the frequency range of 2.65 to 3.00 GHz. The antenna uses stacked radiating patches that are aperture coupled to the microstrip feed line. The isolation between two polarizations is 50 dB while the cross-polarization for both H-and V-polarization is −55 dB using an optimized 2×2 subarray technique. The subarray is used in a 2×20 elements array to attain the required cross-polarization at various angles (azimuth) in the range of −60° to 60°. The simulated S-parameters for the antenna element and the subarray radiation patterns at both polarizations are presented. The radiation patterns of the phased array at various scan angles are also presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A Wideband CP Cavity-Backed SIW Antenna Fed by Printed-RGW Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In This paper, a novel wideband circularly polarized (CP) cavity-backed substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna is introduced for wireless communications in the millimeter-wave band. The designed antenna is fed using printed ridge-gap waveguide (Printed-RGW) technology with impedance bandwidth from 27.05 to 29.38 GHz. The proposed antenna is achieved a directive pattern with a gain of 7.4 dBic at 28 GHz. In addition, it has a wide-angle 3-dB axial ratio, which can be a good candidate for mm-wave satellite communications.

articleTitle: Low Cost IR-UWB Radar for Multisubject Non-Contact Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Impulse Radar Ultra-Wideband (IR-UWB) radar has a high range resolution due to its available wide band; thus, it can precisely localize more than one target along its range. However, it has been criticized for its inefficiency in terms of complexity and cost when used for vital sign detection. Here, we utilize a low-cost novel IR radar chip for non-contact vital-sign sensing that could be used for either single or multiple subjects' vital sign detection. The approach uses a commercial low cost 8 GHz IR-UWB Doppler radar chip with a combination of arctangent demodulation (AD) and Short-Time State-Space Method (ST-SSM) algorithms to successfully and accurately extract the phase variation signals to estimate the respiration rate and heart rate of a subject. Precise range information of the scene is utilized to clearly discern multiple targets, making it possible to detect vital signs multiple targets within the few cm range resolution. The proposed method can accurately operate in real time and it is feasible to be used for patients' health tracking, elderly care, emergency surveillance, and infant sleep apnea monitoring as well.

articleTitle: Compact High-Gain Dual-Band Antenna for Full-Duplex Terahertz Communication in CubeSat Mega-Constellations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: With the rise of CubeSat constellations, higher data rates are desired for commercial and scientific applications in space. A candidate technology for high-data-rate CubeSat communications is the terahertz (THz) band (0.1-10 THz), providing a large bandwidth at smaller wavelengths, pushing towards more compact technology. In this paper, a dual-band feed horn, utilizing a single commercially available WR3 waveguide, enhanced with a deployable reflector is designed and simulated. Gains of 40 dBi and 42 dBi are achieved at 218 GHz and 295 GHz respectively. The antenna can compactly fit on a 12U CubeSat and is explored as a solution for high-gain THz antennas within CubeSat requirements.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband RF Self Interference Cancellation Filter for STAR Radios
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Spectrum scarcity in a highly congested radio environment call for simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) radios. A key challenge in STAR radios is the self-interference cancellation (SIC) of the signals that leak from the transmitter into the receiver. With this in mind, this paper presents an ultra-wideband (UWB) RF-SIC filter capable of more than 20dB cancellation across 1GHz bandwidth. This SIC is part of a multistage cancellation scheme achieving more than 100dB of STAR isolation. Our presented SIC employs a filter bank with weight optimization to reach the noted unprecedented bandwidth. This design ensures phase linearity estimating the minimum number of filter stages. For optimization, a discrete-gradient descent algorithm is used to arrive at a practical SIC filter bank.

articleTitle: Multi-GPU based Leapfrog CDI-FDTD Method for Large-Scale Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A multi-GPU based implementation method is proposed for the recently proposed leapfrog complyingdivergence implicit finite-difference time-domain (CDI-FDTD). For solving the tridiagonal systems of leapfrog CDI-FDTD method with multiple GPUs, the SPIKE algorithm is employed to decompose the tridiagonal systems into sub-systems, which can be solved in parallel. Numerical results are given to evaluate the performance of the proposed multi-GPU based method.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Wideband Dielectric Rod Antenna with Surface Wave Manipulation at a Low Cost
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A rectangular dielectric rod antenna (RDRA) 3D printed using a liquid crystal display resin method, aiming at the improvement of the radiation pattern for a narrow beamwidth, low sidelobe level, and wide bandwidth is presented. To realize both good radiation performance and fabrication simplicity, aluminum oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})}$</tex> powder and air holes are used to modify the permittivity of the commercial resin. In addition, a horizontal air-cavity penetrating the middle of the dielectric rod is designed to eliminate higher-order surface wave modes. The antenna is 3.97 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}}$</tex> in length and holds an identical orthogonal cross-section of 0.48 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}\times 0.35}$</tex> λ0. Measurement results show that the proposed RDRA exhibits a gain of 12.7 dBi and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{32^{\circ}}$</tex> half-power beamwidth (HPBW) in both E- and H-plane at 24 GHz.

articleTitle: Design Method of Broadband Flat Metasurface Lenses by Using an One-Dimensional Distributed Transmission-Line Model
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a design method for broadband flat metasurface lenses by using an one-dimensional distributed transmission-line model. The design formula of the line length is shown and how to determine the characteristic impedance is stated. Circuit simulations are carried out to confirm the validity of the design method and broadband operations of a designed flat metasurface lens are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Jaumann-like Tuneable Rasorber with Enhanced Angular Stability and Polarisation Insensitivity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of a Jaumann-like reconfigurable rasorber is presented with wideband absorption and angularly stability. The rasorber is defined by a three-layer structure with two resistive layers composed of a Jerusalem cross surrounded by a square ring and tapered dipole arms loaded with resistors, whilst the lossless layer is composed of four small square ring slots. All three layers can tune their passband in the range from 4.4GHz to 6.9GHz using varactors biased by polarisation insensitive DC lines. Also, the three-layered structure has a small periodicity to provide angular stability up to 30° while also maintaining low insertion losses below 1.5dB.

articleTitle: A 230 GHz Orthomode Transducer with Simple Fabrication Steps
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a J-band orthomode transducer, featuring a simple structure for ease of fabrication using CNC machining. Two orthomode transducers are fabricated and measured which are shown to achieve an operational bandwidth of more than 7%, over which the return loss at all ports is better than 10 dB, and cross-polarization isolation is better than 30 dB. The insertion loss is minimized to an average between 2 and 3 dB using electroless gold plating.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Radiation Pattern Microstrip Patch Antenna with High Mode Purity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A single-layer, dual-mode circular microstrip patch antenna is presented to achieve reconfigurable radiation patterns with high mode purity. The broadside radiation pattern is achieved by a central circular patch, whereas conical radiation pattern is realized through a concentric shorted ring patch. With the simultaneous excitation of the two operating modes, the proposed antenna can generate self-scanning and self-nulling radiation patterns. The proposed antenna was fabricated and tested. Simulated and measured results show that the antenna produces stable broadside and conical radiation patterns with high mode purity at the design frequency of 10 GHz.

articleTitle: AWideband Slotted Microstrip Patch Antenna for mm-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A slotted microstrip patch antenna for 5G applications is presented in this paper. The proposed design addresses the intrinsic narrow bandwidth of patch antennas by introducing disconnected H slots to broaden the bandwidth. The slots introduce two extra resonances to broaden the bandwidth of the design. An impedance bandwidth of 24.31 – 31.11GHz was achieved to cover the entire 28GHz 5G band. A peak gain of 11.2dBi was also achieved with a minimum beamwidth of 34° over the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Polarized 5G Base Station Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-polarized base station filtering antenna with high selectivity is proposed. The four slots on the radiation patch and the metal block between the two ports are used to improve the port isolation. The slot lines can also adjust the resonance points of the antenna. The octagonal slot in the middle of the feed patch is used to adjust the input impedance, attaining the antenna operating band of 3.3-3.6 GHz with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 1.5. Besides, a high out-of-band gain-suppression level (>24 dB) can also be obtained without adding any filter structure. The proposed antenna has high potential in the 5G massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) applications.

articleTitle: Dual U-Slot Patch Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A new dual U-slot single microstrip patch antenna for 5G applications is presented. The antenna slot parameters are optimized to obtain a return loss below 10dB from 26.8GHz to 30.4 GHz and a gain values ranges between 8.3dBi and 9.3dBi within the same frequency range. These figures are considerably improved as compared to other slotted single patch elements available in the literature hence, the proposed element can be potentially used to design MIMO antennas for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Deterministic Wireless Propagation Model Assisted Indoor Positioning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we explore the application of deterministic wireless propagation models for the generation of radio maps used in fingerprinting-based indoor positioning. Four positioning algorithms, namely, the k-nearest neighbors (kNN), weighted k-nearest neighbors (WkNN), maximum a posterior (MAP), and minimum mean squared error (MMSE), are investigated. Their performance is examined with respect to the density of radio maps as well as the number and location of wireless access points.

articleTitle: Resonance-based Radar Target Classification using the Matrix Pencil Method and the Cauchy Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A comparison of the Matrix Pencil Method and the Cauchy Method is studied. The two methods both serve as natural resonant frequency extraction algorithm but is based on information in different domains. Their performances are analyzed using synthesized data and full-wave simulated data. Both methods present the capability to extract NRFs from targets. Numerical results are presented to show the similarity and differences between the two methods.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Stable Discretization of the Electric Field Integral Equation based on Poincaré's Lemma
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Integral equations become inaccurate in the low-frequency regime not only due to a low-frequency breakdown (i.e., growth of the condition number), but also due to catastrophic round-off errors in the discretization of the excitation. In this work, we propose a testing strategy for the excitation that results in a low-frequency stable discretization irrespective of the topology (i.e., simply- or multiply-connected) or orientability of the object. We obtain this by leveraging the lemma of Poincare to derive vector potentials for a general class of excitations. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Flexible and Scalable Additively Manufactured Antenna Array Tiles for Satellite and 5G Applications Using A Novel Rugged Microstrip-to-Microstrip Transition
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel flexible and scalable tiled antenna array operating at Ku band, with individual patch antenna tiles and a corporate feeding network achieved by microstrip-to-microstrip transition. Both simulation and measurements for a 2 by 2 array show good matching and radiation at center frequency. The basic structure of the four tiles array can be scaled to any larger array of 2^N elements by duplicating the feeding element. The feed line is flipped to make connection to each patch antenna. This design can be applied to scalable active phased-array radars and support future demand for high volume 5G communication.

articleTitle: Isolation Improvement in MIMO Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A high isolation in a closely spaced multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed in this article. Two rectangular dielectric resonators (DRs) are placed on top of substrate and are capacitively coupled to the microstrip line through rectangular slots. The isolation is achieved by applying a pair of metal strips printed on the lateral walls near the adjacent edges of the DRAs. The realized MIMO DRA has −10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 11.06%(14.1-15.75 GHz) with an isolation level of −25.5 dB to −32 dB. The realized gain ranges from 8.5 to 9.2 dBi. The performance comparison between the conventional (with no metallic strips) and the proposed design is conducted by keeping the minimum inter-element spacing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g=0.1$</tex> mm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.005\lambda_{0}$</tex>). The mechanism of the isolation improvement and the design procedure are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-based Stacked Patch Antenna for Wideband Circularly-Polarized Radiation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A metasurface-based stacked antenna is proposed for wideband circularly polarized (CP) applications. The proposed antenna consists of a metasurface, a patch radiator, a stacked patch, and a coaxial feed along the diagonal line. The antenna prototype is with 2- VSWR bandwidth (2- VSWRBW) of 30.9% (3.28 GHz - 4.48 GHz), 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (3dB-ARBW) of 17.5% (3.65 GHz - 4.35 GHz), and gain greater than 7.25 dBic across the 3dB-ARBW with maximum gain of 8.25 dBic at 4.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Ku/Ka Wide-Band Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Shared-Aperture Phased Array Antenna with High Aperture Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A Ku/Ka wide-band dual-band dual-polarized shared-aperture antenna with high aperture radiation efficiency is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of 8×8 Ku-band vertical-polarized dipole antenna array fed by microstrip line to strip line and 8×8 Ka-band horizontal-polarized waveguide antenna array fed by microstrip line to substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) to fin line, which are both used to connect with T/R modules and brick chips. To increase the aperture radiation efficiency, each Ku-band linear array is inserted in its adjacent two Ka-band linear arrays along the wide side of the Ka-band waveguide elements. Thanks to the super thin thickness of the Ku-band end-fire antenna (only 0.644 mm), it does not increase any extra aperture area for the whole array. Therefore, the aperture radiation efficiency can reach to 86.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>-96.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> and 82.1%-96.9% at Ku- and Ka-bands, respectively. In addition, by using wide-band radiating elements for both two bands, a broad impedance relative bandwidth 25% in Ku-band and 11.4% in Ka-band can be obtained. By eliminating the blind area within the scanning process, the wide scanning angle of ±60°, ±50°, ±35° at 14 GHz, 16 GHz, 18 GHz, and ±40°, ±40°, ±35° at 33 GHz, 35 GHz, 37 GHz can be achieved in both E- and H-planes, respectively.

articleTitle: Switched Beam Steering Antenna System at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An electronic switched-beam steering antenna system based on multiport grid array antenna (GAA) is demonstrated at Ka-band of 28 GHz. The proposed GAA antenna system consists of a nine-port GAA and a switching network board. The nine beams can be steered electronically in different directions with a coverage of ±20° with antenna gain greater than 14 dBi at 28GHz.

articleTitle: A Biodegradable Textile-based Graphene Antenna for 5G Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a textile-based antenna for the currently deployed fifth-generation (5G) wireless bands. The proposed antenna consists of a coplanar-waveguide (CPW)-fed patch with truncated sides and a pair of L-shaped stubs as a part of ground geometry. The antenna has a bandwidth of 3.3-3.8 GHz, a peak gain of 3.17 dBi at 3.7 GHz and an efficiency of 64%. The antenna is designed on denim fabric and offers desired flexibility and ease of integration as a part of a garment, environmentally friendly and biodegradable attributes of graphene due to non-metallic nature, and affordability in terms of manufacturing cost.

articleTitle: Magnetic Coupling WPT Efficiency Improvement by Inserting Relay Coil with Optimized Load Impedance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method using optimized load impedance and parasitic relay coil to improve the power transmission efficiency in the magnetic field coupling wireless power transmission. Although the relay coil is effective to enhance the WPT efficiency, it is not always effective in improving the maximum power transmission efficiency that uses a matching circuit. To address the issue, this paper adopts inserting a load in series with coil port. By optimizing the load impedance using an electromagnetic field analysis, the efficiency without the matching circuit can be increased. The difference between the efficiency and the maximum power transmission efficiency with the matching circuit can also be reduced. Both of the efficiency and the maximum efficiency of WPT could be improved by inserting the relay coil when the same impedance elements are loaded on all of the power transmission coil, power reception coil, and relay coil.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Integral Quantities of Over the Air Automotive Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This document outlines the Over the Air (OTA) testing methodology which is currently employed for full automotive antennas and provides a pertinent Figure of Merit.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Circularly polarized Single-layer Metasurface Antenna using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized single layer low profile metasurface (MTS) antenna fed through a Coplanar waveguide (CPW). The metasurface is constituted by 3x4 rectangular loop cells. In a different way to that of the conventional rectangular MTS, the proposed loop unit cell presents a compact size due to its inductive effect. The characteristic mode analysis shows that two orthogonal modes can be excited for circular polarization radiation. Simulated results show an impedance band of 20.8% and a 3dB axial ratio band of 5.1% with a peak realized gain of 8dBi.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Study of E Shaped Slotted Microstrip Patch Antenna by HFSS for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes simulation study results of E shaped slotted Microstrip patch antenna using HFSS for possible application in 5G, GPS, WiMAX/WLAN applications. A novel defected ground structure (DGS) microstrip rectangular patch antenna with narrow slot is studied for multiband operation. The proposed antenna resonates at three distinctive frequencies such as 4.6 GHz, 8 GHz, and 10 GHz. With bandwidth in the 90 MHz-500 MHz range and maximum gain 8.03 dB.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Three-Port Antenna for Compact Polarization and Pattern Diversity Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a compact three-port antenna enabling polarization and pattern diversity at the 915 MHz ISM band. In order to achieve small-form-factor, the proposed design combines a miniaturized bow-tie patch split in half with an air-gap and a short top-loaded folded monopole. The folded monopole is located along the gap in the middle of the patch on a small common ground. The complementary characteristics of voltage-current distribution between the patch and monopole in the middle allows them to be co-located with minimal mutual coupling effects. The patch is fed by aperture coupling and feed probe independently to produce two orthogonally polarized broadside radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of A Compact Archimedean Spiral Antenna for 2-18 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A hybrid technique of using an electromagnetic (EM) absorbing material and a set of resistors are proposed to improve the low frequency matching and axial ratio of an Archimedean spiral antenna for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2-18\ GHz$</tex>. A cavity of depth 5 mm is maintained to make the structure extremely compact. Simulations are performed to analyze the effects of these approaches separately. A Wideband matching and polarization purity are observed over the entire frequency range with a maximum right-hand circular (RH) gain of 8.2 dBiC.

articleTitle: A Wave Matrix Approach to Designing Azimuthally-Varying Cylindrical Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A general wave matrix approach to efficiently analyzing and designing cylindrical metasurfaces is proposed. The targeted structure is formed by cascading several concentric, azimuthally-varying metasurfaces (sheets of patterned metallic claddings supported by dielectric substrates). Given a specified cylindrical field transformation, the required inhomogeneous sheet admittances are determined through optimization. The proposed framework accounts for higher-order coupling, which circumvents the fabrication difficulties of previous works.

articleTitle: Circumferentially Short-circuited Circular Sector Patch Antenna with Broadened Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Circular sector patch antenna with circumferential short-circuited, wide beamwidth characteristic and low profile is presented and studied. Two radial-resonant magnetic dipoles with asymmetric boundary have been placed and the radiation principle have been analyzed. As will be seen, the resultant antenna would exhibit a wide E-plane beamwidth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{90^{\circ}}$</tex> and maintain a greatly low profile with 0.036-guide wavelength.

articleTitle: Boundary-Source Coherent Beamforming Using Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A method of boundary-source coherent beamforming (BSCB) using metasurface is proposed. Unlike conventional methods where a boundary surface is designed to simple primary sources such as plane-wave or spherical wave, the proposed method extends the design method to arbitrary primary sources for a shaped secondary scattering beam. For proof of concept, two reflective metasurfaces are designed, one to a realistic Vivaldi antenna of non-spherical wavefront and the other to an ideal point source. By comparison, the proposed BSCB method shows advantages in side-lobe level, Axial-Ratio (AR) beamwidth and beam pointing. The proposed method can be used for reflective beamforming in satellite communication, reconfigurable intelligent surface and so on.

articleTitle: A Dual-layer Ku/Ka Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Reflectarray Antenna Based on Structure-Reuse Technique
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-layer Ku/Ka dual-band shared-aperture reflectarray antenna based on the structure-reuse technique. The reflectarray composes of two substrates and three metal layers. The upper-metal-layer is the Ka-band array structure composed of three-loop unit cells. The middle-metal-layer is the Ku-band array structure consisted of cross-slot unit cells. The lower-metal-layer is the metal ground. Based on the structure-reuse technique, the reflected ground of the Ka-band element is instead by the cross-slot structure. This method can reduce the mutual interference between the different arrays, which is beneficial to improve the radiation efficiency of a large frequency ratio dual-band reflectarray antenna. The measured gain of the proposed reflectarray is 28.2 and 37.2 dBi at 13 and 38 GHz, and the corresponding efficiency is 44.9% and 41.8%, respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain Open Resonator Antenna Using a Flat Impedance Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This research presents a theoretical implementation of a wideband open resonator antenna (ORA) using an impedance surface acting as a ground plane. The impedance surface realization is based on the Bessel filter design methodology. It will be shown that the proposed methodology provides an alternative approach to design ORA without using complicated structures. Our proposed ORA design shows significant improvement in the 3dB gain bandwidth - 24.7 % - with a peak gain of 16.9 dBi. Simulated results are shown and compared with the ORA design with discretized metallic and flat ground.

articleTitle: Coating Metasurfaces Enabling Antenna Frequency Reconfigurability for Cognitive Radio System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we report a new approach for the design of frequency reconfigurable antennas equipped with cognitive capabilities. Specifically, we show how the complex-valued input impedance of a wire antenna can be tuned by using an appropriate conformal metasurface. We prove that, by properly engineering the metasurface response, it is possible to modify the operative frequency of the antenna without compromising its radiation pattern and impedance matching with the source. As a relevant example, the case of a reconfigurable dipole antenna coated by a multi-layered metasurface loaded with varactor diodes is discussed. By tuning the junction capacitance of the varactors, the antenna operative frequency can be continuously shifted within a quite broad range of frequencies (2/3 octave bandwidth), enabling wideband reconfigurability capabilities.

articleTitle: Design of a Reflective Metasurface for Near-Field Focusing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a metasurface reflector array for near-field focusing is proposed. A novel wideband symmetrical metasurface unit is proposed to realize the polarization insensitive characteristics. For both X-polarization and Y-polarization, the reflection phase shifts of the proposed unit can achieve 370° to 520° at corresponding frequencies in the X-band.
