Then a single-feed metasurface with a single near-field focus at X-band (10 GHz) using 27 × 27 units is designed, fabricated and measured by a planar near-field scanning system. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Electromagnetic Scalar Field Estimation of a Patch Antenna Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Artificial neural network (ANN) is emerging as an alternative approach for numerical electromagnetic (EM) antenna modeling. In this paper, we focus on predicting the near-field properties of antennas using a data-driven approach, and exploiting the universal function approximator feature of the ANNs. Specifically, we demonstrate the use of a convolutional neural network (CNN) to estimate the surface current on a patch antenna. This field analysis prediction allows a pathway for the prediction of near-field and far-field properties and has the potential to replace full EM modeling. Based on our results, our neural network predicted with only an 11% error on average the desired surface currents, showing promise for the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Accurate Modeling and Rapid Synthesis Methods for Beamforming Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A general synthesis technique for beamforming metasurfaces is presented which utilizes accurate modeling techniques and rapid optimization methods. The metasurfaces considered consist of patterned metallic claddings supported by finite grounded dielectric substrates. The metasurfaces are modeled using integral equations which accurately account for all mutual coupling and finite dimensions. A beamforming metasurface is designed in three phases: an initial Direct Solve phase involving the solution of the integral equation via the method of moments to obtain a complex-valued initial design satisfying the desired far-field beam specifications, a subsequent Optimization phase to convert the complex-valued metasurface into a purely reactive metasurface, and a final Patterning phase to realize the metasurface as a patterned metallic cladding. The metasurface is optimized using an adjoint optimization method. The method calculates the gradient of the cost function in only two forward problem solutions. An example metasurface designed using this approach is presented.

articleTitle: Vector Parabolic Equation Modeling of sub-6 GHz 5G Propagation in Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Vector Parabolic Equation (VPE) method is an established numerical technique that can accurately and efficiently model wave propagation in tunnels of arbitrary cross-section. Hence, VPE is a natural choice for evaluating various emerging 5G communication systems in tunnels and mines. This paper presents VPE simulation results on the propagation characteristics in tunnels of rectangular and arched cross-sections at sub-6 GHz 5G frequencies. We use these results to estimate path loss exponents and break-points, showing the feasibility of in-tunnel communication systems at these frequencies.

articleTitle: Microwave Head Imaging System for Detection of Blood Clots inside the Brain
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Microwave head imaging can be a cost-effective alternative to MRI or CT scan for detection of any strong scattering object such as- a tumor or blood clot inside the brain. In this paper, a microwave head imaging system is proposed for detection and localization of a blood clot inside the brain by dividing the head imaging plane into four quarters and scanning over one quarter at a time. A miniaturized wideband antipodal Vivaldi antenna design is incorporated to scan the head using a monostatic approach. An image of the head is reconstructed by scanning each quarter of the head. Finally, the images obtained from four quarters are compared for detection and approximate localization of the blood clot inside the brain.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Microstrip Branch-Line Hybrid Coupler Using Two Sections and Coupled-Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized microstrip 3dB quadrature branch-line hybrid coupler (QBLHC) is presented for size reduction. The proposed QBLHC is composed of single coupled-lines, parallel coupled-lines, and cascaded two sections in structure, which gives the wider operation band, good impedance matching, and the excellent isolation. By comparing with conventional microstrip 3dB quadrature hybrid coupler, the proposed hybrid coupler has 77% size reduction at the frequency band of 0.65~1.05GHz with almost equivalent electrical performance.

articleTitle: Hybrid Active-Passive Beamforming for Scalable sub-Terahertz Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: For massive multiple-input multiple-output applications in sub-terahertz band, both active and passive beamforming methods encounter challenges. This paper proposes a concept of hybrid active-passive beamforming using a combination of both to address the issues. We also introduce an implementation platform using glass interposer with patch antenna array on polymer build-up layers and integrated-circuit chips embedded in the glass core.

articleTitle: Wideband Design of A Circularly Polarized Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel design of Fabry-Perot cavity antenna (FPCA) is proposed to achieve circularly polarized (CP) radiation over a wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth. Degenerate orthogonal modes of a square-shaped slotted patch are excited by using the dual-offset feeding technique and the patch has been used as a primary radiator of the proposed CP-FPCA. An approximate gain improvement of 7–11 dB is achieved just by using a specially engineered superstrate which consists of strategic square patches. The boresight gain of the antenna varies between 11.5-16.2 dBi over its 25% matching as well as AR-bandwidth. The AR value remains below 1 dB over the operating bandwidth and has a 25° AR-beamwidth. Estimated values of boresight cross-pol and sidelobe levels are below −27dB and −8dB, respectively.

articleTitle: PIFA antenna for smart watch application in the 2.4 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA) design for a smartwatch application, optimized to operate on the 2.4 GHz Bluetooth frequency band, on the proximity of the human forearm. The PIFA antenna is mounted on the watchstrap that is used as the antenna substrate. The antenna is fed in a singular way, since a coplanar wave-guide (CPW) transmission line is used to excite the antenna. The antenna is integrated in the watchstrap, curved over the phantom forearm and simulated along with the watchcase. A return loss of −20 dB is obtained at 2.4 GHz, and an efficiency of −5 dB, which represents a good efficiency taking into account the effect of the human forearm.

articleTitle: Gradient Metasurface Dome for Phased arrays able Reducing the Grating Lobes within Single-side Scanning region
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Antenna arrays with large interelement spacing are marginally used in practical applications despite their highly directive main lobe. Their disuse is primarily attributed to the onset of grating lobes even for low scanning angles. In this contribution, we propose the design of a gradient metasurface dome able to reduce the grating lobe amplitude of a dual-polarized phased array. The dome consists of an array of Huygens unit-cells exhibiting an extremely low insertion loss and a properly designed phase of the transmission coefficient. The proposed solution is based on the scanning range shifting approach, which exploits the lower grating lobe levels exhibited by the array when radiating towards directions close to the broadside. A proper set of numerical simulations have been performed considering a 1×4 phased linear antenna array covered by a properly designed metasurface dome, showing its capability to significantly reduce the grating lobe amplitude without significantly reducing the performances in the pointing direction.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Dual Mode Antenna for On/Off-Body Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual mode antenna for on and off body wireless communication in the Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) band. The proposed design resonates in ISM band at two different frequencies i.e., 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz. The radiation pattern of the antenna is omnidirectional at the lower frequency band and directional at the higher frequency band. The influence of the human tissues on the performance of the antenna such as S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and the bandwidth of the antenna is minimized by creating a large ground plane on the second layer of the substrate. The overall size of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$44\text{mm}\times 44\text{mm}\times 1.6\text{mm}$</tex>. To investigate the effect of the antenna on the human body, tissue layers have been utilized at 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz. The results show that the proposed antenna is stable under the proximity of human tissues and it features a perfect candidate for on and off-body communication.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Scheme for Rapidly Reconstructing 3D Permittivity Maps from GPR C-scans
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based scheme for rapidly reconstructing subsurface 3D permittivity maps from ground-penetrating radar (GPR) C-scans. In this approach, a U-shaped deep convolutional neural network (CNN), 3D U-Net, is adopted to build the mapping relationship between GPR C-scans and 3D permittivity maps. The network consists of an encoder and a decoder with skip connections. A set of C-scans and their corresponding permittivity maps from random subsurface scenarios are produced to train and test the 3D U-Net based on mean square error loss. Our preliminary results show that the mean absolute percentage error and structural similarity achieved on the testing data are 0.0994% and 0.9980, respectively. The computation time required for estimating one permittivity map for a given C-scan via the proposed scheme is only 2.9 ms. Note that even computation of one C-scan in the classical reconstruction schemes takes 40 minutes. This makes the proposed method at least 800,000x faster than the classical reconstruction schemes. The results clearly demonstrate that our proposed methodology allows accurate and super-efficient reconstruction of the subsurface 3D permittivity maps from GPR C-scans.

articleTitle: Application of Microwave Imaging in Detecting Valuable Ores
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This study investigates using microwave imaging (MWI) to identify valuable minerals or metals in ores and its potential application in sensor-based ore sorting in mineral processing. The confocal MWI algorithm is performed on ore models in full-wave microwave scattering simulations. The simulation results successfully verify the effectiveness of using MWI to potentially identify valuable minerals in ore samples.

articleTitle: A Generative Adversarial Network Approach for Indoor Propagation Modeling with Ray-Tracing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Ray-tracing is widely used for radio propagation modeling in indoor environments. Accurate simulations necessitate a high number of ray interactions with the environment, in terms of reflections, transmissions and diffractions, as well as the launching of a large number of rays. A machine learning approach can instead utilize fewer ray interactions and a smaller number of rays launched, to produce an accelerated output. In this paper, a generative adversarial network is trained by low resolution 2-dimensional maps of received signal strength in an office environment. Then, it generates higher resolution RSS maps, thereby significantly reducing the required simulation time. Apart from resolution compensation and solver acceleration, it can also accurately generalize to other frequencies and receiver points.

articleTitle: Multiplicative-Regularized Bases-Expansion Subspace Optimization Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a multiplicative-regularized bases-expansion subspace optimization method (MR-BE-SOM) is proposed to solve nonlinear electrical impedance tomography (EIT) problem. The main advantage of the proposed method is to avoid to adjusting the regularization parameters in the inversion process. The proposed method is tested using both synthetic and experimental data. The reconstructed EIT imaging shows good edge-preserving, anti-noise performance, and high stability which is promising in providing quantitative images for potential clinical applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Liquid-Metal Antenna with Polarization and Continuous-Frequency Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Aiming to the limitations of traditional reconfig-urable antennas, this paper proposes a liquid-metal-based novel antenna that can achieve the reconfiguration of four polarizations and continuously-tuned frequency. The main body is a probe-fed circular patch with crossed slots in the center. The lengths of the slots can be controlled by changing the amount of the liquid metal filled in the 3-D printed channels to cover the slots. The antenna can work under four polarization statuses, i.e. left-hand circular polarization (LHCP), right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and two linear polarization (LP) modes. The working frequencies under the LP modes can be tuned continuously. The measured results are of good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Model-Based Data Generation for Support Vector Machine Stroke Classification
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new and efficient method to generate a dataset for brain stroke classification. Exploiting the Born approximation, it derives scattering parameters at antennas locations in a 3-D scenario through a linear integral operator. This technique allows to create a large amount of data in a short time, if compared with the full-wave simulations or measurements. Then, the support vector machine is used to create the classifier model, based on training set data with a supervised method and to classify the test set. The dataset is composed by 9 classes, differentiated for presence, typology and position of the stroke. The algorithm is able to classify the test set with a high accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized Base Station Antenna Design using Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> dual-polarized base station antenna with a simple structure is proposed, and the method of machine learning assisted optimization(MLAO) is introduced. The time of full-wave simulation is reduced by establishing a Gaussian process regression(GPR) model, and the genetic algorithm(GA) is used to predict and iterate the optimal solution. Finally, a dual-polarized base station antenna with a gain greater than 9.5dBi, a horizontal half-power beam width(HPBW) of 65.69°, and a coverage of 2496 - 2690MHz was designed.

articleTitle: Strata: An Open-Source C++ Library for Computing Green's Functions for Layered Media
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The multilayer Green's function (MGF) is often required in the integral equation modeling of structures involving layered dielectric substrates. Implementing the MGF can be a challenging and time-consuming task. We present Strata, an open-source C++ toolkit for computing the MGF in both the spectral and spatial domain. Written with modularity and readability in mind, we hope that Strata will contribute towards collaborative and community-driven advancement of research in electromagnetic solvers based on integral equations.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Reflectarray Unit Cell using Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a reflectarray unit cell element using vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>). Two halves of a quarter wavelength copper patch are joined using a VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film. The VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> serves as the switching mechanism for the unit cell allowing dual state reconfigurability when thermally actuated. When heated, the resistivity of the material significantly decreases changing the properties from dielectric to conductor. Traditional methods of reflectarray reconfiguration such as the addition of diodes, MEMS switches and ferroelectric materials typically exhibit high losses. Alternatively, this element achieves 181° of phase shift while maintaining a maximum loss of 0.44 dB at 35 GHz making it an extremely appealing option for reconfigurable reflectarray design.

articleTitle: Horn Antenna Misalignments at 100, 300, 400, and 500 GHz in Close Proximity Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper experimentally assesses the performance of terahertz (THz) wireless links in line-of-sight (LoS) propagation due to misalignments at 100, 300, 400, and 500 GHz carrier frequencies employing off-the-shelf horn antennas. The identical horn antennas both at transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) ends that send as well as receive single-mode beams covering the lower end of THz gap in three waveguide bands (i.e., WR-10, WR-3.4 and WR-2.2) at far-field positions are considered for performance evaluation in terms of path loss results. These results manifest that at 0.5 m distance, the vertical misalignment of 4 cm can deteriorate 5.75, 5.05, 0.70 and 0.75 dB at the utmost for 100, 300, 400 and 500 GHz frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: Wavefront Computing in Solids: The Design Parameters and the Ideal Lens
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical derivation for the design parameters of wavefront computing (WFC) system in solids including the aperture/transducer sizes, focal length, and the ideal lens. To achieve Fourier transform at the expected focal plane based on the wavefront computing system with ideal lens, the design parameters are derived for various transducers arrays from 4 by 4 to 32 by 32. Based on the theory in geometrical optics, the equations of ideal thick plano-concave lens are derived in solids for a given focal length and material properties. To validate the derived design parameters and the ideal lens, time domain simulation is used to show the propagation of the elastic waves in fused silica block. It can be observed that the waves excited by four piezoelectric transducers will get focused at the expected focal plane after the ideal lens.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Enhanced Small Circular Array for Amplitude Only Direction Finding
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A 4-element circular array of monopoles with central conducting post is designed, built, and tested for operation at 2.45 GHz. The antennas are resonant, well matched (~ −15 dB), and highly decoupled (< −25dB) at the frequency of interest, as seen in both measurement and simulation. The array's applicability to amplitude-only direction finding near the horizon is investigated in conjunction with a machine learning based algorithm. Two neural networks are trained to both demonstrate improvement over the correlation method counterpart (16-53% and 24-30%) particularly in the low signal-to-noise ratio regimes. Root mean squared error less than 5° is demonstrated in low to moderate noise scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of a Circularly-Polarized Tightly-Coupled Microstrip Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) tightly coupled microstrip patch array (TCMPA) operating in K/Ka-band is presented. The unit-cell element of the proposed array is a microstrip patch with chamfered corners and cross-slot printed on a single Rogers 4350B substrate. The use of cross-slot contributes to both, wider 3 dB axial ratio (AR), and impedance bandwidths. In a tightly coupled array environment, the designed simple element enables phased array bandwidths characterized with broadside AR < 3dB and VSWR < 2:1 of ~15% and ~65%, respectively. Moreover, radiation and aperture efficiencies are >97% and ~100%. A wider-angle scanning with slightly degraded AR is seen in an elevation cone of ±60° in all cardinal and inter-cardinal planes.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Dual-Polarized Conformal Phased Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an easily machinable broadband dual-polarization phased array based on tightly coupled dipole is designed. The majority of previous studies on wideband phased arrays are focused on planar arrays. Whereas, the designed structure is implemented by a cylindrically conformal array consisting of 4 × 4 radiating elements, which has much more preponderance in airborne and high maneuver applications. The simulation results demonstrate that the infinite array achieves VSWR less than 1.4 at broadside and less than 2.4 out to θ = 45° over a bandwidth of 6–10 GHz (50% bandwidth) in the E- and H- planes. The simulated gain of conformal array ranges from 12 dB to 16.2 dB at 6 ~ 10 GHz and the cross-polarization levels are typically less than −20 dB.

articleTitle: A Metasurface for Biomedical Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of a metasurface film as an imaging modality in the microwave regime. The fundamental principle of this technique relies on using a metasurface structure as a sheet to absorb the transmitted electromagnetic energy through the object under test (OUT). An image that correlates to the composition of the OUT is reconstructed by recording the power impression on the metasurface. Numerical experiments were carried out on numerical breast phantom, demonstrating the viability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dually-Polarized Compact Folded-Shorted Patch Array for Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-band, folded-shorted patch (FSP) antenna array is presented for CubeSats like microsatellites and picosatellites. The adopted folding and shorting technique for the individual patch elements, allows for size reduction of the conventional quarter-wavelength shorted patch. Also, to further miniaturize the array, the single-element FSPs are realized with meandering on the top-layer. These design approaches result in a compact array with a total size of 5 × 5 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> considering a 2 × 2 arrangement. This structure also offers dual-circularly polarized (DCP) radiation which is made possible by an eight-port feeding configuration for the array (i.e. two ports for each element). Given the dual-band nature of the individual FSPs, which is not typically exploited, the developed array is made operational for 1.1 GHz and 2.1 GHz. These features can simultaneously allow for downlink and uplink communications and/or satellite-to-satellite data links at L-band and S-band frequencies, while also, not consuming excessive area on the satellite itself. This is because the proposed 2 × 2 array can support these multiple transmitting and receiving functions, with a single antenna array structure for example, whilst leaving space on the CubeSat itself for other devices, sensors, solar panels, and deployable systems.

articleTitle: A Fast Calibration Method for Digital Metasurface with Periodic Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A fast calibration method based on periodic phase modulation for digital metasurface is proposed and verified. By controlling the phase of the metasurface periodically, multiple harmonics with different frequencies are generated in the received calibration signal. Then with the multi-point discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and least square method, the unbalances of amplitude and phase carried in the harmonics can be easily estimated from the measured harmonic complex gains. Simulation result is provided to verify the feasibility.

articleTitle: Compact Magnetically Symmetric Antenna Design for Implantable Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a coplanar waveguide feed (CPW-fed) based patch antenna for implantable biomedical applications operating at Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. The antenna has a magnetically symmetric configuration with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\ \text{mm}\ \times 30\ \text{mm}$</tex> l. In free space, the proposed antenna covers a wideband ranging from 2.39 - 2.57 GHz, thereby posing a -10 dB bandwidth of 180 MHz with a peak gain of 2.23 dB. For implant case, the antenna is simulated by creating a three-layered human tissue model in CST MWS 2019. The proposed design also offers -10 dB bandwidth covering the ISM band after implanting inside muscle layer with a peak gain value of -6.46 dB. A prototype of antenna is fabricated for measurement proposes. An ex-vivo testing of proposed design was performed by placing the fabricated antenna inside a fresh pork slab. The measured and simulated results demonstrate the significance of proposed antenna for wearable and implantable biomedical applications.

articleTitle: 3D Metal Printed Broadband X-Band Septum Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An X-Band septum polarizer covering the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Deep Space and Near Space Bands was fabricated using 3D metal printing. The polarizer was implemented using a series of stepped septums, with rectangular waveguide input ports and a circular waveguide output port. The A6061 RAM-2 aluminum alloy was used in the 3D printing process due to its smooth surface finish when compared with similar aluminum alloys. The polarizer's performance was tested as part of a horn antenna assembly in a compact antenna range. The measured cross-polarization was better than 20 dB over a wide frequency range of around 7 GHz to 8.8 GHz.

articleTitle: A Broadband S/SSTDR-VNA for Energized Circuits
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose the use of the Spectral Time Domain Reflectometry (STDR) and Spread Spectrum Time Domain Reflectometry (SSTDR) methods as a substitute for a vector network analyzer (VNA) to extract complex impedance and S-parameters. S/SSTDR can be used on energized systems, opening up opportunities for new test capabilities of real time measurements on functioning systems from near-DC through higher frequencies. This test modality also opens up the opportunity to test multiple channels simultaneously by using multiple uncorrelated PN codes. This could prove useful in applications such as medical imaging (MRI or microwave imaging), where scans between many antennas are combined to create the image.

articleTitle: A Circularly-Polarized Mechanically Beam-Steerable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Risley prism inspired circularly-polarized 2D beam steerable antenna with large beam-scanning range, high gain and wide bandwidth. It consists of a feed horn and two planar metasurface transmitarrays. The main beam of the antenna could continuously scan within a large conical region through rotating TA1 and TA2 separately. The simulations successfully verify the design prediction. Simulated peak gain is 27.1dBi at 29GHz and gain variation over the conical scanning range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0 < \theta < 41^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0 < \varphi < 360^{\circ})$</tex> is less than 2dB. Other reasonable results include promising realized gain and axial ratio over the working frequency band.

articleTitle: Dual Band 4-Port MIMO Antenna for Bluetooth/5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A 4×4 MIMO design is reported for dual band application covering Bluetooth (2.38-2.45 GHz) and 5G (2.96-4.01 GHz) range. Two asymmetric U-shaped slots are embedded in the radiating patch to achieve the dual band characteristics. The composite ground plane with four metallic strips is used to improve the isolation (≤ 18dB) between the multiple radiating patches. The MIMO design is kept compact and small with dimensions 38×38×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The antenna radiation patterns, S-parameters and necessary diversity parameters are calculated to demonstrate the significance of the proposed design applicable for different wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Wearable Microstrip Circular Patch Antenna for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Women across the world are affected by Breast cancer with the highest incidence and mortality rate. In the early days old women were mostly affected but now the scenario completely changes. In recent years, breast cancer cases are gaining pace among young women. It asks the researchers to concentrate on advanced technology apart from the conventional methods. Early detection and diagnosis reduce the mortality rate. In this paper, an ultra-wide-band circular microstrip patch antenna with M & U shaped slots is designed to detect breast cancer. The antenna is designed by choosing jeans fabric as substrate with a dielectric permittivity of 1.7 and copper is used for ground and patch designs. The results obtained are largely satisfying and prove that the proposed antenna is a candidate for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Moment (Adam) Estimation Optimization Applied to AVM-FEM for Rapid Convergence
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam) is a kind of gradient descent optimization algorithm and by far the most common way to optimize neural networks. This paper proposes a gradient-based EM optimization method that updates parameters by means of Adam, based on gradients calculated by adjoint variation method (AVM) applied in finite element method (FEM) solutions. A benchmark that optimizes the design of a wave impedance transformer compares Adam's performance with other commonly-used gradient-based and global algorithms. These concepts are then integrated into a representative example of optimization of a rectangular inset-fed patch antenna.

articleTitle: Coherence Factor-Based Delay-Multiply-And-Sum Image Reconstruction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Microwave imaging is one of the most promising imaging modalities for the early detection of breast cancer. Many image reconstruction algorithms have been developed. In this paper, we propose a fast Delay-Multiply-And-Sum (DMAS) beamforming algorithm with an additional weighting factor. Simulation results show that the side lobes are suppressed by using the coherence of received signals. Moreover, the computational load order is lower than DMAS.

articleTitle: The Bluering Array Receiver System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: “Bluering” is the name given to a phased array receiver system that has considerable flexibility. This flexibility is in both the RF frequency range as well as the digital signal processing and communications. Bluering integrates a large number of very different technologies into one system package. In this paper a description of the major parts of Bluering are provided as well as some initial testing results.

articleTitle: Terahertz Valley Transport in Photonic Crystal Slab
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Photonic topological insulator has aroused great attention due to its advantage of backscattering-immune in propagating. In the photonic crystal, valley state has raised widespread concern as a new degree of freedom. Based on quantum valley-hall effect, topological valley photonic crystal was designed with low dissipation, wide bandgap, and backscattering immune. In this paper, a composite honeycomb lattice structure with petal air holes is proposed. In the all-dielectric photonic slab, the edge modes of electromagnetic wave are confined below the light cone. Through analyzing band structure and full wave stimulation, topological valley transport and scattering-immune propagation of terahertz wave is demonstrated in proposed topological valley photonic crystal slab.

articleTitle: Graphene-based Reconfigurable Reflecting Surface for Future Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a reflecting metasurface is proposed to control the reflection angle by manipulating the chemical potential (CP) of graphene. The surface can operate in three anomalous reflection modes for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=45^{\mathrm{o}}, 60^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> while it is illuminated with a normal incident electromagnetic wave (EMW). Moreover, by tuning the chemical potential of graphene sheets the proposed surface can switch off the reflection mode of operation by absorbing the incident EM power.

articleTitle: A Low-cost Sub-Terahertz Circularly Polarized Antenna for 6G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This article presents the experimental validation of circularly polarized (CP) resonant cavity antenna (RCA) operating at 300 GHz. The CP-RCA consists of two main parts, one operates as a base feeding antenna (five metallic layers), while the other one generates high gain with circular polarization (aperture-type frequency selective surface (FSS) metallic layer). Both parts are designed and fabricated to be directly mounted onto a standard WM-864 waveguide flange. The proposed CP-RCA prototype is made of metallic layers and its design relies on the laser cutting brass technique to simplify fabrication and low-cost. The measured 3-dB RHCP directivity bandwidth is 10 % with a peak directivity of 17 dBic. This antenna yields a measured axial ratio (AR) bandwidth (AR < 3dB) of 5.12 GHz. This work, to the best of our knowledge, is the first one to develop a CP-RCA antenna aperture FSS-based layer at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: Effective electromagnetics teaching, no matter what!
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetics education has evolved through the years, transitioning from the traditional face-to-face, instructor-led delivery mode to more modern practices, encouraging the active participation of students in their own learning. In 2020, educators around the world were forced to transform their teaching mode into online delivery due to the global pandemic. More recently, with the ease of COVID-19 restrictions in some countries, educators have adopted blended-learning strategies. However, despite the type of teaching modality adopted, it is important that educators maintain a curriculum that promotes active experimentation, uses computer modeling and visualization resources, and encourages engineering applications. This paper emphasizes important features that educators should consider when structuring or restructuring an electromagnetics course.

articleTitle: Compact and Wideband Terahertz Lens Integrated Bow-tie Antenna for detector
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and wideband lens integrated bow-tie antenna with center-fed is presented for detector applications. It contains a pair of slot stubs for broadening the bandwidth and a pair of complementary metals for the compact design. Additionally, the introduction of two pads where the Schottky diode is integrated across the feeding terminals of the bow-tie antenna improves the impedance bandwidth with creating a new resonance which simultaneously leads the low-frequency signal with a small footprint. To suppress surface wave propagation, a quartz lens is presented, which can simultaneously enhance the gain. The size of the bow-tie is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.7 \text{mm}\times 0.51\ \text{mm}$</tex>. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of the proposed bow-tie antenna is 205–374 GHz, which covers the atmosphere windows of 220 GHz and 340 GHz.

articleTitle: A Wideband Stripline-to-Stripline Transition for K/Ka-Bands
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The use of millimeter-waves is believed to be one of the most effective methods to achieve wider bandwidth in the modern communication systems. With this, several problems arise, especially the progressive smaller size of radiating structures and their feeding networks. In real systems, the connection between these smaller antennas and the RF frontends can be done through a via-hole. This paper proposes a wideband stripline-to-stripline transition using vias, which cancels any undesired behavior of such structures in high frequencies, achieving a perfect impedance matching throughout a wide frequency range.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Phased Array Architecture with Reduced RF Ports Based on Software-Defined Radio for Beyond 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a software-defined phased array architecture using two-port half-loop antenna topology for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathrm{G}$</tex> and beyond applications. The proposed architecture is exemplified as directivity, beam-steering and polarization reconfigurable phased arrays based on pre-defined weighting vector matrix in 28GHz spectrum. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> two-port half-loop antenna is designed using a low temperature cofired ceramic process to verify the feasibility of the proposed concept. The proposed concept features multiple polarizations and a half of the spherical beamforming coverage which are selected from infinite theoretically available modes and the fabricated model is experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Bypassing Rozanov's bound for short-time pulses
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Here, we explore the scattering and absorption efficiency of a short-time pulsed wave that impinges on an absorbing layer that consists of a time-varying layer that is backed by an ideal conductor (PEC). The analysis is done by solving in-time the Green's function of the TL equivalent of the layered system. Its numerical evaluation is accelerated by using the fact that its only contribution comes from discrete spectrum waves, and thus any spectral integration can be replaced by an efficient summation. Due to the switching process the absorption is enhanced in comparison to Rozanov's bound that was derived for linear and time-invariant (LTI) wave systems. We demonstrate the better absorption efficiency for both ultra wideband (UWB) and quasi-monochromatic pulses.

articleTitle: A Compact Multi-Band MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a low-profile, compact, multi-band antenna. The design consists of 8 rectangular microstrip patch antennas integrated with a slotted Vivaldi. Results indicate that all integrated patches achieve gains above 5 dB even though the radiation patterns of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{y}$</tex> polarized patches are perturbed by the Vivaldi. Despite the low isolation of 6.6 dB and 8 dB between the Vivaldi and the two patches nearest to its feed, isolation greater than 10 dB is achieved between all other antennas. The proposed antenna can be utilized in microcells, repeaters, and may be extended to massive MIMO.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO Antenna Based on Quarter-Mode SIW and 90-Degree Bent Planar Dipole
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 2-element wideband, multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with a quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) and a 90-degree bent planar dipole based on the complementary antenna principle for sub-6 GHz applications is proposed. The dielectric aperture of the QMSIW acts as a magnetic dipole and the 90-degree bent planar dipole acts as an electric dipole. The proposed complementary antenna is fed coaxially. A prototype is fabricated with a substrate thickness of 2.54 mm, which achieves a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 29%, isolation higher than 18.6 dB (varying between 18.6 dB and 44.2 dB), an envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) of less than 0.005, maximum realized gain of 5.22 dBi and, a channel capacity loss less than 0.4 b/s/Hz. The effect of the substrate thickness on the bandwidth is studied.

articleTitle: Planar 40-port Slot Array for Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we present a new array of MIMO antennas for energy harvesting and data transmission purposes, especially for 5G and healthcare applications. Each pair of antennas consists of folded slots as a radiating element. To reduce mutual coupling between these elements, a rectangular ring parasitic element is used. The 40-port antenna has dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$220\times 135\ \ \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> and operates at 2.45 GHz. Although the individual antennas are densely packed, all combinations of mutual coupling between ports exhibit better than 12 dB isolation. For initial study, the antennas are fabricated on FR-4 printed-circuit-boards. The proposed antennas are investigated by simulation and validated through measurements.

articleTitle: Radiation Calculation of Wedge-shaped Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, analytical formulas are deduced to determine the field distribution in a wedge-shaped cylindrical leaky-wave antenna. Using this approach, radiation field can be accordingly evaluated based on the surface field distribution. This model can be an effective and accurate method for designing 2-D beamforming of cylindrical Fabry-Perot leaky-wave antennas.

articleTitle: On User Effects of a Low-Profile MIMO Terminal Antenna with Wideband Multimodal Excitation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: When in use, a mobile terminal is often held in the hand by the user. However, conventionally terminal antennas are only evaluated in free space, disregarding the effects of user interaction. In this paper, the performance of a low-profile twoport multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna that offers wide symmetrical bandwidth and low correlation in free space is investigated in presence of a user hand. Full-wave simulation results show that the one-hand grip mainly causes an unbalanced absorption loss across the two ports and a degraded correlation performance, with the latter being due to pattern distortion.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Based Dual-Mode Monopole-Like Multifunctional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the excitation mechanism of the first two monopole-like modes of a modified mushroom antenna, consisting of four circular mushroom unit cells and a feeding top-loaded pin. Four more shorting pins and four slots are introduced for each cell to shift the zeroth-order resonance (ZOR) up and high-order mode down, respectively. The top-loaded circular patch of the feeding pin is printed above the mushroom cells and located at the center of the antenna to simultaneously excite the two modes. Dual-mode resonant property is achieved with operating frequency from 3.38 to 3.676 GHz. The simulated results show that the realized peak gain is higher than 4.3 dB and total efficiency is over 92% among the frequency band. The antenna element can be used as a unit cell of the metamaterial with zero-phase reflection, which is useful for composite antenna design.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction for Compact Wideband Two-Element Dual-Polarized Array by Utilizing H-Shaped Interdigital Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An effective mutual coupling reduction method using a novel planar single-layer parasitic H-shaped interdigital structure is developed for wideband, compact, two-element, dual-polarized (DP) arrays. The center-to-center spacing between the antenna elements is 0.5 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> indicates the the wavelength in the lower bound of the array's operational bandwidth. It is indicated that by incorporating the H-shaped interdigital structure into the closely spaced two-element DP antenna array, the isolation levels between the co-polarization ports and those between the inter-element cross-polarization ports are both significantly improved across the entire working band of 1.7-2.2 GHz (a ~ 25.6% fractional bandwidth) without deteriorating the radiation efficiency of the array. Particularly, the E- and H-plane coupling levels are respectively reduced by more than 10.7 dB and 18.8 dB when the array is incorporated with the developed interdigital structure.

articleTitle: Van Atta Arrays Exploited Towards Flying UAV Position Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents the initial implementation of a flying UAV position detection using a ground based interrogating radar and two alternative Van-Atta array configurations which are used for enhanced back-reflection. The two versions of Van Atta arrays are: planar 5 elements arrays attached on the four sides of a pyramidal structure and two 5 element conformal arrays attached on a conical surface. The operation frequency is 5.8 GHz and the radar cross section (RCS) of the arrays for different oblique angles are investigated. The planar array has maximum RCS value of 6dBsm at normal incidence while the conformal version Van-Atta array has superior performance in oblique incident wave directions since it demonstrates simulated RCS values greater than −5dBsm for a wide range of −20° to +20° angles on incidence.

articleTitle: UWB Supershaped Dielectric Lens for Beam Control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of an ultra-wideband (UWB) dielectric lens for pattern shape control. The lens is meant to be easily installed on a wideband double ridged horn antenna to handle its beam in both elevation and azimuth planes. Specific applications, such as compact interferometric panels and panoramic scanning, require the antenna to instantaneously cover large angular sectors with a reduced physical area. The geometry of the lens has been optimized with an error-weighted quantum particle swarm optimization (EWQPSO) algorithm. The designed lens allows to conveniently guide the phase of the electric field radiated by the horn antenna in order to provide the desired boresight realized gain and half-power beamwidth (HPBW) on the principal planes maintaining high efficiency. Moreover, the lens can be easily realized in additive manufacturing technology, providing a size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C) solution. The antenna performance are extremely promising in terms of reflection coefficient, boresight gain, and shape of patterns.

articleTitle: Compact Antenna Approaching the Lower Q-factor Theoretical Bound Suitable for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact antenna suitable for integration in Internet-of-Things (IoT) terminals and whose performance approach the lower Q-factor theoretical bound is presented. The proposed antenna structure is a parasitic element array based on two Inverted-F Antenna (IFA) radiators sharing the same ground plane. The antenna exhibits a directive pattern that can be electronically steered integrating a simple reconfigurable feeding network.

articleTitle: Polarization-insensitive Absorptive Microwave Device With Electronically-Controllable Reflectance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper an absorptive microwave device with electronically-controlled reflectance is proposed. The device is insensitive to the polarization of incident wave. The numerical simulation results as well as equivalent circuit model results are presented to predict the device performance. The device is also fabricated and the measurement results are presented to experimentally investigate the device performance.

articleTitle: Fixed Frequency Beam Scanning 5G Antenna Array with Switchable Multiple Beams and Wide Beam
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Here a fixed-frequency beam scanning 5G antenna array operating from 3.3 GHz to 3.8 GHz is proposed, which has the advantages of low profile, high gain and flexibly switchable multi-beam and wide beam. The simulation results show that the scanning angle of the antenna can reach 33° at 3.6 GHz and its peak gain can reach 14 dBi. The operating mode can be switched between multi-beam and wide beam.

articleTitle: Machine-learning-based optimization method in metasurface Mosaic antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A machine-learning-based method is proposed to optimize metasurface Mosaic antennas. Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are utilized to build an accurate and efficient surrogate model. Both forward and inverse processes are discussed for the performance prediction of antennas. In the forward process, the geometry information of antenna is the input of the ANN while the outputs are S-parameters of the antenna. In the inverse process, the input of the ANN is the targeted S-parameters while ANN outputs the geometry value of the antenna. Moreover, bandwidth information is introduced into the inverse process to get the unique solution and improve the accuracy of the proposed method. A metasurface Mosaic antenna is utilized as an example to validate the proposed machine-learning-based method. The results show that the proposed method is promising for accurate antenna optimization applications.

articleTitle: Decoupling Method for Two Planar Inverted-F Antennas using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a decoupling method for Two Planar Inverted-F Antennas (PIFAs), which are mounted on a ground plane, using Characteristic Mode Analysis. According to the simulation results of Modal Weighting Coefficient, two types of mode (in-phase mode and anti-phase mode) are observed and total inner product of modes is calculated. When the total inner product value is close to zero, the excited current from the two ports is orthogonal to each other, resulting in a reduction of the mutual coupling. Based on this, we use four L-shaped elements, which are placed on several certain positions on ground plane, to excite a dominant mode in order to adjust the total inner product value to be closer to zero. As a result, the total inner product can be adjusted from −0.43 to −0.3 and the mutual coupling can be reduced from −6.6 dB to −10.2 dB.

articleTitle: A Liquid Crystal Beam Scanning Antenna Based on Even and Odd Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A liquid crystal beam scanning antenna based on even and odd modes is proposed. It is a microstrip patch antenna, which is divided into two parts by a bending slot. Benefiting from the introduction of the slot, this antenna can work at even and odd modes within the frequency band. Through using the method of characteristic mode analysis, the resonant frequency and radiation characteristics of the two modes can be obtained. The results show that the resonant frequency of even mode is lower than that of odd mode and the radiation patterns of two modes are different. Therefore, through choosing liquid crystal as its substrate, this antenna can change its main operating modes by varying the permittivity of liquid crystal. An antenna model has been investigated. The simulation results show that the main beam can be scanned from +17° to +27° at 26 GHz in the E-plane.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Broadband Phased Array Using Self-Similar Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper outlines an approach to design ultra-broadband phased arrays using self-similar elements. Each indi-vidual lattice element covers an octave of bandwidth and is scaled in powers of 2 until the entire desired bandwidth is realized. For this design, we used a three layer vertically oriented element that can cover a 2:1 bandwidth and is packed into a dense lattice. The system is designed and optimized using a custom state-of-the-art Genetic Algorithm (GA). In this illustrative example, we designed a phased array to achieve an operating frequency range of 1 GHz – 8 GHz. The resulting structure forms a quasi-fractal that can be applied without fundamental restrictions on bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Compact Four-Element Self Decoupled MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The proposed work explains the design of a compact and wideband four-element multiple-input-multiple-output antenna for sub-6 GHz 5G applications. The antenna provideswider impedance bandwidth ranging from 3.42 GHz to 5.22 GHz (41.6%) with minimum isolation of 15 dB for the entire working band. Also, the presented MIMO antenna provide better gain, improved radiation efficiency, and excellent envelope correlation coefficient by keeping the compact antenna size. Hence the proposed antenna is applicable for working in Sub-6 GHz 5G applications.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Phase Retrieval and its Application to Reflector Antennas Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a new approach to the general phase retrieval problem. By profitably using the ‘Spectral Factorization’ technique in conjunction with multipole expansions derived from the ‘Orbital Angular Momentum’ aperture antenna theory, the approach allows to effectively solve the problem by exploiting only one measurement surface. By so doing, and without requiring the exploitation of computationally-expensive global-optimization algorithms, the approach allows the reflector antenna surface diagnosis starting from far-field phaseless data.

articleTitle: Dual-mode Bandpass Filter based on Circular Fractal Patch Resonator for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A new miniaturized dual-mode bandpass filter (BPF) based on fractally slotted patch resonator is presented in this paper. By increasing the number of iterations of the geometry of the fractally slotted resonator (FSR) and introducing the stepped impedance resonator (SIR) structure, the resonant frequency of the FSR is reduced to achieve the miniaturization of the filter. The proposed filter is centered at 2.45 GHz, which is suitable for wideband filtering of WLAN. There are several transmission zeros (TZs) on both sides of the passband ensuring high selectivity. The return loss in the passband is more than 26 dB, the minimum insertion loss is less than 0.6 dB, and the relative bandwidth of 3 dB in the passband is 23.9%.

articleTitle: Differentially-fed Two-element Laminated Resonator Antenna Array With Low Cross Polarization and Broad Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 2$</tex> Laminated Resonator Antenna (LRA) array with broad bandwidth and improved radiation properties. The LRA array are constructed by a pair of single-ended LRA elements fed by L-probes in opposite directions. Differential feeding technique is employed to suppress the cross polarization and improve the symmetry of the radiation patterns in the array design. The number of probes is reduced to half in the proposed array comparing with the array adopting the differential LRA elements so that the complexity and loss of the feed network will be reduced. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed LRA array achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 21.92% with a stable gain around 10 dBi and a high radiation efficiency large than 95%. Featuring low-cost, simple and planar structure, the proposed LRA array is promising for future sub 6G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: An Analytical Approach for the Generation of Second-Order Floquet-Bloch Mode for Anomalous Reflection Using Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel analytical technique for the excitation of second-order Floquet-Bloch mode with the elimination of all other higher and lower order modes is proposed using a metagrating configuration. The structure has been designed using a periodic configuration of unit cells consisting of a single conducting wire loaded with SMD capacitor. The proposed theory has been validated by comparing the electric fields obtained from the analytical model and the CST simulation at two different reflection angles.

articleTitle: System Simulations for MIMO Antenna Designs
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a simulation methodology to optimize MIMO antenna designs for the system performance parameters. The proposed design flow provides a co-simulation bench to evaluate MIMO antenna designs with system-level criteria. In one example, two MIMO antenna designs are considered, where both of them meet conventional antenna design parameters. The proposed methodology identifies the antenna design which statistically results in higher system throughput.

articleTitle: The Dyadic Green's Function for the Rectangular Dielectric Cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Using the vector basis function expansion method, the Dyadic Green's Function in dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is deduced, in which the eigenfunction satisfies the hybrid boundary condition of PMC and continuous boundary condition. The radiation patterns of DRA are computed by the deduced DGF at the terahertz frequency and the results show that the radiated far field is mainly determined by the equivalent magnetic current on the surface of DRA.

articleTitle: Scattering Analysis of Metallic Nanowires with Nonlocal Response Based on GNOR
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we combine the Mie theory and a novel nonlocal dispersion model named Generalized Non-local Optical Response (GNOR) to study the electromagnetic scattering of metallic nanostructure. We first introduce the GNOR model briefly. Then the Mie theory based on GNOR model is introduced to analyze the scattering of infinitely metallic nanowires. Finally, numerical examples are presented to show the effect of the metallic nanowires based on GNOR model by Mie theory.

articleTitle: Identification of individuals through a new Gait Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Each individual has a particular way of walking which characterizes him. This has led to the consideration of gait as a means of recognizing individuals. This paper presents a sensor-free approach which allows to recognize the subject's gait by relying on (ANN)Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) technique. Furthermore, the efficiency of the use of the received signal strength as a source of gait recognition is investigated.

articleTitle: Design Method for Bowtie Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth and Controllable Gain Using 3D-Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of antenna's bandwidth enhancement and gain control by taking advantage of the third dimension available through three-dimensional (3D)-printing technology. As a proof-of-concept, an ultra-wideband bowtie antenna is proposed using a novel design methodology which involves defining 3D piecewise-linear rate arms and an advanced optimization algorithm based on Trust Region Framework (TRF). Polylactic acid (PLA) thermoplastic is used to simulate the dielectric part of the antenna. The antenna can be fully manufactured using 3-D printing technology. The proposed antenna demonstrates 110% increase in bandwidth in comparison with the initial planar structure. Additionally, it is demonstrated that the gain of the antenna can be controlled by tuning the length and height of the 3D piecewise-linear rate arms in the structure of antenna.

articleTitle: Optimization of 2D Heterogeneous Lenses via BFGS and Volume Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we apply a quasi-Newton optimization algorithm called BFGS to optimize heterogeneous lenses in 2D by using the volume integral equation method. Different preliminary designs are presented with frequency selective focal point.

articleTitle: Interconnect-free DRA-SAW RFID Sensing System for High Temperature Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new sensing system with a Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) serving both as interconnect-free package and antenna for a Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) sensor aimed at high temperature industrial monitoring applications. The DRA is made of Alumina (99.7% of purity) well recognized by its permanent and steady properties at high temperatures exceeding 1000°C. It is placed on an AlN/Sapphire plate on which the SAW sensor is printed. The system operates at 2.45GHz where an excellent matching is obtained with a quite good radiation characteristics for the DRA which offers a wide range of angles for interrogating the sensor.

articleTitle: Zero Thickness Sheet Model of Dispersive & Nonlinear Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A systematic method to represent and analyze a practical nonlinear metasurface exhibiting temporal dispersion, using an equivalent zero thickness sheet model is proposed. The method is based on Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs), where the metasurface is described in terms of linear and nonlinear surface polarization densities modeled using a nonlinear Lorentz oscillator. The equivalent Lorentz parameters are extracted from unit cell simulations, and using numerical examples, it is shown that they can successfully replicate the dispersion and intensity-dependent nonlinear response of the finite-thickness metasurface.

articleTitle: Platform Tolerant UHF RFID Tag Design using Multi-resonant Surface for Supply Chain Visibility
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a platform tolerant ultra-high radio frequency identification (UHF RFID) tag design for hard to tag supply chain items such as large metal and wooden containers. The proposed design consists is backed by multi-resonant surface carefully designed using characteristics mode analysis. As a result, this tag design features a long read range and covers most of UHF RFID frequency bands. The evaluation of the read range associated with fabricated prototype of proposed tag configuration is done through turn on power measurements using Tagformance Pro setup. A variety of subjects with different physical constitutions such as metal, wood and glass are considered in order to demonstrate the robustness of our solution. The proposed tag offers a relatively longer reader range of 12.5 m after mounting on piece of metal, wood and glass materials. Therefore, this tag design is suitable candidate for supply chain visibility and cargo monitoring.

articleTitle: Sparse Composite Array with Enhanced Angular Resolution for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a sparse composite array (SCA) approach for automotive radar applications with enhanced angular resolution without additional hardware. Based on popular 3T4R MIMO radar chip, we adopt an end-to-end complete simulation approach to include radar waveform generation, MIMO array architecture, MIMO propagation channels, signal noise, digital beamforming (DBF), radar ranging signal processing, and data processing to implement the SCA concept in digital domain. The presented results would be more informative and convincing to validate the proposed SCA concept that can double the angular resolution (halving the beamwidth).

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Huygens Source Antenna Based on Two Stacked Dielectric Resonators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a cross-shaped dielectric resonator antenna arranged in a stacked configuration is proposed to realize a Huygens source in circular polarization at 2.45 GHz ISM band. The antenna principle relies on the combination of two pairs of orthogonal electric and magnetic dipoles. The antenna is designed and optimized with numerical analysis using far-field simulations in Ansys HFSS. It finally has a radiation pattern oriented in one half-space without the use of a ground plane.

articleTitle: A Broadband Multilayer Magic-T Using Coupled Microstrip-Slotlines for Monopulse Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband multilayer planar magic-T using coupled microstrip-slotlines is proposed. Sum and difference function in this design are realized by utilizing the even and odd transmission mode of the coupled microstrip-slotlines. The magic-T is conducive to the miniaturization of monopulse antenna systems by using a 3-layer circuit board structure and reasonable port placement. Simulation results show that the operating frequency range is 1.25-2.52 GHz with return loss higher than 10 dB, while in-band isolation between sum and difference port is greater than 50 dB. It also has amplitude and phase imbalance of less than 0.1 dB and 0.4° respectively.

articleTitle: Flat-Earth Finite Difference - Guided Mode Model for Long Wavelength Propagation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a 1-D finite difference (FD) eigenvalue problem for the analysis of long wavelength propagation in a 2-D Earth-Ionosphere Waveguide (EIWG) model. Application of Maxwell's equations and the FD method to the 2-D waveguide results in a matrix equation with a single partial derivative. An eigenequation solver is used to calculate the guided mode wavenumbers and modal profiles (height gain). This approach results in a smaller matrix size than typical FD 2-D discretization schemes.

articleTitle: Impact of Microwave Pulse Characteristics on Thermoacoustic Signals Generated during Pulsed Microwave Ablation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Microwave-induced thermoacoustic (TA) imaging is an emerging method for real-time monitoring of microwave ablation (MWA). In this study, we conduct a series of simulations to investigate the impact of two system parameters on TA signal characteristics; microwave frequency and microwave excitation pulse width. We compare the relative impact of these parameters and find that the microwave pulse width becomes less influential on the TA signal peak frequency as microwave frequency decreases due to the impact of microwave frequency on microwave absorption distribution. This study provides valuable insight into the impact of typical system parameters on TA signal characteristics.

articleTitle: Broadband Millimeter-Wave Feed Structure for Log-Periodic Toothed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Presented is the investigation of a broadband millimeter-wave log-periodic toothed antenna (LPTA) with an integrated impedance transforming feed structure. The feed structure provides a broadband impedance match to standard 50 Ω system impedance while in the same plane as the radiating structure, resulting in an entirely 2D implementation of the LPTA. Rogers 5880 (∊<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=2.2, tanδ=0.0009) is used as the design substrate. A finite-element solver (Ansys HFSS) is used to carry out simulation of the structure to demonstrate an input match of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>< −10 dB starting from 22.8 GHz and extending outward beyond 60 GHz with a peak realized gain of 7.48 dBi.

articleTitle: Non-Conformal SS-SIE Formulation Without Treatments on Junctions for Composite Objects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A modular efficient single-source surface integral equation (SS-SIE) formulation is proposed to solve the electro-magnetic problems induced by arbitrarily penetrable and perfect electric conductor (PEC) objects. In the proposed formulation, each penetrable object is first replaced by the background medium independently, and an equivalent model with only the surface electric current density on the boundary is derived. Then, the equivalent model for the composite object is obtained through combining all the modular equivalent models together. The proposed formulation is flexible, easy to implement, intrinsically supports non-conformal meshes, and does not require additional boundary conditions to couple the shared boundaries. Numerical results validate its robustness and accuracy.

articleTitle: Interface Waves in Parallel-plate Metasurface Waveguides with Duality Symmetry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a parallel-plate metasurface waveguide, where duality symmetry is realized by spatially arranging two kinds of metasurfaces with opposite equivalent reactance, inductive and capacitive. Period patch and grid arrays are designed to achieve different artificial impedance surfaces. Equivalent impedance boundary conditions are extracted based on simulated dispersion curves of unit cells. Simplified uniform waveguide models based on impedance boundaries are established to further investigate robust transport of interface waves along various routes. Due to the protection from duality symmetry, the interface waves are tightly bounded at the center of the waveguide. The proposed waveguide may pave an important research direction in wireless components design.

articleTitle: A Compact Differential Quasi-Yagi Antenna With Broadband and Uniplanar Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact differential quasi-Yagi antenna with broadband and uniplanar characteristics. An impedance transformer is designed combining a section of tapered coupled microstrip lines (TCML) and a section of coplanar strips (CPS). The proposed antenna exhibits a −10 dB differential-mode (DM) return loss bandwidth of 54.1% (7.95 to 13.85 GHz) with efficiency of around 94%. The front-to-back ratio is better than 9.1 dB while the cross-polarization is less than −20 dB. Besides, simulated results demonstrate that the maximum common-mode (CM) rejection is 0.6 dB and the gain is from 3.4 dBi to 5.5 dBi within the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Decoupling of Horn Antennas Using Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The technique of enhancing isolation between horn antennas by using metamaterials is investigated in this work. For horn antennas arranged in E-plane and H-plane with an edge-to-edge spacing 1/10 wavelength, the isolation is enhanced by more than 20 dB across a 22.6% bandwidth.
