Meanwhile, the patterns of the horn antennas are only slightly affected after adding the metamaterials.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-frequency MIMO antenna with High Port Isolation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact dual-frequency microstrip multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with high isolation is proposed in this paper. The proposed dual-frequency microstrip MIMO antenna operates at 2.58 GHz and 4.8 GHz. In addition, a new defective ground structure is proposed, which can effectively reduce the coupling of the MIMO antenna at the two operating frequencies. Then, two rectangular metal strips are loaded between the two radiating patches to further reduce the coupling of the MIMO antenna at the high resonant frequency. Finally, the coupling coefficients S12 at 2.58 GHz and 4.8 GHz have been reduced by 22 dB and 19 dB, respectively. Therefore, the isolation between the antenna elements is effectively improved.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Phased Array Using 16 Surface-Wave Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel surface-wave phased array, which consists of 16 antenna elements. The element comprises a surface wave launcher, a tapered radiating structure, and a large metallic ground. The width of a single element is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.56\lambda_{0}}$</tex> at the center frequency, which makes the antenna array very compact. The surface wave launcher employs a cone-shaped coaxial probe, a metallic ridge, and a parallel-plate waveguide with a modified parabolic reflecting wall. The metallic ridge enhances the bandwidth and smooths the transition from the parallel-plate waveguide to the radiating structure. Simulations show that the return loss is better than 8 dB from 6 to 12 GHz. This phased antenna array scans up to 45° in the H-plane at 9 GHz and has a peak gain of 19.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Harmonic Characteristic Analysis of Direction-finding System using Multi-element Time-modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a direction-finding system using a multi-element time-modulated array is implemented in Lab-VIEW and experimentally verified in real time at 2.45GHz S band frequency using a universal software radio peripheral (USRP). The set contains dual band monopole antenna elements separated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> distance, an Ultra Wide Band RFSP8T0018G switch (0.02-18GHz), Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) and LabVIEW. The experiment exhibits precise results with low hardware complexity and less calculation time. Simulation of this method estimates the angle with 100% accuracy along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm\pi/2$</tex> and experimental set up gives an average error of 1.97° in the range of 0° to +90°.

articleTitle: Sparse Cylindrical Arrays with Low Discrepancy Element Spacing Based on Van der Corput Sequence
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Designing sparse cylindrical arrays without grating lobes is a challenging task due to the large element spacings. Aperiodic spacing can reduce the grating lobes, however random approaches typically increase the average sidelobe level. This paper explores the use of nonuniform element spacing based on the low-discrepancy Van der Corput sequence. Array pattern results are presented for cylindrical arrays with element spacings larger than one wavelength and we show that this approach is capable of removing the grating lobes.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-polarized Base Station Antenna for LTE/5G Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel broadband dual-polarized base station antenna with the operating band of 3300MHz~3600MHz in LTE1900/LTE2300/LTE2500/5G. In the design, the radiation structure is made up of a dipole antenna with” H” slots and a semicircle. This antenna includes four parts: 1) a pair of metallic feeders printed on the top of the FR4 substrate with ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 4.4 and the thickness of 0.5 mm; 2) two pairs of dipole antennas printed on the bottom of the FR4 substrate; 3) a metallic reflection plate; 4) a pair of coax feeds connected to the center of top substrate. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of 67% (1.9~3.8GHz) for S11<-10 dB with an isolation of 25 dB, and the average gain reaches about 9.6 dBi. Moreover, the antenna achieves a half-power beamwidth of 65 ± 5°. Thus, this broadband dual-polarized antenna is potential for LTE/5G base station applications.

articleTitle: MTM-EBG-based Microstrip Bandstop Filter for the 900 MHz ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Metamaterial-based electromagnetic bandgap structures (MTM-EBGs) have predictable and controllable bandgaps, a property which makes them useful for microstrip bandstop filtering applications. In this paper, five MTM-EBG unit cells are cascaded in order to create a bandstop filter for use in the 902 MHz-928 MHz ISM band. Instead of cascading five identical unit cells, mirrored asymmetries were used in order to achieve improved passband performance. The final design achieves a 10-dB rejection bandwidth of 29 MHz and a peak rejection of 81 dB.

articleTitle: Star-Shaped Supershaped Patch Antenna for 5G
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a star-shaped supershaped patch antenna is proposed for 5G applications, operating at 3.5 GHz. The Gielis Formula, also called Superformula, was used to design the antenna and minimize its patch size. The characteristics of the antenna, such as return loss, realized gain and radiation pattern are simulated, and the return loss is compared with the measured results. The designed antenna attains a −40.84 dB return loss at 3.5 GHz, with operational bandwidth from 3.47 GHz to 3.52 GHz for −10 dB, with the peak gain around 7 dBi for 3.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation, and Measurement of Passive Microwave Reflectors Optimized for Field Coverage
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present design, simulation, and measurement of passive microwave reflectors that are optimized for field coverage in high-frequency communication applications. The reflectors are designed in an optimization environment based on genetic algorithms and full-wave simulations. Optimally corrugated surfaces are fabricated via 3D printers and coated with conductive paint to obtain compact and lightweight prototypes that successfully demonstrate desired reflection characteristics. The results show both the success of the proposed design procedure and the feasibility of compact reflectors that can be suitable for new-generation communications.

articleTitle: A Kapton-Based Flexible Wideband Antenna with Metamaterial Resonators for Millimeter-Wave Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip metamaterial antenna with eight resonator elements is proposed for wideband 5G flexible wireless devices. The proposed antenna, designed on a 0.1 mm Kapton film, exhibits a large fractional bandwidth of 57.3 %, from 21.4 GHz to 38.6 GHz. By exploiting the benefits of metamaterials, a S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> better than - 40 dB and a gain as high as 4.5 dBi were achieved over the operational bandwidth. Furthermore, the metamaterial antenna demonstrated a stable performance even being bent, i.e., less than 5% variation in bandwidth.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Carbon Nanotube Dimer Embedded in A Lossy Dielectric Slab
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the electromagnetic behavior of carbon nanotube (CNT) dimers embedded in a lossy dielectric slab. The numerical results show that CNT embedded in a dielectric slab exhibits interesting phenomena that are not detected while in homogeneous environment. The CNT resonance frequency decreases with the depth of the CNT inside the slab. Symmetric CNT dimer behaves as an asymmetric CNT dimer when embedded in a dielectric slab. The resonance and power level varies significantly due to the proximity between the slab interface and the CNT network.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new passive frequency beam-steering patch antenna array is proposed for 28GHz mm-wave applications. The proposed shape consists of a circular patch which has been fed by an inset microstrip line, consist of vertical slot cuts placed on top of it, and arc-shaped microstrip as the reflecting element is realized in order to achieve broad band characteristics having gain of 8dBi for single element. The proposed structure is transformed into a four-element array in order to increase the gain up to 13.3dBi with a beam-steering range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\boldsymbol{46}^{\boldsymbol{\circ}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+\boldsymbol{17}^{\boldsymbol{\circ}}$</tex> over the desired frequency of interest 26 to 28.33GHz. With the advantages of simple and compact structure, wide beam scanning range, and low-cost processing, the proposed array would be a potential candidate for the next generation 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: A Metasurface Antenna with the Characteristic of Broadband and Stable High Gain
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A broadband and stable high gain metasurface antenna is proposed in this paper. The presented antenna consists of a non-uniform metasurface fed by a pair of slots. With the modification of the geometry of patches to reduce the out-of-phase currents, the impedance bandwidth and the gain are enhanced. As shown in the simulated results, the peak gain of the presented antenna is about 11 dBi. Furthermore, it exhibits a −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 60% and has a stable high gain with a 1 dB gain bandwidth of 30%.

articleTitle: Double U-slotted Antenna for RFID Tags Mountable on Metallic Surfaces using rectangular-loop feed
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A double U-slotted antenna for radio frequency identification (RFID) tags mountable on metallic surfaces is presented. A novel rectangular-loop feed structure without any via-hole or shorting plate is proposed to perform inductive reactance. A pair of U-slots is presented to perform broad impedance band. The proposed design is verified by simulation and measurement. The measured maximum read range on a metal with a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$200\mathbf{mm}\times 200\mathbf{mm}$</tex> is 1.4m <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{EIRP}=0.4\mathbf{W})$</tex>. The measured impedance is proximately corresponding to the simulated results.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Model for Fast Recognition of Orbital Angular Momentum Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Vortex beams are widely investigated due to its great potential in wireless communication. Effective recognition of orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes is essential for radio vorticity communication. In this work, a novel recognition method to detect the OAM mode of the vortex beams based on machine learning is proposed in radio frequency (RF). To gen-erate enough training samples as well as improve the robustness of the proposed method, additive Gaussian noise is introduced. Based on the helical phase front profiles with different noise level, a machine learning model is obtained. Numerical results show that the proposed model could identify the vortex modes of noisy vortex beams with high accuracy, validating the possibility of applying this method to wireless communication. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first time that machine learning has been introduced to recognition of topological charges in radio frequency.

articleTitle: Antenna Designs for a Milimeter Wave Massive MIMO Testbed with Hybrid Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-out (MIMO) technology and mm wave are important technologies in 5G/6G to enhance the spectrum efficiency and system capacity. However, it has a lot of challenges in mm wave range, such as high hardware cost and power consumption in such systems. Hybrid beamforming is an interesting solution with less number of RF transvers than antennas. In this paper, we will present antenna designs for a 28GHz hybrid beam forming massive MIMO system with 64 antennas and 16 RF transvers.

articleTitle: Multiplexing Dual Circular-Polarized Vortex Beams by Spin-Decoupled Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a spin-decoupled metasurface for the independent control of dual circular-polarized (CP) OAM beams. By combining geometric with propagation phase in the metasurface, the generated dual CP vortex beam can be manipulated independently. As a proof-of-concept demonstration, the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) beam is directed towards <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta_{1}, \varphi_{1})=(30^{\circ}, 0^{\circ})$</tex> carrying the OAM mode of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{1}=+1$</tex>, while the left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) beam is pointed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta_{2},\varphi_{2})=(30^{\circ}, 90^{\circ})$</tex> carrying the OAM mode of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{2}=-2$</tex>. The proposed structure has been investigated and confirmed by the full-wave simulation, which validates the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Experimental Realization of Bespoke Multi-Band GRIN Lens Using Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Gradient index (GRIN) lenses are powerful tools to improve the directivity of antennas. However, traditional GRIN designs are typically limited to single-band performance and small index variations. In this paper, we propose a multi-objective optimization strategy for designing GRIN lenses for multi-band operation, where the two targeted bands are widely separated. Using additive manufacturing, a typical lens prototype is fabricated and tested, demonstrating excellent dual-band performance.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual-Polarized Patch Antenna with L-shaped Feeds For C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized dual-polarized patch antenna with differential feeding is proposed for base stations. The dual-polarized patch antenna is composed of a radiating patch with the shape of triangle bends and L-shaped stepped type slots, two pairs of mutually vertical inverted L-shaped probes and feeding networks integrated on a reflector. The proposed patch antenna achieves the impedance bandwidth (the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR)<1.5) of 16.3% ranging from 3.33 GHz to 3.92 GHz covering C-band and port isolation higher than 28 dB. And more importantly, the size of the patch antenna is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.24\times 0.24\times 0.174\ \lambda_{0}^{3}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free space wavelength at center frequency). The realized gain is greater than 7.6 dBi with a stable radiation pattern over the whole working frequency band.

articleTitle: Single Feed Dual Beam Antenna using Metamaterial Surfaces for Near-Field Phase Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Dual beam antennas with similar gain and beam-width require multiple antennas fed separately with controlled input phase shifts or a single antenna with a complicated feeding mechanism. To reduce this design complexity, this paper presents an approach that uses one antenna, a simple feeding network and a pair of simple metamaterial-based frequency selective surfaces with uniform rectangular unit cells. Four different surfaces are studied for a 13.6 GHz scalable design fed by one planar source antenna at a time. Results show that different combinations vary the near field phase, which affects beam orientation and gain, and that a single far field beam can be transformed into a dual beam with a split up to 34°. The best design has simulated and measured gain of 14.5 dB for the boresight beam and ∼11 dB for each of the dual beam.

articleTitle: Surface Wave Launcher Based Multi-beam Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel antenna design wherein multiple beams are achieved using surface wave launcher (SWL) elements, in conjunction with a partially reflecting surface (Bull's eye) structure, to form a planar 2-D leaky-wave antenna (LWA). Simulation results present four narrow beams generated at a broadside tilt angle of ±57° in two different planes with 3 dB beamwidths of 14°. The antenna has a gain of 8.5 dB. The presented leaky wave antenna is useful in 5G base stations and access point applications where multi-beam antenna systems are required.

articleTitle: Wideband 1-Bit Dynamical Beam Steering Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a linearly polarized transmitarray operating at X-band with 1-bit phase resolution is proposed. Rectangular receiving and E-shaped transmitting metallic layers are designed and printed on each side of the substrate to compose the transmitarray unit cell. Two PIN diodes are mounted on the receiving layer to obtain 1-bit phase resolution (two different states with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{180^{\circ}}$</tex> phase difference). Numerical results shows that the insertion loss are 1.17 and 1.7 dB for Case 1 and Case 2 at 11.0 GHz. A transmitarray using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{8\times 8}$</tex> proposed elements is developed and performed to obtain different beaming direction with different coding sequence.

articleTitle: Design of Metasurface for performance improvement of feed source
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The three dimensional meta-structure is proposed in this article, which shows increased performance in the feed source in terms of directivity, gain and the side lobe level. The proposed antenna has the advantages of low profile while maintaining the fixed flare angle of the feed horn, thus supports constant aperture dimension where the phase variation is decreased from 316.27° with horn feed only condition to 19.54° with the placement of proposed prototype above the horn feed. Using numerical simu-lation various key parameters i.e. radiation patterns, directivity, gain, phase variation and side lobe levels have been computed. Results show that at design frequency of 12 GHz, the computed directivity, gain, side lobe level in H- and E- planes are 20.5 dB, 20.5 dB, −26.5 dB and −12.4 dB with only horn case and with proposed prototype placed above the horn these values improved to 22.1 dB, 21.9 dB, −15.5 dB and −17.5 dB respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency-Beam-Scanning Nonreciprocal Transmissive Polychromatic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present the theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration of frequency-beam-scanning nonreciprocal transmissive polychromatic metasurface. Such a metasurface is composed of a frequency- and space-varying super-cells possessing engineered phases and magnitudes. The metasurface provides directive and diverse radiation beams, and the beams may be steered by changing the control direct current (DC) bias of the super-cells. Other interesting features include three-dimensional prism functionality with digitally controllable angles of refraction, and nonreciprocal power amplification.

articleTitle: High Gain Slot Antenna Array Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide at Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile compact antenna array based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is proposed. Its structure is a twelve-channels equal power divider connected with twelve column slot antenna arrays. Each slot antenna unit of the proposed antenna array is located in the top metal, and the feeding process is realized by connecting coaxial-to-waveguide adapter through the opening of the bottom metal. The size of the proposed antenna array is 92.08mm×61.6mm×1.72mm, which is extremely compact. The proposed antenna array works from 34.4GHz to 35.6GHz, achieving greater than 20dBi and a reflection coefficient lower than −12dB, and relative bandwidth reaches 3.43×.

articleTitle: Deterministic-Based 5G mmWave Propagation Characterization in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The new requirements of context aware environments within the framework of Smart Cities and Smart Regions come with the implementation of the Fifth-Generation (5G) wireless technology and the use of millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequency bands. However, signal propagation at these frequency bands also comes with different channel impairments that needs to be completely understood before the design and implementation of a wireless communication system. Therefore, in this work, the spatial and temporal channel characteristics of a typical urban environment have been identified for wireless networks in 30 and 70 GHz frequency bands by means of an in-house deterministic approach.

articleTitle: Efficient 2-D Plane Wave-to-Surface Wave Couplers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A large dielectric metasurface for converting a plane wave into a surface wave with a high efficiency is designed in 2-D TM polarization, which is derived from a modulated reactance surface. The spatially modulated reactance of the coupler is synthesized as a leaky wave antenna in the transmitting mode, which is the same device as the wave coupler. For a physical design, a 2-D depth-modulated dielectric backed by a ground is presented and its performance is verified by full-wave simulation. For a 80-wavelength-long coupler, a high coupling efficiency over 82% is predicted.

articleTitle: Metasurface Lens Design for High-Gain WPT System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The development of metasurface (MS) lenses for microwave power transfer (MPT) is presented. The design methodology includes the design of lenses composed of dielectric materials for computational efficiency, which are later replaced with MS lenses once a lens design is finalized. The final design is required to achieve a 3-fold power increase, which was met by the lens providing a gain increase of 4.9 dB compared with when no lens is present.

articleTitle: 360° Beam Steering with Circular Polarization Based on the Superposition of Circular $\text{TE}_{\mathrm{n}1}$ Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to generate a circular polarized radiation with a conical beam which is full <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{360^{\circ}}$</tex> steerable. In this approach, beam steering is accomplished by exciting multiple circular <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TE}_{\mathbf{n}1}$</tex> modes in conjunction with their degenerate modes for the first time. Unlike phased array antennas where beam steering is achieved by excitation of multiple equally spaced antenna elements, in this approach, beam steering is provided by exciting all the modes within the same region, which allows for saving area. As a proof of concept, an antenna structure realizing the proposed method and its preliminary simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: CubeSat Link Budget as Antennas Class Project
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna class project where students are led through main elements of a CubeSat link budget and assigned to study, choose, and design antennas for CubeSats in two different Orbits.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Adjoint Variation Method for Finite Element with 3D Edge Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Evaluating sensitivity of EM designs is of interest to antenna engineers, and also important in gradient-based optimization. It is efficiently calculated by adjoint variation method (AVM), but this usually entails the additional cost of finding the gradients of system matrices. This paper reviews AVM applied to finite element method (FEM), and proposes a procedure to calculate the gradients of system matrices and excitation vectors that are critical in AVM. The method is adapted to tetrahedral elements and its 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>-order edge basis functions. A representative example that derives gradients of return loss of a partially-loaded rectangular waveguide is presented.

articleTitle: A One-Stage O(N log N) Algorithm for Generating Nested Low-Rank Representation of Electrically Large Volume Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we develop a new <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N\log N)$</tex> algorithm to generate an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}^{2}$</tex>-representation for electrically large volume integral equations (VIEs). This algorithm requires only one stage to build nested cluster bases, which combines the advantages of both nested cross approximation and random pivot selection. Numerical experiments on electrically large 3D arrays of dielectric cubes and drones demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Low Insertion and Large Dynamic Range Substrate Integrated Waveguide Equalizer on Ceramic for Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design method of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) equalizer fabricated on ceramic substrate with surface resistance, operating in millimeter wave band, is presented. Different from the previous SIW equalizers in [1], the surface resistance (TaN) is discretely introduced into SIW equalizer. The measurement results show that: over the entire Ka-band, the equalizing values are 3.12 dB, 6.25 dB, 9.05 dB, 13.01 dB and 16.84 dB, respectively, while the return losses are all better than −15.40 dB. Correspondingly, the insertion losses at the maximum frequency (40GHz) are only 0.94, 1.94, 2.59, 2.79 and 2.10, respectively.

articleTitle: A Notch-Band UWB Tightly Coupled Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an ultrawideband (UWB) tightly coupled array (TCA) with a capacitive circuit ring (CCR) is proposed to achieve rejection notch-band through the operating bandwidth. The CCR is sandwiched between the antenna and the ground to introduce additional resonance around 3.5 GHz. The simulated broadside rejection gain is more than 15 dB. In particular, the TCA achieves a 5.7:1 bandwidth (1.3-7.5 GHz) with the active VSWR < 3 when scanning to ±60° in the E-plane and ±45° in the H-plane.

articleTitle: Multibeam 2D Lens Antenna Based on Metasurface Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the application of the metasurface technology to the design of a multibeam 2D lens antenna inspired by the Rotman lens concept. The lens is based on a multilayer metasurface structure with printed elements. The printed elements are modeled as tensor surface impedances to simplify the design process. The designed lens exhibits satisfactory performance in terms of radiation patterns and directivity.

articleTitle: Effect of diagonal slot dimensions on Axial Ratio and S11 at 26 GHz Design Frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A matrix of possible slot dimensions to create circular polarization on a square patch antenna with symmetric diagonal slot are considered. The antenna is designed on 10 mil thickness Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 (1/2 oz Copper Cladding, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{r}=2.2$</tex>) with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \Omega$</tex> edge-feed (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_{o}=0.741\ \text{mm}$</tex>) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{o}=26$</tex> GHz. Surface plots at the design frequency indicate that best Axial Ratio and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> follow non-linear trends and will intersect.

articleTitle: Two-Level Antenna Modeling with Domain Confinement and Explicit Dimensionality Reduction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations are essential to reliable evaluation of modern antenna structures. Yet, high computational cost of EM analysis poses a serious challenge for EM-driven antenna design. A possible workaround is to utilize fast surrogates. However, the curse of dimensionality hinders the applicability of the conventional surrogate-assisted frameworks beyond simple structures described by a few parameters. A workaround is offered by the recently proposed nested kriging technique, where the surrogate domain is confined to the parameter space region containing high-quality designs, which allows for setting up reliable models at a low cost. Here, this expenses are further reduced through an explicit domain dimensionality reduction by means of principal component analysis.

articleTitle: One-way Guiding by Acoustic Sub-Diffraction Chain Under Transverse Mean Flow
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this presentation we explore acoustic propagation along a sub-diffraction particle-chain waveguide under trans-verse mean medium flow. In the presence of longitudinal flow, that is, parallel to the waveguide, nonreciprocity is expected. In contrast, under the influence of medium flow that is transverse to the propagation axis, even nonreciprocity in phase accumulation is surprising, let alone one-way guiding. Here, we theoretically show one-way guiding in such a setup, under certain structural conditions. Our results may open another venue for the design of nonreciprocal acoustic wave devices for various applications, and may imply also on analogous systems in electromagnetics.

articleTitle: A Modular Microstrip Phased-array Antenna for Low-Cost, Beam-Steerable Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a K-band (17.7-19.7 GHz) beam steerable phased-array antenna for satellite communication (SATCOM) application. The microstrip patch antenna with PIN diode switches loaded can provide 2-bit phase resolution, thereby realizing the two-dimensional beam scanning. To illustrate the feasibility of this method, we used the reconfigurable 2-bit element to make a modular sparse subarray. Through the subarray splicing technology, full-wave simulation was performed on the regularly arranged 7 subarrays. The simulation results show that the array antenna has a stable left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) radiation pattern, which can be steered to an elevation angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45^{\circ}$</tex>. For all directional beams, the sidelobe levels (SLLs) and axial ratio (AR) performance can be maintained well.

articleTitle: Large European Deployable Reflector: RF Modeling and Measurement Correlation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present the RF model and correlation with measurements in K band (18.7 GHz) of a 5.1 m diameter deployable reflector antenna in lightweight mesh technology. The RF model includes the manufactured surface shape, electrical properties of the lightweight mesh, a designed and non-circular rim as well as feed tower and truss. Good agreement between main beam shape as well as sidelobe and grating lobe positions between measured and predicted patterns is found.

articleTitle: Multipath Machine Learning Assisted Optimization and Its Application for Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A multipath machine learning assisted optimization (MP-MLAO) method is proposed for antenna applications. In practical antenna design tasks, the modulation of the balance between exploration and exploitation of the conventional MLAO method always relies on experience of designers, which largely impacts the performance and robustness of the algorithm. A multipath strategy is introduced based on the implementation of multiple lower confidence bound constants to enhance the robustness of the MLAO algorithm. Moreover, with the aid of variable-fidelity-based modeling, the increase of the computational burden is largely avoided. Compared with the conventional MLAO method, the proposed MP-MLAO achieves obvious performance improvement, which is validated by applying it to design a practical cavity-backed slot antenna.

articleTitle: Wideband FSS as reflector for circularly polarized millimeter-wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband frequency selective surface (FSS) resonating at V-band frequency is proposed in this paper. It can be used as reflector for circularly polarized millimeter-wave antennas. The FSS unit cell is having two similar spiral shapes separated by a substrate at the center. It provides a wideband width of 20 GHz from 50 GHz to 70 GHz for both TE and TM modes. The proposed FSS is used as a reflector for a CPW fed circular polarized 4 × 1 circular slot array antenna. The antenna array with 13 × 5 FSS panel is simulated to obtain an impedance bandwidth of 33%. Indeed an enhanced gain of 10.2 dBi is obtained and axial ratio maintained less than 3 dB in 55–65 GHz band of frequency.

articleTitle: A Simple Gaussian Model for Ionospheric Scintillation in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simple Gaussian model for ionospheric scintillation in Singapore. The model is simple and consists of only one Gaussian term and a raised constant to characterize the S4 index. The model parameters are determined based on the 90th percentile of S4 scintillation data collected in Singapore. Comparisons of model and scintillation data over various months in Singapore indicates that the model predicts relatively well the scintillation activity in Singapore.

articleTitle: Compact Antenna for Optimized Platform Installations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new concept of antenna installation is presented to overcome the metal close proximity effects typically present in conventional platform installations. A wideband omnidirectional antenna electrically near to a metallic structure suffers of destructive interferences and the input impedance is affected by the inductance contribution generated from the ground proximity. A compact antenna has been designed to operate from 2 GHz to 6 GHz in close proximity of a metallic structure providing ultra-wideband impedance matching and stable patterns.

articleTitle: Study on Scattered Magnetic Field from a Metal Cylinder Covered with a Lossless Medium
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We study a high-frequency scattered magnetic field from a two-dimensional (2-D) coated metal cylinder which is made of a metal cylinder covered with a lossless medium layer. The geometric optical ray (GO) series solution including multiple reflection effect is valid in understanding scattering phenomena because it can derive the Brewster angle. The validity of the GO series solution is confirmed by comparing with an exact solution.

articleTitle: Thinned Antenna Array Synthesis Through Quantum Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An approach for the design of thinned antenna arrays based on the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) is here proposed. The problem of deciding which antenna elements are turned on or off is formulated in the quantum computing framework and the QFT algorithm is used. A preliminary proof-of-concept result is reported and discussed to show the behavior and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-band Reflect-Transmit-Array Antenna with High- Gain and Low- Profile
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel reflect-transmit-array (RTA) which combining reflectarray and transmitarray with high-gain and low-profile characteristics. The x-polarized incident waves will be reflected by the proposed RTA around 10 GHz while the y-polarized waves can pass through it around 14 GHz. The reflection mode and transmission mode can be excited simultaneously and controlled independently. An antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) is utilized as the source feed to reduce the block effect of the reflection mode. Simulation results showing a peak gain of 25.8 dBi and 27.4 dBi, 1-dB gain bandwidth of 11.5% and 6.2%, and 3-dB gain bandwidth of 18.4% and 11.8% for the reflection and transmission modes, respectively.

articleTitle: Effects due to Corporate Feed Network in a $16\times 16$ Element 24GHz Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Effects of the feed network is an important factor in the radiation performance of a large antenna array. The design and development of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16$</tex> element 24GHz printed planar patch antenna array is presented. A corporate feed network is adopted. Three different variants in the feed network viz., a) basic feed network, b) feed network with via fence and c) differential feed network with a 180° phase offset, are analyzed in terms of their corresponding effects in the radiation pattern and realized gain. Simulations show that the symmetric differential feed network has marginally better realized gain than the basic feed network, both with and without via fence.

articleTitle: A Self-Isolated Wideband Circularly Polarized MIMO Antenna for 5G communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact planar dual-element broadband circularly polarized (CP) MIMO antenna is presented. The proposed antenna contains two elements arranged adjacent to each other, high isolation can be obtained without utilizing any extra decoupling structures. By loading an L-shape stub and inserting a horizontal slot on the ground, wide impedance bandwidth (IBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) are achieved. The measured results suggest that the MIMO antenna can realize wide IBW of 55% (3.92-6.92 GHz) and ARBW of 25.8% (4.04-5.24 GHz), which matches well with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering From Dielectric Problems by PMCHWT-SASF
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a fast direct solver based on strong admissibility skeletonization factorization (SASF) and Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) is proposed for electromagnetic scattering from conducting objects. Different from weak admissibility skeletonization scheme, the proposed method constructs the sparse-data representation, in which interactions of well-separated groups are compressed by low-rank algorithm. As a result, the approximation rank is relatively small, and the computational efficiency will have significant improvement. Subsequently, SASF is applied to the compressed system matrix. The system matrix can be factorized into products of a series of block unit triangular matrices and a block diagonal matrix. The arising fill-in blocks corresponding to far-field interactions are compressed and eliminated by a novel and efficient method to maintain the high efficiency and accuracy of the factorization procedure. The computational complexity and storage requirement of proposed factorization scale as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N^{1.5})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N\log N)$</tex>, respectively. Several numerical results are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Multibeam Substrate Integrated Horn Array for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multibeam planar horn array covering a full azimuth direction. The proposed antenna array is made of compact substrate integrated horns. The beamwidth of a single horn is 30°. Therefore, the full azimuth coverage can be achieved by using twelve horns. The radiation patterns of the neighboring horns intersect with each other at − 3 dB beamwidth. This antenna array has a wide relative bandwidth up to 32% in Ka-band. In the operating frequency, all the beams are well isolated to each other by a low mutual coupling below −45 dB. The proposed array is fabricated using a single-layer printed circuit board with a thickness of 1.5 mm. The compact size makes the integration of this array easy. Additionally, the omnidirectional pattern of the array can be used to support high speed beam tracking and overcome blockages for unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact wideband frequency reconfigurable (FR) antenna is designed for the cognitive radio (CR) applications in this paper. The antenna covers 4.33 to 7.21 GHz frequency range when tuning the capacitances of the varactors. By introducing the planar periodic slow wave structure on the patch, the dimension of the antenna is drastically reduced to 4 × 4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Simulated results indicate the antenna holds satisfying radiation performance with low cross-polarizations. In applications, the proposed antenna is suitable for the portable devices with CR capacities.

articleTitle: A Microwave Tomography System For Ischemic Stroke Based on Distorted Born Iterative Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a microwave tomography system for ischemic stroke. The developed device consists of a measurement prototype, a matrix switch and a vector network analyzer(VNA). and it equipped with an efficient imaging method for the reconstruction of the distribution of the relative permittivity of the human body under test. It has been preliminarily verified by experimental data. The results show that the system can effectively detect inclusions with different sizes and positions in the head model under consideration.

articleTitle: Simplified Human Body Models with Reduced Types of Tissues for MRI at 1.5T
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Simplified human body models with a reduced number of tissues are developed using the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). Different tissues are grouped into several clusters based on the tissue electrical parameters. Using three human body models (the Duke, the Ella, and the Obese) from the virtual family project, electromagnetic simulations were conducted for original models and simplified models respectively when the models are under the emission of an MR RF coil. The electrical field distributions were extracted for comparison.

articleTitle: Indoor WiFi Channel Measurements with Printed Endfire Beam-Steering Pixel Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a combined use of indoor localization system SpotFi and a 2-port reconfigurable beam-steering pixel antenna. SpotFi is particularly modified to act as a signal processing algorithm for determining the position of the connected device from its feedback signals. With this localization information, a reconfigurable beam-steering antenna is able to keep track on the direction with maximized signal strength and therefore enhancing the channel throughput.

articleTitle: Isolation Improvement of 5G MIMO Antenna Based on the Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna with the analysis of DGS based on the theory of characteristic modes (TCM). The use of TCM enables a systematic approach to predict whether the isolation can be further improved. In this paper, the proposed MIMO antenna is composed of different elements and its operating bands can cover the 3.3 ~ 3.6 GHz and 4.8 ~5 GHz bands applied in 5G communication systems, and the possibility of improving the isolation by using DGS for the MIMO antenna with different elements is explored. The simulated results show that the minimum isolation of the designed antenna is 21.6 dB in the operating bands, and the maximum gain of the antenna array is 8.4 dB.

articleTitle: Printed radome for reconfigurable antenna radiation pattern in 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative radome in order to customize antennas radiation pattern for 5G applications. For that, a 3D direct writing process is used to print patterns onto a half sphere radome. In this way, the radiation pattern of a ring patch antenna is more directional, and the gain is increased from 2.39 dBi to 4.55 dBi.

articleTitle: COVID-19 Wake-Up Call: Technology-Based Electromagnetic Education Revisited
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The teaching of electromagnetics courses faced significant challenges during the COVID-19 epidemic era. Convergence to online and virtual teaching, added significant difficulties in motivating students and ineffectively explaining and demonstrating this what is considered abstract and highly mathematical subject. Our team at the University of Hawaii quickly resorted to the CAEME software and extensively used available multimedia models, virtual labs demos, and simulation software to help with teaching in this completely virtual teaching modality. We also developed “Virtual Organization” website, to help students share their simulation results and discuss issues and bottle necks in learning the presented material. This paper highlights some of these ongoing activities and provide a brief assessment on the viability of the adopted approach.

articleTitle: Multi-Layered Flat Meta-Lenses for Conical Beam Scanning via Optimization of Geometrical Optics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a methodology for the design of multi-layered flat meta-lenses that are fed off-axis based on a numerical synthesis algorithm hybridizing Geometrical Optics (GO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). In previous work, the algorithm was applied for the design of on-axis fed flat meta-lenses. In this work, we use the algorithm to synthesize off-axis fed flat lenses with circular symmetry thus producing conically scanned beams. Descriptions on how to realize the synthesized lens using metamaterial elements of variable sizes distributed on planar dielectric substrates are provided. Full-wave simulation results of a 10 cm multi-layered flat meta-lens operating at 13.4 GHz fed from various locations along the ring-shaped focus demonstrate the lens conical scanning capabilities.

articleTitle: Investigating the Use of Matching Metasurfaces in Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We consider the use of matching metasurfaces for enhanced interrogation of the object of interest (OI) in microwave imaging. For an OI immersed in water, we perform synthetic data collection in air with the aid of matching metasurfaces, and then invert the scattered field data under the assumption of infinite water background medium.

articleTitle: Analysis of Empirical Propagation Models in Suburban Areas at 800 MHz and 1.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the differences in performance, among different empirical propagation models at 800 MHz and 1.8 GHz in suburban areas. These frequencies can be applied in broadcasting and 4G Long Term Evolution (LTE) bands. Measurements were conducted in the vicinity of the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN), in the city of Natal, in the northeast of Brazil. Results were compared with the ones obtained using Ericsson, Third Generation Partnership Project TR 36,942, Stanford University Interim (SUI) and Electronic Communication Committee (ECC-33) models, simulated in MATLAB. Also, analysis was performed in terms of root mean square error (RMSE) and similarity between distribution data sets, provided by Wilcoxon rank-sum test.

articleTitle: A Stretchable Liquid Metal Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a stretchable liquid metal antenna array. While liquid metal devices are not new, non-toxic gallium based liquid metals have caused an increase in research for related applications. Stretchable liquid metal antennas and phase shifters can provide the reconfigurability for wideband applications while delivering beam control at low cost. This research presents the design, simulations, and measurements of a stretchable liquid metal array based on two stretchable liquid metal antennas and a stretchable liquid metal phase shifter. The 2-element array prototype demonstrates 180° beam steering, active return loss better than 15 dB, and gain above 3.5 dBi, thus indicating the possibilities of using liquid metals for an antenna array system.

articleTitle: Antenna for satellite and UAV communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This article presents a prototype of an antenna that will be part of the communication system between a picosatellite and an unmanned aerial vehicle UAV. The designed antenna is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> array of patch antennas and has an axial ratio below 3dB in a large beam width (140° roughly). The S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter is below −10 dB in a good bandwidth. Two 1to 4 power dividers are used to feed the array antenna. In both cases, the impedance bandwidth is better than 680 MHz

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum Multiplexing Based on Angle-dispersive Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel angle-dispersive metasurface to multiplex two beams incident from axisymmetric angles as orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams with orthogonal modes. This OAM multiplexing requires the metasurface with anti-symmetric angular phase dispersion. A series of asymmetric meta-atoms are designed to meet the required phase response and high transmission efficiency. Spiral phase and amplitude profiles are obtained from the simulation results under axisymmetric illumination angles, which demonstrate the OAM multiplexing capability of the metasurface.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Conformal mmWave Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a pattern reconfigurable conformal mmWave antenna at 28 GHz for 5G applications. Using a T-junction power divider and PIN diodes, eight <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> sub-arrays of microstrip patches are configured to radiate independently creating separate states capable of 360° of discrete coverage.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Implantable Antenna and Discussion of Concentration of Fields
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a two-coil design for implantable antenna miniaturization is presented. As implantable medical devices (IMDs) get smaller, prior work has shown that a set of focusing rods made of a biocompatible, conductive material may be useful to guide power from an external plane wave to the IMD. Prior research has also optimized a 3D ring array design for medical telemetry focusing. In this work, we evaluate the effect of these field focusing designs if coils are used as the transmitting and receiving antennas. A comparison of the coils with and without the focusing rods is presented.

articleTitle: Near-Field-Focused 2-D Frequency Scanning Ridge-Gap Waveguide Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A millimeter-wave self-progressive near-field-focused (NFF) 2-D frequency scanning array antenna is presented in this paper. A compact self-progressive phase-shift network without additional area is proposed to generate the desired high phase progression. The ridge-gap waveguide is applied to build the compact double-layer folded transmission line with the contactless structure. Simulation results present a good focusing performance in the near-field (NF) region, showing good prospects in NF fast-scanning applications, e.g., electromagnetic imaging and detecting systems.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum Based Isolation in Full Duplex Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Full duplex wireless systems suffer from self-interference due to crosstalk between the transmitter and receiver antennas operating in proximity of each other. The orthogonal nature of signal carrying different orbital angular momentum modes, can be used to create an isolation between two adjacent transmitter and receiver antennas. This has been shown experimentally and through simulations in High frequency simulation software (HFSS). To date we have been able to achieve an isolation of 3.6dB through simulations, and 2.6dB through experiments.

articleTitle: Long Range Dipole with Omnidirectional Pattern Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A long range dipole with omnidirectional pattern based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) structure is presented in this paper. The dipole consists of an SSPPs structure and two monopoles with reversed phase. Although the length of the dipole is twice the wavelength of the center frequency, it can have stable high gain and beam non-bifurcation characteristics at the same time. The realized gain is 4.6-6.3 dB within the band of 4.4-4.55 GHz and 5.45-5.55 GHz.

articleTitle: On the Manufacturing Process of a 3D Printed Patch Antenna with Variable Trace Height
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Conductive filament such as Electrifi can be used to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3\mathrm{D}}$</tex> print conventional and unconventional geometries of microstrip antennas. A modified manufacturing method is presented in this paper to realize non-planar antennas with variable trace height using the additive manufacturing method.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide Band Antenna for True Wireless Stereo Earphones
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the new design technique of the Ultra Wide Band (UWB) antenna for the True Wireless Stereo (TWS) earphones is proposed. The newly proposed antenna structure is designed using two short structures to cover the UWB band of TWS earphones within a minimal antenna area. Consequently, the proposed antenna satisfies <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 2$</tex> in the frequency 6.2 GHz to 9.7 GHz range. Therefore, the proposed antenna is available in the High Band of DS-UWB and Band Group #3 and #4 of MB-OFDM. The proposed design technique can contribute to TWS earphones that require the design of UWB antennas with minimal antenna regions.

articleTitle: A Compact Waveguide-Based Reflection-Type Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a waveguide-based reflection-type phase shifter is proposed. The phase shifter is composed of one orthogonal mode transducer (OMT) and one polarization converter. The linear-polarization signal is input from one single-mode port of the OMT, and then transferred to the polarization converter through the common port of the OMT. The signal is reflected and converted to orthogonal linear polarization. As such, the orthogonal signal can be output through the other single-mode port of the OMT. The phase can be tuned by changing the position of the polarization converter.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Frequency Diverse Array with Frequency Offset Errors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Frequency diverse array(FDA) can produce an Sshaped beam pattern by applying a small frequency offset between array elements. It provides the possibility of jointing range and angle estimation of targets and range-dependent interference suppression, which can not be achieved by phased array. However, the frequency offset is one of the main parameters in FDA and its errors will inevitably affect the array performance, while little literature has studied this at present. In this paper, an approach is proposed to investigate the influence on array performance caused by frequency offset deviation. Numerical results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Simulation of Shaped Metasurface antennas, including the Feeder Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An effective Method of Moment (MoM) tool able to rapidly and accurately analyze arbitrarily shaped metasurface (MTS) antennas is provided. The MTS is assumed to be fed by a coax probe as is usually the case in practice. The feed as well as the MTS are meshed with local basis functions. The calculation of the interactions between the MTS basis functions, which are the dominant unknowns, is accelerated with the FFT. The surface current is then computed iteratively using the GMRES algorithm. Once the currents on the MTS and on the feed are obtained, the efficiency of the antenna can be derived. The method is validated with an in-house numerical tool developed for the particular case of circular MTSs. An excellent comparison is observed.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of anomalous spectral features of SKALA4.1 antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this communication, we present a detailed measurement process of the SKALA4.1 antenna frequency response as the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> of its coupling with a reference antenna in an anechoic chamber environment. This is the first experimental evidence of anomalous spectral features of SKALA4.1 antenna. We validate the consistency of the results by examining the error between measurement and a corresponding FEKO simulation. Finally, we pinpoint all the spectral features inherent in SKALA4.1 antenna and examine their occurrence in measurement and simulation.

articleTitle: Aperture-Coupled Feed for Surface-Mounted Additively Manufactured Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The use of additive manufacturing (AM) for antenna arrays offers both fabrication simplicity and design flexibility. Integrating and feeding such arrays in conventional microwave systems, however, is still a challenge. This paper explores the use of aperture-coupled feeds for AM arrays to simplify the assembly process and increase the viability of AM arrays in highly integrated systems. The simulated performance of two aperture designs is compared to measurements of proof-of-concept arrays printed in aluminum, showing feasibility of the approach.

articleTitle: A Near-Field Focused Circular Array Based on Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a near-field focused circular array antenna operating at 2.45GHz is reported. The array antenna is implemented by using 16 rectangular dielectric resonator antennas placed on two circles. The proposed rectangular DRA fed by a coaxial probe is made up from high permittivity (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=38). By adjusting the radius of the circles, the antenna achieves a controllable focal distance. The focusing distance can be calculated from the inner and outer ring radius and in agreement with the simulation result.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Single-Lane Multi-Tag Vehicle Identification Scenarios with UHF RFID
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The influence of the position offset of a vehicle within a single lane of an Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)-based free-flow tolling system is analyzed. Its performance when using two windshield tags is compared to the case when only one tag is used. It turns out that one tag is enough to hold the number of reads at an acceptable level even if only half of the vehicle is on the considered lane.

articleTitle: New Approach on Generating Electromagnetic Waves for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new method to improve the performance of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) devices. Existing TMS coils are limited in their ability to target desired neural populations due to depth-focality tradeoff and their reliance on high-energy pulse sources, which raises safety concerns. However, the proposed method utilizes the modulated magnetic field of a permanent magnet, which is equivalent to a lossless electromagnet. The magnetic reluctance of the medium surrounding the permanent magnet is modulated to alter magnetic flux intensity and direction, resulting in a time-variant field. The simulation results show that the focality and penetration depth is improved while using significantly less power than conventional TMS devices that use figure-8 coils.

articleTitle: Applying GSTCs in Electromagnetic Surface Inverse Design Using Optimization and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic metasurface design based on far-field constraints without the knowledge of the fields on both sides of the metasurface is typically a time consuming and iterative process, which relies heavily on heuristics and ad hoc methods. This paper proposes an end-to-end systematic and efficient approach where the designer inputs the desired far-field parameters such as nulls, sidelobe levels, and main beam level(s); and a 3-layer non-uniform passive, lossless, omega-type bianisotropic electromagnetic metasurface design to satisfy them is returned. The surface parameters to realize the far-field criteria are found using the alternating direction method of multipliers on a homogenized model derived from the method of moments. This model incorporates edge effects and mutual coupling. Optimization through the physical unit cell space integrated with machine learning-based surrogate models is used to realize the desired surface parameters with physical meta-atom (or unit cell) designs. A passive and lossless multi-beam example is shown to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Compact and Wideband Design of Substrate Integrated Waveguide Fed Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A planar array of dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) integrated with a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is designed to operate at millimeter wavelengths. The proposed design is very compact (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 4.3\lambda\times 3.6\lambda$</tex>) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\times 4$</tex> DRA array elements excited through the slots on the SIW. An impedance bandwidth (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>≤−10 dB) of 13% is achieved and a peak-gain of approximately 19 dBi is realized over the operating frequency band 34-38.5 GHz. The radiation efficiency is also maintained above 90% over this band. The front-to-back ratio and the sidelobe level are satisfactorily maintained below −24dB and −12dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Terahertz Scanning Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of novel Terahertz (THz) groove gap waveguide(GGW) technology seamless scanning leaky wave antenna is presented. GGW provides the advantage of un-touching technology that reduce the difficulty of manufacture at THz bands. The scanning range reach to at least 15° due to the extension of the applicable frequency band. 3D printing technology is employed to make it ease for THz components manufacture. Simulation results showed that the antenna has bandwidth of 100GHz of vswr(vswr<1.2).

articleTitle: Wideband Radial-Line Slot Array Antenna Technology for Near-Field Meta-Steering Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper reviews wideband radial-line slot array design and its suitability to develop wideband beam-steering antenna through near-field meta-steering (NFSM). A low-profile and highly efficient beam-steering antenna system can be realized using the wideband RLSA and pair of metasurfaces, which are placed in the near-field region of the RLSA. In NFMS systems, the base antenna remains fixed while the metasurfaces are rotated to steer the beam in both azimuth and elevation directions. The concept was first demonstrated with narrowband medium-gain antenna, and since then, it has been extended to design high-power systems, dual-band high throughout systems, and wideband steering systems.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for Evaluation of Multilayered Media Green's Functions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this study, a novel approach is presented for efficient evaluation of Sommerfeld integrals arising in spatial-domain Green's functions in planar multilayered media. This approach allows us to tackle the difficulties encountered during the integration of the Sommerfeld integrals, which exhibit highly oscillatory and slowly decaying nature occurring especially at very high frequencies, e.g., at millimeter waves, that are finding increasing use in applications such as 5G and beyond. The oscillatory behavior of the integrand is modeled through an efficient interpolation and extrapolation scheme with a few samples needed to represent the integrand. Since the integrand is represented with a few exponentials, analytical integration can be used to speed up the process. The proposed approach is tested on different Green's functions and a good agreement is obtained.

articleTitle: A Compact Reconfigurable Antenna for Borehole Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A borehole radar (BHR) is a kind of ground penetrating radar that runs in a borehole for subsurface investigations. Considering the limited borehole size and the need for three-dimensional positioning of the unknown targets, BHR antennas are generally required to be both compact and directional. In this paper, a compact reconfigurable antenna is proposed, which can be potentially used for a directional BHR. This antenna contains four dipoles and a certain number of cross-shaped structures. Some PIN diodes are used to control the on-off between the dipoles and the cross-shaped structures for reconfiguring the radiation pattern of the antenna. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna can achieve a wide bandwidth of 52% from 129 MHz to 220 MHz and high directional radiation.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Uniform Linear Array of Electrically Small Huygens Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A uniform linear array of electrically small Huygens dipole antennas (HDAs) that is realized on a single ultra-thin substrate is presented in this paper. The HDA consists of a pair of near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) elements and a simple driven antenna element. The NFRP elements are metamaterial-inspired electrically small structures - the Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) and the capacitively loaded loop (CLL). They are excited by an electrically small dipole antenna connected to a 50–Ω source by a twin-line microstrip line. This HDA generates a cardioid radiation pattern with a high realized gain (5.4 dBi) and wide beamwidth (151° in its H-plane). A uniform 1×4 linear array formed with four of these HDAs operating at 2.45 GHz with a center-to-center spacing of 0.45 λo has been developed to achieve higher directivity. The array is excited by a 1-to-4 microstrip feed network. The entire system is realized on a single piece of 0.0042 λo thick PCB substrate. The −10 dB impedance bandwidth covers 70 MHz, from 2.415 to 2.485 GHz. The realized gain is stable over it with a 8.7 dBi peak value. A very broad beamwidth (162°) is realized in the H-plane. The array is an ideal candidate to act as the base station antenna for 5G and beyond wireless power transfer (WPT) applications.

articleTitle: Broadband Green's Function-KKR-Multiple Scattering Method for the Calculations of Band Structures in Topological Acoustics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Topological states in photonics were initially proposed by Haldane in analogy to the quantum Hall (QH) effect in electronic system. Topological acoustics has also been demonstrated recently. In this paper, we apply the Broadband Green's function-KKR-Multiple Scattering Theory (BBGF-KKR-MST) to calculate band eigenvalues and band field solutions in topological acoustics. The advantage of the method is that low order cylindrical waves are used to derive the matrix eigenvalue equations for the bands. For the first two bands, the dimension of the matrix equation is only 7 by 7. Using the eigenvalue and the eigenvector, the band field solutions and the normalization are calculated with higher order cylindrical waves. The CPU time requirements, including setup, is 0.006 seconds for a band eigenvalue. The band field solution requires only 15 coefficients of higher order cylindrical waves for the entire hexagonal cell.

articleTitle: The Edge Diffraction Effect on the Radiation Pattern of Elements for Antenna Array Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper analyzed the edge diffraction effect of elements for antenna array synthesis using equivalent edge current (EEC) theory, and it is shown that the difference between the radiation pattern of different elements can be reduced by the circular edge compared with the straight edge. Its effectiveness is illustrated by two examples.

articleTitle: Screen Printing Reliable Wearable Microstrip Antennas on Rough Textile Substrates
