publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Textile-based antennas are typically realized using conductive fabrics adhered to thick non-woven fabrics such as felt, which are not suited for additive manufacturing due to their roughness. This paper presents screen printing on thin and breathable polyurethane films as a method for realizing e-textile antennas without altering the feel of the fabric, demonstrated through a microstrip antenna on standard felt fabric. The fabricated proximity-coupled patch maintains at least 100 MHz (4%) bandwidth from 2.46 to 2.56 GHz regardless of bending and human proximity, 6.6 dBi measured gain, and 69% radiation efficiency. The robustness of the proposed antenna is demonstrated, for the first time, through the measured radiation properties, showing that the antenna maintains its peak gain and radiation patterns after more than 10,000 bending cycles.

articleTitle: Choice of Optimization Parameters in an Inverse Metasurface Design Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We consider the choice of optimization parameters for a conjugate gradient (CG) based inverse metasurface design approach. An analytical formula to calculate the step length at each iteration of the CG algorithm is derived. In addition, some guidelines for the choice of appropriate regularization parameters associated with the enforcement of the local power conservation and the smoothness of equivalent currents are provided.

articleTitle: An FSS-loaded PUMA Array with 16.5:1 bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile, planar ultrawideband modular antenna array loaded with frequency selective surface (FSS) is implemented. Through the tightly coupled elements and the extra FSS layer between dipole radiator and ground plane, the bandwidth of PUMA array is effectively extended. A 16.5:1 bandwidth, low profile(0.054λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf>) antenna array with good scanning performance is realized, and the scanning angles of E-plane and H-plane reaches 60° and 45°.

articleTitle: Finite-State Markov Modeling for the Non-stationary Wideband Vehicular Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Developing an accurate wideband vehicular channel model is a key issue for the transmission scheme and protocol design of vehicular communications. Although finite-state Markov chain (FSMC) has been extensively investigated, most of the literature about FSMC modeling only considered channel fading in the time domain or frequency domain. Only few FSMC channel models describing channel fading in both the time and frequency domains lack the support of measurement data. In this paper, we propose an FSMC model in both time and frequency domain for vehicular channels based on real measurements. We validate the accuracy of steady state probability (SSP) of the proposed model via real measurement data. And we also discuss the influence of different subband partitions and the size of the modeling region on multi-subband interval change probability (MICP). The conclusion of this paper can be used in future FSMC modeling for the non-stationary wideband channel.

articleTitle: Design of a radiation-type low-profile programmable antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a radiation-type coding element with the integration of radiation structure and metasurface phase modulation structure is proposed. The radiation mode of element can be adjusted by switching the integrated PIN diode states, so that the radiation phase of element has a 1-bit encoding characteristic. A low-profile two-dimensional (2-D) array antenna containing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 16$</tex> elements is designed to verify the adjustable characteristics of radiation beam. The simulation results demonstrate that the antenna has excellent radiation beamforming and beam scanning capabilities.

articleTitle: Wideband RFI Cancellation Using true-time delays and a Hadamard Projection Operator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) in a devastating problem for high-sensitivity phased arrays. This paper explores a method of mitigating RFI in a receiving array using a combination of true-time delay with a truncated Hadamard projection that can place a wide-band spatial null over the RFI. The operations involved can be performed with analog circuity before sampling for the digital signal processing engine in order to enhance dynamic range. The modified beamformer solution is briefly derived and performance is compared to the existing maximum SINR beamformer using analytical phasor domain models. The results show successful null placement at the expense of control of the main lobe shape and side lobe levels.

articleTitle: Generalized Design Considerations of Leaky-Wave Antennas Based on Multi-Mode Resonator (MMR) Concept
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the generalized design considerations of a broad class of leaky-wave antennas based on the multi-mode resonator (MMR) concept are holistically investigated and described. First of all, unified design guidelines depending on the composition principle of MMR-based radiating discontinuity (RD) are briefly introduced in terms of equivalent circuit models, which can be extracted from computational field simulations. Next, the benefits and potentials of RDs featuring a flexible mode-control capability for realizing multifunctional and versatile LWAs are presented and explained. Finally, a practical example exhibiting flexibly engineered radiation and filtering characteristics is examined and demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Multi-functional Polarization Reconfigurable Metasurface for C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable polarization metasurface (MSF) is presented that uses pin diodes to convert the linearly polarized (LP) incident wave into a reflected wave with either linear polarization in the perpendicular orientation or with circular polarization. The multi-functional behavior occurs in the wide frequency range of 4.45–5.50 GHz and it is based on the response of the novel dumbbell shaped unit cell which is loaded with a parallel combination of a PIN diode with a 0.15 pF capacitor. The MSF presents polarization conversion ratio (PCR) better than 90% and axial ratio (AR) better than 3 dB in C-band frequencies.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of Doppler effect suppression by subcarrier spacing in ultra-high-speed environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The rapid development of Hyperloop puts forward the new requirements of wireless communication. The purpose of this paper is to improve the existing standard wireless communication system, and to suppress the Doppler effect by expanding the subcarrier spacing to meet the communication requirements in the ultra-high-speed environment. In this paper, a verification system was built based on the SDR(Software-Defined Radio), and the performance analysis of the system under high-speed mobile conditions was completed, and the block error rate and constellation of the PDSCH (Physical Downlink Shared Channel) in the system were obtained. The results verify the feasibility of this method, and the development and evolution of railway wireless communication is further promoted.

articleTitle: A T-shaped defected ground structure for decoupling circularly polarization microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel T-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) is presented to reduce the mutual coupling between dual feed points circularly polarization microstrip antennas. In this paper, the mutual coupling between the same polarization ports decreases by 12.8dB and 7dB in parallel and series arrangement, respectively. The gain and radiation efficiency are increased from 7.2dB to 7.58dB and from 94.6% to 95.6%, respectively. The axial ratio has also been optimized from 1.74dB to 0.36dB.

articleTitle: Miniatured LPF Design on a Double-Layered Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A defected ground structure (DGS) lowpass filter is designed on a double-layered substrate. By increasing the effective dielectric constant on a DGS plane, the DGS pattern can be minimized. An equivalent circuit model is presented and circuit elements are extract to design the lowpass filter. The simulated, modeled, and experimental results have been well matched to the new design method.

articleTitle: Square Plate Active Limiting Frequency Selective Surface at X-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Limiters are commonly used in receivers to protect against high incident RF power levels. The power level input to the limiter is dependent on the system's antenna gain, so receiver protection is usually designed for a specific antenna. In this paper, receiver protection in the form of an active limiting frequency selective surface is proposed. This allows the receiver protection to be located before the antenna, making it independent of antenna performance. A design at X-band is presented and simulated.

articleTitle: Compact Multi-frequency Feed Horn for Radiometer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this article, a structure and design procedure of a novel compact three-frequency-band horn antenna with a stable phase center for radiometer is presented. The antenna incorporates two series ortho-mode transducers (OMT), and a multimode conical structure. The two compact OMTs section are designed to be fed by standard WR-27 and WR-29 waveguides respectively, while the third band wave is fed by WR-30 waveguides followed with the second OMT. The proposed compact design utilizes two profiled OMT to separate the three bands wave, at the same time profiled multimode conical horn employed to yield symmetric radiation pattern. Simulations results show that the antenna impedance bandwidth (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 1.5$</tex>) is 82 to 100 GHz, 122 to 136GHz and 160 to 175 GHz respectively. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits 14–17 dB gain, and less than 1 mm phase center variation over the operating frequency range. Due to the aforementioned features, the proposed antenna is suitable as the feed for three frequency band radiometer. The design is numerically validated by full wave simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Broadband Dual-polarization Antenna for 2G/3G/LTE Base Station
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This article proposed a novel broadband dual-polarized antenna for 2G/3G/LTE base station. This designed dual-polarized antenna is composed of two perpendicularly crossed dipoles, and a broadband is achieved by designing the “+” shaped and rectangular parasitical groove. The two pair of dipoles are printed on the bottom of the FR4 substrate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{r}=4.4)$</tex> with the thickness of 0.8mm, where the cross feeding-lines are also printed on the top of the substrate. The stacked metallic disks are connected by four Nylon cylinders. Two coaxial cables are connected to the center of bottom substrate. The simulated results by HFSS show that the dual-polarized antenna has the operating bandwidth of 1.65~2.73 GHz for S11 <-10 dB, and an average isolation of 29 dB. Besides, the dual-polarized antenna has a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of around 65º, and an average gain of 9.0 dBi.

articleTitle: Stabilizing Impedance Matching for Differentially Fed Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Due to the coupling between feeding coaxial cables, it will influence impedance matching of a differentially fed base station antenna. To solve this problem, a method has been proposed. By nested metal tubes outside coaxial cables, stable impedance matching is obtained. Finally, to verify the design theory, a differential fed base station antenna with nested metal tubes outside coaxial cables was fabricated. Measured results agree well with simulated results, so theoretical analysis has been verified.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Numerical and experimental analysis of a dual-band microstrip patch antenna for the fifth generation (5G) mobile communications are presented. The numerical analysis of the antenna is performed using the finite-difference time-domain method and CST software. The proposed antenna is implemented on a low-cost FR-4 substrate and operated at 24 and 28 GHz. The antenna maximum gain values are 3.20 dBi and 3.99 dBi in the x-y plane at 24 and 28 GHz, respectively, and provides almost omni-directional patterns suitable for 5G mobile communication devices.

articleTitle: Flexible Quasi-Yagi-Uda antenna for 5G communication
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental of a single and array Quasi Yagi-Uda antenna at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna is implemented on MFLEX flexible material with a thickness of 0.120mm for 5G applications. A wideband antenna operates within 24 to 29.5 GHz and exhibits almost the same end-fire radiation pattern over bandwidth with an average gain of 6.2dBi and 10.15dBi for single and array antennas. The flexible antenna was tested under bending conditions and results showed excellent performance at the 28GHz region.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition using Deep learning Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In human-device interaction, hand signals are extremely significant. Despite the growing relevance of human hand signals, hand gesture recognition technology is still unreliable due to complicated hand gesture feedback or environmental influences. We suggest Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) as a technology to solve this issue in this article. RNN has the benefit of being able to learn time series data, which significantly improves the efficiency of human-device interaction. We used a Sinuous antenna with a bandwidth of 6.0-8.5 GHz and a gain of 8 dB to collect data from the five hand signals and conditioned them using RNN. The proposed RNN's classification result was accurate to the tune of 80%

articleTitle: Error Analysis of Isosceles Triangular Interpolation for Non-uniform Grid
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The isosceles triangular interpolation based on the non-uniform grid is proposed to further speed up the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). The non-uniform grid is transformed into a uniform grid by using Lagrange polynomials. The interpolation errors of the second order isosceles triangular interpolation based on the non-uniform grid are analyzed. Numerical results show that the isosceles triangular interpolation is more efficient than the Lagrange interpolation.

articleTitle: Wearables for Joint Effusion Detection: An Analysis for Magnitude-/Phase-Only vs. Combined Readings
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Detecting and diagnosing joint effusion is a costly and often invasive process. Our previous work introduced a seamless wearable system consisting of transmit and receive loops that was able to detect changes in synovial fluid build-up via transmission coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\mathrm{S}_{21})}$</tex> measurements. The system relied on magnitude and phase measurements conducted each at different frequencies. This work simplifies the previous design by enabling monitoring of both magnitude and phase at a single frequency. Another improvement is the elimination of any lumped elements attached to the loops to ease the wearable implementation. Our studies provide an optimal design at 1485.2 MHz that is robust to frequency fluctuations within a bandwidth of 30 MHz. Key performance metrics are identified and compared for magnitude-Iphase-only designs vs. the proposed combined approach.

articleTitle: A Feed-through Sharing Structure of a Wireless Power Transfer Coil and Stimulation Electrodes for Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a combined structure of a wireless power transfer (WPT) coil and stimulation electrodes for implantable medical devices. This structure has only a pair of wire connections, and the coil and electrodes are connected to circuits through a shared pair of feed-throughs. It reduces the number of feed-through connections from 4 to 2 and improves hermetical sealing capacity and fabrication complexity. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21 \times 19$</tex> mm sized 2-turn coil is fabricated and measured with platinum electrodes of 1-cm diameter in a saline solution. The performance degradation of the wireless power efficiency is 2.2%. Stimulation voltage drop and current consumption increase are 2.5% and 3.1%, respectively. With a stimulation and WPT circuit module, wirelessly powered stimulation waveforms are verified.

articleTitle: A Hybrid SIE-PDE Formulation Without Additional Boundary Conditions for Electromagnetic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A hybrid surface integral equation partial differential equation (SIE-PDE) formulation without boundary condition requirement is proposed to solve the challenging electromagnetic problems. The computational domain is first decomposed into the overlapping SIE and PDE domains. An equivalent model with only the surface equivalent electric current density on the bound-ary is constructed in the SIE domain. Then, through embedding the surface equivalent current density into the inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation, a hybrid SIE-PDE formulation is derived. This new hybrid formulation is mathematically equivalent to the original physical model, which does not require boundary conditions to couple the SIE and PDE formulations. Numerical results demonstrate its accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of W-band Multi-OAM-mode Antenna with High Purity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A new design of W-band multi-mode OAM antenna with high purity is presented. The antenna consists of two parts, one is the microstrip ring/circular-patch antenna, which is used to generate vortex beams with OAM modes of l = 1 & 2, and the other is waveguide ring-slot antenna, which is used to generate vortex beams with OAM modes of l = 3 & 4. The two parts are effectively combined to obtain a compact structure, which can provide a new idea for the generation of multi-mode vortex beams.

articleTitle: Green's Function for Pedagogical Development II: Inhomogeneous Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Green's function for the Poisson's equation in one dimension previously constructed from physical consideration with homogeneous boundary condition is being extended to the case with inhomogeneous boundary conditions. Two different methods are employed, namely a physical approach based on superposition and an analytic approach based on the Green's identity. Identical results are obtained. It can be seen by comparing the outcomes that it is more efficient to use the Green's function with homogeneous boundary condition for the distribution integral in the domain for the potential function, while relying on the boundary integrals to account for the contributions due to the inhomogeneous boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Dimer Dielectric Huygens' Metasurface: Realizing Perfect Anomalous Reflection at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper reports a coarsely discretized dielectric Huygens' reflective metasurface featuring two meta-atoms known as meta-dimer per metasurface period. We termed the resulting metasurface as dimer dielectric Huygens' metasurface (Di-DHMS). The coarse discretization dramatically simplifies the design and reduces mutual coupling effects, leading to a cost-effective, robust, and highly efficient metasurface design. Through full-wave simulations at 60 GHz, we demonstrate that the proposed Di-DHMS can achieve perfect anomalous reflection for the oblique plane wave incidence.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Resolution for Large Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the steering resolution for phased array antenna with a given number of antenna elements controlled by digital phase shifters. The steering resolution is illustrated through main beam pointing error. The approximation formulas of square, rectangular and linear arrays using two-dimensional quantization method and simple/regular round-off are unified into one approximation, as a result, beam steering resolution is more dependent on the array size rather than the array shape. Besides the quantization phase errors, the phase error from typical HPF/LPF phase shifter topology is also considered in the study.

articleTitle: Miniaturized 3D Multi-Segment Wire Antenna for 5G
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The development of 3-D miniature segmented monopole antennas is presented. Each segment is oriented randomly in space to reduce the volume occupied by the antenna while obtaining good characteristics: compactness, efficiency, impedance matching, and bandwidth. Its small size and broad bandwidth make it suitable for 5G systems. Because of the absence of any dielectric losses, a segmented wire antenna is a good alternative to planar antennas in particular when very high efficiency is required. A multi-objective genetic algorithm has been implemented to optimize the design. A 7-segments antenna that occupies a volume of A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/4.81 ×. A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/6.10 × A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/7.03, where A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength at 3.28 GHz, was obtained. Its impedance is fairly close to 50 ohms in all bandwidth (3.28-3.61) GHz, and the reflection coefficient is better than −12 dB. The radiation efficiency is higher than 95% for the entire C-band (3500–3600 GHz), and the polarization of the antenna is linear.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized LTCC Modular Phased Array Antenna at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) phased array antenna is proposed and demonstrated experimentally at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Ka}$</tex> -band of 27.5 GHz - 30.5 GHz. The proposed phased array antenna system consists of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> CP antenna elements with 16 Anokiwave ICs. For good CP performance, each <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 2$</tex> antenna subarray with one core chip is excited in a sequentially rotated manner. The beam can be steered electronically with a coverage of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> with gain of greater than 21 dBic across the frequency band of 27.5 -30.5 GHz.

articleTitle: High Gain and High Efficiency UHF Tag with Enhanced Complementary Spilt Ring Resonator Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A passive, high gain and high efficiency RFID tag antenna with two kinds of enhanced complementary spilt ring resonator (ECSRR) units is proposed in this paper. The tag is composed of a centered folded dipole and period-arrayed metamaterials bilaterally, which named top /bottom bad circle ECSRR (TBCSRR/BBCSRR) units. Simulated results show that the tag's working band is 908 MHz-927MHz. The return loss is 33.7dB, realized gain is 3.92dBi, the 3dB beam width is 184°, the total efficiency and power transmission coefficient are 82.4% and 0.9996, respectively, at the best resonance frequency of 916.7MHz. The maximum reading distance of the tag is 25.8m when the Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP) is 2W and 36.5m when it is 4W at 916.7MHz.

articleTitle: Toward improved prediction of RCS reduction bandwidth of checkerboard metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An existing semi-empirical expression for predicting the RCS reduction bandwidth of checkerboard metasurfaces (CMS) is examined. The bandwidth predicted by this equation, which is based on the unit cell reflection coefficient, is inconsistent with the simulated array bandwidth. By using two approaches, it is shown that the bandwidth prediction is improved considering the effect of mutual coupling. In approach (1), the mutual coupling coefficients are extracted using a discrete-port-based method and employed to update the unit cell reflection coefficient. The bandwidth predicted with the updated reflection parameters better matches the simulated array bandwidth. In approach (2), PEC baffles are introduced in the CMS to mitigate mutual coupling, resulting in a good match between unit cell reflection coefficient-based bandwidth and the array bandwidth.

articleTitle: Challenges in Development of Bended Passive UHF RFID Moisture Sensors on a Sponge Cloth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present fabrication and evaluation of embroidered passive UHF RFID moisture sensors on a bended sponge cloth. The sensors were firstly tested as flat, where moisture only affected the substrate properties, and as bended, where moisture also straightened the initially bended sensor tag. The sensor tags showed read ranges of 5 meters, and the flat sensors were found to be good indicators of moisture exposure. However, several challenges were encountered in sensor fabrication. Further, the main goals of the study, the bended sensors, showed very unstable performance. In this paper, we introduce the above-mentioned challenges.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Broadband Nonuniform Metasurface Antenna for 5G Terminal Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A low-profile broadband metasurface antenna using nonuniform unit cells is proposed for 5G communication systems. The nonuniform metasurface is formed by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> adjustable square patches and fed by an L-shaped coupling probe. By properly optimizing the dimensions of sub patches, four resonances are generated to cover the N77-79 frequency bands (3.3-5.0 GHz) with reflection coefficient of less than −6 dB and total efficiency of better than 70%. Meanwhile, the independent tuning characteristic of the four resonance modes is also analysed. The proposed nonuniform MS antenna has a low profile of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.028 \lambda_{0}\ \lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at the center frequency), which is promising to be applied to mobile devices.

articleTitle: Some Observed Outcomes of the Shape Synthesis of Dual-Band Transmitarray Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The shape synthesis of dual-band transmitarray elements is described. Example outcomes are discussed, and reasons why such shape synthesis might be desirable are given.

articleTitle: Embedding a priori information in inverse scattering problems using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Incorporating extra information in solving physical problems by deep learning can beneficially decrease the required time and data. In addition to the physics of the problem, spatial a priori information is also available for some inverse problems e.g. microwave imaging. Embedding this kind of information in the learning process can also be useful to speed up the training phase. It can also lead to more accurate results. Here, we suggest and compare three ideas to incorporate spatial a priori information in solving inverse scattering problem using deep learning approach. The results show that in all cases, training phase is accomplished faster and with better quality.

articleTitle: Improving the 5G Massive MIMO Performance for Aerial Base Stations by Exploiting Triangular Lattice Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The impact of the antenna array lattice on a 5G massive MIMO system has been addressed with a particular focus on aerial base stations. The investigation highlights as triangular lattice arrays allow improving significant performance metrics such as the Spectral Efficiency (SE) with respect to square ones in case of a multi users scenario, making them attractive in massive MIMO systems.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Wideband Monopole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, two 3D printed wideband monopole antennas are presented. The antennas are an elliptical monopole. First one is printed on Kapton and the second one is on 3D printed dielectric substrate. The silver conductive traces are printed using a reactive ink with conductivity close to bulk silver. Both antennas show ultra wideband performance and omnidirectional radiation patterns.

articleTitle: An Omnidirectional Vertical-Polarized C-V2X Antenna with High Gain and Low Profile
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel C-V2X (Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything) antenna with high omnidirectional gain and very low profile. The antenna is based on a two-layer structure with Rogers 5880 substrates. The first layer is a hollow circular patch with multiple sorting pins working as reflector. The second layer is a triangular patch with shorting points and a ring-shaped slot in the middle working as the main radiating patch. The gain of the antenna is over 4.5 dBi in all horizontal directions at the working frequency of 5.9 GHz, which is the standard frequency band for C-V2X antennas. Also, the antenna is vertical-polarized, so that horizontal noises can be avoid in practical use. The simulation results of the proposed antenna are presented to prove its capability.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band Dual-Antenna Building Block for 5G Mobile Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact dual-band dual-antenna building block is proposed in this paper for 5G mobile communication application. The building block consists of two miniature monopole antennas bridged by a meander line in the middle. The two monopole antennas are closely placed and arranged symmetrically in a mirror image. The meander line acts as a neutralization-line to effectively reduce the amount of coupling between the two close-placed antennas and optimize the isolation. Each antenna of the proposed building block is able to operate in two resonance frequency bands of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.2\sim 3.6$</tex> GHz and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.75\sim 5.0$</tex> GHz with reflection coefficient less than −6 dB, which can completely cover the 5G Sub-6GHz bands of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.3\sim 3.6$</tex> GHz and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.8\sim 5$</tex> GHz. In addition, the isolation between the two antennas of the building block is more than 10 dB in the operating frequency band. Moreover, as the antenna building block only occupies a single side of the handset frame, it has advantage of compact size and leaves more space and design freedom for mobile phone to accommodate more internal components.

articleTitle: University of Utah Hybrid-Flexible Education
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes methods we are using in ECE at the University of Utah to support a Hybrid Flexible (HyFlex) classes. Classes are offered both in person and online. We describe the teaching approach for two asynchronous online courses – Intro. to EM and Numerical EM and a synchronous freshman circuits course. We will also describe three hands-on take-home labs – Intro. to EM. Microwave Eng I, and Intro. to ECE (freshman circuits). Finally, we will report on an undergraduate research project on what students want in post-Covid education.

articleTitle: Two-way Passive Phased Array Antenna for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost and low-profile passive two-way phased array antenna (PAA), which can be used for simultaneous transmit and receive signals at two different frequencies. It consists of two linear interleaved patch array antenna, two power dividers, and two-way phase shifters as the beamforming network. The simulated results show that the proposed two-way PAA is capable of continuously steering the main beam directions from −30° to +30° in both receive and transmit paths, while its transmitted and received beams remain aligned.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Absorbent Frequency-Selective Radome Unit for Low-RCS Ka-Band Transmit and Receive Satellite Communication Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-performance absorbent frequency-selective radome (AFSR) unit cell is designed. Two types are proposed: one is metamaterial absorber (MA) upper layer which has an effect of low-frequency absorbing, and the other is bandpass FSS lower layer which can achieve high-efficiency wideband transmission and serve as the ground plane of the MA layer. The structure of the unit cell is highly parameterized to be applied to different frequency bands (Ka-band transmitting and receiving here). Simulated results indicate that it can possess a remarkable absorbing range from 6.2 GHz to 17.4 GHz (relative bandwidth 95%) and 9.5GHz to 25GHz (relative bandwidth 90%), while the passband center frequencies are 19 GHz and 29 GHz with low insertion loss at receiving and transmitting status of antenna individually.

articleTitle: Low-cost antenna architectures with control of the local environment for 5G and beyond 5G
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we discuss the use of a local controllable environment (LCE) for the terminals of massive MIMO systems, and we show that the use of this technique allows improving the performance of the systems, allowing to communicate with a larger number of terminals.

articleTitle: Comparison of electromagnetic force densities evaluated in the electrodynamic lattice-Boltzmann method and finite-difference time-domain method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Centered-difference electromagnetic force densities are challenging to implement in the finite-difference time-domain method. Since the Yee-lattice electric and magnetic field components are offset by half unit-cells and time-steps, local averaging is required which can introduce numerical error. The alternative electrodynamic lattice-Boltzmann method can solve time-domain electric and magnetic fields of greater accuracy on a single lattice, which also simplifies its implementation. This letter extends the electrodynamic lattice-Boltzmann method to the evaluation of centered-difference electromagnetic force densities, and compares these time-averaged force densities with those evaluated by the finite-difference-time-domain method.

articleTitle: Small Footprint Triangular Shaped HF band NVIS Antenna based on Noise related Parametric Studies
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A low-profile triangular shaped HF band receive antenna is optimized for a long-distance communication system for Near-Vertical Incidence Skywave propagation. Currently, antennas that are used for this purpose are generally half-loop profiles that require bigger surface area. An alternative shaped antenna is optimized that is easy to be fixed on the vehicle with similar noise related performance. The antenna is validated by comparing the measured ambient noise with the reference curves.

articleTitle: Compound GRIN Lens Fanbeam Antenna for Wide-angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A Ka-band fanbeam GRIN lens antenna using two GRIN lenses for enhanced beamscan is proposed and validated in full-wave simulation. Over the band of interest, the two-lens system achieves an average maximum scan loss of 2 dB for a 100° field-of-view corresponding to a scan loss envelope of cos<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(θ). The total on-axis depth of the system is reduced by > 50% by incorporating a 90° bend in the parallel plate waveguide.

articleTitle: A Broadband High-Efficiency Electromagnetic Wave Mode Excitation for Terahertz Waveguide Using Tightly Coupled Stub-lines
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In Terahertz (THz) band, the insertion loss of interconnection between waveguide and other transmission lines is high and the micro-assembly process is complex. In this paper, a novel broadband high-efficiency electromagnetic wave mode excitation for THz waveguide is presented. The excitation combines an array of tightly coupled stub-lines. The tightly coupled stub-lines are fed by grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) and show multiple resonance modes which are similar to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode used to excite waveguide transmission mode. The tightly coupled stub-lines have multiple resonance modes and thus wideband waveguide excitation would be realized. The main excitation structure is embedded between waveguide and the GCPW bottom grounded side in order to reduce radiation losses. The excitation has advantages of high efficiency, easy fabrication and wideband performance. A 0.2 THz interconnection from GCPW to rectangular waveguide is designed as an example with 22% bandwidth of 15 dB return loss and 0.4 dB insertion loss.

articleTitle: Compact Ferromagnetic WGM Resonator for Sensing Applications at Sub-Centimeter Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact microwave resonator that excites the travelling-waves Whispering-Gallery-Modes (WGM) on a ferrite ring when coupled to a microstrip-line at a definite distance. A permanent magnet is installed beneath the substrate to activate the non-reciprocal effect of the ferrite, and thus acquire two resonances for the clockwise and counter-clockwise WGM modes. The proposed device is compact, planar, low-profile, and non-reciprocal. Besides, it is an open structure and of high-quality factor which make it a good fit for many sensing applications. The sensor performance in both reciprocal and non-reciprocal modes is practically demonstrated through the in-lab measurements in the frequency range 22 - 32 GHz using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) setup.

articleTitle: Collapsible, Wideband, Dual-polarization Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual polarization, collapsible patch antenna was designed and developed to reduce the stored volume. The antenna has a top square patch, two sets of differential series-resonant flexible vertical feeds, a microstrip balun and a ground plane. The antenna can be collapsed to reduce the height from about 30mm to about 3mm. The achieved bandwidth is about 40% with gain around 7 to 9dBi.

articleTitle: High-Aperture-Efficiency and Short-Longitudinal Length $2\times 2$ Square Horn Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a high gain horn antenna with high aperture efficiency. The proposed horn consists of a waveguide coaxial adapter, 1-to-4 rectangular waveguide feed network, and 4 square horn units. This square horn unit is composed of five discontinuous sections, which can form a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 \lambda\times 3\lambda \lambda$</tex> is the wavelength at 3.0 GHz) uniform electric field distribution on the final rectangular horn face with basically same phase characteristics. Finally, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> array, which is fed by 1-to-4 network, forms an aperture size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6 \lambda\times 6 \lambda$</tex>. The optimized horn is fabricated and tested, and the measured results agree very well with the simulated results. At 3.0 GHz, the aperture efficiency is improved to 97.4% and this horn can generate good radiation patterns with nearly equal 3-dB beamwidth in both H- and E-planes.

articleTitle: A NFFF approach using spheroidal wave functions in a cylindrical scanning geometry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We develop a Near-field/Far-Field technique to characterize oblong shaped antennas using data acquired in a cylindrical scanning geometry. The approach is based on enclosing the Antenna Under Test in a prolate spheroid and on representing the field on the spheroidal surface using Prolate Spheroidal Wave Functions. We set up an inverse problem to recover the representation coefficients from the measured data through a Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based inversion of the operator linking the field on the spheroid to the field on the cylinder. The approach significantly reduces the number of needed expansion coefficients as compared, for example, to a spherical harmonics expansion, positively affecting the problem conditioning. Numerical results are shown.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Computation of the Spontaneous Emission Rate of a Transmon Qubit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Understanding the spontaneous emission rate of transmon qubits is an important step in the design of many quantum electromagnetic devices, such as single photon sources and quantum computers. Despite its importance, the spontaneous emission rate is often determined using approximate circuit models or is inferred from measurements on a fabricated device. To improve the accuracy of predictions, it is better to use full-wave numerical methods for this problem. In this work, we show how this can be done with a recently developed field-based description of transmon qubits coupled to an electromagnetic environment. We demonstrate this process by computing the spontaneous emission rate of a single photon source and find qualitative agreement with a similar fabricated device.

articleTitle: Beam Steerable Leaky Wave Antenna using FPMS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Leaky wave antenna (LWA) with beam steering capability achieved by controlling substrate permittivity using Field Programable Microwave Substrate (FPMS). The planar antenna consists of grounded dielectric slab (GDS), surface wave launcher (SWL) and FPMS unit cells. The leaky wave radiations are produced by interaction of surface waves and metallic strips which are mounted on surface of the substrate. The FPMS unit cell has the ability to change the substrate permittivity in a range of frequencies thus enabling maximum steering of 17° at 10 GHz. The antenna occupies 101 × 20 mm2 with a −10dB bandwidth of 0.4 GHz.

articleTitle: A 3D Dual-band Electrically Small Monopole Antenna for Internet of Sea Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Sensing and retrieving data from ocean to land are challenging and expensive tasks, while the Internet of Sea (IoS) concept can help to monitor ocean environment in a low-cost way. In this paper, an Electrically Small (ES) dual-band monopole antenna is proposed for the IoS application. Dual-band operation (GSM-900, LoRa, and BLE bands) and vertical polarization are maintained in a very compact size. The proposed antenna operates as a folded monopole antenna at 900MHz, and as a simple monopole antenna at 2.4 GHz, by combining the top-loaded folded monopole antenna and the 2-layer monopole feeding structure. The proposed antenna has ka of 0.45 at the LB, with a decent polarization purity and radiation efficiency of 54%. The proposed antenna is designed with a low-cost additive manufacturing material system.

articleTitle: High Gain Waveguide Tilted Slot Antenna for Millimeter Wave application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband and high gain waveguide slot antenna at 26 GHz for millimeter wave beamforming. As millimeter wave beamforming network requires a high bandwidth and high gain to cover the demands of traffic and users increasing for current millimeter wave and 5G technology. Waveguide slot antenna has the capability of providing high gain and power handling capability. Thus, in this work the bandwidth is increased by tilting the slot orientation that implemented on the broad wall and narrow wall of the waveguide and produces a dual beam in different directions. The proposed antenna has a six slots distributed on the top and narrow wall of the waveguide structure and tilts by 10°. The performance of the proposed waveguide slot antenna is analysed using CST software. A good reflection coefficient of −27 dB and a bandwidth of 2 GHz are obtained. The simulated gain of 13.7 dB and 6.95 dB are recorded at broad and narrow wall with a low slidelobes levels of −13 dB. Thus, the proposed antenna is a good candidate for millimeter wave beamforming applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Series Array for Intelligent Transportation System in C-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a compact antenna printed on a commercial substrate and optimized for obtaining the maximum gain in the radio channels assigned to the Intelligent Transportation System, with particular emphasis on the central frequency of 5.8 GHz. The design of the antenna is based on the concepet of series-fed array, applied to a modified rectangular patch. Measurements confirm simulations results, with a maximum gain of 9.4 dB at 5.8 GHz and 4 dB at 5.9 GHz, as well as a reasonable gain from 5.2 GHz to 6.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Coexistence-Mode Composite Right/Left-Handed Transmission Line and Its Application for Folded C-Type SIW Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In order to meet the widespread application of the large-scale integrated circuits in the future and reduce the size of the multibeam array antenna. The miniaturized beamforming network (BFN) is the key to solving the large size of the multibeam array antenna. In this paper, a novel transmission line technology based on the coexistence mode composite right/left-handed (Comode CRLH) folded C-type substrate integrated waveguide (FCSIW) is presented. The interdigital slot (IDS) is introduced into the traditional FCSIW transmission line to realize the dynamic control of the folded TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode and the folded TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</inf> mode. By increasing the difference between the two modes of the phase constants, the miniaturized directional coupler and the miniaturized cross coupler can be realized. Finally, the Co-mode CRLH <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 \times 4$</tex> FCSIW butler matrix (BM) is obtained. Compared with the traditional FCSIW counterparts, the longitudinal size of the proposed BM is reduced by 30.7%.

Author Keywords: coexistence mode composite rightl left-handed (Co-mode CRLH)

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Band-Gap Leaky-Wave Antennas Based on Grounded Dielectric Lattices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of an Electromagnetic Band-Gap (EBG) leaky-wave antenna consisting of a two-dimensional lattice of dielectric cylinders above a ground plane. The radiation from an electric line source embedded in the EBG open waveguide is modeled by means of suitably excited leaky modes. An in-depth dispersive analysis has showed how a multiplicity of modes, both guided and leaky, propagates within the structure. However, by properly placing an elementary source within the lattice, a single leaky mode of the EBG structure has shown to provide a highly convergent representation of the radiated far field. Based on the knowledge of the leaky-mode attenuation constant, it is possible to truncate the structure longitudinally in order to obtain a radiation efficiency of 96 %. This study led to the design of an antenna operating at a frequency belonging to the 5G millimeter-wave bands. Excellent agreements have been obtained between the theoretical results based on leaky-wave radiation and ad-hoc and full-wave commercial simulators.

articleTitle: Extended GHI-LFM Algorithm for Sparse Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The recently proposed method for general holographic inversion with linear frequency modulation radar (GHI-LFM) for millimeter wave imaging (MMWI) is further extended to sparse array systems through the use of phase center error compensation. Synthetic imaging results demonstrate good imaging performance and high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Yagi-Uda Array of Bond Wire Antennas with High Front-to-Back Ratio
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Yagi-Uda array of bond wire antennas (BWAs) with high front-to-end (F/B) ratio. The proposed antenna array achieves a F/B ratio of more than 40 dB by utilizing bond wires as the reflectors and the directors. Meanwhile, a higher gain can be obtained by this means. Good consistency is observed between the simulation and the measurement. According to the measured results, the 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna array is from 56.7 GHz to 62.2 GHz (9.3%), and the maximum gain is 13.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Accurate Closed-Form Expressions for Maximum Radiated Power and Surface Wave Loss of Printed Antennas on a Thick Substrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A new approximation of the Green's function of a grounded dielectric slab is found to calculate analytically the radiated space wave power of a printed antenna element operating in a regime of maximum radiated power. A simplified expression for the surface wave propagation constant is also obtained. The calculated antenna efficiency is within ∼ 1% of the exact numerical value, independent of substrate permittivity.

articleTitle: Optimizing Rotmen Lens Topologies for 5G Wireless Grids
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of high-gain, orientation-agnostic systems capable of efficiently capturing the high transmitted EIRPs by the 5G base stations is key to enabling the 5G infrastructure as a Wireless Power Grid (WPG). In this effort, the authors present a framework for the design of fully-printed, planar, and highly-customizable mm-wave Rotman-lens-based rectennas. A scalability study evaluates the performance of the lens with different numbers of antenna and beam ports, resulting in a successful architecture offering a combination of high gain and wide angular coverage. A structure, involving eight antenna ports and six beam ports, was then inkjet-printed on a thin, flexible substrate and its S-parameters were measured. This structure, breaking the trade-off between high gain and large angular coverage, is at the core of the realization of Rotman lens-based mm-wave rectenna and backscattering mmID tags for the 5G WPG.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Circular Patch
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a narrowband single-fed polarization reconfigurable microstrip antenna at S-band. The antenna is composed of a circular patch that is connected to a reconfigurable feeding network placed underneath it through vias. The feeding network is composed of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{90^{\circ}}$</tex> hybrid coupler connected to a single pole double throw (SPDT) absorptive RF switch. The antenna is able to change between left-hand and right-hand polarization states according to the switch condition. A prototype model is fabricated and tested where the simulated data agree with the measured ones. The acquired radiating characteristics show the antenna to perform with a reflection coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{ < -15\text{dB}}$</tex>, realized gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{> 4\text{dBic}}$</tex>, and an axial ratio of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{< 0.3\text{dB}}$</tex> at the center frequency. The antenna forms a stack topology reducing its overall size to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\pi\ \mathrm{x}\ 25^{2}\text{mm}^{2}}$</tex> for compact communication systems.

articleTitle: Designing Reflective Metasurfaces by Exploiting Composite Vortex Theory
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The aim of this contribution is to exploit composite vortex theory to manipulate the beam reflected by a single metasurface. In particular, by structuring the metasurface for reflecting both a vortex and a vortex-free component, its scattering pattern can be tailored according to the amplitude and phase of the two components. Full-wave numerical simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach, which could find applications for beam-shaping at different frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Maximized SNR against RCS from Overrepresented MIMO Virtual Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents experimental verification and results for a novel process of creating an optimized virtual array for a Multi-Input, Multi-Output (MIMO) antenna array. MIMO radars utilize the concept of a virtual array to increased range and angular resolution as compared to non-MIMO phased array radars. There exist certain linear phased array antenna geometries where the MIMO virtual array can become overrepresented. Generation of an optimized MIMO antenna virtual array can be accomplished using full virtualization, the process of creating separate virtual arrays. Experimental results are shown to match with the theoretical prediction of SNR improvement.

articleTitle: Dual-band Shared-aperture Microstrip Antenna Array for 4G/5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-band shared-aperture microstrip antenna array is proposed for 4G and 5G communication systems. In the proposed array, two lower band units are diagonally placed in the center while six upper band units are closely integrated side-by-side around them in the same plane. Both lower and upper band units achieve the wide bandwidth by using a gridded-slotted radiating patch, covering 2.32-2.73 GHz and 3.3-4.3 GHz respectively with reflection coefficient less than -10 dB. A three-layer structure is introduced to reach a low profile of 0.088 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}, \lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength of the lowest frequency of the lower band. Isolations between different ports are better than -13 dB. The proposed design is presented in this paper with numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: A Symmetrically Stacked Phased Array Exhibiting Enhanced Spherical Coverage CDF for mmWave Cellular Handsets with Metallic Frame
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a symmetrically stacked planar phased-array (SSPA) concept to fundamentally improve the spherical coverage CDF of millimeter-wave cellular handsets featuring full metallic frames. The proposed SSPA achieves three independent main beam directions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm z- \text{axes} /+x-\text{axis}$</tex>) by adjusting the input weighting matrix of the SSPA. It has been experimentally verified that the proposed SSPA concept significantly improve the spherical coverage CDF of the present-day cellular device without structural deformation of the metallic frame. The measurement results confirm that the proof-of-concept model achieves a maximum beamsteering angles of ±43° (peak gain: 8.4 dBi) in the broadside modes and ±33° (peak gain: 5.1 dBi) in the endfire mode. The use of SSPA modules improve the spherical coverage CDF more than 5 dB at the 25th percentile compared to the reference model.

articleTitle: Terahertz Signal Generation Measurements in Photoconductive Antennas using Time Domain Spectroscopy System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the signal generation measurements of LT-GaAs photoconductive antenna (PCA) emitters. These measurements were developed in an open-bench time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) system. The main challenges presented here are associated with the alignment of the PCA devices and the location of the terahertz (THz) pulse with respect to the optical delay in the system. The position of the slow delay line was crucial for the location of the THz pulse, which helped in the correct alignment process of the emitter and detector devices.

articleTitle: Tolerance Analysis of Spherical Conformal Array Antenna based on Interval Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel interval analysis (IA) method for manufacturing tolerances of spherical conformal antenna arrays (CAAs) based on interval arithmetic is proposed. The uncertain factors in patch antenna manufacturing are described as interval variables. Interval arithmetic is used to establish an interval analysis model of the influence of uncertain factors on the electrical performance of a CAA, and interval analysis is carried out to study the influence of radius intervals on the power pattern intervals of the CAA. Comparisons between the results of the IA method and those of the Monte Carlo method verify the effectiveness of the proposed IA method.

articleTitle: Distributed Amplitude Weighting and System Noise Figure in Active Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an active phased array antenna, beam-forming network, multichannel receiver to implement distributed amplitude weighting, and signal amplification are explained. A three-stage distribution circular Taylor amplitude weighting is applied to achieve lower antenna sidelobes, i.e., T/R module, active RF manifold, and at digital IQ data. Distributed amplitude weighting and its effects on the overall active antenna noise figure is analyzed. This paper's proposed scheme results in significant improvement in the active antenna noise figure and enhances the radar system performance in detecting week echo signal in clutter and jamming environment.

articleTitle: Reference solutions for thin-wire MoM codes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The thin-wire MoM formulation as presented in most textbooks does not rigorously handle the singularity present in the formulation. Recently, a number of reseachers have advanced methods to correctly include the singularlity in the self-term. This paper discusses the improved results which can be obtained, and outlines how they could assist in reference solutions for benchmarking MoM codes.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Polarized Dual-Band and Wideband Multi-Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by Two L-Probes with a Cavity Structure for Stable Gain Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized dual-band and wideband multi-ring microstrip antenna (MR-MSA) fed by two L-probes with a cavity structure. The proposed antenna consists of two circular ring patches arranged at the top and middle layers of a triple-layered dielectric substrate and two L-probe placed orthogonally in the bottom layer with a large thickness for dual-polarized dual-band and wideband operation. In order to obtain stable gain characteristics against finite sizes of the dielectric substrate and the ground plane, a cavity structure which is composed of a square ring patch on the top layer and several vias connecting to the ground plane is introduced surrounding the radiating patches. The cavity structure is designed in a small size without affecting the dual-band and wideband performance of the MR-MSA by using the numerical simulation with ANSYS HFSS. The design frequencies of the MR-MSA are around 3.5 GHz and 4.75 GHz. The simulated results reveal that dual-band and wideband performance of 26% and 23% fractional bandwidths less than −10 dB reflection is observed. It is also confirmed by the simulation that stable gain characteristics against sizes of the substrate and the ground plane of the designed MR-MSA with the cavity structure are obtained in comparison with the same MR-MSA without the cavity structure.

articleTitle: Wideband, X-band Series-Fed Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband, series-fed patch array operating at x-band was designed, fabricated and tested. The antenna is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 6$</tex> array of wideband microstrip patches, feed by an optimized series-fed network. The measured sectoral beam provides realized gain greater than 10 dB at ±2.5 degrees in narrow plane and ±10 degrees in wide plane from 9 to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: A Tunable Wearable Band Reject Sensor for Enhanced Glucose Monitoring Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a non-invasive glucose-monitoring sensor that is based on a tunable band reject filter. The filter topology comprises a feeding network at a top layer that excites eight open loop resonators embedded in the ground plane. The shape of the resonators is inspired by the vasculature anatomy of a human arm. The embedded resonators are designed to resonate at 8 different frequencies in order to track the variations of the glucose level across the 1.5 GHz - 2.4 GHz frequency span. Furthermore, the filter's frequency operation is also tuned by relying on integrated varactors in order to enhance the sensor's dynamic responsiveness to glucose variations. The proposed tunable filter is fabricated and tested on diabetic rats, and in a clinical setting. A high correlation between the scattering parameters of the proposed sensor and the variations in glucose levels is noted. A Gaussian Process regression model is also developed using data obtained from experiments. Results demonstrate that the proposed sensor detects glucose variation with an accuracy that reaches 98.55% well within clinically acceptable performance.

articleTitle: Design of a Shape Optimized Printed-circuit Beamformer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the experimental realization of a printed-circuit beamformer designed using shape optimization. Shape optimization of the printed-circuit beamformer is enabled through the use of a circuit network solver that utilizes reduced-order models of printed-circuit unit cells to rapidly evaluate device responses, and the adjoint variable method to evaluate gradients. The designed beamformer is patterned on a microwave substrate and interfaces with a 3-D printed tapered aperture antenna. It produces nine orthogonal beams and has isolated input ports that are impedance matched. Experimental results for the performance of the 3-D printed antenna and the beamformer will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: A Novel Partially Reflective Layer for Improving the Performance of X-Band Printed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel partially reflective layer (PRL) for improving the impedance and the 3-dB gain bandwidths of a printed antenna operating in X-band. The proposed PRL is constructed by two arrays of two different partially reflective unit-cells (PRUCs) arranged on both faces of the same substrate. The PRL is used as a superstrate over a dual-layer printed antenna. Broader impedance and 3-dB gain bandwidths of about 39.25 % and 41.13% are achieved. Thus, the designed single-layer PRL is very useful for boosting the 3-dB gain and the impedance bandwidths of X-band printed antennas.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Cloak Using Phase Gradient Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new electromagnetic (EM) invisibility cloak is proposed utilizing phase gradient metasurfaces. The metasurfaces with high transmission efficiency are first design based on the generalized Snell's law and then verified by the phenomenon of abnormal refraction. By the proper arrangement of the metasurfaces, a transmissive invisibility cloak is constructed to guide the EM wave to travel round the cloaked rhombic region. The plane-wave illumination is applied in simulations and the result validates this new method.

articleTitle: On the Effect of Design Parameters on Fringing Fields of a Loop-Based FSS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) are periodic arrays of conductive elements that act as spatial filters of electromagnetic energy. FSSs have found recent application as sensors, filters, reflectors and radomes, amongst others. Often miniaturization techniques are used to improve the stability of the FSS to incident angle (of the excitation). However, due to the type of coupling (internal/self vs. external/mutual with adjacent elements), some designs are more responsive to miniaturization techniques than others. Hence, this paper quantifies the effect of the ratios of inter-element spacing-to-substrate thickness (S/h) and side length-to-substrate thickness (SL/h) on fringing fields (and hence coupling and potential for miniaturization) of a loop-based FSS. To do this, the effective perimeter and electrical periodicity of the loop (resulting from fringing fields) is calculated based on the effective permittivity of the substrate and the resonant frequency for various substrate thicknesses. The results indicate that external coupling (with adjacent elements) dominates when S/h is less than SL/h and hence such designs are more receptive to miniaturization techniques.

articleTitle: Some Numerical Experiments on Enhanced-Directivity Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The broadside directivity achievable by a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) located on a conducting groundplane is investigated using a shape synthesis process.

articleTitle: Compact Coaxial Waveguide-Based Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Most waveguide antennas use hollow waveguide with arrays of slot elements, offering a simple and highly efficient structure. Coaxial waveguide allows a smaller cross-section, and using just one element, or two co-located elements, leads to a compact antenna. We present new, dual- and single-slot designs based on coaxial waveguide that are compact and wideband. The designs include a coaxial feed, and are fabricated and measured to verify their performance.

articleTitle: Study of Different Canonical UHF Antennas Integrated in the Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the study of different canonical radiating structures integrated in a vehicle's body. Dipole, wire patch and loop structure are studied at 800 and 2000 MHz for mobile communication application. EM simulation shows that wire patch antenna provides the best coverage for cellular communication.

articleTitle: Investigating Dielectric Covers to Reduce Unwanted Lobes in Near-Field Meta-Steering Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A diligent full wave analysis is performed to investi-gate the potential of dielectric covers in suppressing the undesired lobes in a Near-field Meta-Steering system. The phase-gradient metasurfaces with dielectric covers show lower side-lobe levels in the predicted 2D far-field patterns.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized MIMO Microstrip Patch Antenna Array with EBG- and Slot-Loading
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact four-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna array based on the miniaturized mi-crostrip patch is presented. The reduction in array form factor is realized by partially populating the ground plane with elec-tromagnetic band gap (EBG) cells constructed from cross slots, in combination with reactively loading each patch with a slot. The resultant 2 × 2 array system demonstrates excellent inter-element isolation and can be easily fabricated using traditional milling and printing techniques, as it exploits a 2D layout that can be conveniently implemented on two sides of a single-layer substrate, without the need for any via structures. The operation of the array near the 2.5 GHz band is verified with full-wave simulations. The size of the new design is approximately 42% of that employing conventional patch elements.

articleTitle: Compact Polarization Transformation in a Geodesic Luneburg Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a compact polarizer that rotates the linear polarization of a fully metallic geodesic Luneburg lens antenna for applications requiring polarization diversity. The polarization rotation is achieved by loading the radiating aperture of the antenna with two metallic screens. The integrated antenna operates in the K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band, from 25 to 31 GHz, showing around 20% bandwidth with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> below −10 dB, and a scanning range of 100°.

articleTitle: A Low Frequency Device for Non-invasive Detection of Pulmonary Malignancies
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of an innovative, non-invasive radio-frequency system for the detection and the diagnosis of malign lung lymph nodes (LNs) is presented. First, we introduce the theorical concept behind the proposed methodology and the relative hardware system design; then, we perform accurate full-wave simulations aiming to assess the procedure feasibility. The obtained numerical results demonstrate the possibility to correctly detect malign lymph nodes inside pulmonary tissues and, thus, to overcome the current invasive techniques such as biopsy. These observations suggest the feasibility for an innovative near-field clinical device, to be employed in future for non-invasive detection and monitoring of lung conditions, encouraging further analysis.

articleTitle: Compact Filtering Planar Inverted-F Antenna With Two Radiation Nulls
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact filtering planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) with two radiation nulls is presented. Firstly, a PIFA is designed at the center frequency of 2.5 GHz.
