The conventional PIFA has a gradual frequency response. Then, a coupling quarter-wavelength resonator is designed to create one radiation null at the lower frequency band. At last, a defected microstrip structure resonator is applied to create the other radiation null at the upper frequency band. The simulated two radiation nulls are located at 1.44 GHz and 3.92 GHz, while the measured two radiation nulls are located at 1.37 GHz and 3.92 GHz. The created two radiation nulls can improve the frequency selectivity greatly. Moreover, the effects of two radiation nulls on the radiation band are very small. Measured and simulated results agree well.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of a SIW-Reconfigurable Antenna With Improved performance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based reconfigurable slot antenna is presented. The structure is initially implemented to use of SIW cavity with two shorting pins. These two shorting pins played a key role in obtaining better impedance matching. At the same time, to vary with co-axial feed with the help of stepper motor and Arduino Uno micro-controller is achieved the frequency reconfigurable. The measured bandwidth of 2.15%, the maximum gain of 9.79 dBi, and radiation efficiency of 87.25% are achieved. The antenna is fabricated and tested. The measured results are matched with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A novel Non-orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing scheme for interference avoidance in SM-STBC Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Generalized frequency division multiplexing (GFDM) is a primary nonorthogonal multicarrier waveform candidate for beyond fifth generation. Due to its attractive properties, it fulfills the requirements of the scenarios such as Internet of Things (IoT). On the other hand, spatial modulation (SM) is regarded as a key promising technology for 5G and beyond wireless networks. Its robustness against multipath fading environments can be increased by space-time block coding (STBC) at the transmitter when the receiver complexity should be kept minimal. In this paper, we propose a new solution merging the viable advantages of GFDM and SM-STBC and evaluate its bit error rate performance (BER) against spatial modulation - orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (SM-OFDM) in frequency selective channels.

articleTitle: Conformal Perfectly Matched Layer for Matrix-Free Time-Domain Method in Unstructured Meshes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Arbitrarily shaped conformal perfectly matched layer (PML) has been a numerical challenge especially in unstructured meshes. In this paper, we develop an algorithm to realize conformal PML in the Matrix-Free Time-Domain (MFTD) method. The algorithm allows for the implementation of PML in unstructured meshes with the same ease as that in a regular grid. Numerical experiments have validated its accuracy.

articleTitle: High-efficiency Reflectarray Using Dielectric Resonator Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dielectric resonator-based unit-cell is used to design a reflectarray antenna with improved efficiency. The unit-cell is a dielectric structure composed of a cylindrical element placed on a squared base having a ground plane at the bottom. The diameter of the cylinder is the parameter chosen for controlling the phase of the reflection coefficient. To verify its effectiveness, the proposed cell is employed to design a Ka-band offset reflectarray consisting in 52 × 52 elements. Simulated results show that the antenna is able to achieve a maximum gain of 32.3 dBi at 30 GHz, corresponding to an aperture efficiency of 55%.

articleTitle: Novel Offset Complementary Split Ring Resonators on Narrow-wall of Waveguides for HPM Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel offset Metamaterial-based complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) and its characteristic behavior on the narrow wall of a rectangular waveguide is considered, for the advancement and implementation of high-power microwave (HPM) antennas, operable at L-Band along with other potential frequencies. The architecture improves the properties of traditional slots and split ring resonators (SRRs) mounted on the narrow wall of selected waveguides (radius= 24mm, thickness=3.5mm, chord=0.8., offset=2.7mm)., with their designated frequency regimes. The inter-spacing and offset tuning of the array elements have core effects on mechanical strength, coupling, phase, radiation efficiency, as well negative index properties. The design supports high tunability for adaptation on other architectures, as well as decent phase consistency with THz prospects.

articleTitle: Effect of Circular Polarization in a UHF LP-WAN communication
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, the performances of different antenna polarization, including linear and circular, in a Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN) scenario is studied experimentally. The Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) 868MHz unlicensed band is targeted with LoRa modulation. The terminals used for test are compact and representative of industry like devices for Internet of Things (IoT) usage. A measurement protocol with 3 devices, each one using a different polarization, was set to study multiple scenario and communication channels. The gateway is using a 6dBi dipole antenna with vertical polarization. After analysis we can see that Circular Polarization on end-device offer a better robustness than linear polarization for indoor communication. For outdoor environment, vertical polarization provide the better performance.

articleTitle: Mobile Apps, Online Assessments and Examination for Electromagnetics Education
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the enhanced electromagnetics (EM) education using mobile apps that incorporate innovative computational electromagnetics (CEM) methods. The key features of CEM methods well-suited for educational mobile apps are highlighted, including small computing resources, real-time interactive, user-configurable and fast-forwardable simulations. These features can be realized using efficient multiple one-dimensional (M1-D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, innovative models and unconditionally stable fundamental implicit FDTD schemes involving concise, simple and efficient update equations with matrix-operator-free right-hand sides. Besides teaching and learning, thorough online assessments and examination are discussed with EM question setting including intermediate workings of vector operations, integration, etc.

articleTitle: Pixel-based Inversion of Induction Logging Data in Anisotropic Media with Supervised Descent Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a pixel-based inversion scheme with supervised descent method (SDM) for the inversion of induction logging responses in anisotropic formations. The scheme divides the unknown formation into small pixel units, and inverts the electrical property of each unit by pre-training the descent directions according to the prior knowledge. Therefore, the inversion has flexible generalization ability and can effectively avoid the interference of initial value and local minimum. Besides, several measures are adopted to improve the inversion performance of SDM and obtain more stable predictions. Some examples are also given to indicate that the proposed inversion method has good inversion performance and flexible generalization ability.

articleTitle: Nonuniform Metasurfaces for Gain Enhancement of Dual and Circularly Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Partially Reflective Surfaces (PRS) are highly reflective metasurfaces that are well-suited in design of antennas for beamforming and high gain applications. Periodic PRS, made of uniformly spaced elements, has limitations in optimal design of the antenna, particularly in trade-off between gain and sidelobe level, and/or in achieving a prescribed shaped-beam pattern. In this work, we investigate PRS structures made of non-uniformly spaced inclusions tailored after Grid-Graph Hamiltonian Cycles that, when globally optimized, provide various antenna functionalities including dual and circular polarizations with high gain and significantly reduced sidelobe levels. Examples for both optimized uniform and nonuniform PRS arrays are presented.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circular Patch Antenna Excited in the Broadside $\text{TM}_{12}$ Mode
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The predominance of the sidelobes in the antenna patterns, polarization impurity and the requisite of larger physical dimensions has inhibited the exploration of the wideband capability of the higher order broadside modes. Overcoming all these constraints, in this paper, a novel circular microstrip patch antenna excited in the broadside TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> mode with a 45% impedance bandwidth is presented. The superiority of the proposed antenna is that its radius is on par with that of the antenna excited in the dominant TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode and more importantly the realized radiation patterns are stable and free from sidelobes.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Planar Antenna with AMC Screen for On-Body Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band planar meander line antenna with an AMC screen for on-body applications. The antenna is aimed to operate at 0.86 and 2.4 GHz. The AMC screen is used to mitigate the effect of the human body into the antenna performance, so it has been designed to work appropriately in the two bands. Simulations of the AMC unit cell and the integration with the meander line antenna will be shown.

articleTitle: Integrated Multi-Standard MIMO Antennas for 5G n-RNA Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An integrated multi-standard slot-based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is proposed in this work. The design is suitable for 5G new radio access networks (n-RNA) applications. It comprises of 2-elements frequency reconfigurable (FR) and 2-elements ultra-wide-band (UWB) MIMO antenna developed on the same substrate. The dual-band FR antenna covers the frequency bands from 1.36-3.19 and 3.6-5.6 GHz while UWB operates over a frequency bands from 1.27-4.415 GHz. Continuous frequency sweep is achieved over both bands using a single varactor diode. The multi-functional antenna design that operates independently as a FR MIMO antenna, an UWB MIMO antenna as well as an integrated front-end solution covered several standard. It is a compact antenna design with total substrate dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{120\times 60}mm^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Technique for Efficiency Evaluation of Vertical Monopoles over Imperfect Earth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The use of short vertical monopoles with imperfect ground radial systems has become more common at medium and low frequencies as property area for such systems has become more valuable. A simple and straightforward method for evaluation of the efficiency effects of such restricted size systems is described.

articleTitle: Study of Time-Domain Characteristics for Liver-Implant Ultrawideband Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Recently, the use of wireless implantable devices has gained attraction in the medical field for its promising novel applications which open new opportunities for medical treatments and preventions. Ultrawideband (UWB) communication system is a potential candidate to be implemented on wireless implanted devices thanks to their high-speed transmission, low power consumption, and small size. Nevertheless, the design of UWB in-body communication system is challenging and there are still various concerns that should addressed before actual implementation. This paper presented an initial investigation of time-domain channel characteristics for liver implant via simulations. The results presented that data transmission for liver-implant communications can reach several hundreds of Mbps for the distance up to 95 mm approximately suggesting viable high-speed in-body communications performance.

articleTitle: A Dual Circularly Polarized Antenna Array With Compact Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual circularly polarized antenna array with a compact feeding network is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. The antenna element consists of four sequentially rotated patches fed by a high-order mode cavity to reduce the dielectric loss in the feeding network. Right-hand circular polarization(RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization(LHCP) are achieved by adopting a coupler and a phase shifter between the two input ports. The measured and simulated results agree well, showing its good performance of high gain and wide impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Regenerative RF Sensing System for Detection of Weak Electromagnetic Radiation from Biofilms
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Emission of electromagnetic (EM) waves from biological cells as a means of communication has recently been postulated. Detection of such signals requires a very sensitive receiver. In this paper, we present a novel regenerative sensing system for detection of very weak RF radiation from biofilms (communities of microorganisms). The system uses the concept of regeneration (also known as positive feedback) for the amplification of a signal with a known frequency band. Two identical antennas are arranged facing each other with a sample holder in between to form a closed loop structure. A tunable amplification circuit and a phase shifter are used to control the amplitude and phase of the loop respectively, so that the positive feedback criteria for a stable loop are satisfied at desired frequencies. This system achieves significant enhancement of weak signals, thus is a powerful tool for the investigation of the existence of EM signaling among biological cells. Furthermore, it has the capability of injecting external signals to actively interact with the biological cells, which is useful for exploring the effects of EM waves on biofilm development.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Multilayer Lens Antenna for Circularly Polarized Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multilayer lens structure constructed from a unit cell that is capable of simultaneously increasing the gain of feeding antenna and maintaining the circular polarizationn (CP) of the incoming wave as it can keep the 90 degree phase difference between two modes of the incoming CP wave and does not weaken the amplitude of the modes. A lens prototype was designed at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) frequency of 28 GHz. Three different feeding antennas, a linearly polarized patch antenna, a circularly polarized patch antenna and 2×2 CP array antenna, were used to test the lens. Maximum gains of 19.36 dB, 18.58 dB, and 20.3 dB with bandwidths of 1024, 746, and 540 MHz, were obtained for the three antennas, respectively. The substrate material of the lens is RO4003C with permittivity of 3.38 and the total dimension of the antenna 9.79λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 9.79λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Intermediary Objective Based Optimization Method for Field Focusing through an Inhomogeneous Medium
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Generating target focused fields through a strongly inhomogeneous medium is an interesting and challenging problem in electromagnetics. In this article, we present an intermediary objective based optimization method for solving this problem. Compared with direct optimization methods, the proposed approach does not need to re-iterate for obtaining the array excitations when the target positions of the focused fields changes. Several full-wave simulation experiments were conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High-Power-Capable, Ultra-Wideband, 1-Bit, Reflectarray Unit Cells Using Polarization-Rotation Reflection Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Two ultra-wideband, reconfigurable reflective polarization-rotating (PR) elements are presented in this paper for high-power microwave applications. While one structure provides wider bandwidth, the other one is less challenging to fabricate and is likely more robust mechanically. The proposed structures use two dipole antennas connected to a switching circuit integrated with four, commercially-available, PIN diodes at the backside of a ground plane. Switching between different on-off combination states of the PIN diodes provides 0° or 180°phase shifts yielding a tunable, 1-bit, phase-shifting unit cell. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations predict that both PR unit cells should provide a high co-polarization reflection coefficient (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">yx</inf>> −1 dB) and 180° phase difference over an ultra-wide bandwidth. Thermal simulations predict that the PR unit cells should tolerate a continuous-wave illumination power density level of at least 22 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, while keeping the PIN diode switch junction temperatures below 85% of their maximum rated values.

articleTitle: Cavity Antenna Based on AMC-Reflector and FSS Superstrate for Gain improvement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Cavity antenna with based on AMC and FSS is proposed. The antenna is designed at 5.8 GHz for IoT applications. An I-shaped slot antenna operates at 5.8 GHz, is proposed with an AMC reflector layer, placed under the antenna and a FSS superstrate layers located above the I-shaped slot antenna. Simulated results are presented and discussed to assess the proposed antenna design.

articleTitle: Investigation of modal stored energy approach to mantle cloaking of active antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the potential of cloaking an active radiating element in the presence of an obstacle is studied. It focuses on using modal stored energy analysis and inter-modal coupling coefficient to determine how to successfully cloak a radiating antenna through the scattering cancellation scheme. The obtained result consist in the first step in providing a general approach for cloaking arbitrary active antennas with metamaterial.

articleTitle: A 12 m2Ka-band Reflector Antenna for SAR Earth Observation Missions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> band is of interest for SAR Earth observation missions. Reflector-based antennas can provide high gain and low sidelobes. Here, feasibility and performance of a relatively large K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band antenna of 12 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is presented. Antenna patterns and surface current densities are investigated using Ansys HFSS. Multipath interactions between the reflector and the feed are considered. Instead of applying an ideal feed radiation pattern, the mutual coupling within the feed and with the reflector are considered as well as non-zero back lobe radiation.

articleTitle: Passive RFID-based Intelligent Gloves for Alternative and Assistive Communication - A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We introduce intelligent gloves based on passive ultrahigh frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) technology, which comprises of four antenna parts and three RFID integrated circuits (ICs). Each of the ICs (in middle finger, ring finger and small finger) have their unique IDs, which can be activated by gentle touch of thumb, and used to send a specific message, which is displayed on a computer screen. Two users tested the gloves in an office environment with M6 mercury RFID reader and a specially developed software. The achieved success rate in these preliminary tests was 100 %. We consider these results promising first steps for future wearable passive RFID-based augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) solutions.

articleTitle: A wideband miniaturized 3 dB hybrid coupler for passive beam switching application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband miniaturized 3 dB 90° hybrid coupler for passive beam switching application. The hybrid coupler is usually employed in an antenna array feed network in a butler matrix. For ease of fabrication and measurement, the operating frequency of the hybrid 90° coupler is designed from 700–960 MHz. Hence, an operating bandwidth of around 30% is achieved at the center frequency of 830 MHz. A size reduction of 83% is accomplished along with a fractional bandwidth of 30% by carefully adopting a meander structure with optimized spacing to enhance the capacitance within the structure. The proposed design is fabricated on Rogers 4360 substrate and measured results of the prototype show good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: A Compact mmWave SIW Blass Matrix
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a mmWave planar substrate integrated waveguide Blass matrix is proposed. By utilizing a cruciform planar coupler, the normally two-layer beamforming network is reduced to a one-layer design, reducing complexity, while achieving similar performance to its two-layer counterpart. Simulated results show a 15 dB return loss for an operational bandwidth of 1 GHz (24.25 – 25.26 GHz) with an amplitude, and phase deviation less than 2.8 dB, and 10°, respectively.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Waveguide Slot Filtering Linear Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new rectangular waveguide slot filtering linear array antenna, where the filtering function is realized by loading a row of T-type resonators at the bottom broad wall of the rectangular waveguide slot antenna. A four-slot rectangular waveguide slot filtering linear array antenna operating in 5.6-6.0 GHz and rejecting in 7.75-8.75 GHz is designed and simulated. The simulation results show that, compared with the traditional waveguide slot linear array antenna, the proposed antenna has almost the same radiation performance in operating band while achieves an additional 26 dB to 59.4 dB radiation suppression in stopband.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Folded Patch PIFA Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact dual-band planar inverted F-antenna (PIFA) is presented by using characteristic mode (CM) analysis. The proposed antenna consists of a main patch with two PIFA-like folded plates and occupies a total volume of 30×15×2mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In this design, the modal current distribution and modal significance (MS) are calculated to understand the underlying physics of resonant frequency. Additional PIFA-like folded plate is introduced to obtain the resonant frequency. Then, optimizations of the antennas with optimal feed position and compact patch size are explicitly obtained. The impedance bandwidth, determined by 10 dB return loss, of the operating bands reach 6.8% at 2600 MHz and 23% at 4150 MHz, respectively. The maximum gains at the frequencies of 2600, 3700, and 4150 MHz were 2.63, 2.97, and 2.78dBi, respectively. The overall shapes of the radiation patterns are suitable for TD-LTE / 5G mobile communication applications.

articleTitle: Flexible Antenna on Polymer-Conductive Textile Composite for Epidermal Electronics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the applicability of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-conductive textile composite for realization of a robust flexible antenna for skin-mounted applications. For this purpose, we present the design, manufacture, and testing of an ultra high frequency (UHF) 868 MHz loop antenna with the specified material. The antenna performance has been investigated through simulations and measurements on a human forearm phantom. Apart from having a low-profile implementation and being mechanically flexible, and thus comfortable for on-skin use, the novel antenna presented demonstrates a wide operating bandwidth with acceptable gain for epidermal electronics.

articleTitle: Low RCS Transmitarray Using Phase Controllabe Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A phase controllable rasorber, also named as phase controllable absorptive frequency-selective transmission (AFST) surface, is developed in this paper. It is composed of asymmetrical resonators with lumped resistors, achieving an absorption-transmission-absorption response. Compared with other reported rasorbers, the proposed one has an additional feature that is to realize a 1-bit phase change of its element within the transmission band by rotating the element by 90°. A low radar cross section (RCS) transmitarray is designed at 12.5 GHz with a peak realized gain of 24.4 dBi using the developed elements. The 10 dB RCS reduction bandwidths are 18% and 14% for the lower and upper absorption bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Automated Synthesis of Non-Foster Impedance Matching Circuits
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Active non-Foster circuits can cancel out the reactance of a high-Q load and are a potential solution for wideband impedance matching of electrically-small antennas. Due to the inherent instability and non-linearity of non-Foster circuits, the design of such circuits is time consuming and relies heavily on the designers' experience. To make non-Foster circuits more accessible to the society, we propose an automated tool for synthesizing stable non-Foster circuits in real time. The proposed tool employs three machine learning models for non-Foster circuit synthesis: artificial neural networks, k-nearest neighbors, and Gaussian process. The proposed tool can be used to synthesize (i.e., reverse design) non-Foster circuits with a desired negative capacitance within the −385 pF to −52 pF range. To verify the accuracy of the proposed tool, a non-Foster circuit was synthesized (input: target capacitance = −196 pF) and fabricated using commercial-over-the-shelf components with values closest to the synthesized parameters (output). The simulated capacitance of the synthesized circuit is −195.78 pF (error = 0.11%). The measured capacitance of the prototype is −201.41 pF (error = 2.76%).

articleTitle: Effective Acoustic Media for GHz Ultrasonic Lens Focusing in Fourier Transform Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of effective acoustic media for GHz Ultrasonic Lens focusing in solid medium for the Fourier transform of Wavefront Computing (WFC) applications. An ultrasonic WFC module consists of an array of GHz ultrasonic transducers fabricated directly on CMOS on both sides of thick acoustic media, which includes two acoustic blocks and a flat acoustic lens sandwiched in between. Focusing of an acoustic wave, propagating in the acoustic blocks and the lens, depends on the medium of individual regions that it passes through. Suitable materials for the effective acoustic media investigated to achieve good focusing characteristics of the ultrasonic wave at the desired focal plane, and taking into account the impact of fabrication tolerance.

articleTitle: CP Gain Enhancement of MM-Wave SIW-Integrated DRA Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method for enhancing the gain of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)-integrated dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array in a sequential rotation configuration using parasitic DRAs. A hybrid junction SIW splitter is loaded with linear-polarized (LP) DRA elements to generate high purity circular polarized (CP) radiation. E- coupling occurs between the driven DRAs and parasitic DRAs added on one side of the driven DRA. Parasitic coupling provide simple, low cost, and compact mechanism for gain enhancement without adding any complex feeding structure. The simulation results show a symmetric radiation pattern with a maximum CP gain around 13 dBic at 36.50 GHz along with a very low cross-polarization, an impedance bandwidth of 4 GHz, and 3 dB axial-ratio band width of 1.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Bandwidth investigation of UHF antenna fully integrated into 2U CubeSat body
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper proposes a non-deployable UHF 2U CubeSat antenna based on the characteristic modes. It demonstrates the same coupling structure can excite desired modes at 435 MHz for both 1U and 2U CubeSats volume. Additionally, a shallow non-resonant cavity is proposed to increase the impedance bandwidth of the antenna from initial 4 to 9 MHz (225% increase).

articleTitle: The Challenges in Implementing Wearable Antennas for Large-Scale Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The rise of antenna technology, smartphones, and the Internet-of-things (IoT) has enabled wearable antennas for wireless communication between implantable devices such as pacemakers, infusion pumps, etc., and external devices for health monitoring. This work describes the key challenges that need to be addressed for such wireless body area network (WBAN) technologies to be integrated into large-scale health monitoring programs. These include the miniaturization of antennas, fabrication techniques to enable mass production, and methods to protect patients from data infringement and hackers. Furthermore, the role of wearable and implantable antennas is pivotal to realize devices for continuous healthcare monitoring especially during Pandemic situations such as Coronavirus Disease-2019 (COVID-19).

articleTitle: ±45° Dual-Polarization Multi-beam Meta-surface Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a metasurface lens antenna fed by a 2×5 planar ±45° dual-polarization patch antenna array which is lightweight and low-complexity. The designed antenna can cover the 5.8 GHz band and the HPBWs are around 15° and the gains are larger than 15 dBi.

articleTitle: Replacement of the TD Wave Equation by a First Order Equation with Alternative Field Constituents
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A pair of field consistuents, denoted herein as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{E}^{\mathrm{R}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{E}^{\mathrm{L}}$</tex>, are suggested as an altenarive to the conventional pair E, H. These fields obey lower order equations, i.e., the first order Maxwell's curl equations are replaced by a zero order (algebraic) relationship, while the wave equation is now traded for a first order equation. As a result, the conventional use of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\times 6$</tex> scalar, real time domain set is now consolidated a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> complex equations. This consolidated solution tracks exactly the one obtained with the original finite difference scheme.

articleTitle: An Inhomogeneous 3D Block Lens For Hemispherical Scan Coverage In Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of an inhomogeneous dielectric lens using genetic algorithms for hemispherical coverage in mmWave phased arrays. The lens antenna is capable of 2D hemispherical scanning. A 52-element symmetrical phased array operating at mmWave frequencies is used as the feed antenna. A computationally efficient methodology that utilizes symmetry to synthesize scattered field from each radiating element is employed. Using this methodology, an optimal lens antenna is designed and simulated. The lens antenna provides hemispherical coverage while maintaining a peak gain of over 20 dBi at boresight with a maximum scan loss of 1.2 dB when scanning to the horizon. The design can replace multifaceted phased arrays making it ideal for low cost 5G mmWave applications requiring hemispherical coverage.

articleTitle: Minimal-Order Model for Fast Electromagnetic Analysis of On-Chip Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A minimal-order model is proposed to accelerate electromagnetic analysis of realistic on-chip problems with large-scale arbitrarily shaped structures and lossless/lossy inhomogeneous materials. This model can describe fullwave electromagnetic effects from DC to prescribed high frequency by using nullspace modes and a few high-frequency modes. It is effective for not only the frequency- and time-domain simulation, but also a modal analysis that traditionally involves an eigenvalue solution. Numerical simulations of large on-chip power grids validate the accuracy, efficiency, and capacity of this work.

articleTitle: Time-Modulation as a Vehicle for Bypassing the Gain-Bandwidth bound of Small LTI Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Chu bound, developed under the assumptions of passivity, linearity, and time-invariance sets a lower limit on the quality factor of a small antenna. This with the gain properties of the antenna dictates its maximal attainable gain-bandwidth product of an antenna. By revoking the LTI assumption of the properties e.g., by allowing time variation of the antenna properties, better performance may be achieved. In the following presentation we specifically discuss the effect of time-modulation of the antenna structure on the gain-bandwidth product of a system of three coupled antennas. It is shown that time-modulation may give better results beyond that obtained for the corresponding LTI antenna system.

articleTitle: Design of a Patch Antenna Using Materials of Clothing: a Study Under Simulations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In the last decade, body-centric communications have taken on great relevance in the field of Wireless Mobile Communications and with a wide range of applications, such as medical, emergency, military, geopositioning, in the logistics industry, among others. An essential part of these applications is carried out by wearable antennas. This paper presents the design of a wearable patch antenna, using materials and accessories for clothing. The antenna has been designed to work at the 4.15 GHz frequency of the Band C (satellite systems) and which has also been studied to be implemented in 5G technologies. The radiant patch was designed with a metal button (used as an accessory in blue jeans), and the simulated dielectric substrate was made of the same jean textile material with a relative permittivity of 1.6 and a thickness of 1.56 mm. Results of the radiation pattern, gain, reflection coefficient, and efficiency under numerical analysis with specialized software. The good results of the gain stand out, being this one of 8 dBi, and the efficiency of 76.88 % was obtained.

articleTitle: Generalized Cramer-Rao Bound for Passive MIMO Radar Multi-target Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Joint location and velocity estimation for multiple targets under the generalized case is studied for passive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar and the generalized Cramer-Rao bound is derived, where generalized means that the signals of opportunity can be nonorthogonal, the target reflection coefficients from different paths can be correlated, and the clutter-plus-noise can be spatially correlated. The results obtained can guide in implementation of the passive MIMO radar system.

articleTitle: An Ultrabroad Band Absorber Based on Magnetic Absorbing Material for Solving EMC Problems in Chip-Packages
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of an ultrabroad band absorber working in high frequency band using magnetic absorbing material for solving the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problems in chip-packages is proposed. This absorber consists of two squared layers both made of the same absorbing material with difference sizes. The simulation shows that the absorber is able to achieve a reflection coefficient less than −10dB in the frequency range of 27.8 GHz to 65.2 GHz under normal incidence and also has a weak incident angle sensitivity. By attaching the absorber to the margin on the bottom surface of the heat sink in a chip-package model and comparing the simulation results, the effectiveness of this newly designed structure for solving EMC problems in chip-packages is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Parameter uncertainty quantification of components of a CAD mobile phone model
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Numerical simulation plays an essential role in exploring and understanding physics for a real-life scenario. However, the uncertainty is generally inevitable in any numerical simulation process, e.g. model and parameter uncertainties, which potentially hinder the reliability of simulation results. For meaningful simulations, the possible uncertainty along with the simulation responses should be examined. Herein the focus is on the parameter uncertainty quantification in numerical dosimetry based on a computer-aided design of a mobile phone model. The impact of the uncertainty of different components of the mobile phone on the simulation responses is investigated. The sensitivity analysis is conducted to analyze the relative importance of each uncertain input parameter in the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Wide-angle Scanning Metasurface-Enhanced Array for Next-Generation Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The problem of synthesizing a slant +/-45 [deg] dual-polarization waveguide array with wide scan capabilities for 5G applications is addressed in this work. The exploitation of an advanced low-profile wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) superstrate is considered to achieve such a goal, and an innovative system-by-design (SbD)-inspired strategy is customized to the solution of the arising synthesis problem. The results of an extensive full-wave numerical validation are presented to illustrate the effectiveness and performance of the resulting arrangement in terms of scan range, impedance and gain stability, and port isolation.

articleTitle: A multi-band CAD mobile phone model for specific absorption rate calculation benchmarking
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: IEC/IEEE 62704-3:2017 describes the standardized procedure for the calculation of the specific absorption rate (SAR) of mobile phones using the finite difference time domain method. The standard includes some single and dual-band computer-aided design (CAD) mobile phone models as benchmark problems to verify the general approach for the numerical simulations of such devices. The standard is currently being revised to include up-to-date mobile phone models for the SAR calculations. Herein a multi-band CAD mobile phone model is proposed as a possible benchmark problem to be investigated as an international interlaboratory comparison.

articleTitle: Analysis of a fractal small antenna using shorting post and the social spider optimization algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents an applying of the social spider optimization algorithm with combination of two antenna miniaturization techniques, based on the use of a Koch fractal contour and a shorting post connecting the patch and the ground plane, to achieve an outstanding reduction in size and dimensions. The feeding technique is a microstrip line and the matching between the line and the antenna is by inset. The SSO is used to find out the best radius and position of the shorting post and the length of the inset feed. Antenna prototype has been built and the measurements reached a good agreement with the numerical simulation. The resonance frequency of the proposed antenna is reduced from 2.45 GHz to 730 MHz, with a miniaturization about of 70%. The proposed antenna is suitable for applications in the 700–800 MHz frequency range, such as 4G mobile communication systems and broadcast digital TV services.

articleTitle: An Automated Experiment for Parametric Investigation of Voltage Stacking Behavior
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Nonlinearly loaded receiving structures exposed to microwaves have been shown to store energy in the DC component of the induced voltage after the transient response has dissipated. Current modeling techniques of this phenomenon can be time-intensive, yielding limited data. This paper will outline an autonomous experimental procedure capable of performing hundreds of parametric studies in minutes and demonstrate its validity through a study of pulse repetition frequency.

articleTitle: Terahertz Dielectric Waveguide based on Silicon-on-Insulator Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low-loss dielectric waveguide is implemented in silicon-on-insulator (SOI) technology working at the terahertz range of frequencies. The waveguide characteristics are investigated to support fundamental mode using full-wave simulations. A properly designed rectangular grid is utilized to handle the waveguide with minimized effect on the insertion loss of guiding channel.

articleTitle: Single-Mode Wireless Sensing by Nonlinear Parity-Time-Symmetric Circuits
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Wireless sensing in parity-time-symmetric system by interplay between gain and loss have shown enhanced sensitivity due to the nonlinear response. Here, we report single-mode wireless sensing using nonlinear parity-time-symmetric circuits. We observe an exceptional point where the frequency response of system is nonlinear following square-root-topology. We also observe frequency hopping point by single-mode switching due to the nonlinear saturable gain. We demonstrate wireless pressure sensing with enhanced sensitivity at an EP and HP compared to the traditional wireless sensing without gain. Wireless sensing by parity-time-symmetric circuits shows great potentials for highly sensitive biomedical sensing.

articleTitle: A circularly polarized patch antenna matched to liver surface with TX coupling medium
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A probe-fed circularly polarized patch antenna with cross slot and shorting pins is designed as a receiving antenna for ex-vivo microwave liver ablation experiments. For better matching with the liver surface, the antenna is simulated with tissue phantom mimicking the dielectric properties of liver made of TX material as a coupling medium in the background. The reflection loss bandwidth (2.0-2.8 GHz) and the axial ratio bandwidth (2.1-2.9 GHz) of the antenna covers the 2.4-2.5 GHz ISM band used for microwave ablation. The bore-sight gain of the antenna is −42 dBi and 3 dB axial ratio beam-width is 6° around the bore-sight at 2.45 GHz. The diameter of the antenna is 22 mm making it possible to place multiple antennas on the liver sample surface.

articleTitle: A Class of Dielectric Resonator Antennas with Thermally Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A new class of dielectric resonator antennas with co-optimized electromagnetic and thermal characteristics is presented. The use of dielectric materials with high thermal conductivity, such as alumina, allows for a combined electromagnetic and thermal functionality, on the most basic level, of a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna. Perforations are produced in the radiating structure to improve the corresponding thermal characteristics while maintaining suitable electromagnetic performance. The proposed antenna element presents large bandwidth at mm-wave frequencies. Thermal simulations of the stand-alone radiating structure as well as of the relevant 4 × 4 array are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the perforations for heat transfer and temperature mitigation.

articleTitle: An Accurate Solution to Periodic Grating Structure Scattering Using Nystrom Method with An Over-determined Testing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Characterizations of artificial periodic structure scattering is of great importance in various engineering designs. However, accurate theoretical modeling remains an issue especially at large incidence angles. In this paper, an integral equation (IE) formulation is developed to solve the sub-wavelength periodic grating scattering problem. To achieve high accuracy, the Nystrom method is adopted to discretize the IE with the Gaussian-Legendre quadrature rule and the local correction scheme. Meanwhile, an over-determined testing scheme of the IE is proposed to overcome the potential internal resonance issue associated with the surface integral equation. This over-determined testing scheme turns out crucial to the validity of the IE methods when applied to the grating scattering problem, not limited to the internal resonance frequencies. In computing the impedance matrix elements, the periodic Green's functions are evaluated to high accuracy and efficiency by combing a recently developed imaginary wavenumber extraction technique and an integral transformation approach. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by modeling the extraordinary acoustic transmission (EAT) phenomenon associated with the near grazing incidence of a plane wave upon a periodic array of closely spaced circular cylinders, for which case the commercial software Comsol yields non-physical transmittance that exceeds unity. The proposed method can be applied to arbitrary periodic gratings and is of great significance to the design and simulation of such structures.

articleTitle: Development of MACKEY II type M miniaturized using multiple slits
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A meta-surface-inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), which operates in free space and on a metal plate, was investigated in this study. We propose a method for reducing the size of MACKEY II of the 920 MHz band to the card size.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin broadband absorber using active non-Foster devices and FSS-magnetic material
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of an ultrathin and broadband absorber which uses active non-Foster devices and frequency selective surface (FSS)-magnetic material is proposed. The active non-Foster device is placed below the structure and it is connected to the upper metal strips through vertical metal pins. The FSS-magnetic material is used to broaden the absorption bandwidth at higher frequencies, while the active non-Foster device realizes an active impedance matching for enabling absorption at lower frequencies. An absorber with thickness of 0.014λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> at the lower frequency) has been designed with a joint circuital/full-EM optimization strategy, achieving ultra-wideband absorption performance (except for the bandwidth around 1–2 GHz).

articleTitle: Magnetically Tunable 28 GHz Array Antenna Using BaM/PDMS Composite
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a magnetically tunable 2 x 2 array antenna operating at 28 GHz using a screen-printed self-biased magnetic/polymer composite that consists of 70 wt% barium hexaferrite (BaM) and 30 wt% polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Unlike high temperature processing for traditional hexaferrite annealing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(> 800^{\circ}\mathrm{C})$</tex>, this work demonstrates a low-temperature process flow at 7 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\ ^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> making it compatible for organic/PCB board integration and packaging. By applying an external magnetic field of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 240\ \mathbf{mT}$</tex>, a tunability range of 0.3 GHz is achieved. Also, the array antenna structure is simulated using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). The total area of the fabricated device is 0.84 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Nonuniform Planar Array Synthesis Including Mutual Coupling Effects Based on ANN
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A nonuniform planar array synthesis method considering mutual coupling effects is proposed in this paper. The proposed method consists of two steps. In the first step, the active element patterns and the passive S parameters of the synthesized planar array with different location distributions are modeled by artificial neural networks. In the second step, the differential evolution algorithm is applied to optimizing the positions and excitations of the elements in the nonuniform planar array to make the radiation pattern and active S parameters of the synthesized array satisfy the requirements. Since the limitations of the active S parameters are considered in the optimization process, the synthesis results obtained by the proposed method are applicable to both transmitting arrays and receiving arrays. An example of a microstrip array synthesis problem is presented to prove the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: New Scanning-Spot Beam Reflectarray Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this report, a new design for a reflectarray antenna using mirror configuration will be proposed. By adapting to the two characteristics of a reflectarray antenna that changes beam directions using frequency and polarization, it is possible to realize a multi-scanning beam whose performance is as good as a conventional multi-spot beam with one reflecting mirror. Herein, we examine a scanning-spot beam that changes the beam direction by using frequency in the elevation direction and polarization in the azimuth direction in the Ka band. As a result, the proposed design efficiently covered the desired service area.

articleTitle: Analysis of foF2 Observations and Predictions of Modified Ionosphere Model in East-Asia
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The modified ionospheric critical frequency of F2 layer (foF2) model was given, and the predictions of foF2 at two sounding stations in east-Asia are compared with observation results measured by the ionosonde. The statistical results prove that: the foF2 calculated from the new model can be well treated as a similar trend in the variation of the monthly median statistical characteristics of observation data. Specifically, the minimum root-mean-square error (RMSE) is 0.54MHz, and relative RMES are 8.17%. The modified ionosphere model can be supported in fields such as communication, navigation, detection and location, spectrum management, etc.

articleTitle: Early detection of damages in fruits with amplitude-only measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Fighting fruit diseases, farmers are in demand of an automatic Non Destructive Evaluation system for detecting the damages in fruits. In this paper, we propose a proof of concept using amplitude-only measurements associated with a Machine learning of linear Support Vector Machine type, Algorithm for sorting healthy from damaged peaches hidden by leaves. The system operates in W-band and the total accuracy of the classifier is 100%.

articleTitle: Radiated Near Field Prediction based on Equivalent Source Reconstruction Method with Truncated Singular Value Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The equivalent source reconstruction method (ESRM) is a popular method to predict radiated near field. However, the original equivalent currents can't be reconstructed by solving the interaction matrix equation directly because the matrix equation is generally ill-conditioned. There will be a large error in the near field prediction, especially when the region of interest is very close to radiation source. To reduce the error of near field prediction, the truncated singular value decomposition is used to solve the interaction matrix equation. By ignoring small singular values of interaction matrix, its condition number is improved. Thus, the reconstructed equivalent currents are more similar to the original equivalent currents, and the error of prediction can be reduced significantly. Simulation results will be shown to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancement of MIMO-UWB Communications in Underground Mine Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Improving the quality of communication of multiple-input multiple-output ultra-wideband (MIMO-UWB) systems in mining applications, is as compulsory as in conventional wireless channels. The solution proposed herein alleviates the channel fading through the incorporation of the equalization mechanism prior to performing UWB communication over this channel. The effect of mining machinery is also taken into account. The paper investigates two equalization schemes, namely the Zero Forcing (ZF) and Maximum Likelihood (ML), where the superior performance of the latter technique is demonstrated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Dual-Resonant Patch Antenna with Tilted Circularly Polarized Beam
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband tilted circularly polarized (CP) beam dual-resonant patch antenna with low-profile is proposed. Initial size of the antenna is empirically calculated according to the eigenmode functions of the microstrip patch radiator. Pin-loaded technique is employed to tune the antenna and to lead a tilted CP characteristic. As validations, a prototype antenna on air substrate with thickness of 4mm (i.e., 0.034-wavelength) is fabricated, measured and verified at 2.6GHz-band. The proposed antenna with centered angles of 200° exhibits an impedance bandwidth up to 24.1%. It exhibits a tilted CP radiation within the elevation range of θ=10°~40°, with 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth up to 8.2%, maximum gain at θ=15° up to 5.6dBic and average radiation efficiency of 91%.

articleTitle: Accuracy Improvement of the Algebraic Fast Methods for the Volume-Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The method of moments (MoM) based on volume-surface integral equation (VSIE) has been widely used to analyze the scattering of composite conducting-dielectric materials. Algebraic methods such as the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) and pseudo skeleton approximation (PSA) have been used to decrease the computational complexity of the MoM. Due to the different scattering characteristics of conductor and dielectric, the compression of the impedance matrices based on algebraic methods may lose some key scattering factors, which leads to the reduction of accuracy. A novel way is presented in this paper to enhance the accuracy of the algebraic fast methods for the electromagnetic scattering of the composite conductor-dielectric materials.

articleTitle: A noncontact RF sensor with loop antennas based on PT-symmetry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, sensing principle based on PT-symmetry is investigated with perturbation of equivalent elements R, Land C. In addition, a real sensor composed of two loop antennas is proposed between which MUT with permittivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+\delta\varepsilon-\mathrm{j}(0.01+\delta\varepsilon^{\prime})$</tex> is placed. Simulated results show the sensitivity enables to reach 100 kHz/0.001 for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta\varepsilon$</tex> and 10 dB/0.001 for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta\varepsilon^{\prime}$</tex> that is extremely high compared to conventional sensors.

articleTitle: Pre-phased Planar Array with 1-bit Amplitude Control for Single-beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The pre-phased planar array with 1-bit amplitude control is proposed for the single-beam scanning. The pre-phase distribution on the planar array is designed based on the theory of array synthesis, and the normalized amplitude 0 and 1 are utilized for State 0 and State 1, respectively. Using the fixed pre-phase and 1-bit amplitude control for the unit cells, anticipated beam directions can be achieved. Furthermore, the 1-bit amplitude control can achieve a tailored amplitude in the scanning planar, bringing suppressed side lobe level (SLL). As an example, a pre-phased planar array with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\times 20$</tex> unit-cells is designed and numerically simulated for the beam scanning from 0 to 30 degrees with the 10-degree step. Two difference cases are discussed for maximized gains and suppressed SLLs, respectively. The number of State 1 for unit cells is maximized for the maximized gain, and the tailored amplitude is utilized for the suppressed SLL nearly 20 dB during beam scanning.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Thinned Planar Arrays with Accurate Mutual Coupling Modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The synthesis of thinned planar arrays of real radiating elements for 5G communications systems is addressed. A nature-inspired optimization strategy based on the Genetic Algorithm (GA) is employed for defining the simplified array architecture in order to reduce the number of transmit/receive modules and radio-frequency (RF) chains with respect to a fully-populated array architecture. For each iteration of the GA-based optimization process, the array pattern is efficiently calculated by considering a limited set of representative embedded element patterns which allow taking into account the mutual coupling phenomena and to obtain an accurate prediction of the real radiation performance. A representative numerical example is reported to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Several Effective Methods on Reducing Cross-Polarization of a Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Several methods are proposed to reduce the cross-polarization of a patch antenna by adding different additional structures. The first is to add an independent shorting pin on the line where the feed point is located. The other is to add a metal block of a specific height at a certain distance from the radiating edge with a stronger electric field of the patch; Finally, the two methods are combined to obtain even higher polarization purity. The above methods all aim to alleviate the asymmetry of the reversed magnetic currents of the fringing field when patch operates at the fundamental mode. The combined structure shows the suppression of the cross-polarization reaches to the level of −35.5 dB which is 26.6 dB lower than that of the traditional patch antenna. The simulated results verify the effectiveness of these methods.

articleTitle: Optimal Pulse Transmission Criterion for Ultra-wideband Wireless Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A criterion of optimal pulse transmission (OPT) for ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless transmission system is proposed and analyzed. Different from pulse transmission in UWB wired transmission system, the pulse transmission suffers from inherent distortion of antennas and wireless channel in UWB wireless transmission system. The OPT is obtained when the normalized Euclid distance (NED) of the received pulse and optimal received pulse attains its minimum. To verify the OPT criterion, three commonly used transmitting/receiving antenna architectures in UWB wireless transmission system are analyzed theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Near-Field-Based Preconditioning Technique in the Incomplete-Leaf MLFMA for Nonuniformly Discretized Electromagnetic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The potential of incomplete tree structures, previously used in the context of the multilevel fast multi pole algorithm, on developing an effective preconditioning technique for multiscale electromagnetic problems is analyzed. The preconditioning technique is based on the sparse near-field matrix constructed by the near-field clustering definition of the incomplete tree structures for multiscale geometries. The proposed preconditioner is applied to solutions of matrix systems obtained via method-of-moments discretization of potential integral equations since the conditioning of the calculated matrices deteriorates as the problem size grows or the number of unknowns increases. The effectiveness and robustness of the preconditioning technique are demonstrated by numerical experiments on a complex target.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction of Slot Antenna Array Using Coding Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a diffusive frequency selective radome, which has two diffusion bands, is proposed. The integrated structure is comprised of three layers. An <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> antenna array is designed as the bottom layer, which acts as a reflecting ground for the upper two layers. In order to maintain the radiation characteristics of the antenna, different 1-bit coding metasurfaces are designed for the dual-band radar cross section (RCS) reduction based on polarization conversion. The antenna gain loss less than 0.5 dB and two low-RCS bands from 3.9 to 6.1 GHz and 11.5 to 15 GHz are observed under the normal incidence.

articleTitle: Modified Square Loop Antennas with an Increased Axial-Ratio Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Using the method of moments, we analyze two types of loop antennas; they have loop circumferences of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1\lambda}$</tex> and 2λ (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>: wavelength). Each loop is located above a ground plane at height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{h}$</tex>, and a 3dB axial-ratio bandwidth versus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{h}$</tex> is evaluated. It is found that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1\lambda}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\lambda}$</tex> loops have maximum bandwidths of 3% and 2% at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{h}=\boldsymbol{0.18\lambda}$</tex>, respectively. Using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1\lambda}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\lambda}$</tex> loops, we further design a double-loop antenna. It is revealed that the antenna shows a bandwidth of 3%, which is three times as wide as that of a conventional double-loop antenna.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Wideband-Narrowband Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this article a Vivaldi antenna is presented capable of switching its operating bandwidth between wideband and narrowband. Three different operating bandwidths centered at 2.4 GHz are supported in overall, with108%, 28% and 13% impedance bandwidth. This reconfiguration is attained using switching from a CPW-to-slotline feed. The simulated and measured results are presented with a good agreement.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dual-polarized Based Station Antenna with Notch Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A broadband <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 45^{\circ}}$</tex> dual-polarized base station antenna with notch band is designed for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\mathrm{G}/3\mathrm{G}/\text{LTE}}$</tex> bands. The proposed antenna consists of two crossed petaloid dipoles, four folded microstrip lines, two microstrip stubs and a metal uncovered box shaped reflector. In order to obtain the notch band, four folded microstrip lines are introduced. The notch band can be shifted by changing the length of microstrip lines. A prototype of the proposed antenna is fabricated and measured. The measured results show that it has a bandwidth of 1.7-2.7GHz for VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{ < 1.5}$</tex> with notch band from 2.35 to 2. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{57\text{GRz}}$</tex>) port-to-port isolation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{> 22.5\text{dB}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Modeling of Finite-size Fabry-Perot Antennas with Array Feeds
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A model describing the radiation pattern of an array-fed Fabry-Perot antenna is presented. The model is derived from the Fourier transform of the leaky-wave on the partially reflective surface of a periodic structure. The propagation constants of the leaky-wave are obtained through the transverse equivalent network method. The model is validated by the full-wave simulation of a 52 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 52$</tex> mm Fabry-Perot cavity with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> dipole-fed excitation with a spacing of 20mm. The simulated antenna operates at 38.6 GHz, achieving a peak directivity of 25.5 dBi and a 3-dB bandwidth of 2.33 GHz. Compared with the full-wave numerical approach, the model provides a fast and good estimation on the 3-dB Bandwidth and the maximum Directivity of a finite array-fed Fabry-Perot antenna.

articleTitle: Design of a Homogenized Magnetic Metasurface for the RF Magnetic Field Enhancement in 1.5 T MRI
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we propose the adoption of magnetic metasurfaces, whose response is opportunely controlled in order to achieve a homogenized magnetic field distribution, for 1.5 T MRI applications. We firstly introduce the analytical guidelines required to design and control the metasurface response and then we perform full-wave simulations on an arrangement consisting of an actively fed RF coil and the metasurface. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution is able to significantly enhance the RF magnetic field distribution, especially in terms of spatial homogeneity and amplitude. This solution can be extremely useful to enhance the MRI scanner performance by increasing both the covered Field of View and the signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Tailoring Airy Beam from a Two-Dimensional Dynamic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Airy beams possess intriguing non-spreading, self-accelerating, self-healing properties. A two-dimensional dynamic metasurface whose meta-atoms can be individually addressed is designed for the Airy beam generation using the 1-bit phase coding scheme. Both simulations and measurements validate the generation of the Airy beam at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: An Inverse Source Approach for Designing Smart Electromagnetic Enviornments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, the design of smart electromagnetic environments (SEEs) is addressed as an inverse source (IS) problem. The complex scattering phenomena arising within a urban scenario are opportunistically exploited by a “smart” (i.e., scenario-aware) base-station (BTS) antenna in order to induce on the buildings/obstacles the necessary equivalent currents so that a user-defined target field distribution is achieved in a given (non line-of-sight) region. An illustrative benchmark is shown to verify the effectiveness and the potential of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Chipless RFID Tag Detection with a Single Measurement in Presence of Multipath
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a chipless RFID tag detection method to extract the ID of a co-polarized tag with a single measurement in presence of high floor reflection multipath at a read range over 1 m. With one <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> measurement, the components of the signal that do not contain information about the tag's ID are filtered out using a time-window whose start time and duration have been studied. This technique is robust as it can identify different tags' resonant frequencies with an offset below 3 % at a read range of at least 132 cm, no matter the tags' orientation on the plane perpendicular to the antenna.

articleTitle: Topological Edge-Mode Characterization Using Foldy-Lax Multiple Scattering Theory and Interpretation with Classical EM Theory
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Foldy-Lax multiple scattering theory is used to characterize the topological edge-mode and the classical electromagnetic (EM) theory is then used to interpret this property in this paper. The Green's function-the field response of a line source in both the yttrium-iron-garnet (YIG) gyromagnetic photonic crystal and alumina crystal are computed by Foldy-Lax multiple scattering theory. The results show that the EM wave with a frequency within the band gap rotates counterclockwise in the YIG crystal while it does not rotate in the alumina crystal. The Foldy-Lax theory is also used to compute the multiple scattering when the line source is put at the interface of these two crystals with different separation distances. The results show that the one-way edge-mode will disappear at larger distance and this property is interpreted with classical waveguide and band gap theory.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning-Assisted Modeling of Millimeter-Wave Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The conventional physical-statistical models cannot accurately predict the site-specific mmWave channel characteristics when involving complex system configurations and geometric information of transceiver locations. A framework of machine learning assisted channel modeling approach is proposed, in which the statistical models are leveraged for inter-cluster level channel characterization and the propagation properties within each kind of clusters are predicted via a novel set of cluster predictors. In particular, a case study of modeling forward through-vegetation scattering effect is presented using the physics-based and data-driven hybrid approach.
