articleTitle: A Wideband Stacked Patch-Patch Antenna with Hybrid Perturbations for Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband circularly polarized antenna for small satellites to be used with NASA Near-Earth Networks (NEN). This single-fed stacked antenna utilizes the electromagnetic coupling concept and is usable with a duplex transceiver. The circularly-polarized antenna employs hybrid perturbations on stacked patches and covers NASA NEN's both uplink and downlink frequencies, thus replacing the conventional requirement of two separate antennas. It provides a notable wide axial ratio (AR) < 3 dB bandwidth of 1.16 GHz from 7.02 GHz to 8.18 GHz (15.3%). The optimized patch dimensions provide 34.6% VSWR ~ 2 bandwidth from 6,525 MHz to 9,253 MHz. The overall antenna size is 17 mm × 17 mm × 6.6 mm, and has a peak gain of 7.9 dBi. This proposed antenna will overcome solar cell space constraint on smallsat's outer wall by saving at least 50% area required by the conventional two-antenna method.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband Circularly Polarized Spiral Antenna for Conformal Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel compact conformal broadband spiral antenna on a truncated cone. The radiating body of the antenna is composed of two-arm spiral metal strips, and the two arms with 180° differential excitation to generate unidirectional radiation and left-hand circular polarization in the axial direction of the spiral. Exclusive power divider and phase shifter are designed to form the feeding network. The presented antenna has the impedance bandwidth of 49.2 % (2.3-3.8 GHz) of !S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>! <-10 dB and the 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 57.1% (2.0-3.6 GHz). The miniaturized, compact and broadband characteristics of this designed antenna make it advantageous for drones and portable equipments.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Highly Efficient Waveguide Front-End Direct-Conversion Receiver for 60-GHz Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents the characterization of a wideband front-end receiver, based on hollow waveguide technology and multiport concept, for 60 GHz wireless communications applications. The presented waveguide multiport network is composed of four 90° hybrid couplers and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> phase shifter and fabricated on brass material to minimize the insertion losses and noise levels at the first stages. To determine the performance of the receiver, an experimental analysis of real-time wireless data transmission employing modulated phase-shift keying (PSK) signals are provided by a standard test bench setup.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for the Synthesis of High Directivity Wide-Angle Scanning Irregular Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel and effective method is proposed for the synthesis of high directivity and wide-angle scanning irregular phased arrays. The radiation pattern of irregular arrays is decomposed into the product of subarray array factor and subarray pattern. For the reduction of the complexity of the problem, the subarray tiling configurations are first achieved by the direct maximization of the directivity of the subarray array factor. Afterwards, the associated complex excitations are obtained by convex optimization. A numerical example of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16$</tex> irregular array composed of domino-like subarray is used to assess the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarization Broadband Reconfigurable Rasorber with High Selective Passband
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an innovative bandpass reconfigurable wideband rasorber is proposed. The periodic structure is consisted of a lossy frequency selective surface (FSS) with resistors and a lossless passband FSS with a square slot. Both FSSs are loaded with varactors to adjust the transmission band among the absorption band. The simulation results demonstrate that the unit structure can realize the wideband absorption in the range of 5 -20 GHz. Meanwhile, by modifying the value of the varactors in lossy FSS and lossless FSS, a transmission band with high selectivity and low loss can be achieved in the X-band. The proposed structure has great potential for plentiful applications such as radar stealth and electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Compact AMC-Dual-Band Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact dual-band antenna system is designed for wireless body area network (WBAN) devices. The design is based on a CPW-fed slot antenna operating at 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz. To reduce the backward scattering wave towards the human body, a compact double square based on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 3$</tex> artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) array is proposed. The volume of the proposed antenna with AMC is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$54\times 72\times 15\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. Simulated results show that the AMC surface can enhance the isolation of the back radiation from the antenna to the human body. Furthermore, results demonstrate that the proposed AMC integrated antenna has also a significant increase in gain of 7 dBi and 9.54 dBi, and the front-to-back ratio of 13.4 dB and 20.1 dB, at 2.4 GHz and 5.5 GHz, respectively, when placed on the phantom. These demonstrated properties of the proposed antenna make it an ideal candidate for WBAN applications.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Roundness Improvement of Off-center Monopole Antenna Using Electromagnetic Band-gap (EBG) Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A suspended circular electromagnetic bandgap (CirEBG) ring is proposed for improving the radiation pattern roundness of a quarter-wavelength monopole placed off the center of a square ground plane. The study shows that the proposed CirEBG structure localizes the surface currents on the ground plane within a controlled symmetric boundary so that the un-roundness of the off-center monopole antenna is reduced by 65%. The antenna is prototyped and measured to validate the method of the design.

articleTitle: Fast Characteristic Mode Analysis for Material Body with Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Characteristic modes analysis (CMA) for material bodies has become increasingly popular due to its applications to a variety of electromagnetic structures. Apart from focusing on various forms of integral equations, enhancement of the capability of the CMA for material bodies requires fast solving challenging generalized eigenvalue equation to get eigenvalues and eigenvectors. In this paper, the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is embedded into a PMCHWT-formulation based characteristic modes (CM) solver with implicitly restarted Arnoldi method (IRAM). Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed approach, which provides a candidate for fast CM analysis of large-scale material bodies.

articleTitle: A Singulary Cancellation Method Inspired by Differential Geometry for Evaluating Nearly Singular Integrals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Inspired by differential geometry, we present singularity cancellation (SC) methods for curvilinear surface elements. The method relies on an approximate distance function inspired by the first fundamental form of differential geometry. Moreover, we propose four transformations that can accurately evaluate the nearly singular integrals.

articleTitle: Graphene Printed Antenna Array for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed tri-band graphene printed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 2$</tex> planar array antenna for wireless communication use. The antenna is designed to support L band, the fifth generation (5G) sub-6GHz band and 5.2 GHz wireless local area network (WLAN) communication applications with biodegradable and low-cost printed graphene. The graphene laminate which was screen-printed on paper substrate possesses a sheet resistance of 1.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega/\text{sq}$</tex> and a conductivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.5\times 10^{4}\ \mathrm{S}/\mathrm{m}$</tex>. The peak gain of this antenna reaches 2.14 dBi at 3.8 GHz, indicating good power transmission.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Traveling Wave Antenna Development Methodology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A technique is developed to enable automated machine learning design of traveling wave antenna. A planar substrate is built with a reflecting ground plane and upon this an antenna strip with a number of joints is created. A machine learning algorithm is then able to vary the joint angles to reach specific goals such as the resultant reflection coefficient and gain. The outcome from this technique is a planar curl antenna with 65% bandwidth covering 3 GHz–6 GHz. The planar curl antenna is also able to provides a nearly axial beam with a target gain of 6 dBi from the zenith. This machine learning methodology can be applied to automatically develop wideband curl and spiral antenna for a large variety of applications.

articleTitle: Programmable Metasurface-Based DOA Estimation Using Atomic Norm Minimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a atomic norm minimization (ANM)-based direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method using programmable metasurface sensor (PMS). Different from the traditional phased-array, PMS utilizes the low-cost, passive, reflective elements to independently reflect the incident signal. The ANM-based DOA estimation method overcomes the drawback of grid effect by working directly in continuous parameter domain. Simulation results verify that the proposed method based on PMS can achieve better DOA estimation performance with low hardware complexity and low-cost.

articleTitle: Characterization of Rectangular Plates using Complex Natural Resonance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The practicality of extracting natural resonant modes from the late-time target responses of conducting rectangular plates with various length-to-width ratios is studied using the matrix pencil method. The extracted resonant modes follow a similar behavior as the results obtained from a theoretical analysis reported in the literature. Our results show that it is feasible for these modes to be excited using a practical system, which opens the opportunities for automated target recognition.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Patch Antenna Array Using a Metamaterial Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Gain enhancement of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> square patch antenna array using metamaterial superstrate is proposed. The patch antenna array is fed by a power divider. A metamaterial superstrate layer placed at about half-wavelength from the patch array is used to enhance the array gain. The proposed low-profile antenna yields an enhancement in gain of 8.30 dBi at 2.24 GHz with a slight reduction in the resonant frequency. Broadside patterns with improved cross-pol for the superstrate-loaded configuration are also observed.

articleTitle: A Computational Study of COVID-19 Detection using Colorimetric Plasmonic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Traditional molecular techniques for COVID-19 viral detection are time-consuming and can exhibit a high probability of false negatives. In this work, we present a computational study of COVID-19 detection using plasmonic gold nanoparticles. The resonance wavelength of a COVID-19 virion was recently estimated to be in the near-infrared region. By engineering gold nanospheres to bind with the outer surface of the COVID-19 virus specifically, the resonance frequency can be shifted to the visible range (380 nm–700 nm). Moreover, we show that broadband absorption will emerge in the visible spectrum when the virus is partially covered with gold nanoparticles at a certain percentage. This broadband absorption can be used to guide the development of an efficient and accurate colorimetric plasmon sensor for COVID-19 detection.

articleTitle: A Four-Port MIMO Antenna with High Isolation for Sub-6GHz 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper designs a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with a sub-6G frequency band for 5G communication. The MIMO antenna consists of four ports with four microstrip elements. Each single element adopts the coupling feed method, and an annular slot is opened in the bottom substrate to achieve broadband characteristics at low frequencies. Meanwhile, the incomplete grounding substrate is used in the design of the MIMO antenna to improve the isolation degree between ports. The antenna is 62 mm×70mm in size and the simulations by the well-known HFSS software show that it can achieve a bandwidth of 3.43 – 3.85 GHz and an isolation degree of about −20 dB. The MIMO antenna has a small size and a high isolation degree, which are very desirable for 5G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna for LTE Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel planar horizontally polarized (HP) omnidirectional antenna is proposed and validated in this work. The omnidirectional radiation is achieved by eight open slots etched on the bottom of the substrate, including four Vivaldi slots and four straight slots. A 1:4 power divider is printed on the top of the substrate to feed the Vivaldi slots directly. The straight slot which provides an extra resonance is arranged between every two Vivaldi slots to improve the impedance matching and the pattern roundness on the horizontal plane. The proposed antenna achieves a wide bandwidth of 54.6% ranging from 1.61 GHz to 2.82 GHz with a total size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi\times 60\ \text{mm} \times 60\ \text{mm}\times 1\ \text{mm}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Design of 3D-Printed Air-Like Structural Supports for Meanderline Polarizers at L-Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A design approach and demonstration of a 3D-printed lattice structure as a low permittivity foam spacer replacement in meanderline polarizers (MLP) are discussed. Reduced complexity model that relies on the extracted parameters from the lattice structure calculated using the Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) method as frequency-dependent material characteristics is developed and showed to accurately represents the physics in the infinite array environment. Effective parameters of fabricated 3D-printed air-like supports are extracted using NRW method and compared to simulation through multiple iterations to compensate for systematic errors introduced by the utilized 3D printer. Simulated results integrating such a 3D-printed structure with a meanderline polarizer and planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) unit-cell for a tightly-coupled array (TCA) at GPS L1, L2, and L5 bands are presented as well.

articleTitle: A Phase Compensation Technique for the Tradeoff Design of Irregular Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A tradeoff design of irregular arrays is proposed to achieve significant radiation performance within a wide scanning range. Through different phase compensation for the elements in a subarray, the radiation vector of each element is deflected and a conical beam pattern can be formed. Thus, combining tradition irregular array and phase compensation technique, the directivity in the broadside is slightly sacrificed, while that in the wide scanning angles can be improved. Simulation results show that the directivity of irregular arrays after compensation is much larger than that without compensation by more than 2.5dB in the large scanning angles. As for a 16x16 tetromino-shaped irregular array with half-wavelength interelement, the scanning range can be further extended to ±70° after phase compensation. Moreover, the phase compensation is achieved by delay lines, which does not increase the complexity as compared to conventional structures.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction for Wideband Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a low radar cross section (RCS) wideband antenna array is proposed through array-level scattering cancellation. Two types of Vivaldi antenna elements with the same radiation performances and different scattering phase are developed. With these two types of elements, a low scattering Vivaldi antenna array (16×16) is proposed in a chessboard configuration. A reference array with a single type of antenna element is also developed. For radiation, both antenna arrays operate over 8–12 GHz and have similar performances. For scattering, the proposed Vivaldi antenna array achieves an average of 10 dB monostatic RCS reduction over 6–18 GHz under normal incident waves, illustrating the effectiveness of the proposed RCS reduction technique.

articleTitle: Single-Ridged Waveguide Antenna for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A slotted waveguide antenna array based on a single-ridged waveguide (SRWG) with high gain and low side-lobe is designed. Longitudinal slot etched on the broad sidewall of the SRWG is employed for vertical polarization (VP) radiation. An 6 ×56 array at X-band is designed and simulated to validate the slot antenna design, which occupies a total volume of 1420mm× 76mm×10mm. The bandwidth for VSWR<1.2 is 0.7GHz at the center frequency of 9.4 GHz. The realized gain at the center frequency of 9.4 GHz is 31dBi with antenna efficiencies better than 83%. The side-lobe is controlled lower than −33dB over the entire bandwidth. Due to its high gain, compact size, low side-lobe level and ease manufacturing, this array can be combined with the edge-slotted waveguide array to build a two-dimensional dual-polarization antenna array for the applications of sea based X-band radar, satellite communication station, etc.

articleTitle: Pop-Up Card Inspired, 3D-Printed Corner Reflector Antenna-A Novel Deployable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a pop-up card inspired corner reflector antenna, fabricated using inkjet and 3D printing technologies. The reflector is designed with a state-of-the-art folding structure that has an integrated fold limiting mechanism, which accurately sets the flare angle to a predefined position. As a result, the antenna can be easily deployed and stored compactly. The antenna resonates at 6.4 GHz, with a percentage bandwidth of 7.34% and a maximum realized gain of 14 dBi at resonance frequency.

articleTitle: Measurements of 3.5 GHz OAM Misaligned Channels in Indoor Corridor Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents measurements of OAM misaligned channels in an indoor corridor using a spectrum channel sounder. The channel sounder consists of 3.5 GHz eight-element OAM antennas with +1 and −1 modes and a vector network analyzer. First, the large-scale propagation loss of the transmission distance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\lambda\sim 20\lambda$</tex> was measured when the transmitter and receiver were aligned. Then, the received power was measured when receivers were misaligned at different horizontal axis offset angles. In addition, the measurements of the conventional monopole in the identical setup were given as reference. The results show the measurements agreements with the theoretical derivation of propagation loss trends in both aligned and misaligned cases. Moreover, the results also suggest the overall performance of OAM may significantly degrade when the beam diverges as increasing propagation distance.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Series Feed Patch Antenna at Millimeter wave for 5G application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the comparison between microstrip series feed patch antenna array and substrate integrated waveguide series feed antenna array with air vias. The CST studio simulation software is used for the simulation with Roger 5880 substrate where the dielectric permittivity of the substrate is 2.22 with a thickness of 0.508 mm and tangent loss of 0.0009. The antenna is designed to resonate at 26 GHz. Various parameters of the antenna have been investigated such as return loss, gain and radiation pattern. The technique to enhance the sidelobe level is also investigated by applying the air vias substrate that's achieved by penetrating at specific dimensions and distributed along line with the antennas by specific studied conditions.

articleTitle: Digital Pre-Distortion to Correct UWB Pulses in a Boresight Test
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We demonstrate the development of digital predistortion for reducing ringing and improving pulse fidelity of a received ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse. We use a software-defined waveform generator to pre-distort an input pulse (0.5-3.9 GHz) sent to an amplifier and an antenna pair in a boresight test. We show that pre-distortion can reduce average ringing by 4.22 dB and increase pulse fidelity by 14.8%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that demonstrates ringing reduction in transmitted pulses using a software defined technique.

articleTitle: A Cavity-Backed Antenna with a Tilted Directive Beam for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain cavity-backed antenna with a tilted beam is proposed for 5G applications. The proposed antenna consists of a stacked antenna surrounded by a cylindrical metallic rim. The feed antenna fed by a single coaxial probe has an asymmetric structure with some embedded slots to realize a directive tilted beam. When the feed antenna is excited, because of the mutual coupling, the cylindrical rim acts as a second radiator leading to an improvement in the radiation gain. A maximum tilted beam of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$32^{{0}}$</tex> at yz-plane and a maximum gain of 14.2 dBi are achieved by sweeping the frequency. The proposed antenna is of interest for 5G point-to-point communications.

articleTitle: A Wide-band Inner-wall Conformal Antenna for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multiband inner-wall conformal meander line antenna for Wireless Capsule Endoscope systems operating at 403 MHz, 868 MHz, 915 MHz and 1400 MHz simulated within its working environment. According to the in-vivo simulation, the proposed antenna operates from 344 to 544 MHz and from 644 to 1600 MHz. The maximum realized gain of the antenna reaches −31.07 dBi at 403 MHz in muscle. The effect of varying capsule shell thickness on antenna performance is also inspected by simulation.

articleTitle: Dual-band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Fully-Wireless Smart Stent
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the dominant cause of mortality globally and are of an increasing trend. Generally, coronary stent placement is a pervasive treatment to combat CVDs. However, the cardiovascular stent employed as the passive expanded support in the blocked artery frequently introduce a postoperative complication called in-stent restenosis. The innovative self-reported stents integrated with biosensors can offer effective diagnosis and treatment of in-stent restenosis. In addition, the use of biotelemetry is essential in the interaction with physiological signals in the vessel's lumen, ensuring continuous monitoring of internal conditions within a vessel. This paper presents two compact dual-band microstrip antennas with encapsulation and without encapsulation that can implement power and data transmission. In particular, the 1.4 GHz Wireless Medical Telemetry Service (WMTS) band and 2.45 GHz Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) band have been allocated for wireless power transfer and biotelemetry, respectively. The proposed stent antennas employ meander slots on the radiating patch, which can achieve an ultra-small volume of 5 × 5 × 0.64 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Moreover, the antenna configurations, reflection coefficient values, and surface current distribution plots are compared between the encapsulated and unencapsulated antennas.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Pencil Beams Optimum in L1-Sense
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents pencil beams which are optimum in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex>-sense. A convex optimization program for their design is provided. The presented pencil beams exhibit maximum sidelobe level of approximately −21 dB for all array sizes and the lobes that monotonically decrease as the azimuth angle increases. The dynamic range ratio of excitation coefficients increases linearly with the number of elements and generally takes low values.

articleTitle: Acceleration of the Surface Test Integral Using Vertex Functions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In recent years, many papers have reported on the efficient and accurate evaluation of the double surface integrals that arise in the Method of Moments. Most have focused on the careful evaluation of the inner integral and assumed that the outer integral is sufficiently smooth to be easily evaluated numerically. More recently, several papers have appeared where the double integral is treated as a whole using the divergence theorem. These papers show promising results, though their implementation may imply changes to the integration paradigm for the associated codes. Here, instead, we investigate a technique that improves the numerical evaluation of the test integral without affecting the treatment of the source integral. From the integrand of the outer integral, we subtract pairs of quasi-static, so-called vertex functions defined on the source triangle. The approach is compared to standard Gauss-triangle schemes to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Compact Parallel Coupled-Line Bandpass Filter Dedicated to $E$-band Homodyne Front-End Radars
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of a compact millimeter-wave parallel coupled-line bandpass filter dedicated homodyne radars and communication systems is proposed in this paper. This filter is designed to pass the full <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>-band spectrum (60 to 90 GHz). Lowcost technologies and reliable implementation have been selected to realize the filter. It is integrated on a thin 5 mils ceramic substrate using Miniature Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuit (MHMIC) technology. A prototype of the proposed structure is implemented and measured. The measured results show a very good agreement with the simulation one.

articleTitle: A Conformal and Wearable Metasurface for Non-invasive Skin Inflammation Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the use of a conformal and wearable metasurface for non-invasive monitoring of the inflammation status of wounded skin tissue. We first present the designed RF passive metasurface, composed by a matrix of spiral unit-cells, each resonant at a slightly different frequency. In particular, the response of the metasurface can be read by a non-resonant inductive loop mutually coupled with the unit-cells. After that, we conceived a numerical test-case to verify the proposed approach and we performed accurate full-wave simulations. The obtained results demonstrate the excellent metasurface sensitivity and spatial resolution in evaluating the inflammation state; thus, further analyses are encouraged.

articleTitle: A Compact, Dual-band, Polarization-Reconfigurable Antenna for Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band, polarization reconfigurable antenna is developed, in terms of ±45° linear polarizations (LP) in both X- and Ku- bands, respectively. The dual-band polarization-reconfigurable performance is realized through exciting two radiating patches located on different layers by a reconfigurable slot aperture on the ground. Four PIN diodes are integrated into the ground slot to realize the polarization-reconfigurable characteristics. Furthermore, the phased array application of this developed antenna element is investigated by composing it into an eight-unit dual-band reconfigurable linear phased array. Simulated results demonstrate that the array has the scanning range of ±40° and ±20° in X- and Ku- bands, respectively. The developed dual-band, polarization-reconfigurable array are suitable for a certain multifunctional wireless communication applications, e.g., the radar detections and the satellite communications.

articleTitle: Broadband mmWave Filters using Dielectric Waveguide Bends
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This contribution handles a novel, broadband, and non-periodical mmWave filter design. Basing on fundamental considerations for dielectric waveguides, reflectionless high- and low-pass filter designs are discussed. Theoretical and practical design steps, as well as three different exemplary filter structures are presented. The corresponding transfer functions are investigated in simulations and measurements and prove the discussed filter theory.

articleTitle: Wearable Planar Magnetoinductive Waveguide WBANs: Bending Around Anatomical Curvatures
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We recently reported a new class of wearable wireless body area networks (WBANs) based on planar magnetoinductive waveguides (MIWs) that offer extremely low-loss as compared to the state-of-the-art. Examining the bending effects of these WBANs around anatomical curvatures of the human body becomes crucial for their practical implementation. Previous work utilized mostly flat surfaces to evaluate performance of planar-MIW WBANs with only few quantitative data reported for bending scenarios around curved surfaces. In this paper, we provide the complete transmission performance characteristics of these WBANS over the entire frequency band (30-60 MHz) pertinent to several bending scenarios that were not reported in the past. Results demonstrate excellent overlap of transmission characteristics across the operating band with minimal change in performance across various bending scenarios, including extreme bending. Overall, the study confirms the potential of planar-MIWs to connect across various anatomical curvatures and to ultimately form a robust and reliable alternative for future wearable WBANs.

articleTitle: Design of stub loaded transmission line matching circuit for series fed patch array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A stub loaded transmission line based matching circuit is designed for the series fed patch array antenna with Dolph-Tschebyshev amplitude tapering at 78.675 GHz. The short-circuited stub loaded transmission line is designed to replace the quarter wave transformer with unrealizably small width. The designed antenna array is matched well at 78.675 GHz. The 10 dB bandwidth is from 78.12 GHz to 79.2 GHz and the co-polarized gain is 9.277 dB.

articleTitle: Step Substrate Integrated Waveguide Equalizer Based on Microwave Discrete Resistors for Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of step substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) equalizer, which can be applied in broadband feeding network, is proposed. Different from the previous SIW equalizers fabricated on ceramic using Tantalum Nitride (TaN) in [1], the microwave discrete resistors are introduced into SIW equalizer for the first time. The equalizing values of SIW equalizer are approximately proportional to the number of the microwave resistors, which can be considered as step equalizer. The measurement results show that: over the entire Ku-band, in the case of 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 resistors, the corresponding equalizing values are 1.16 dB, 1.75 dB, 2.74 dB, 3.67 dB, 4.28 dB and 4.95 dB, respectively, which is close to a 1dB step. Meanwhile, the return losses are all better than −11.95 dB. In addition, the microwave equalizer is a planar structure implemented on traditional PCB, which has lower cost and is easier to be realized and integrated.

articleTitle: A Simple and Reliable Approach to Stabilizing Output Voltage of A Wireless Power Transfer System for Active Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the insertion of a simple two-element network at the transmission (TX) of a wireless power transfer (WPT) system for active implantable medical devices (AIMDs). The network parameters are optimized to compensate for the changes of mutual-coupling between the TX and receiving (RX) and make the output voltage constant within a specific range. A theoretical condition is analytically derived, simulations and experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system. The variation of the output voltage is kept at about 5% for both rotational and axial misalignments. The specific absorption rate (SAR) of the proposed system is also investigated for safety concerns. The result shows that the proposed system reduces SAR, and it is safe for wireless charging of AIMDs.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Transmitarray Consisting of Unit Cells with Asterisk and Cross Dipole Elements Separated by Ring Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a dual-band transmitarray using asterisk resonators and a cross-shaped resonator as unit elements. Then, addition of ring elements reduces the characteristic degradation between two types of resonators. A 13/30-GHz transmitarray is designed and also a prototype is measured to confirm usefulness of the proposed unit cells.

articleTitle: A Compact Annular Ring microstrip antenna for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a miniaturized Annular Ring (AR) microstrip antenna for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV). A conventional annular ring antenna was opportunely scaled, and a working frequency of 2.4 GHz with a bandwidth of 160 MHz is achieved. To the aim of effectively integrating this antenna onto a UAV vehicle, the radiating element engineering has been carried out. The proposed antenna design has a diameter of 107 mm and height of 16 mm. The weight of the whole system is about 100 g, and it is mechanically and electromagnetically stable, also when the antenna is coated by a dielectric cover which protect it from the external environment.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) Carrying Vortex Wave generation in Dielectric Filled Circular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to generate Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) carrying vortex waves inside a metallic circular waveguide (CW). These waves feature ability to carry multiple orthogonal modes at the same frequency, by the virtue of their unique spatial structure. In essence high data rate channels can be developed using such waves. In free space, OAM carrying vortex waves has beam divergence issues and a central NULL, which makes the waves unfavourable for free space communication. But, OAM modes in guided structures do not suffer from these drawbacks. This prospect of enhancement of communication spectrum provides the background for the study of vortex wave in the circular waveguides. In this work, a radial array of monopoles is designed to generate the vortex wave inside the waveguide. Further, we introduced the dielectric materials inside the waveguide in order to manipulate the operating frequency of the OAM modes. Simulation results shows that the various dielectric materials allow us to tune the working frequency of the OAM beam to a desired frequency.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Network-Based Design of Dielectric Resonator Antenna for mmWave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Characterized by low conduction loss and high radiation efficiency, dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) have been considered as a promising antenna type for the applications of 5G technologies at 60 GHz band. However, the design of the DRA mainly depends on the intuitive reasoning and trial-and-error process, which is time-consuming and resource-demanding. To address this challenge, we developed a generative adversarial network (GAN)-based approach to assist the design of DRA structures. This GAN model incorporates a simulator and generator for the forward prediction and inverse design, respectively. A paired dataset of geometric shapes and S11 parameter was fed into the GAN model to train the neural network. During the training process, the distribution of this dataset was captured by the end-to-end GNA model. The final model is capable of generating new DRA structures according to the desired S11 parameter.

articleTitle: Antenna Miniaturization Using High-Permittivity and Magneto-Dielectric Substrates in VHF-UHF Bands: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we study the effect of high-permittivity and magneto-dielectric host substrates on performance metrics such as radiation efficiency, gain, and bandwidth while miniaturizing the antenna by a same miniaturization factor. The antenna is designed to operate at 300 MHz band. For comparison purposes, different substrates including regular dielectric, high-permittivity dielectric, and magneto-dielectric are investigated, and their performances are evaluated at the operating frequency. The obtained values for the radiation efficiency, gain, and bandwidth of the antenna on high-permittivity material are 0.25 %, −21 dBi, and 3.04%, respectively. The corresponding values for the antenna on magneto-dielectric material are 1.28 %, −13.86 dBi, and 4.75 %.

articleTitle: A Circular Reflectarray for OAM Generation at Terahertz Regime for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A circular reflectarray antenna (RA) for generating Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) modes in the Terahertz (THz) band is introduced. An interlaced unit cell is proposed to reach a phase variation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol {328^{\mathrm{\circ}}}$</tex> at 185 GHz to 188 GHz. Combining RA, OAM, and THz technologies in one structure can be utilized to reach the future requirements of 6G networks. That is due to the additional degree of freedom that OAM beams can provide for data multiplexing in short-distance wireless communication.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Penetrable Objects with Magnetic Materials Based on Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Reconstruction of objects by microwave illumination can be described by integral equation approach and volume integral equations (VIEs) are indispensable for reconstructing penetrable objects due to the inhomogeneity of materials in the imaging domain. Traditionally, the objects are assumed to be nonmagnetic, so only the permittivity distribution is solved from the iterative process of reconstruction. This work considers the reconstruction of penetrable objects with both dielectric and magnetic materials and the full VIEs are needed to describe the problem. The forward scattering VIEs (FSVIEs) are solved by Nyström method while the inverse scattering VIEs (ISVIEs) are solved with a Gauss-Newton method. A numerical example is used to verify the approach.

articleTitle: Dual Band Topside Waveguide-to-Stripline Transition in Multilayer Substrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-band topside rectangular waveguide to stripline transition in multilayer substrate was developed for K/Ka-band applications. The waveguide sits on the top of the substrate. The proposed transition is realized with a standard PCB manufacturing processing, the metal fabrication process is not necessary for the hollow waveguide, this makes it suitable for mass production and practical applications. Two striplines (one for each band) are coupled to two radiating patches through H-shaped slots. Two parasitic patches are added on the top side to enhance the operating bandwidth. Via holes are used to create a cavity around the waveguide profile to prevent leakage from the waveguide.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically characterized gelatinous-based phantoms for breast microwave imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The present work proposes a procedure based on a modified recipe to fabricate electromagnetically characterized phantoms, made of gelatinous-based mixture. As a main advantage we highlight the use of commercially available and very inexpensive gelatin along with the addition of food colorants for the phantom assembly. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that by storing the samples in a refrigerator at a stable temperature of 4°C, the phantoms maintain stable dielectric properties up to 14 days. Their dielectric properties have been measured in the [1-8.5] GHz frequency range using a coaxial probe kit. The promising results demonstrate the potential of the recipe method to realize multistrate breast phantoms representing different tissues.

articleTitle: 24GHz RFID for Orientation Detection and Tracking Applications in Human Activity Recognition and Motion Capture
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Utilizing technology derived from a combination of modulated backscatter and FMCW radar, a simple low cost and highly accurate means to report and track the orientation of a tagged structure is reported. The system is comprised of a pair of closely spaced 24 GHz RFID tags interrogated by an FMCW radar and uses a method of phase difference to infer the orientation of the tagged structure. The result is an ultra sensitive, low cost orientation detection system suitable for use in human activity recognition and motion capture applications.

articleTitle: A Planar Ultra-Wideband Dual Polarized Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A planar ultra-wideband dual polarized reflectarray of tightly coupled dipoles is presented. The unitcell structure of the array is modular in nature, with its dipoles - arranged in an egg-crate configuration to support dual-polarization. The array is designed for broadside operation and exhibits more than 5:1 frequency bandwidth, maintaning an active VSWR < 2.5. To introduce the required phase shift at each unit cell, meandered true time delay lines implemented in planar configuration are used thereby making the proposed reflectarray extremely compact.

articleTitle: Effect of Bending on Metasurface Antenna and Microstrip Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the characteristics of two different antenna types; metasurface antennas (MSA) and microstrip patch antenna (MPA) array are analyzed. To compare their sensitivity to bending, multiple numerical studies have been performed on both designs at different curvatures. The footprint of each design is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$120 \times 90\ \mathbf{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The dimension of designs are optimized to operate in the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band with a center frequency of 5.8 GHz. Simulation results show that the reflection coefficient, the gain and the efficiency of MPA array are more sensitive than that of MSA for bending. The stability of reflection coefficients, radiation efficiency and realized gain makes the MSA a superior candidate for flexible and body-worn devices.

articleTitle: Use of Compressive Sensing in Quantitative Profiling of Non-Sparse Subsurface Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An innovative technique, based on combining compressive sensing (CS) and iterative multi-scale approach (IMSA), is presented for solving large, non-sparse GPR scenarios, using limited amount of data. First, a total variation minimization (TVM) based CS method is applied to localize the non-sparse buried object locations. Then, an iterative multi-scale approach (IMSA) is implemented that adaptively increases the resolution only in those regions that the objects are detected previously. In each step, the stochastic optimization technique of Covariance Matrix Adaption Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) is used to solve the inverse problem (IS). Selected numerical results are presented to reveal the efficiency of the proposed method. It is shown that using TVM in the first step, significantly reduces the number of required data resulting in a decrease in the data acquisition cost.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of THz 1-Bit RRA Element with Series Inductance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a THz 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (RRA) element with integrated GaN-based HEMT device and series inductance is proposed. Analysis of the adjustable load and the antenna impedance is presented, revealing working principle of the THz RRA element. Adding series inductance is proposed to guarantee the 1-bit phase shift with pure-resistive antenna impedance. Further, a systematic design method for the 1-bit element is developed. Designed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.7-\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> GaN HEMT technology, an element example can achieve near 180° phase shift at 0.2THz.

articleTitle: A Wide-Angle Scanning Array Using a Multi-Mode Antenna for mm-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this research study, a new multi-mode antenna element is introduced to achieve wide-angle scanning characteristics when integrated in a linear array. The unit cell structure relies on a hybrid design concept based on the combination of a patch fed by two capacitively coupled ports, and a cylindrical dielectric resonator fed by a third port via a metal pin. Two radiating modes can be enabled by controlling electronically the phase offset at the three input ports. Each mode is used to cover a different scanning sub-range. The antenna element is integrated in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 10$</tex> linear array and the relevant simulated results demonstrate a scanning capability from −75° to +75° with a scan loss smaller than 3 dB across the entire field of view.

articleTitle: A Compact Tri-port Antenna System for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and low-profile tri-port antenna system is proposed for cognitive radio (CR) applications. The proposed system consists of a ultra-wide band (UWB) antenna fed by co-planar waveguide (CPW) structure and two meandered monopole antennas on the same substrate. The spectrum sensing is performed by UWB antenna (3.1 GHz - 10.1 GHz) and meandered antennas operates in several frequency bands for communication purpose. Without any decoupling structure the isolation level between UWB and meandered antennas is higher than 15 dB in the UWB frequency range. The measured S-parameters and radiation patterns are in good agreement with simulation results.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Sparse Arrays With a More Efficient Reweighted $\boldsymbol{l}_{1}$-norm Minimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An improved reweighted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm optimization algorithm is proposed, which can synthesize sparse arrays at a faster rate. The proposed improvement method is also suitable for improving the computational efficiency of other sparse array synthesis algorithms. In the iterative calculation process of the reweighted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l_{1}$</tex>-norm minimization algorithm, the proposed improvement method is to reduce the amount of calculation by adaptively reducing the number of excitation variables to be solved, thereby reducing the time spent in the calculation process. Compared with the traditional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm minimization algorithm, the improved algorithm proposed has higher computational efficiency, and the optimality of the integrated result does not decrease. This method has obvious advantages in synthesizing complex problems such as large arrays.

articleTitle: Hybrid Resolvent Kernel Calibration Technique for Microwave Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work assesses a hybrid calibration technique that uses together measured and simulated data to compensate modeling errors such as fabrication tolerances and positioning inaccuracies. Here, as a proof-of-concept, it is considered a virtual microwave imaging experiment of a human brain stroke condition. The test involves a full-wave software based on the finite element method and 3-D highly realistic system models, including a set of 24 monopoles immersed in a solid brick-shaped matching medium and a single-cavity anthropomorphic head phantom. The studied case shows that under favorable assumptions, the calibration procedure improves the quality of the retrieved images compared to the non-calibrated-kernel approach.

articleTitle: Broadband Direct Coupled Stacked Microstrip Antenna for TVWS Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A stacked MSA is proposed with a direct-coupled feed to achieve broadband frequency response at the TVWS band. To make the antenna compact, H-shaped patches are used at the top layer. To increase gain and front-to-back ratio a cavity is formed by folding the ground plane. The antenna is designed using an Aluminium sheet resulting in a low-cost solution with high power handling capability. The proposed antenna having size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.91\lambda_{0}\times 0.52\lambda_{0} \times 0.19\lambda_{0}$</tex> provides 26.3% bandwidth, 9.8 dBi peak gain, better than 19 dB front-to-back ratio, low cross-pols, and a better figure of merit.

articleTitle: Smart Use of Vehicle's Existing Plastic Substrates for GPS Antenna Integration in Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a smart use of the vehicle's native plastic substrates for GPS antenna integration. The main objective is to integrate the antenna into the vehicle's body while respecting its aesthetics and leveraging plastic layers available in the part. The proposed antenna was optimized to provide a circular polarization for L1 GPS frequency. A prototype was fabricated and measured demonstrating a good agreement with simulation results and promising performance.

articleTitle: An Efficient Higher Order MoM-PO Method for EM Scattering From Electrically Large Objects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient higher order hybrid method of moments (MoM)-physical optics (PO) modeling technique is developed for the analysis of electromagnetic scattering from electrically large conductor objects. This technique utilizes curved triangular patches for geometric modeling, and higher order (HO) basis functions for current modeling, i.e., higher order hierarchical vector (HOHV) basis functions for MoM region and phase-extracted (PE) basis function for PO region. Benefitting from the “double” higher order discretization in both MoM and PO regions, the number of unknowns can be reduced remarkably, and the accuracy and efficiency increase, in comparison to the conventional low order MoM-PO solution. A numerical example is given to demonstrate the validity and efficiency of this HO-MoM-PO.

Author Keywords: higher order hierarchical vector (HOHV) basis functions

articleTitle: Conformal Modulated Reactance Surface Synthesis for Leaky-Wave Radiation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A design methodology for 1-D conformal modulated reactance surfaces for leaky-wave radiation is presented. A visible region field on a curvature surface associated with a desired pattern is retrieved by projection from a hypothetical planar surface. Evanescent surface waves are subsequently introduced and optimized to make the surface lossless at every point. When excited by a surface wave, the retrieved reactance surface operates as a leaky wave antenna, realizing the desired pattern with a high efficiency.

articleTitle: High Isolation MIMO Antenna Using Dielectrically Loaded Printed Dipole For 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is presented to increase the isolation between antenna elements in antenna arrays. A new type of antenna, called Dielectrically Loaded Printed Dipole Antenna (DLPDA), is designed and analyzed. The main design principle of the antenna consists of affixing high dielectric substrate on both sides of a dipole. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> Multi-input Multi-output antennas (MIMO) are optimized using DLPD for Full Duplex (FD) and 5G applications. By using the proposed method, the isolation is increased by 10dB. Moreover, the impedance bandwidth is widened and the length of the dipole arms is decreased. The resonance frequency of the proposed antenna is 3500 MHz and the operating band is from 3350 MHz to 3700 MHz (10%).

articleTitle: Planar Spiral Resonators for remote tracking of displacement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless displacement sensor based on a planar spiral resonator (SR) interrogated by a microstrip probing loop. The working principle is based on the relationship between the mutual coupling between the two RF components and the input impedance at the loop terminals. The distance estimation is obtained by monitoring the magnitude of the real part of the loop input impedance, at the operating frequency (about 860 MHz), which is a function of the tag-loop distance (d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tag</inf>). The proposed design benefits of simplicity, robustness, single-frequency interrogation, high scalability potential, and accurate high-resolution measurements in the operating range.

articleTitle: Real-Time Dielectric Sensing of Liquids using Waveguide Supercoupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental setup for real-time measurement of the complex dielectric constant of liquids at X-band. The dramatic field enhancement in a sub-wavelength height cut-off waveguide is used to generate narrow band frequency tunneling (“supercoupling”). A narrow liquid channel is introduced into the waveguide to create a perturbation to the tunneling frequency which is inverted to give the complex dielectric constant of liquids. The proposed method can measure permittivities from 1 to 80 and loss tangents from 0 to 2 with a measurement error of 0.33 %. This range covers all polar liquids and aqueous solutions.

articleTitle: Achieving Hemispherical Beam Coverage for a 39 GHz Integrated Lens featuring Double-Elliptical Boundaries through sequential GO and multiple Scattering
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes an accurate and efficient integrated lens antenna (ILA) design method for beam coverage enhancement and scan loss mitigation. The complex topology is first devised based on geometrical optics, in which a two-dimensional raytracing model is formulated to calculate the refractive trajectories on double-elliptical boundaries. A novel particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is developed for geometric parameter optimization. Afterwards, electromagnetic scattering is utilized to take into accounts of the realistic constraints of the source radiator. Using this methodology, the exemplified ILA achieves a main beam scanning angle of 83° and scan loss of 2.20 dB with broad operational bandwidth. Using this method hemispherical beamsteering antennas can be effectively devised. This method is expected to alleviate the mmWave 5G antenna CAPEX (capital expenditure) by more than 50%.

articleTitle: Embedded Split Ring Resonator Tunable Notch Band Filter in Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Novel design techniques for tunable and fixed frequency notch band filters are presented and validated with experiments. A notch band filter based on an Embedded Split Ring Resonator (ESRR) in a Microstrip Transmission Line (MTL) is presented. The physical dimensions of the ESRR determine the filter resonance frequency, which, when combined with a Varactor (Varactor Loaded ESRRs or VLESRRs), provides a continuously tunable resonance frequency. Tunable notch bands centered from 1.5 GHz to 5 GHz are obtained with resonators having a length of 0.05 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}}$</tex> at the lowest frequency.

articleTitle: Dual-port Stacked Annular Ring Microstrip Patch Antenna with Vertical Pins for Isolation Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-port stacked annular ring microstrip patch antenna (ARMSA) for polarization diversity applications and/or full-duplex communications is presented and implemented. Differently to traditional designs which employ an highly symmetrical dual anti-phase feed network structure for achieving two ports with identical performance and canceling coupling effects, in this design vertical pins which extend from SMA connector internal pins have been employed to realize a coupling cancellation path. Isolation between the two ports have been optimized with the commercial software Ansys HFSS, and measurement on a manufactured prototype for ultra-high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) applications have revealed a maximum isolation of 42 dB at the frequency 922 MHz and a maximum difference of only 2 dB between two ports behavior in terms of impedance matching.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Tree-Based Antennas for SLF-VLF Signal Reception
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A full-wave electromagnetic simulation and experimental study is carried out to explore the effects of tree-induced dielectric loading on the receiving properties of an electrically small, earth-grounded wire monopole. It is demonstrated that by connecting the upper end of the wire to the tree trunk, the input impedance of the monopole can be significantly transformed, leading to an enhancement in the received signal strength that becomes more noticeable as the frequency is decreased; for example, at the lowest frequency considered, it is seen that the tree-loaded antenna can increase the received load voltage by as much as ~40 dB, when compared to the case without tree loading. An application of the tree-based antenna for low-frequency power line signal monitoring is presented. Overall, simulation results for the input impedance and received signal response are in good agreement with measurement data.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Omnidirectional Antenna for WAIC System Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an omnidirectional antenna with low-profile characteristic is proposed for wireless communication in the cabin. The antenna can well operate in the band assigned for the Wireless Avionics Intra-Communications (WAIC) for wide signal-coverage inside the cabin. The antenna is evolved from a short monopole antenna but having a top-loading hemisphere and surrounded by folded spherical helices to achieve good impedance matching and symmetric radition patterns, as well as reduce the height of the antenna. Results show that the antenna owns a low-profile of only one seventh wavelength with satisfactory omnidirectional radiation patterns. Particularly, the antenna possesses the capability of resistance to the ground effect on omnidirectional radiation. The low-profile and omnidirectional radiation characteristic make the proposed antenna be a promising candidate for WAIC system applications.

articleTitle: An Efficient Wideband 94 GHz On-Chip Air-Cavity Backed Planar Inverted-F Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient, wideband 94 GHz on-chip air-cavity backed planar inverted-F antenna for future mm-Wave radar and imaging applications. The compact planar physical construction of this on-chip antenna allows for ease of integration and fabrication. The air-cavity relies on the reflection from the air/silicon interface, and thus does not require through silicon vias (TSVs). The presence of the air-cavity enhances the overall bandwidth, radiation efficiency, and inter-element substrate mode isolation for array applications. The simulated results of the proposed antenna show 7.55% fractional bandwidth, a quasi-omnidirectional radiation pattern with a peak realized gain of 1.57 dBi, and radiation efficiency greater than 82% in the operating band.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Differential Antenna Using Gradient Planar Slow-Wave Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized differentially-fed patch antenna using gradient planar slow-wave structure (PSWS) is proposed in this paper. Due to the large propagation constant and slow-wave effect of the PSWS combining with the utilization of the coupled shorted patches, the effective size of the antenna is reduced to 0.09 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}\times 0.1\ \lambda_{0}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the vacuum wavelength at 2.92 GHz. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed antenna operates at a simple coupled TM10 mode with excellent cross-polarization levels, which is an attractive candidate in the differential wireless communication systems for portable applications.

articleTitle: 3D printed torso phantom for UHF WIMD measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the manufacturing of a torso phantom used for radio frequency (RF) measurements of a Wireless Implanted Medical Device (WIMD) implanted in the pulmonary artery. This devices work in the UHF (Ultra High Frequency) band. This phantom has a detailed internal anatomy, with 3D printed organs, to achieve a better approximation than homogeneous phantoms found commercially.

articleTitle: Small Triple-Band Meandered PIFA for Brain-Implantable Bio-telemetric Systems: Optimization of Substrate/Superstrate Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We optimize and characterize our latest reported small triple-band implantable planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) resonating at Medical Device Radiocommunication Service (MedRadio) band (401–406 MHz), and Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) bands (902–928 MHz and 2400-2483.5 MHz) for wireless brain implants. To this end, we used a numerical 7-layer human head model to assess the impact of the substrate and superstrate properties on the peak gain of the antenna. Our results have demonstrated the gain improvements of 2 dB and up to 4.4 dB in the MedRadio and ISM bands, respectively, by optimizing the substrate properties and removing the superstrate.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Dual-Polarized Metasurface Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized metasurface antenna is proposed using characteristic mode analysis (CMA) for Ka-band applications. To achieve the dual-polarization, a primary patch is introduced with orthogonal microstrip-feeds in the same layer with a low profile, low cost and low back lobe level. Furthermore, the single-feed and differential-feed are adopted for vertical polarization (VP) and horizontal polarization (HP), respectively, to enhance the port isolation. A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> metasurface is presented for wideband operation and the CMA is used to determine the modal behaviors of the entire structure. Simulation results show that the return losses of both ports are better than 10 dB and the isolation is higher than 20 dB over 30.1-39.6 GHz. The simulated gain ranges 4.7-6.9 dBi and 7-7.5 dBi for VP and HP, respectively.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized CPW-fed Antenna for GNSS Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact circularly polarized (CP) coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed antenna used for global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) applications is proposed. The antenna has only a single layer and a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$70\ \text{mm}\ \times 70\ \text{mm}$</tex> which is about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.28\lambda_{0}\times 0.28\lambda_{0}$</tex> at the lowest frequency of the operating bandwidth. The 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is about 28.4 % (1.21 - 1.6 GHz) with a 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of about 31.5% (1.2 - 1.65 GHz), which overlaps the entire impedance bandwidth. Also, the 3-dB gain bandwidth of the antenna covers the entire impedance and axial ratio bandwidths. The peak right handed circular polarization (RHCP) gain of the antenna is about 3.62 dBic, which makes the antenna suitable for GNSS applications.

articleTitle: A Scalable Deep Learning Model for Arbitrary Transmitter Configurations in Inverse Scattering
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: State-of-the-art Deep Neural Network (DNN) based approaches for solving the Inverse Scattering Problem are con-strained to the locations and number of transmitters used while training. This requires retraining the network for every new configuration which is cumbersome. Here, we propose a DNN model that is scalable to arbitrary transmitter configurations.

articleTitle: Airborne Radar Clutter Suppression in Angle-Doppler Domain Using Clutter-Proximity Feature
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an innovative ground-moving target detection technique based on clutter-proximity feature is proposed for airborne radar. The clutter-proximity feature is extracted from the radar echoes in the angle-Doppler domain. After that, target and clutter are classified using the extracted proximity features from the domain. The proposed technique is particularly suitable for the suppression of the unknown ground clutter. The simulation results have validated the effectiveness of this new approach.

articleTitle: mm-Wave Phased Arrays Consisting of GCPW Feeding Networks with HIS in Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a design methodology of feeding networks in millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) phased arrays for mobile terminals by comprising grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) with via fences based on a single-layer FR-4 PCB. The 8-elements phased arrays consist of compact one-dimensional electromagnetic bandgap (1-D EBG) antenna elements and 1×8 T-junction power divider including the predetermined phase delay lines. In order to minimize leakage power in feeding networks of phased array, island-shape GCPW transmission line (TL) with via fences featuring high-impedance surfaces (HIS) is presented. By investigating various types of feeding networks in mobile platforms, the proposed GCPW topology with via fences can improve the realized gain at coverage efficiency of 50% by more than 3 dB between 26 GHz and 36 GHz.

articleTitle: A Chipless Ultra-Wideband RFID Tag Based on Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) tag based on cylindrical dielectric resonator (CDR) is proposed. The tag includes inner air loops that are externally invisible. The RFID tag can work in a ultra wideband (UWB) and generate multiple peak-valley pairs which are used to encode information. The multi-dimensional frequency point method is used to increase the coding capacity based on the imaginary part amplitude of the input impedance. Simulation results show that 6 peak-valley pairs can be achieved within a 1 - 5 GHz bandwidth for the tag with a height of 20 mm and a radius of 127 mm.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of RF Coils for Low-Field Portable MRI
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The emerging Permanent Magnet Array (PMA) based portable MRI scanners is promising technology to enable a mobile and low cost version of this imaging modality. The Radio-Frequency (RF) coils in low-field MRI systems require high band-width and low Q-factor in contrast to the conventional RF coils due to highly inhomogeneous static B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> field generated by the PMA. To develop highly efficient RF coils for low-field portable MRI, it is important to study the comparative performance of conventional RF coils in low-field and mid-field MRI to gain insights on the critical parameters. In this paper, we study and analyze a number of widely used RF coils in MRI engineering at both mid-field (1.5 T, 64 MHz) and low-field (0.117 T, 5 MHz) through numerical simulations. The parameters under investigations include the B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-field distribution, Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) bandwidth, Q-factor and field homogeneity.

articleTitle: Utilizing a Tunable Non-Foster Circuit for Wideband Matching of a Resistively Loaded Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A tunable non-Foster matching network is teamed with a wideband resistively loaded dipole antenna to improve signal reception especially at the low end of the operating band where the resistive loading becomes ineffective. Network stability is examined and shown to be manageable. A novel variant to the matching network enables easy tuning for optimized reception across the wide band.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Sierpinski Carpet Antenna with Cross-Slot Superstrate For 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates dual-band Metamaterial (MTM) Sierpinski carpet antenna (SCA) with and without MTM superstrate for 5G applications. The proposed antenna design is based on the second iteration of SCA, and the cross-slot MTM unit-cell is incorporated in the slots of the SCA.
