The MTM-SCA has been designed on a Rogers TMM4 substrate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\varepsilon_{r}=4.5, h=}$</tex> 1.524mm), and the simulation was done using CST Microwave studio. The simulation results indicate that the proposed antenna operates at 3.5GHz and 5.6GHz with a gain of 4.2dB and 3.6dB, respectively. The overall dimension of the SCA is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{25\times 30\text{mm}^{2}}$</tex>, which refers to a size reduction of 45% compared to the conventional microstrip patch antenna (MPA). A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{5\times 4}$</tex> cross-slot MTM superstrate was loaded above the MTM-SCA with different spacing to identify and study the gain variation. The MTM superstrate has been kept 3.9mm above the MTM-SCA, which gives an improved gain characteristic of 4.67 dB and 7.4dB at 3.5GHz and 5.6GHz, respectively. The proposed MTM- SCA with and without MTM superstrate shows dual-band characteristics, an excellent size reduction, high-gain and efficiency, and leads to an easy fabrication process, which makes them an excellent candidate for 5G applications.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Dual Band (28/38GHz) and Dual Polarized Antenna for 5G MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a low-profile dual-band and dual-polarized / dual port antenna at 28 GHz and 38.5 GHz is proposed, to meet the requirements of 5G millimeter-wave communications. The dual-band performance is achieved by optimally utilizing ring-shaped and slot stacked patches, which are electromagnetically coupled fed by two orthogonally placed feeding transmission lines, whereas the overall size of the antenna is kept physically small (11×11×0.762mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). The -10dB bandwidths (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf><-10dB) at 28 GHz and 38.5 GHz bands, are 1 GHz (27.5-28.5 GHz) and 2.2 GHz (37.2-39.4 GHz), respectively. The peak gains of the above bands are 7.6dB and 7dB, respectively. The presented antenna will be utilized for loading a MIMO system and achieves good port isolation below -19dB. The simulated envelope correlation coefficient between the ports has a maximum value of less than 0.02 over the operating bands.

articleTitle: Real Time Correction of Multipath Error in Satellite Positioning using FPGA-Accelerated Ray Tracing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Affected by the shadowing effect of high and large buildings, the traditional positioning method will have errors that suffer from the effect of multipath and non-line-of-sight propagation. In order to solve the above problem, this paper uses 3D maps and ray tracing method to correct multipath error. In order to meet the requirements of real-time positioning and portable computing, the acceleration system of multipath error correction is constructed by using FPGA and ARM structures of ZYNQ development board. Simulation and measurement results show that the speed of ray tracing running on the FPGA is much higher than on ARM, and multipath error is effectively reduced by using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Constrained Semidefinite Optimization of Reactively Loaded Antenna Arrays: Verification and Tolerances
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An optimization framework for maximum wireless power transfer efficiency in the near-field adapted for far-field gain maximization under impedance matching constraints is applied on a dipole antenna array to verify its performance on both maximum gain and impedance matching in practice. As shown, the result is well-realizable in practice. Beyond that, the effect of manufacturing tolerances and actual loading component values is analyzed.

articleTitle: Beam Reconfigurable Reflective Metasurface for Indoor Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A reflective metasurface with reconfigurable beam is proposed for indoor wireless communications. It consists of 8 × 8 unit cells with tunable capacitors. By varying the capacitances, the reflective phase across the metasurface can be designed to facilitate different reflective angles for an incident wave. The simulation results show that the proposed reflective metasurface can deflect the incoming wave from the broadside by up to 47 degrees, with the maximum side lobe level of −11dB. The proposed design is envisioned for mitigating the problem of blind spots in indoor wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Compact Large-scale Antenna with High Isolation for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a design of large-scale base station antenna array with compact structure and high isolation. The artificial dielectric layer (ADL) with high dielectric constant and metal pillars are introduced as main decoupling measures. The simulation results show that the two decoupling structures increase the isolation of the antenna array by around 5-10dB, and all isolations are greater than 20dB in the operating frequency band (6.4-7.2GHz), which demonstrates the correctness and effectiveness of the designed structure.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Reconfigurable Antenna using Quantum Genetic Algorithm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a volumetrically folded antenna design that is further miniaturized and reconfigured by employing Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA). The employed QGA determines the pixelated topology of the antenna structure, its feeding point, and the position of the single switch reconfiguring the antenna's frequency operation. As a result, the antenna operates at 868 MHz and 1.865 GHz when the switch is ON and regains operation at 2.4 GHz when the switch is OFF. In addition, the antenna size is reduced by 87% at 868 MHz, in comparison with planar antennas operating at the same frequency. The presented reconfigurable antenna can be proposed for Wi-Fi enabled Internet of Things (IoT) devices' integration.

articleTitle: Tackling Nonlinearity in Inverse Scattering by Suitable Rewritings of the Basic Equations: Recent Results and Possible Developments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution we focus on the possibility to reduce the nonlinearity of inverse scattering problem trough a smart rewriting of the relevant equations. In particular, we review, compare and discuss, under a common perspective, different rewritings of the equation which relates the currents induced in the investigation domain to the target properties.

articleTitle: Real-Time Human Activity Recognition System Exploiting Ubiquitous Wi-Fi Signals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In recent years, the development of wireless network provides the hardware foundation for wireless perception within indoor environment. The wireless sensing system has been applied in many fields, such as intrusion detection, search rescue, gesture recognition and abnormal human activities detection such as falling, wandering behaviour, breathing and heart rates and so on. Among of them, Wi-Fi sensing has proven to be effective since it exploits off-the-shelf low-cost small wireless devices operating at 2.4 GHz frequency band and also a potential field for real-time sensing method for human recognition. This paper presents foundation for real-time Wi-Fi sensing system to detect various human activities when performed in indoor settings.

articleTitle: Wide Angle ESA Fed Reflector Active Range Demonstration
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Traditional PAFR (Phased Array Fed Reflector) systems are limited by scan performance and can normally scan 5°-10° off boresight. WAEFR (Wide Angle ESA Fed Reflector) provides wide band performance with an electronic scan volume increase of up to 20x over traditional PAFR systems. This scan volume increase was demonstrated with a dual pol active array and a ring focus reflector. The range demonstration was able to show scan from 45°-55° and verify the ring focus optics associated with the system. The phased arrays operating frequency spanned Ku, K, and Ka bands and the tests were completed in Lockheed Martin Space's <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5^{\prime} \times 5^{\prime}$</tex> planar near field range.

articleTitle: Wearable Radio-frequency Plasmonic Resonance Sensor for Non-contact Vital Sign Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We report a wearable sensor that supports localized spoof surface plasmon resonances for sensitive non-contact monitoring of cardiopulmonary activity. The sensor comprises two layers of conductive textile on a cloth substrate, which can be integrated with clothing and wirelessly interrogated by a nearby antenna. Motions of the human chest from cardiopulmonary activity modulate the dielectric permittivity around the sensor, which are sensitively transduced into variations in the resonant frequency of the sensor measured from the reflection spectrum. We fabricate the sensor using conductive textiles and characterize its resonances. Experimental measurements with biological tissues show that the sensor operating at 4 GHz provides sensitive detection of periodic motions mimicking chest motion during respiration (190 MHz shift for 2 mm displacement) and heartbeat (100 MHz shift for 0.5 mm displacement).

articleTitle: Wideband Indoor Channel characterization of Massive MIMO System at 3.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the delay spread characteristics and power delay profile of wideband Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in an indoor environment is presented and analyzed. The analysis is based on the results of a measurement campaign performed at 3.5 GHz with two different bandwidths of 100 MHz and 200 MHz. Both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation scenarios are considered. The results include a statistical description of the delay spread in such number of sub-channel system. In addition, a case study of the effect of the transmission bandwidth on the RMS delay spread is presented. The results showed that larger transmission bandwidth has smaller RMS delay spread with lower variance over the Massive MIMO array.

articleTitle: Enhanced Born Approximation for Wave Equations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present an enhanced Born approximation inversion (EBAI) scheme for wave-like equations based on data to Born (DtB) algorithm. Due to multiple scattering, direct inversion methods usually perform poorly with artifacts in inverse scattering problems. By approximating the single scattering data through Taylor expansion, the DtB algorithm managed to remove the multiple scattering effects. Therefore, the nonlinearity between the scatterers and the scattering fields is unraveled. Without the optimization process usually needed for nonlinear inverse scattering problems, the EBAI scheme incorporating the DtB algorithm can achieve fast and accurate imaging. It is validated with 2D synthetic data.

articleTitle: Low frequency transmission of mechanical antenna across the interface of air-water
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The transmission loss of EM wave under water is very large and only the VLF/ELF may be available with huge antenna. The transmission system under water based on miniaturized mechanical antenna is investigated in short distance. Multiple sets of transmission experiments underwater and across the interface of air-water in short distance were carried out. And the terminal received clear signals despite the differences between those cases.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized Circular Horn Antenna Integrated in Multilayer PCB
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new dual-polarized circular horn antenna integrated in a multilayer PCB. The horn antenna is fed through two CPW transmission lines in the middle of the substrates. The height of the horn antenna is low profile, approximately 2.5 mm in 28 GHz band. Both the impedance and isolation bandwidths obtain more than 3 GHz and 2.5 GHz, respectively which cover the 28 GHz band in Japan.

articleTitle: Bridging the materials' permittivity traceability gap for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper reports recent efforts of the intersectoral iNEMI consortium towards bridging the traceability gap in the characterisation of dielectric materials used in 5G applications. Several GHz resonators, in SCR, SPDR, and FPOR topologies are applied to four samples fabricated from the same COP coupon. Characterisation is performed at three laboratories, using VNAs of different form-factors, and covering the frequency range of 10–110GHz. Excellent agreement is demonstrated between the methods and the samples. Consistent measurements at 10 GHz provide a trace to more conventional material measurements in the microwave range.

articleTitle: Fully Collapsible Lightweight Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Flexible, deployable phased arrays enable novel and diverse applications but necessitate similarly flexible radiators. Here we present a light and flexible 10GHz dipole antenna, which is co-cured to a glass-fiber composite and suited for flexible phased arrays. The antennas are designed to dynamically conform to new array shapes and be flexible enough to fold completely flat and pop back up upon deployment. We employ a pop-up dipole with a capacitive fingers feed for impedance matching that is highly robust against manufacturing errors. Upon deployment, the antennas exhibit a −10 dB-bandwidth >1.5 GHz and >110° half-power beam width single lobe pattern suitable for beamforming.

articleTitle: Compact Single-Layer Dual-Patch Antenna Fed by Dual Strips for 5G Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A millimeter-wave (mm-wave) dual-patch antenna fed by dual strips is proposed. The dual patches and dual strips are closely placed on the same layer and produce dual resonances, which assures the key features including compact size, wide bandwidth, single layer with simple structure and low profile. Considering performance, cost, and easiness of forming array, the proposed antenna is preferred for 5G mm-wave applications. The size of antenna element is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.36\times 0.37\times 0.05\ {\lambda_{0}}^{3}(\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the wavelength in free space at the center frequency) and a prototype of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 4$</tex> array is fabricated for demonstration. The measured 10-dB impedance matching bandwidth is from 22.7 GHz to 27.9 GHz and the peak gain is 14.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Rotman Lens-based High Gain Retrodirective Beamformer for Wireless Power Transfer at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A high-gain retrodirective beamformer based on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{9\times 15}$</tex> waveguide Rotman lens is proposed for far-field wireless power transfer at Ka-band. The proposed system includes the Rotman lens and an array of E-plane sectoral horns, which are designed to allow beam-steering over a range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 20^{0}}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{5^{0}}$</tex> steps. The proposed design is tested via simulation, demonstrating an impedance bandwidth of 32-38GHz and beam-scanning capability over the desired scan range and the gain of up to 26.9 dBi.

articleTitle: Near field sampling compression based on matrix CUR decomposition
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We presents a near field (NF) sampling compression method based on matrix CUR decomposition. By applying CUR decomposition directly to NF data, one only needs to perform NF sampling at a small number of randomly selected sampling points and then can recover the field values of the rest of sampling points, which significantly reduces the expenditure of NF sampling. Simulations using synthetic and measurement data are presented to show the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed sampling method.

articleTitle: Broadband L-Shaped Probe Fed Suspended Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A suspended metasurface antenna with an L-shaped probe is proposed for broadband operation. A metasurface printed onto the bottom surface of a thin substrate is separated from a ground plane by an air gap with a thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.1\lambda_{0} (\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at the center operating frequency). With a compact metasurface area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.34\lambda_{0}\times 0.43\lambda_{0}$</tex>, the proposed suspended metasurface antenna can achieve an impedance bandwidth of 38.4% with a stable radiation pattern and a peak gain of 9.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Beamforming Array for Far Field Wireless Power Transfer Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a high gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> reconfigurable beamforming array of patch antennas for far-field Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) at 2.4 GHz. A reconfigurable feed network implemented with alternative microstrip lines can steer the main beam in three predefined directions: 0, −20 and +20 degrees. To increase the gain of the array four <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 1$</tex> broadside linear arrays are used with gain 10.7dBi, 10.4dBi and 10.3dBi. The two dimensional array gain in 10.7 dBi with the highest sidelobe level to be 17. dB lower.

articleTitle: An Optically Transparent Glass Absorber using a Multi-Fractal Ring Structure for Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An optically transparent metamaterial absorber is presented. First, a study regarding the metal mesh is conducted to understand the trade-off between its electrical and optical properties. Next, an optically transparent metamaterial absorber is designed using multiple fractal rings and 250 μm-spaced metal mesh. Such structure enhances both the bandwidth and absorption for oblique incident waves. Numerical simulations indicate an absorption over the frequency range of 25.54 GHz-31.40 GHz. Moreover, a stable absorption up to 45° is ascertained for both TE and TM oblique incidences.

articleTitle: A Compact Low SAR Antenna AMC-Backed for WLAN/WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, a new compact CPW-fed antenna with low SAR is designed for wireless body area network (WBAN) devices. It covers the Industrial, Science and Medical (ISM) band of 5.8 GHz. This proposed antenna is backed with an AMC reflector to enhance the gain and isolate the human body from unwanted electromagnetic radiations. To evaluate the antenna performance, the antenna system was placed on a flat phantom equivalent to the human body. The realized gain of the antenna system varies from 3.1 dBi to 10.28 dBi. In addition, the inclusion of the AMC reflector reduces considerably the SAR value to 0.115 w/kg, making the proposed antenna safe and suitable for use in WBAN applications.

articleTitle: An Exponentially Convergent Quadrature Method for Evaluating Convolutional Integrals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) and Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) related convolutional integrals can be reduced to a summation of one dimensional (1D) integrals, which are prone to numerical errors when the observation points are in the vicinity of the sources. We propose that sinh transformations be used to improve the accuracy. A variety of numerical examples show that the relative errors of the proposed method drop exponentially with respect to the number of Gauss-Legendre quadrature points.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed Convolutional Neural Network for Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The received signal strength indicator (RSSI) from wireless access points in indoor environments can be employed for user localization. The accuracy of RSSI-based localization can be greatly improved from advanced knowledge of the propagation characteristics of an environment, via extensive measurements or computationally costly simulations. This paper introduces a machine learning approach, leveraging a convolutional neural network, aimed at producing high-resolution power maps of complex indoor environments through low-cost ray-tracing simulations. The produced power maps are integrated with a k-nearest neighbors (kNN) algorithm that performs user localization. The proposed approach is successfully demonstrated in a localization case study across the floor of an office building at the University of Toronto campus.

articleTitle: Beamforming Comparison of a Multi-Mode Array with a Dipole Array of the Same Aperture Size
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A fair comparison of a multi-mode antenna array with a dipole array in terms of beamforming is presented in this paper. The comparison is based on the assumption of same array aperture and thus a different number of array elements. It is shown that this multi-mode array is able to outperform the dipole array for all scan angles. The reasons for this advantage are explored and discussed.

articleTitle: Electrically Small VHF MIMO Antenna For Underground Coal Mine Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the implementation of an electrically small MIMO antenna configuration for underground coal mine applications. The proposed MIMO antenna configuration works at VHF band. The MIMO antenna configured using two electrically small antenna elements placed orthogonally relative to each other to achieve diversity performance. A study on MIMO input impedance and mutual coupling w.r.to inter-element spacing is performed. The proposed MIMO antenna exhibits good impedance matching less than −15 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and inter-element isolation of more than 30 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{dB}$</tex> at the operating frequency. The diversity performance of the proposed MIMO investigated for realistic non-uniform (Gaussian/Uniform) indoor and outdoor propagation environments. The electromagnetic radiation safety limit for the human body from the proposed MIMO antenna is also verified using the human voxel model.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of a Wideband Implantable Peano Antenna for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact wideband implantable antenna working at industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) 2.45 GHz band is presented. The fractal geometry strategy based on the Peano curve is used to miniaturize the size of the antenna. An impedance bandwidth (BW) of 85.7 % is achieved from 1.2 to 3 GHz with overall dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{7\times 8.2\text{mm}^{2}}$</tex>. A gain value of -19.8 dBi is obtained and good omnidirectionality performance at 2.45 G Hz. These features make the antenna a good candidate for invasive biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis in Radar Cross Section of Low Profile and Conventionally Sized UHF SATCOM Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we show and compare the results in radar cross-section (RCS) between metamaterial-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\text{low}}/40$</tex> low profile tactical UHF SATCOM antenna, operates in the band of 245 MHz - 310 MHz, and conventionally <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> sized aperture. The monostatic RCS results of both differently sized apertures have been examined in the frequency range of the S-band, under both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varphi$</tex>-polarized plane wave incidence angle up to 60°. A reduction of one-tenth in antenna profile yields a considerable decrease in RCS.

articleTitle: A Compact and Dual-Band CRLH Based Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new compact and dual-band composite right left handed (CRLH) antenna is designed, simulated and measured. The antenna operates at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz respectively. CRLH unit cell consists of the interdigital capacitors to provide the series capacitance and the shunt short-circuited stub for the parallel inductance. It radiates through interdigital capacitor in the 2.4 GHz band and the via holes are used to concentrate the fields on the interdigital capacitor. In the 5 GHz band, the whole patch along with the interdigital capacitor radiates. The antenna is fed by conductor backed CPW and fabricated on FR4 substrate with a thickness of 1.6 mm. The measured results show the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of −15 dB and −20 dB at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: A novel approach for the contactless estimation of the surface impedance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A contactless method for estimating the surface impedance of piezoresistive materials is proposed. The process is performed by placing the sample under test between two waveguides separated by a fixed distance. An electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) surface is used to prevent the field leakage in the air-gap between the two waveguides. The surface impedance of the piezoresistive sheet is obtained through an inversion procedure based on a circuit representation of the junction.

articleTitle: Dual-Function Dielectric Layer Enabling Compact Wideband End-Fire Millimeter-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A design methodology to accomplish compact and wideband end-fire millimeter-wave antenna is presented. A dielectric-loaded cavity-backed slot antenna is utilized to achieve the compact design. In addition, a dielectric matching layer is employed to enable the wideband operation. The antenna achieves a voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of 2.1 from 27.4 GHz to 40.8 GHz with an antenna realized gain in the end-fire direction ranging from 4 dBi to 5.5 dBi. A compact design of 2.2 × 2 × 5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which is 0.2 × 0.18 × 0.45 λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>max where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> is the free space wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. Moreover, the antenna is fed by the microstrip line feed, which is an advantage when the connection to RFIC is considered

articleTitle: Innovative mm-Wave AiP-based Designs to Handsets: AiPiA and AiPaA
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of two innovative designs to handsets based on the millimeter-Wave (mm-Wave) antenna-in-package (AiP) solution; they are mm-Wave antennas-in-package integrating non-mm-Wave antennas (AiPiA) and mm-Wave antennas-in-package as non-mm-Wave antennas (AiPaA). The AiPiA and AiPaA designs are able to attain the attractive miniaturized 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation mobile communications (5G) total solution for antennas to handsets, which hence greatly benefits design efforts and facilitates product developments.

articleTitle: A novel almost all-angle-insensitive FSS structure for high-performance radome
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel almost all-angle-insensitive FSS structure for the high-performance radome based on strong coupled FSS (SC-FSS) is proposed in this paper. The transmission poles and zeros are always maintained at 2 GHz and 3.4 GHz separately for both TE and TM modes, even if the incident angle increases to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{88^{\circ}}$</tex>. Furthermore, a corresponding equivalent circuit model (ECM) is developed to analyze the working principle, whose simulation results have good agreement with full-wave simulation results. As a result, the proposed FSS structure is a good candidate for the high-performance radome insensitive to incident angles.

articleTitle: 360-degree beam steering antenna based on subsrate integrated frequency selective structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for designing mm-wave beam steering antennas with dual polarization and 360° azimuth beam steering angular range. To achieve 360° beam steering, we have added several new features to our previous 180° beam steering antennas based on reconfigurable substrate integrated frequency selective structures and PIN diodes. First, transitions from radial waveguides to microstrip lines are designed to feed the radiating elements. Then, the microstrip lines are bent to leave space for RF connectors. In the next step, meander-line microstrips are optimized for equal-phase and equal-amplitude excitations of the radiating elements. Finally, holes are inserted in the printed circuit board in order to place the RF connectors. Based on the proposed design methodology, a dual polarized 360° beam steering antenna operating at 28 GHz is presented. Full-wave simulation results are shown to validate the proposed concept and an antenna prototype was fabricated.

articleTitle: Unity and Diversity in Computational Electromagnetics – A Retrospective: Special Session “Towards a Unified View of Computational Electromagnetics”
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper summarizes the evolution of numerical methods in electromagnetics from a group of seemingly unrelated algorithms to a unified methodology for solving Maxwell's equations. The unified approach is based on a projective approximation of the solution in function space, employing the Method of Weighted Residuals known from the Method of Moments. It clarifies the relationship between various methods and elucidates what they have in common and what distinguishes them from each other, providing deeper insights and heralding new developments in computational electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Design of a High Gain and Miniaturized Inter-digital CPW Antenna for Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this study, an attractive compact and high gain antenna design suitable for radio-frequency identification (RFID) and energy harvesting (EH) applications in the UHF band (ultra-high frequency) is proposed. The antenna is a potential candidate for wireless applications for sub-GHz and low UHF frequency band. It is constituted of two by one an inter-digital metal structure fed by co-planar wave-guide (CPW) configuration. The size of a single element is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25 \times 35mm^{2}$</tex>. The antenna features a simple structure and small size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\times 63mm^{2}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.08 \lambda_{o}\times 0.21 \lambda_{o}$</tex>. The antenna is fabricated on a low-cost FR4 0.8mm substrate. The experimental measurements were conducted to verify the practical results with the simulation performances. The operating bandwidth of the proposed antenna is around 340 MHz and extending from 920 MHz to 1.26 GHz with reflection coefficient of 6 dB. The peak realized gain is 4 dBi and is propagated in the end-fire direction. The design simulation was accomplished using the electromagnetic HFSS software. A good matching results were obtained between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Clutter Removal for Detection of Slow-moving Targets with a mm-Wave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work tackles the problem of the detection of slow moving targets. Point-by-point subtraction and Principal Component Analysis methods were applied to mm-Wave FMCW radar measurements and compared.

articleTitle: High Gain 6X6 Patch Phased Array Antenna For Millimeter-wave 5G Applications at 28 Ghz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain 6X6 phased array patch antennas is designed for future 5 G millimeter wave. The proposed antenna array is fed by a combination of three series-parallel and vertical feeding network. The antenna design has a compact size of 46x46 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. 13 beam switched states are generated using required amplitudes and phase excitations for the antenna elements. A good scanning performance of a range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 20^{\circ}}$</tex> in horizontal and vertical axis is achieved, while maintaining a high gain of 19 dBi for all beams.

articleTitle: Novel Planar Fixed-Beam Leaky-Wave Antenna With Dual-Beam Radiation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a dual-beam fixed-beam leaky-wave antenna (LWA). It has a very simple structure, which is essentially a grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) printed on a “devil ray” shaped PCB, and almost no tuning is needed during its design. Despite from its simplicity, it has very decent performance, with measured gain around 16 dBi, return loss better than 13.1 dB, and beam scanning less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 0.75^{\mathrm{o}}}$</tex> at all frequencies from 26 GHz to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Small-And Large-Scale Strain Sensing Using Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) are arrays of conductive elements or patches that have specific reflection and transmission responses. In this work, an FSS sensor designed to measure small (0% – 0.5%) and large (0% – 5%) scale strain is presented. The proposed unit cell of the sensor consists of two passive dipoles (of different dimensions) arranged normal to one another. This was done to reduce the error of small-scale strain on the large-scale strain measurement, and vice versa. Strain sensing is achieved by monitoring the change in the resonant frequencies of the two dipoles using an interrogating signal linearly polarized and aligned with the long dimension of the element under interrogation. Simulated results indicate that the sensitivity of the sensor to small-scale strain is 15 MHz/0.1% strain and 150 MHz/1.0% strain large-scale. The error in measurement can be partially alleviated, with a remaining error of 6 MHz for both measurements.

articleTitle: Selection of Suitable Inorganic/Organic Substrate for In-Body Antenna Implants: Impact on Antenna Characteristics in Deep Tissue Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper is primarily aimed at choosing the suitable biocompatible substrate for in-body implantable antennas from a pool of commercially available inorganic polymer ceramics, polymides and organic substrate material. We first consider an in-body antenna at 2.45 GHz, and then optimize it without body phantom, for range of substrate relative permittivity variation 2.5< εr < 30. After integrating the antenna with body phantom, we monitor the antenna reflection coefficient, maximum permissible radiated power, as well as specific absorption rate (SAR) in the tissue, in order to formulate a strategy for suitable substrate material selection in Wireless Implantable Medical Devices (WIMDs)

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Ranging Using a Dual-Channel IEEE 802.11 Legacy Preamble
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a method for joint communications and wireless high-accuracy ranging using a dual-channel IEEE 802.11 waveform. The radio frequency spectrum has increasingly become more congested in recent years as the numbers of both wireless sensing and communication systems have rapidly increased. Combining sensing and communication waveforms together helps improve the spectral efficiency, but often leads to reduced sensing capabilities and involves complex signal processing. We explore the use of the IEEE 802.11 Legacy Short Training field (L-STF) combined with a two-tone waveform to improve spectral efficiency and reduce the signal processing complexity needed to interleave sensing and communication waveforms. The underlying two-tone waveform obtains near-optimal range accuracy while the L-STF modulation provides range disambiguation properties. We experimentally demonstrate a 40 MHz training field modulated with a two-tone waveform with 80 MHz tone spacing on a 5.32 GHz carrier, corresponding to two channels in the IEEE 802.11ax standard, achieving a peak-to-sidelobe level of −1.92 dB, and ranging accuracy of 4.56 cm.

articleTitle: Dual Band FSS Based on Four Arms Star Geometry for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an alternative for frequency selective surfaces (FSS) operating in multiple frequencies. The geometry is based on four arms star elements, and the structure is intended to operate at two main 5G frequencies: 700 MHz and 3.5 GHz. Details about the four arms star geometry are presented and the final design is characterized. The structure was analyzed and simulated, showing good results for both frequencies and, therefore presenting good potential for 5G related applications.

articleTitle: Monochromatic Near Field Calculation of Aperture Antenna and Its Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a study of the electromagnetic field that is created by a flat circular aperture in the near zone. The analytical method, used for calculating the impulse response function (IRF), adequately estimates the electromagnetic field intensity of the aperture antenna when a monochromatic signal is radiated. This is shown via comparison the well-known finite integration method (FIT) calculation results with analytical ones. The advantage of the analytical method in terms of computing resources is presented.

articleTitle: Calculation of Far-Field Scattering from Nonuniform Reflective Metasurfaces: A Critical Perspective
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: To design and characterize radio environments with metasurfaces, it is necessary to know the scattering properties of finite-size anomalously reflecting (phase-gradient) metasurfaces. Recently, different approaches have been proposed to tackle this problem. In this presentation, we will present a comparison between alternative analytical models. We will first derive a general formulation for the far-field scattering by reflective metasurfaces based on the Huygens principle. Then we will specify the assumptions of known models. The first model that we will study is based on the assumption that at each point of the metasurface the reflected field equals the incident field multiplied by a controllable reflection coefficient. Then we will analyze the same structure with an analytical model based on the use of macroscopic reflection coefficients following the theory of diffraction gratings. Finally, we will numerically analyze the structure and compare the results.

articleTitle: C-shaped Waveguide for Spin-dependent Propagation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a chiral waveguide design characterized by extrinsic chirality and strong transverse spin. The waveguide provides confined, spin-dependent unidirectional propagation. This means that when excited with a right-hand circularly polarized dipole, the supported waveguide mode will propagate only forward while it will reverse the direction when excited with a left-hand circularly polarized dipole. The spin density is calculated showing high transverse spin maps across the unit cell of the waveguide design. The directionality ratio is calculated to be 95%.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Structural Constraint Approach for Enhancing Electromagnetic Inversion through Acoustic Inversion
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: To take the advantages of the high resolution of acoustic inversion and the high contrast of electromagnetic (EM) inversion, a joint inversion method, named a hybrid structural constraint approach (HSCA), based on the subspace-based optimization method (SOM) is proposed, which enhances EM inversion through acoustic inversion. In this method, acoustic inversion is firstly carried out to obtain a high-resolution result. Then, the scatterers are distinguished from the background by Markov random field (MRF) method. The EM inversion is only executed in the scatterers domain and constrained by the cross-gradient function. Numerical examples validate that HSCA-SOM can obtain an EM inversion result with much higher resolution and less computation cost than other similar joint inversion methods.

articleTitle: An Improved Particle Swarm Optimization for Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with high efficiency and low time consumption is presented in this paper. The optimization adopts the method of interval prediction, and it combines multiple parameters into a new fitness value to judge the optimization direction. In order to verify the proposed optimization, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and bandwidth of a classic patch Yagi antenna are simultaneously optimized by the improved PSO method. It shows that the optimization speed is increased by 80% comparing to traditional PSO.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Compact High-Power Mesoband Generation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An assessment of a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) integrated in a high-power electromagnetic mesoband source is presented. The electric field radiated by the antenna when connected to a switched oscillator (SWO) is analyzed by numerical simulation. The DRA is easy to assemble, compact, with a diameter of 0.32λ and height of 0.17λ, and can radiate high-amplitude fields. The overall performance is comparable with bigger and bulky radiators.

articleTitle: A Circular Polarized Ku-Band Phased Array using a Triangular Lattice
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a circular polarized Ku-Band 20-element phased array. The array utilizes a triangular lattice to reduce the number of antenna elements to fill a given aperture size, while mitigating grating lobes. The phased array uses a sequentially rotated triangular lattice to achieve wide scan angles, while maintain low axial ratios (AR) and over wide bandwidths. Our array demonstrates up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50^{\circ}$</tex> scanning while maintaining an AR of less than 3 dB over a 9% fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: Conversion of Electromagnetics Courses to Synchronous Online Delivery Using Active and Problem-Based Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents and discusses conversion of undergraduate electromagnetics courses to synchronous online delivery using active learning, conceptual questions, and problem-based learning in response to the situation caused by COVID-19 pandemic. The presented approaches are generalizable and applicable to post-pandemic times as well and can be useful as part of the community discussion about transforming electromagnetics education after COVID. In addition to damage-controlling electromagnetics education given the constraints imposed by the pandemic situation, the community is also taking advantage of the opportunities presented to us by the situation and foreseeable trends.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Monopole Element Printed Quasi-Yagi Antenna using a Meandered Driven Element
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized monopole element printed quasi-Yagi antenna (PQYA) with broad bandwidth (BW) is presented. The length of the driven element is meandered to reduce the lateral size of the antenna. The lengths of the reflector and director are not meandered and kept just enough to ensure their respective functions. Through this design, an overall size reduction of 32 % has been achieved without compromising the other electrical characteristics. A simple 50Ω microstrip line feeds the proposed antenna. Measured results show that the fabricated prototype has broad impedance BW from 1.52-2.31 GHz (41.3%) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert \leq-10$</tex> dB. The maximum gain of the antenna is 4.5 dBi, with the total efficiency reaches up to 83.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. The cross-polarization levels are below -22 dB and a front-to-back ratio greater than 10 dB in the entire BW. Moreover, the gain variation is within 0.8 dBi over the operating band. The measurement results are consistent with simulated results.

articleTitle: Towards A New Figure of Merit for Reflector Antenna Based Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A synthesis imaging pipeline for radio interferometric arrays is presented, developed to enable the direct mapping of antenna performance metrics to image quality. A brief overview of synthesis imaging for radio astronomy is given, providing background to the main functions in the developed pipeline. The features of the pipeline are discussed and an example of results presented, showing dirty images produced from complex visibilities. The pipeline is simplified to allow fast enough evaluation time for in-line optimization in reflector antenna design loops.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Band Variable Linear Polarization Rotator With High Cross-polarization Discrimination For Scanned Beams
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design and performance of an ultra-wide band (UWB) variable linear polarization (LP) rotator with high cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) for wide azimuth scanned beams are presented here. The rotator is a cascade of two UWB 90° meanderline polarizers (MLP) and a double linear grid layer. This device is placed in front of a dual-polarized phased array to convert either the vertical or horizontal polarized scanned beam into one with arbitrary polarization. Worst case XPD observed at 45° scan with 45° polarization rotation angle is more than 35 dB.

articleTitle: SbD-Synthesis of Electromagnetic Smart Skins Enabling Optimal Wireless City Coverage
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of large-scale electromagnetic (EM) smart skins covering the facades of buildings and enabling optimal wireless city coverage is addressed. According to the smart electromagnetic environment (SEE) paradigm, the complex scattering phenomena arising within a urban scenario are profitably exploited to enhance the overall quality-of-service (QoS). Owing to the very large electrical dimensions of the scenario at hand, a suitable System-by-Design (SbD) approach is proposed in order to efficiently optimize the EM characteristics of the smart skins so that the field strength is enhanced within selected non line-of-sight (NLOS) regions. A proof-of-concept is shown to check the effectiveness of such a new design framework.

articleTitle: Contention Based Medium Access Control Protocol for Point-To-Multipoint Backhaul Networks in the 3.65 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Unrestricted Contention-Based Protocol (CBP) implemented in release 1.1 complies with the FCC requirements for the 3.65 – 3.7 GHz band. This feature allows the adjacent networks to share the same (unlicensed) radio channel with other wireless communication devices. The protocol is based on a collision-avoidance mechanism similar to CSMA/CA (Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance) used in IEEE 802.11. The rule of CBP is to listen before any attempt to transmit over the air and defer the transmission if the interference level exceeds a certain threshold. This paper evaluates the performance of the CBP protocol for point-to-multi points backhaul networks.

articleTitle: Projection-assisted Indoor Attenuation Parameter Compression based on Curve Fitting
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Channel state information (CSI) describes the at-tenuation factor of signals on each propagation path. This paper proposes a oblique projection assisted indoor attenuation parameter compression algorithm based on curve fitting. First, a oblique projection operator is constructed to process the original CSI data. Then the curve fitting based on the least-squares algorithm is performed to realize the compression. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has a considerable compression ratio under the same fitting residual.

articleTitle: Small 3D-Dipole Antenna for RFID Tag Mounted on a Full Container of Water
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This study developed a novel 3D-dipole antenna for radio frequency identification (RFID) that mounted on a container of water. Conjugate matching of the resistance and inductive reactance of the antenna to the desired impedance of Alien Higgs-4 chip (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.2-j148.5\Omega$</tex> at 925 MHz) can be performed by simply tuning the C-arm length of the 3D-dipole. After analysis and optimization of the tag antenna has an overall size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$32\times 25\times 3.2\ \text{mm}^{3} (0.10\ \lambda_{0}\times 0.08\ \lambda_{0}\times 0.01\ \lambda_{0})$</tex>, the fabricated tag mounted on a container of water testing of an RFID reader with an effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of 4.0 W yield the maximum read ranges in an outdoor environment of 5.3 and 3.9 m, respectively. Measurement data agreed with simulation results.

articleTitle: A W-band Dielectric Loaded Antenna with Sum and Difference Beams for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a W-band dielectric loaded antenna (DLA) with sum and difference beams for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Compare with the metallic horn antenna with equivalent structure, the DLA enhanced the gain of the sum beam and reduce the beam width of the difference beams. As a result, the peak gain of the sum beam is 17.12dB, and the null depths of the difference beams are as low as -41.33 dB. The proposed antenna could be fabricated by the low-cost 3D printing technology to have a compact light-weight structure. It enables the UAV with the function of tracking the targets in high precision.

articleTitle: Frequency-Selective Structure With One Reflection Band And Two-sided Absorption Bands
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An absorptive frequency-selective reflection structure with one reflective band and two-sided absorptive bands is presented in this paper. The structure, equivalent circuit model and working principle are investigated. Simulation results show that a reflective band at 5.86-6.83 GHz and two absorptive bands at 3.21-4.92 GHz and 7.41-10.99 GHz are obtained.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Wireless Security Through the Rotation of Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wireless communication system with rotating linearly polarized antennas is built and tested as a method for increasing physical layer security. Controlling the linear polarization angle from 0° to 180° yields bit error rates greater than 20% for 40° of rotation.

articleTitle: Non-Radiating Sources: A New Powerful Recipe for Designing Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Innovative concepts and strategies for the design of reflectarray antennas are discussed in this work. More in detail, the synthesis of the antenna surface currents is addressed from an unconventional point-of-view, exploiting the inverse scattering (IS) theory and the non-uniqueness of the solution dictated by the existence of non-radiating (NR) current contributions. Thanks to such an approach, the designer is given the capability of imposing specific constraints on the geometry and implementation of the synthesized layout without any compromise on the desired far-field radiation features. An illustrative result is shown to provide the reader with an example of the effectiveness and potentialities of such a novel design framework.

articleTitle: Depolarization Characteristics of Rough Materials at mm-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A RT (ray tracing) simulation and a measurement campaign are carried out to investigate the depolarization characteristic of diffuse scattering over 40 GHz to 50 GHz for granite, rock and plastic carpet. The results indicate that rough surface of the construction materials has a great influence on the received power and polarization mode at millimeter wave bands, which should not be neglected.

articleTitle: A Study of Plasmons in Optical Nano-Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An analytical model of the response of a free electron gas within a nano-antenna interacting with an electromagnetic wave with normal incidence was developed. By examining the longitudinal oscillations of the plasma in the nano-antenna, a relationship was obtained for the wavelengths generated by the plasmons in the nano-antenna. The nearfield amplitudes are expressed in an analytical way. Finally, the amplitudes of the scattered fields at a given distance from the nano-antenna are compared. It was shown how the intensity of the dispersed Electromagnetic Field decays as a function of the excitation modes and we see that these can be functions in the visible regime, a property sought in these devices for energy applications.

articleTitle: Tightly Coupled Dipole Array with In-Line Guanella Transformer and Balun
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A 3.6:1 bandwidth, efficient, single-pol tightly coupled dipole array antenna fed using an in-line Guanella transformer is presented. The array is designed to operate from 0.57 – 2.05 GHz with radiation and aperture efficiencies of > 88% and > 99%, respectively. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 3$</tex> when scanning in elevation out to ±45° is demonstrated. The dipole elements are integrated with the balun on a two-layer printed circuit board (PCB) with an edge launch SMA coaxial connection per element. This integrated balun design and transformer maintains the simplicity and the low-profile nature of the dipole array. A unit cell design is presented to validate the concept.

articleTitle: Time Reversal Based Multi-Point Focusing Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of multi-user receiving power, we present a time reversal based multi-point focusing wireless power transfer (TR-MF-WPT) method, which can simultaneously power multiple devices. Based on this method, a TR-MF-WPT system is built. Experiments show that the system can not only power multi-users at the same time, but also selectively power users that need power transfer.

articleTitle: Flexible Passive Smart Skin Temperature Sensor for Remote Sensing in Structural Health Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, for the first time, the authors present a Smart Skin based temperature sensor for Structural Health Monitoring. The sensor topology employed is flexible, passive, form-factor, surface agnostic, sensor design enabling local tem-perature monitoring. The static operating frequency of this sensor is 23.26 GHz with a total foot print of 7.5 cm X 4.5 cm enabling a compact form factor solution to wireless passive sensing. The temperature response of the Smart-Skin based sensor is reported with an estimated sensitivity of 2.16 MHz/°C providing a highly sensitive, chip-less, flexible realization for Structural Health Monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Can We Improve on the Dipole Antenna for Space-based Low Frequency Radio Astronomy?
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the shortcomings of dipoles in space-based low frequency radio astronomy. It is at these frequencies that it is expected to uncover more information about the beginning of the universe, the Dark Ages. At this moment there is a 5 m tripole setup, part of the Netherlands-China Low Frequency Explorer (NCLE) on Earth-Moon-L2 Halo Orbit. However, the dipole is limited in terms of bandwidth, size and impedance. To further increase the sensitivity, more advanced structures are needed which can be packed in the same volume. This paper will present multiple solutions to the problem in the form of inflatable antennas and the usage of shape memory alloys which are both viable options. A future solution is a combination of both for packing efficiency and rigidization.

articleTitle: UAV Positioning Based on L-Shaped Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In recent years, the “black flight” of UAVs has brought many security threats to people. Therefore, there is an urgent need for a UAV positioning technology to improve the efficiency of airspace supervision. This paper proposes a UAV positioning technology based on the L-shaped antenna array, which has better performance in estimating the direction of arrival. This technology utilizes an L-shaped antenna array to receive UAV signals, and the Recursively Applied and Projected (RAP) - Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm is selected to estimate azimuth of arrival (AOA) and elevation of arrival (EOA). Then multiple receivers (A receiver represents an L-shaped antenna array) are used to cross-locate the UAV. Finally, Wireless Insite (WI) software was applied to simulate the flight scene and signal of the UAV, and the 2D and 3D positioning errors were 0.48m and 2.4m, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband Patch Loaded Substrate-Integrated Cavity Backed Slot Array for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A broadband patch loaded substrate-integrated cavity backed slot antenna (SICBAS) is proposed for 5G millimeter-wave (mmW) communications. The proposed antenna utilizes a compact symmetrical substrate-integrated cavity (SIC) to excite <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 4$</tex> E-shaped patches through coupling slots, and it achieves an impedance bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert S_{11}\vert < -10\text{dB})$</tex> of 38.2-53.8 GHz with a gain of 13-15.4 dBi over 41–55 GHz. Incorporating with a 16-way power divider, the SICBAS is extended to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> array to achieve a higher gain greater than 22.5 dBi over 40–51 GHz. The proposed SICBSA array is fabricated and measured, which demonstrates that it is very promising for mmW broadband applications.

articleTitle: A Differential Dual-Polarized Laminated Resonator Antenna With Backed SIW Cavity Excitation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave dual-polarized Laminated Resonator Antenna (LRA) differentially fed by a backed SIW cavity. The degenerate diagonal modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TE}_{120}$</tex> and TE210 are excited in the square SIW cavity by the two pairs of differential signals, respectively. By etching a cross-shaped slot on the top surface of the SIW cavity, the LRA element is successfully stimulated and works at the dominant modes TE101 and TE011 for dual-polarized radiation. Combining the modes of the coupling slot and the LRA, the proposed antenna shows a wideband differential impedance bandwidth of 20.37% with low cross-polarization and high port-to-port isolation.

articleTitle: Mesh Sharing Based Fast Parameter Sweep for EM Simulation Accelerated by H-matrix
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose the mesh sharing based method for fast electromagnetic (EM) simulation that involves parameter sweep. The proposed method leverages mesh sharing for the common portion of the designing space, which has to be processed separately from scratch without special solutions. The system matrices resulted from discretizing the governing integral equation for different parameters would have a large proportion of identical elements thanks to mesh sharing. Instead of explicit extraction from the super-matrix, we propose the implicit approach that integrates elegantly into the iterative solver and avoids redundant computation in the meantime. Besides, the proposed method is compatible with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mathcal{H}}$</tex>-matrix framework, which is adopted to accelerate each single round EM simulation. Numerical examples show that our proposed method leads to accurate results for different configurations with single round <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}$</tex>-matrix construction, which demonstrates its effectiveness and efficiency for fast parameter sweep and design.

articleTitle: Wideband Millimeter-wave Slot Antenna Using Dielectric Cover for Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a wideband millimeter-wave slot antenna using dielectric cover to enhance the gain for wireless communications. The proposed antenna adopts ladder-shaped slot as the radiating aperture, which is fed by the substrate integrated waveguide. The proposed antenna achieves wide impedance bandwidth of 30.4% from 53GHz to 72GHz, and enhances the peak gain from 8.59dBi to 13.14dBi when using the dielectric cover. It possesses of small radiating aperture, compact structure and light weight, which is suitable to be applied to the millimeter-wave wireless communications.

articleTitle: FDTD modeling of transparent conducting oxide metasurfaces for near infrared reflection control
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, transparent conducting oxide (TCO)/silver(Ag)/TCO nanodisk arrays on Ethylene tetrafluoroethylene (ETFE) substrate have been modelled and compared with silver nanodisk arrays as benchmark. The radii of the proposed geometry is tuned for near infrared reflection applications between 750–1500 nm. Reduction in thicknesses of transparent conducting layers reduce dips in the transmittance spectra that is attributed to reduction of normalised absorbed optical power due to the transparent conducting layers. The TCO/Ag/TCO geometry is optimized for high transmittance of upto 95% in the visible range (400–700 nm).

articleTitle: Common Mode Suppression Technique for Dual-Band Array Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A method for mutual coupling reduction is proposed and demonstrated for a dual band array environment which operates from 698–960 MHz and 1.695-2.700 GHz. Upon the excitation of the low-band (LB) dipole in the baseline design, common mode (CM) currents are induced on the mid-band (MB) dipole feed stems which lead to unwanted radiated emissions. The proposed design technique improves the LB radiation characteristics in the presence of the MB sub-arrays by suppression of the CM currents. Improvements in beamwidth stability, cross-polar radiation, front-to-back ratio, and gain are demonstrated through simulation and measurement. The proposed technique improves the measured LB system gain from 4.33 dBi to 6.92 dBi at 805 MHz, a 2.59 dB improvement.

articleTitle: Beam Steerable HF Inverted V Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Due to variation of High frequency as well as distance between transmitting and receiving stations, it is not always feasible to change the height of wide band HF dipole antenna in order to adjust radiation take off angle. The paper provides effective solution for adjusting beam take off angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30$</tex> degree electronically without physical height variation of HF antenna. Tilting angle for antenna radiation pattern has been controlled by gradually varying the capacitor value positioned at one end of dipole keeping fixed value of parallel inductor.

articleTitle: Urban and Suburban Bay Area Radio Environment for the UAV communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: UAV wireless communication using unlicensed bands, avoiding interference from other wireless systems is an important issue. In the unlicensed bands, many kinds of radio systems are sharing the band. This paper describes the UAV airspace's radio environment's evaluation results in the 920 MHz and 2400 MHz in the urban and suburban bay area. The measuring equipment was installed in a building with a height of 100 m or more for about one week to evaluate the radio environment. The measurement results show little difference between the urban and the suburban bay areas at the 920 MHz band. At 2400 MHz, the received power of the urban area is 16 dB higher at 0.9 points of CDF (cumulative distribution function) than the bay area. It is assumed that this reason is due to building density and height in the surrounding environment.

articleTitle: A Pattern/Polarization Diversity Antenna Based on Three-mode Composite Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this communication, a pattern and polarization diversity antenna is proposed for millimeter-wave application. The multi-mode transmission line is adopted to drive the three radiation mode, which means the three different radiation modes totally share the radiation aperture and excitation transmission line. The multi-mode composite transmission line confine the fields of all transmission modes in the same space, which greatly simplifies the complex feed network of conventional antennas with diversified radiation patterns. A prototype working at 28 GHz is designed with a overlapped bandwidth of 13.8%. Hollow beam radiation, vertically polarized end-fire radiation and horizontally polarized end-fire radiation are respectively excited by TEM-mode, TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l0</inf>-mode and a special folded TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2o</inf>-mode.

articleTitle: Rotationally Symmetric Antennas Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a method analyzing rotationally symmetric patch antennas is presented based on characteristic mode analysis (CMA). The symmetric meshes are carried out on a square patch, a regular pentagon patch and, a regular hexagon patch antenna. Generalized eigenvalue equations are used to deduce the eigenvalue of some characteristic modes (CMs) follow the same distribution. Moreover, the density of these modal currents demonstrates rotational symmetry as the antenna shapes. These modes are degenerate modes (DMs). A loop antenna loading lumped inductive components is designed to split the DMs for circular polarization (CP). The loop antenna of measured axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 8.3% ranging from 2.3 to 2.5 GHz is fabricated. The simulated and measured results agree well.

articleTitle: A Full Analog Power-Based Direction-of-Arrival Sensor
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a simple direction-of-arrival (DoA) sensor for power-based direction-finding is introduced. The sensor consists of two arbitrary antennas connected to a network of three Wilkinson power dividers (WPDs) working at 2.6 GHz, which separates the received power into three output ports. The DoA is deduced from these powers using simple calculations. The proposed sensor was tested and yielded less than 5 degrees of error.

articleTitle: Measurement of compact MIMO antennas with 0.3 \lambda$ spacing under different polarization and coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Channel performance of a compact dual-port MIMO antenna system with element spacing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3\ \lambda$</tex> in 2.4 GHz is measured and analyzed, in line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) scenarios under different polarization and mutual coupling. Results show that the channel capacity of the antenna with electromagnetic band gap (EBG) with lower mutual coupling is greater than that of the antenna without EBG with higher mutual coupling. Especially when the antenna with EBG is placed horizontally in the through-the-wall NLOS scenario, its channel capacity is the largest, which is 97.34% of the independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) Rayleigh channel capacity. In addition, in the scenario of through-the-wall, for the antennas with same coupling, the channel capacity of the horizontally polarized antenna is larger than that of the vertically polarized one, and the correlation coefficient and condition number are reduced. In conclusion, the performance of the MIMO system is closely related to the coupling, polarization and propagation environment of the antenna and their interactions.

articleTitle: Implantable Antenna Design for Surface-Wave Based In-Body to On-Body Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Adapted design methods for implantable antennas intended for on-body communication (e.g. for a pacemaker-smartphone link) are presented. Fundamental feature for optimal antennas are derived on basis of the Green's function for in-body to on-body propagation. Through the antenna characterization with dedicated on-body antenna parameters, the path loss im-provements of optimized antennas can be precisely predicted.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Radio Coverage in Tunnel Boring Machine
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
