abstract: Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) is a machine used to excavate tunnels. There are kinds of demands of communication services in the TBM, such as video surveillance, operating state monitoring and voice communications. To meet the above service requirements, a WiFi system is built in TBM. There are two schemes to realize the tunnel radio coverage, one is by using antenna and the other is by using leaky feeder cable (LFC). To analyze the radio coverage quality of the two schemes, a measurement system is built in the TBM. Based on the measurement results, we conclude that antenna is suitable for radio coverage for the TBM which less than 50m while the LFC can provide better and more uniform radio coverage for the TBM with big size.

articleTitle: Unified GPU Parallel Framework Based on Discontinuous Galerkin Method
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we designed a unified parallel DG framework. Based on the characteristics of DG discretization, we built a preprocessing part in the framework. Then designed different kernel functions to match different numerical problems, such as Maxwell's equation and Euler's equation. A speed-up of 160 has been achieved over an equivalent CPU code. Compared with CPU code, the computing efficiency has been greatly improved.

articleTitle: Robust Microwave Transport via Nontrivial Duality-Based Rhombic Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A simplified model of a metallic spin-type photonic topological insulator on a rhombic lattice is presented and analyzed. Instead of the more commonly used hexagonal unit cells, a reduced symmetry rhombus is employed, which is both simpler and allows for easier integration into more traditional microwave systems. The non-trivial nature of the transport is shown via full-wave simulations of interface models, which demonstrate strong unidirectional excitation and robustness to sharp turns.

articleTitle: Statistical Characterization of Signals Backscattered from Stationary Ground Targets for Radar Refractivity Estimation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a statistical analysis of the radar signals backscattered by stationary ground targets is presented. Correct identification of stationary targets is a fundamental step for radar-based refractivity estimation algorithms. Current target identification techniques are based on measurements derived from the phase of the received signals, but they are often affected by atmospheric variations. This usually causes erroneous identifications. The received signal amplitude is virtually insensitive to these atmospheric variations, so taking into account amplitude information to discriminate between stationary and non-stationary targets should improve the results. Additionally, knowledge of the statistical characteristics of the received signals helps to analyse and improve the performance of the refractivity estimation algorithms.

articleTitle: Intervention to enhance PsyCap in EM courses
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The unprecedented challenges arising from the COVID-19 pandemic have highlighted the value of personal resources, such as optimism and resilience, that equip people to successfully adapt to stress and uncertainty. Within higher education, this suggests that employability skills should incorporate personal resource development, in addition to occupational skill/knowledge acquisition and professional network expansion. This paper outlines a framework for developing students' personal resources of hope, self-efficacy, resilience, and optimism (i.e., psychological capital). The framework can be easily embedded within the engineering curriculum and implemented in both face-to-face and online delivery modes. The framework aims to improve students' personal resources, immediately impacting their academic performance, engagement, and satisfaction in the short-term. In the long-term, it aims to provide students with key employability skills linked to individual and organisational success in their future career. We provide guidelines on how to embed such a framework into an electromagnetics engineering course.

articleTitle: Fork-shape Wideband Monopoles for Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates two low-profile wideband fork-shape monopole designs for microwave imaging. The antennas have stable near-field radiation when in contact with skin tissues and bandwidth of around 3GHz. The designs, with low profile and fabrication cost, demonstrate great potentials to be used in future microwave imaging system.

articleTitle: E-band Point-to-Multipoint Antennas Based On Wide-Scan Focal Plane Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An antenna-system concept is explored where a wide-scan focal plane array antenna is used for point-to-multipoint communications at E-band. As a preliminary study the directivity is investigated for a beam scanning to boresight for several array sizes and inter-element spacings and the azimuthal cuts are compared to the ETSI class-III radiation pattern envelope.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low-Profile Fabry-Perot Antenna Employing a Multi-Resonant Metasurface Based Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband, low-profile Fabry-Perot antenna with a multi-resonant metasurface superstrate is presented. The superstrate consists of a patch-type and an aperture-type metasurface printed on the top and bottom surfaces of a Rogers 5880 dielectric, respectively. A small-size version of a waveguide fed Fabry-Perot antenna achieved a measured 3-dB gain bandwidth of over 40% without resorting to multi -layered superstrates. In addition, a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 24% was also achieved. The aperture efficiency in both cases is 64% for an aperture size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1.7 \lambda_{\mathrm{C}} \times 1.7 \lambda_{\mathrm{C}}}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{C}}$</tex> is the free space wave length at the central frequency of 11.8 GHz. Two prototypes were fabricated and tested to confirm the design concepts.

articleTitle: Power Delay Profile Analysis of 28 GHz Indoor Channel using Massive 3D-MIMO Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Taking the advantage of super wide bandwidth, millimeter-wave (mm-wave), is regarded as a promising technique for the fifth generation (5G) mobile communication system and beyond. In this paper, an indoor channel measurement campaign in large conference hall environment is introduced, using virtual uniform rectangular array (URA) to obtain spatial channel characteristic at 28 GHz in various antenna array. The delay resolution was 0.25 ns from the signal bandwidth of 4 GHz, and the array characteristics were achieved by rotating vertically polarized biconical omnidirectional antenna at side of transmitter. The results of the experiment indicate that the power delay profile (PDP) has obvious energy fluctuation along the array direction in the delay lobe with obvious energy. All our preliminary results reveal on the essence of channel array characteristic.

articleTitle: Body-to-Antenna Gap Effect on a UHF Wearable Textile Antenna Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The effect of gaps in-between a human body and a wearable textile RFID antenna operating at 923 MHz is investigated. Due to a high isolation provided by a ground plane, the resonant frequency of the antenna is only slightly altered. The antenna gain and communication range increase to the highest value at a quarter-wave length gap between the antenna and the human body, then decrease when the antenna is moved further.

articleTitle: A Time-domain Carrier Generation Rate Model for Optoelectronic Device Simulations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The nonlinear interactions between electromagnetic fields and carriers in optoelectronic devices call for a multiphysics simulation approach to be carried out in the time domain. The widely used Poynting vector-based carrier generation rate model leads to an unphysical divergent solution when strong low-frequency fields are generated by moving carriers. This work proposes a material absorption-based carrier generation rate model for time-domain simulation of optoelectronic devices. The optoelectronic material is described by a Lorentz dispersion model with poles in the optical frequency range and negligible absorption at lower frequencies. The instantaneous optical absorption, which is computed from the polarization current density, is used to obtain the generation rate. Numerical examples show that the proposed method is more accurate than the Poynting vector-based model and is stable even when the generated lower-frequency fields are strong.

articleTitle: Impact of Phase Shifter Design on Beam Squinting in Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Phased array technique is essential for beam-forming and beam-steering in mmWave applications like radar, imaging and 5G. Beam squinting in a phased array is one of the limiting factors to support wide bandwidth operation. This paper discusses the impact of phase shifter design choices on beam squinting in the phased array. Although true time delay circuits can circumvent beam squinting, it becomes impossible when the array size becomes larger as the large slope of phase versus frequency within the bandwidth crosses 360 degrees (1 carrier cycle). A look-up table based reconfigurable phase shifter is proposed to reduce the beam squinting over a large bandwidth and the method is validated by extensive phased array simulation.

articleTitle: Phase of Radiation From a Square Principal Source Region
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The radiation from a square-shaped principal radiation source ring (Sq-PriSoR) is simulated using a metaloop antenna supporting a traveling wave current with dual propagation phase constants (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta < 0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta > 0$</tex>). It is found that the phase progression as a function of azimuth angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> does not change in a perfectly linear fashion. It is also found that the phase progression singularly behaves when the Sq-PriSoR has a loop length of two guided wavelengths, depending on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta/k_{0}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k_{0}$</tex> being the free-space phase constant. As an example, the phase progression for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta/k_{0}=+0.5$</tex> is demonstrated; the gradient of the phase progression is changed at specific depression angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta_{\Gamma}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Towards Solution of Integral Equations in Electromagnetics on Quantum Computers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present some of the fundamental methods in quantum computing for matrix equations, framed in terms of their applicability to solution of integral equations in electromagnetics. In particular, we describe the HHL algorithm for matrix inversion and matrix vector products, as well as techniques of Hamiltonian simulation for general matrices.

articleTitle: A Vasculature Anatomy Inspired Flexible Slot Antenna for Continuous Non-invasive Glucose Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this study, we introduce a vasculature-anatomy-inspired sensor for non-invasive continuous glucose monitoring. The sensor is based on a flexible slot-antenna that can be integrated inside a wearable glove, and enables sufficient penetration of the radiated electromagnetic waves in order to wirelessly monitor blood glucose variations. Serum-based experiments demonstrate high fidelity across the diabetic glucose range [10mg/dl – 500mg/dl]. Furthermore, human studies exhibit clinical accuracy of 98%, between the reference glucose levels and the sensor's output, in twenty-one subjects who underwent a total of sixty-three oral glucose tolerance tests.

articleTitle: A Dual Power Weighted Clustering Algorithm for Indoor Millimeter-Wave 3D MIMO Channel
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual power weighted clustering algorithm based on spectral clustering is proposed for indoor millimeter wave (mm Wave) three-dimension multiple input multiple output (3D MIMO) wireless channels in this paper. The proposed algorithm performs power weighting in the construction of similarity matrix and the calculation of multipath component distance (MCD) respectively. The results show that compared with the traditional K-means clustering and spectral clustering (SC) algorithms, the proposed algorithm can cluster multi-dimensional channel parameters accurately and better characterize the characteristics of indoor mmWave 3D MIMO wireless channels.

articleTitle: AI-Assisted Computationally-Efficient Global Optimization for Inverse Scattering
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The fully non-linear inverse scattering problem (ISP) is addressed as a global optimization problem and solved with high computational efficiency. Towards this end, a novel system-by-design (SbD) approach is proposed leveraging on the suitable interconnection of functional blocks aimed at (i) “smartly” defining a limited-dimensionality yet highly-flexible set of degrees-of-freedom (DoFs), (ii) formulating a suitable cost function to minimize, and (iii) integrating a global optimization approach based on evolutionary algorithms (EAs) with a computationally-fast digital twin (DT) of the accurate (but time-consuming) full-wave solver, which is adaptively “reinforced” while guiding the optimization towards the global optimum. An illustrative example is shown to assess the effectiveness and the high computational efficiency of the proposed inversion method.

articleTitle: A Pure-Water Inverted-L Antenna With Frequency Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel pure-water antenna with an inverted-L structure and frequency reconfigurability. It consists of a transparent double-layer resin container with water, a ground plane and a probe feed inserting into the container. The inverted-L structure of transparent container is exquisitely designed to shape the liquid. By controlling the filling status of water, i.e., only occupying inner layer (state 1) or the whole container (state 2), the radius of water rod is altered, which results in frequency reconfigurability. The radiation principle is based on the high-order mode of dielectric waveguide. Reflection coefficients of these two different states have been here provided. It is found that the working frequency can be tuned from 1.1 to 1.86 GHz. It should be mentioned that more layers and thinner layer thickness can be used to achieve continuous and wide tuning range from 1.1 to 2.2 GHz. The proposed antenna shows advantages of low cost, low profile, wide frequency tuning range and broadside radiation.

articleTitle: Beamforming Experiment of Time-Modulated Array Using Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Time-modulated array (TMA) has been investigated to achieve ultra-low side lobe pattern. We have proposed a time-modulated array using phase shifters. In this method, a desired pattern can be achieved in a time average procedure by temporally controlling of each element phase. It can be also used to compensate amplitude and phase excitation errors in phased arrays. In this paper, the effectiveness of the proposed method is confirmed by experiments using an active phased array.

articleTitle: Quad Band Corrugated Horn and Smooth-Wall Profiled Horn as Reflector Antenna Feeds
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The performance of the corrugated horn and the smooth-wall profiled horn as extended C- and Ku- band reflector feed is investigated in this paper. The corrugated horn exhibits low cross-polar levels and sidelobes across all 4 bands and enables the cross-polar discrimination (XPD) within the -1dB beamwidth of the secondary patterns to be met. The smooth-walled horn shows higher cross-polar levels and sidelobes but the resulting secondary patterns still marginally meets the required XPD level. The secondary pattern gains for both feed types meet the nominal requirements with those from the corrugated feed showing higher gain at C-band but have similar gain at Ku-band.

articleTitle: Elliptic Stripline Resonator Antenna on Glass-Epoxy Substrates for X-band Circular Polarization Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact circular polarization array antenna. 4-antenna array is taken to compose 64-antenna array on Glass-Epoxy substrates <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon \mathrm{r}\ 4.6,\ \text{tan}\ \delta$</tex> 0.010. 4-antenna array is made by orthogonal arrangement, parallel feeding, and the minimum length of feeding wire. 16-antenna array is composed to minimize feeding length and loss by high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tan}\ \delta$</tex> under the synchronous condition of each antenna. By 3D computer simulation, wideband characteristics were obtained as axial ratio less than 2dB, directive gain 21.8 dBi or more, and the size is the 162 mm width. This configuration contributes to reduce the cost of easy chemical processing.

articleTitle: A Monolithic, Spherical Beamsteering Strategy based on Heterogeneous Antenna-on-Surfaces (AoS) for Beyond 5G Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new design philosophy denoted as Antenna-on-Surfaces (AoS) to maximize the beamsteering coverage for multi-faced mobile devices operating at mmWave/THz spectrum. The proposed AoS enables the implementation of conformal, monolithic phased-array systems by collectively combining different surfaces comprising a mobile device. The AoS is exemplified through the integration of antenna-on-display (AoD) and antenna-in-package (AiP) situated on the front and back faces of the device, which can greatly improve the spherical coverage CDF. The fabricated prototypes demonstrate spherical, dual-polarized, beamforming, and beamsteering capabilities with four independent main beam directions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\pm z-\boldsymbol{\text{axes}/+x}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+y$</tex> axes) in 5G mm Wave bands of n257/n258 (24.25–29.5 GHz) and n260 (37–40 GHz) spectrum. The system-level simulation clearly demonstrates that a fully-integrated AoS prototype significantly enhances the spherical coverage CDF of UE by more than 1 dB in all percentile ranges with fewer transceivers.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Dipole Antenna fed by Dual Quadrature Hybrid Couplers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) dipole antenna fed by dual quadrature hybrid couplers (QHCs) is presented in this paper. In a conventional CP antenna, such as a sequentially rotated structure, the electrical length of the line connecting the radiating elements changes as the frequency changes. A modified QHC with minimal variation in the phase and amplitude difference between the output ports over a wide frequency range is used to achieve wide AR bandwidth and stable radiation patterns. The antenna with a compact dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.42\lambda_{\mathrm{o}}\times 0.42\lambda_{\mathrm{o}}\times 0.004\lambda_{\mathrm{o}}$</tex> at 6 GHz. has −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 4.3-7.6 GHz, the 3-dB AR bandwidth of 4.9-7.9 GHz, and the 3-dB gain bandwidth of 5.0-7.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-polarization phase retrieval in near field far-field transformation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In near field far-field transformation (NFFFT), accurate recovery of the current distribution is subjected to the phase measurement. Phase retrieval is an alternative way to recover the current distribution by utilizing the magnitude-only near field sampling data. In phase retrieval algorithm, sufficient independent measurement data are required. Multi-polarization algorithm is employed to generate different current distribution, then, obtaining more independent near field data. Experimental validations of a numeric examples show its potentialities and interest.

articleTitle: Analysis of Scattered Fields by an Impedance Sphere Coated with Multilayered Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the formulation for the far scattered field due to the plane wave incident on the impedance sphere coated with multiple layers of dielectric is presented. The expression for far scattered fields is derived using the Debye potential and generalized reflection coefficient. The impedance boundary condition is used to derive the local reflection coefficient from the impedance sphere. The result obtained from the proposed formulation is also verified through simulated results.

articleTitle: Development of a Practical Ray-Tracing Program for Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Ray tracing technique has been widely used in radio propagation modeling. We develop a graduate course dedicated to the fundamental theory and hands-on applications of ray tracing algorithms. The goal of this one-semester course is to help students build a ray tracing tool that can be of practical value. We found that, with proper guidance, students can develop a MATLAB code that performs key functions of ray tracing in a realistic outdoor city environment.

articleTitle: The Hybrid Embedded Domain Decomposition Method for Scattering by Bi-anisotropic Objects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An embedded domain decomposition method based on the finite element method and boundary element method is presented to solve scattering by bi-anisotropic objects. This method ensures the field continuity of different subdomains through the volume equivalence principle, and ensures the continuity of the boundary conditions of the subdomains through Robin transmission conditions. Numerical results are used to verify of the method.

articleTitle: A Near-Omnidirectional, Low-Profile, Broadband, Metamaterial Absorber Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile, broadband metamaterial absorber with the advantage of near-omnidirectional absorption for TM polarization, is developed based on characteristic mode analysis (CMA). By utilizing CMA to synthesize omnidirectional radiation pattern of the absorber's unit-atom under full PEC condition, the developed absorber can then convert the omnidirectional radiation pattern into near-omnidirectional absorption pattern based on dissipation tailoring. The developed absorber is three-dimensional, and its top layer is patch-type with broadband and angle-stable absorption within small incident angles. And the middle part is a lossy pillar to provide broadband absorption at large incident angles. The simulated results demonstrate that, in the frequency range of 1.2-3.0 GHz, corresponding to the FBW of 85.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, the absorption of TE-polarized wave is over 90 % when the incident angle is less than 40°. For TM polarization incident wave, the absorption is over 90% when the incident angle is less than 80°.

articleTitle: Compact Antenna with Enhanced Filtering Capabilities by Using a Novel Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel structure is proposed to feed a patch antenna. This structure has filter characteristics that affect the matching properties of the antenna. The aim of this antenna structure is to relax the specifications of the antenna filters in future massive MIMO (mMIMO) communication systems. Simulation and measurement results are shown to quantify improved performance characteristics and validate the concept.

articleTitle: Planar Phased Array Design for Quantum Free Space Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a design approach for optical phased arrays for quantum communication applications. The proposed scheme aims at reducing the complexity of the array architecture while handling very large element spacing due to the technological constraints of programmable photonic circuits. The methodology exploits radio frequency phased array techniques based on evolutionary algorithms for the optimization of the array geometry, minimizing the number of antennas while complying with quantum communication applications requirements in terms of side lobe levels and beam width.

articleTitle: On Changing the Phase of the Radiated Field from a Microstrip Patch Antenna Using a 3D-printed Conformal Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 3D-printed conformal metasurface was used to change the phase of the radiated field from a single microstrip patch antenna. The metasurface had 25 complementary split ring resonators (CSRR) and was placed in the radiating far-field of the patch antenna. The conformal metasurface was printed with flexible NinjaFlex (substrate) and Electrifi (conductors) filaments, and the phase shift of the radiated field was achieved by changing the curvature of the conformal metasurface. The proposed system was simulated in HFSS. Furthermore, a prototype was measured, and the results validated the simulation results. The radiation pattern was shown to shift by up to 20 degrees in response to the curved metasurface. This proposed approach could eventually be used to achieve beam steering by combining a conventional patch antenna and 3D-printed metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Experiences from teaching an online short-term course on bioelectricity during the pandemic
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This manuscript identifies and describes the main elements in teaching an interdisciplinary short-term applied electromagnetics course on bioelectricity in an online mode. The major takeaway of this study is the identification of enablers for the learning process, when there is no physical interaction between the teacher and the student. The suitability of the assessment methodology when there is no face to face learning is also evaluated during this study.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Ridge Substrate Integrated Waveguide (RSIW) Endfire Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: a wideband circularly polarized (CP) ridge substrate integrated waveguide (RSIW) endfire antenna is presented. By introducing a single ridged blind vias in conventional substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) endfire antenna, its bandwidth is enhanced. Moreover, a pair of linearly symmetrical step notches are etched at the top layer and bottom layer to obtain CP characteristics, and a dielectric load is placed to yields better CP radiation and gains. The proposed antenna obtains impedance bandwidth from 20 to 50 GHz (85.7%), and the axial ratio bandwidth from 25.15 to 48.05 GHz (62.6%) which covers the entire Ka-band.

articleTitle: Implementation of DORT to a MIMO Radar with Planar Transmit and Receive Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A multiple-input-multiple-output radar system is configured to detect the position of different point targets in a multi-path environment using decomposition of the time-reversal operator technique (DORT). The system includes ma network analyzer operating in stepped frequency mode as the transmitter and receiver for the S-band signals connected to a switch box for sequentially feeding and receiving the array elements. Vivaldi antennas are used in the array for high directivity and broadband performance. The antennas are arranged as a planar array so they can obtain both the azimuth and elevation angle of arrival of the signals from the scatterers. DORT method is applied to the data to obtain the excitation signals for array factor calculation to focus the array on each target and produce radar images of the scatterers. Using 4 transmit and 4 receive elements for the planar array arrangement is shown to selectively locate six radar targets in the room.

articleTitle: Predicting RF Coupling to a UAV Wiring System Using the Equivalent Circuit Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Developing a full-wave electromagnetic model of the complete wiring system of a practical device is computationally challenging. In this work, we show how the Equivalent Circuit Approach (ECA) can be used to develop a computationally efficient representation of the RF coupling to the complete wiring system of a quadcopter UAV. The ECA is based on modeling the direct coupling to the wiring system with a Thevenin equivalent circuit. We show how the equivalent circuit could be updated to account for variations in the environment of the wires such as the metallic enclosure where the wiring system is housed. The coupling results from the equivalent circuit show excellent agreement with the full-wave simulations at a fraction of the computational time. The developed UAV model and the corresponding equivalent circuit can be used to guide RF coupling to UAVs and other practical devices.

articleTitle: Should SAR Guidelines Include Variability?
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Variations in 1-g and 10-g specific absorption rate (SAR) values due to variation in tissue dielectric properties are determined. To accomplish this goal, stochastic finite difference time domain (S-FDTD) and Monte Carlo methods are compared. A 3D head model with variable dielectric properties is exposed to a half wave dipole antenna at 835 and 1900 MHz. The results show that these variations can significantly affect the peak 1-g and 10-g SAR values and should be considered in SAR guidelines for cell phone assessment.

articleTitle: Evaluating Oral Exams in Large Undergraduate Engineering Courses
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: While studies have shown that oral exams are a valuable method of assessment, their use has been limited due to concerns about scalability, examiner bias and student anxiety. This paper presents preliminary results on incorporating oral exams into two large undergraduate engineering courses, examining the potential viability of these assessment strategies. This work was done when the courses were offered remotely due to COVID-19, but the results offer valuable insights that could carry over to in-person instruction as well.

articleTitle: Power Efficient RF Self-Interference Cancellation System for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Mono-static full duplex systems employ a single antenna and a circulator to provide isolation between the transmit (Tx) and the receive (Rx) radio chains. As much as 50 dB isolation is required to avoid receiver desensitization due to leakage of high power transmit signal. However, available circulators are typically designed to provide ~20-30 dB Tx/Rx port isolation. Therefore, additional cancellation circuits are required to enable simultaneous transmission and reception (STAR). In this paper, we present a novel STAR system that incorporates two circulators, a hybrid coupler, and a Self-Interference Cancellation (SIC) circuit based on a hybrid Finite Impulse Response (FIR) and a resonator topology. Preliminary simulations show promising results with an average Tx/Rx port isolation of 55 dB across a 20 MHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Antenna's Radar Cross Section (RCS) Measurements
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the results of the characterization of an antenna by the measurement and simulation of its backscattering parameters. Several steps associated with the calibration process make it possible to identify the main modes, the structural backscattering mode and the antenna re-radiating mode. The structure-mode is linked to the geometric and material parameters of the antenna. The antenna mode depends on the effective area of the antenna, which defines the quantity of captured energy, and the load impedance placed at the input port of the antenna, which by its mismatch (coefficient of reflection close to ±1) causes the re-radiation of the antenna. This method of non-contact measurement of the backscattered fields of the antennas would be particularly suitable for small antennas, identification tags and for the detection of the emission spectra of antennas or antenna arrays in general.

articleTitle: RF Based Real Time Human Motion Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Recent research has shown that the propagation of Radio Frequencies signals is affected by human movements taking place between the RF transmitter and receiver antennas. Artificial intelligence has been widely used to classify the patterns of signal propagation. With the help of a universal software radio peripheral device, a system was developed based on a real-time machine learning classification algorithm to ensure alerts of incidents are received in a timely manner. The machine learning model was built to distinguish between “No Activity” and “Movement” status of a single human subject. The model recorded a high classification accuracy of 97.8 % which enabled an accurate classification of new data in real-time.

articleTitle: Flexible Frequency Selective Surfaces With Ultra-Large Incidence Angle
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose a flexible stopband Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) based on a novel self-similar structure designation with ultra-large incidence angle ranging from 0° to 88° for TE and TM polarization on flexible polyimide substrate. The structure has four semicircle arcs with C4 rotation symmetry and is optimized using second order self-similar architecture. Ultimately, the two-order fractal designation exhibits great performance and simulation results indicate that the structure has great polarization and angular stability under different incident angles and polarizations.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Antenna with High Efficiency and Low Side Lobe
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The design of a reflectarray antenna(hereinafter referred to as a reflectarray), is generally based on the resonant element spacing to suppress the grating lobes in free space. However, considering that this condition is not sufficient, we designed a resonant element spacing to suppress the grating lobe in the dielectric. This paper compares the radiation pattern and gain designed with the resonant element spacing obtained under these two conditions, and evaluates the efficiency and side-lobe characteristics.

articleTitle: Impacts of Patient Postures on the RF-induced Heating for An External Fixation Device
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the influences of body postures on the radiofrequency (RF)-induced heating for patients with an external fixation device under 1.5 Tesla (T) and 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) system. Two patient postures, the natural posture and the hand raised, were used in the study. The external fixation device is placed on the forearm of the human model. The RF-induced heating at four landmark positions, corresponding to the head scan, the cardio scan, the liver scan, and the pelvis scan were studied. The peak 1g averaged specific absorption rate (SAR) was used to evaluate the RF-induced heating. For the head landmark, the natural posture has the lowest RF-induced heating and for other landmarks, the heating of the hand raised was lowest, at both 1.5 T and 3 T. Therefore, the RF-induced heating of the external fixation device can be reduced by adopting the appropriate posture.

articleTitle: Square Ring Element for Tilted Beam Radiation Utilizing Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, metasurfaces are utilized to support off-broadside radiation. The design consists of a square ring element printed in the vicinity of non-uniform metasurfaces. The non-uniform metasurfaces are designed to improve the realized gain of the tilted beam and to enhance the matching performance of the radiating element. The proposed design yields a tilted beam with a maximum realized gain of 9.7 dBi. The design operates from 4 to 5 GHz with a reflection coefficient below -10 dB. The overall height profile is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.07}\lambda_{4.5GHz}$</tex>.

articleTitle: On the Phase and Amplitude Coverages of the Phase Modulation Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Phase modulation (PM) techniques are introduced into the time modulated arrays (TMAs) to achieve a scannable radiation beam at fundamental frequency. In this conference paper, the phase and amplitude coverages of a PM waveform with constant amplitude are derived. The conclusions derived in this paper can be used to guide the design of PM waveforms of TMAs. The numerical example illustrate that a steerable radiation pattern with low ripple of efficiency at fundamental frequency in the entire scanning space can be obtained.

articleTitle: On The Evaluation Of Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency Between Two Antenna Apertures In The Fresnel Region Over Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper deals with the use of wideband signals for wireless power transfer (WPT), analyzing the achievable power transmission efficiency (PTE) between two apertures in the Fresnel region and comparing it with that of conventional single carrier solutions. By assuming an uniform aperture excitation (which can be implemented over a wideband in an easier way than a focus excitation), it is shown that the PTE exhibits some local maxima/minima over the bandwidth, contradicting the general idea “higher frequency larger PTE”. An energy transfer efficiency is then defined to include the effect of wide spectrum signals excitation, and constrained spectrum optimization is investigated to take also into account possible radiated power density limits of standard regulations.

articleTitle: Array Antenna Decoupling and Low-Sidelobe Beamforming Based on Active Element Pattern Synthesis in 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A 16-element equally spaced linear microstrip array antenna operating at 3.5 GHz in 5G Sub-6 is designed. Using the improved genetic algorithm, we can get the optimized target beam by controlling the its amplitude and phase based on the active element pattern (AEP). The low-sidelobe cosecant-square beam is synthesized, and the sidelobe is less than −30 dB.

articleTitle: On the Coupling Between a Transmission Line Additively Manufactured with Electrifi Filament and a Copper Stepped Impedance Filter in the S-Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Electrifi is a 3D printable conductive filament that has shown promise in radio frequency and microwave applications. Investigation into an Elecrifi-based microstrip line is still in it's early stages, particularly with its behavior in antenna arrays. This paper will present the coupling characteristics of an Electrifi-based transmission line in the presence of a stepped impedance filter constructed with copper. The results from this experiment will be compared with a copper transmission line (receptor) in the same scenario.

articleTitle: A High Aperture Efficiency Switched-Beam Lens-Based System with Tightly-Coupled Array Feed
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a switched-beam lens-based antenna system using a tightly-coupled <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{8\times 8}$</tex> all-metal Vivaldi array feed. A planar gradient-index (GRIN) lens is designed and optimized for maximum aperture efficiency from 10–40 GHz. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\times 2}$</tex> subarrays of the array are used to feed the lens and generate nine scanned beams. Over the operating bandwidth, the proposed antenna system has nine high-quality scanned beams with low cross-polarization contamination scanning up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{15^{\circ}}$</tex> in principal and diagonal planes. Moreover, active VSWR < 3.2:1, directivity > 12.5 dBi, and aperture efficiency >70% (up to 90% over a wide portion of the band) are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization of Horizontal Beam Switching in Urban Overtaking Scenario
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Nowadays, the Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) has attracted much attention. With more and more breakthroughs in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technology, ITS is becoming increasingly intelligent. This paper pays attention to vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication. The existing research on V2V communication has included many scenarios, such as fixed transmitters, vehicle turning, but there is rarely presented research on the beam switching under the condition of both vehicles moving. Therefore, this paper focuses on the horizontal beam switching on the channel in overtaking scenario and uses the ray-tracing (RT) simulator to characterize the channel at the 22.1 GHz-22.4 GHz frequency band. The results of RT simulations can guide the construction of vehicle antenna for future V2V communication.

articleTitle: Design of Reconfigurable Transmission Unit Cell with Independent and Continuous Manipulations of Amplitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a reconfigurable transmission unit cell with independent and continuous modulations of amplitude and phase in C band. This structure mainly contains four parts of receiving and transmitting antennas, programmable attenuator with PIN diodes, and programmable phase shifter with varactor diodes. By changing the voltage bias of PIN diodes and varactor diodes, the transmission amplitude and phase can be varied separately, and the simulation results show good independent transmission properties. For the advantages of low profile, low cost and easy configuration, this design have a great potential in advanced radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: Collimation of Experimental Antenna Array Using Embedded Calibration Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the realization scheme of embedded calibration lines in the 64-element prototype is demonstrated to monitor active array health and collimate the active phased array. The experimental antenna array's radiation characteristic is measured in the Near Field Test Range (NFTR), demonstrating successful collimation of the active phased array by using the embedded calibration lines and achieving maximum directivity, minimum BPE, and low Peak SLL.

articleTitle: Wideband Low-Profile Patch Antennas Using High-Dielectric Fluids and Hybrid Metal Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel liquid patch with hybrid metal structures has been presented to address the fundamental performance limitation of microstrip patch antenna in terms of bandwidth versus antenna thickness and size. Our proposed design example has realized over 33% impedance bandwidth with only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.06\ \lambda_{0}$</tex> antenna height through a multi-mode integration and improved impedance matching method. This work has shown state-of-the-art performance for wideband low-profile patch antennas, demonstrating significant advantages brought by the new type of antenna design using hybrid liquid dielectric and/or metal structures.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Patch Antenna Using Metasurface Lens
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-gain transmitting lens antenna with a metasurface lens. The lens unit consists of a rectangular metal ring and a square patch inside. In this work we use the X-band microstrip antenna as the feed source. Through this structure, a transmission phase range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[-178^{\circ},179^{\circ}]$</tex> is realized, the gain of the patch antenna increases by 12.58dB, and the efficiency of the lens antenna reaches 35.92%. This lens antenna provides a new choice for high-gain antennas.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Wide-Band Dual-Polarization Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel wide-band dual-polarization reconfigurable frequency selective surface (RFSS), which consists of only one dielectric substrate with switchable FSS printed on it. The FSS is composed of metal grids in oblique arrangement with the notched square patches inside them. Four PIN diodes are symmetrically placed on each side of the metal grids. When they are forward biased, the proposed RFSS operates in transmission mode and in reflection mode when they are reverse biased. The simulation result shows that the structure has a switchable bandwidth greater than 40% for the angles of incident waves ranging from 0° to 45° under TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: A D-Band Stacked Patch Antenna with Air Trenches in BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a micromachined millimeter-wave stacked patch antenna at D-band for high resolution radar applications. The top most two metal layers in the backend of line of a 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology is utilized to feed a main patch loaded by another parasitic patch with a different length in order to widen the bandwidth. The silicon under the antenna is selectively removed to synthesize air trenches to get rid of the poor radiation efficiency in silicon substrates. The simulated radiation pattern exhibits <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$108^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> half-power beam widths in the two principal planes with a peak radiation efficiency of 62%. A prototype chip is fabricated to validate the design where the radiation pattern is measured across frequency and the peak effective isotropic radiated power over frequency is compared with a single patch counterpart prototype.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband CRLH magneto-electric phased array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel concept of ultra-wideband phased array based on the composite right/left handed (CRLH) metamaterial theory. The proposed metamaterial array consists of magneto-electric (ME) radiation sources, which are formed by a series of tightly-coupled CRLH unit cells. The array can be excited using microstrip lines directly fed by unbalanced broadband coaxial lines. Consequently, unlike a tightly-coupled dipole array (TCDA), the proposed concept can achieve multioctave ultra-wideband performance without need of a complex balun or feed structure.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metamaterial-Inspired PMC-PEC for Waveguide Miniaturisation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable metamaterial-inspired unit cell is proposed that can be reconfigured to behave either as a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) or as a perfect electric conductor (PEC) and its application to waveguide miniaturisation is demonstrated. The unit cell is designed to operate in the sub-6 GHz band at 3.6 GHz with a PMC bandwidth of ≈ 150 MHz and has a simple construction that makes the design easy to fabricate. The phase response of the reconfigurable unit cell is presented and a prototype design of a miniaturised waveguide using the proposed unit cell is also proposed. The performance and field distribution of the waveguide are analysed which demonstrate the existence of a pass-band spanning ≈ 160 MHz below the cutoff frequency and the presence of a quasi TEM mode.

articleTitle: Minimally Invasive Deep Brain Stimulation Using Intracranial Stents
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Deep brain stimulation is a multipurpose therapy indicated for a host of neuropsychiatric disorders including treatment resistant depression, Parkinson's disease, and refractory epilepsy. However, current systems require invasive surgery and have a high risk of complications. This paper explores an alternative solution using non-invasive electrodes and an implanted intracranial stent. A comparison of active stimulation and passive stimulation at 915 MHz is presented.

articleTitle: Antenna Design for Improved Non-Linear Radar Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a set of custom dual-arm folded-probe-fed patch (DFPFP) antennas are designed to improve the performance of a non-linear radar (NLR) system. To improve the system performance, the custom antennas are designed to have high gain, relatively narrow bandwidth, good linearity, and good size, weight, and power (SWaP) performance. Two DFPFP antennas are built and tested, one each for transmit and receive. The VSWR and gain of the fabricated antennas are measured. The measurements show good agreement with simulated results. The performance of the fabricated antennas is then compared to a pair of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) antennas that are currently used for NLR system testing. The VSWR and gain measurement results of the DFPFP antennas compare favorably with those of the COTS antennas, and suggest improved NLR performance. Lastly, the performance of a NLR system using the two sets of antennas is evaluated. By replacing the COTS antennas with the custom DFPFP antennas, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvements as high as 20 dB are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Homogenized Magnetic Metasurface for Misalignment Robustness Enhancement in Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the adoption of a magnetic metasurface whose response is opportunely controlled as a method to alleviate the misalignment issue in resonant inductive Wireless Power Transfer. In particular, we first present the analytical framework thanks to which the metasurface response can be homogenized, avoiding undesired truncation effects. Then, a numerical set-up is designed to demonstrate the validity of the proposed approach. The results obtained through accurate full-wave simulations show that a homogenized metasurface can outperform a traditional one in terms of misalignment robustness, while maintaining the same efficiency level. This work can pave the way to the adoption in WPT applications of response-controlled metasurfaces with respect to the traditional version.

articleTitle: New Concept for BAW Antenna Induced by Magnon-Phonon Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Recently, a neoteric thin-film bulk-acoustic-wave (BAW) antenna has been demonstrated with 1–2 orders of magnitude miniaturization over the conventional counterparts. In this paper, we theoretically propose several new concepts for BAW antennas in the aspects of radiation efficiency, antenna modulation and polarization modes. Specifically, induced by the strong magnon-phonon coupling effect, radiation efficiency can be 100-time enhanced, and antenna modulation can be substantially simplified. Additionally, a right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) radiation field can be observed in the strong magnon-phonon coupling region.

articleTitle: Design of Circularly Polarized End-fire Antenna on Gap Waveguide for Automotive Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an end-fire antenna with circu-lar polarization utilizing gap waveguide technology for 77 GHz automotive radar band. The proposed device contains a 1 × 4 planar array antenna and a gap waveguide part consisting of a 4-way power divider on ridge gap waveguide and a transitive groove gap waveguide. The impedance and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidths of 74.8 ~ 79.2 GHz and 75.6 ~ 78.0 GHz are achieved in simulation, which can cover the 77 GHz radar band well. A stable end-fire beam and a gain in the range of 11.6 to 13.4 dBic are obtained as well over the whole operation band.

articleTitle: Patch Antenna Array Design through Bottom-Up and Bayesian Optimizations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and the optimization of a 2 × 2 antenna array through two optimization techniques, namely bottom-up optimization (BUO) and Bayesian optimization (BO). These sequential optimizations tackle the difficulty problem of antenna array design by predicting the suitable number of single radiators and by sizing the configuration of feeding circuit using BUO and BO methods, respectively. The proposed method leads to the design of high performance antenna arrays in terms of bandwidth, gain and radiated patterns where all the overall optimization process is performed with the combination of electronic design automation tool and a numerical analyzer. To validate the proposed method, a patch antenna array is designed and optimized in a frequency band from 12.9 GHz to 13.7 GHz with the maximum gain of 17.9 dB in the considered band.

articleTitle: Efficiency Angle as Figure of Merit for Reciprocal MIMO Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The efficiency angle is originally only defined for single-input single-output power transfer systems. It acts as an angular figure of merit for the efficiency. However, multiple-input multiple-output power transfer systems are on the rise. In this work, the definition of the efficiency angle is extended to general reciprocal systems with multiple sources and loads. As a result, the efficiency angle can be applied to reciprocal systems with multiple transmitters and receivers; it facilitates the design, optimization and comparison of (wireless and wired) power transfer systems.

articleTitle: UHF Tags Array for Holographic Target Localization and Wireless Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a contactless, low-cost, scalable technique capable of localizing close targets and detecting their breathing rates based on an array of UHF RFID tags. To create a hologram of the target and extract the desired information, the system collects the phase and RSSI information from each unique tag in the array, processes the data using digital beamforming algorithms and reconstructs the image based on holographic methods. The paper highlights the hardware choices that play a critical role in constraining the dominant propagation paths and presents the localization and vital signs estimates of the system. The current system can localize targets angularly and can be readily extended to 3D localization, without interfering with daily activities.

articleTitle: Monitoring COVID-19 Patients Using Cardio-Pulmonary Stethoscope RF Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The COVID-19 disease recognized as pandemic in 2020 created worldwide shortage of medical resources causing hospitals to admit only the severe cases and leaving the rest to selfcare. The identified covid19 patient with non-life-threatening stage had to monitor the disease progression based on the escalation of symptoms or do imaging tests like CT scans, x-ray. The imaging method while reliable comes with its own limitation and risks of exposure. In this paper, we checked the efficacy of utilizing Cardio-Pulmonary Stethoscope (CPS) to monitor the COVID-19 patient and assess the disease progressive status. The simulations were ran on anatomically realistic human model with infection at various location, size and spread reflecting real COVID-19 infected lungs. The least detectable size of injury was found to be the ellipsoid of ~0.9 cubic cm, and the most consistent result was observed in the healthy lung with water content of 20%. The results presented in this paper suggest that CPS could be used as the alternative to CT scans for continuous monitoring.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A deep learning method is introduced to improve the solution of electromagnetic inverse scatteing pronlem(ISP). By combining the deep learning network of R2U-Net with Subspace-based Optimization Method(SOM), the reconstruction result is better than without embedding deep learning, the proceeding of the method is given and the advantage of introducing deep learning is shown in improving the results of reconstructing the spatial parameters of scatterer, especially the strong scatters with higher permittvity.

articleTitle: Design of a 5G End-Fire Meta-Surface Antenna Array for Mobile User Equipment Using SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an end-fire antenna array for mobile user equipment, using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology and targeting the n257 and n258 5G frequency bands is proposed. Two rows of meta-surfaces are used to match the SIW to free-space. The final design of the single element has a bandwidth of 27%, covering 23.75 GHz to 31.25 GHz. The simulated array, consisting of eight elements, has a gain of 10.4 dBi and is able to scan up to ±55° at 24.25 GHz.

articleTitle: A New and Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna using CRLH-TL and CDRA Loading for S and C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new idea is introduced for the first time to enhance the bandwidth of compact antenna by using the combination of composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line (TL) and cylindrical dielectric resonator (CDR) loading. The proposed antenna design starts with a narrow-band CRLH-TL loaded antenna and wider bandwidth and circular polarization radiation is obtained due to the loading of a CDR. The antenna provides a compact dimension of 0.22λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.22λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.10λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at the first resonance 2.69 GHz. The fabricated DR loaded compact antenna offers a wider IBW of 99.6% with axial ratio bandwidth of 15.27%.

articleTitle: Novel Slot Array Mechanical Reconfiguration Approach Based on Accordion Structure and Micro-actuator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel approach to mechanical reconfiguration is demonstrated with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> slot array operating at 16 GHz. Accordion structures connected to a microactuator are used to vary element spacing while maintaining uniformity, yielding 30° of continuous scanning with high polarization purity. This proposed design allows a significant reduction in cost, size, and complexity when compared to standard electrical reconfiguration approaches. The combined ease of integration and high power handling capabilities make this approach a candidate for next-generation reconfigurable antennas arrays.

articleTitle: Folded Terahertz Antenna based on $MoS_{2}$ and Gold for Biomedical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid antenna design for terahertz communication. The proposed antenna operates in the frequency range of 0.85–0.95 terahertz (THz). Full wave electromagnetic simulations show that combination of molybdenum disulfide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$MoS_{2}$</tex> material, and gold improves the antenna efficiency from around 60% to almost 85% in the desired frequency band. The proposed hybrid design can be used in high-resolution imaging and suitable for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Continuous Transverse Stub Array Fed by Stripline Ports
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS) arrays are generally fed using a line source. In this paper, we use a two-dimensional arrangement of planar striplines to create such a line source. The whole feeding network is realized in planar form using standard PCB manufacturing process. The planar network is then integrated into the parallel-plate waveguides under the radiating slots. The proposed solution avoids using bulky corporate networks or quasi-optical systems to feed the CTS. Unlike classical CTS configurations, where scanning is allowed just in a single direction, in the proposed feeding scheme the beam can be steered in any direction when the appropriate amplitude and phase are provided to the inputs. An array of 4×8 has been designed to operate in the Ka transmitting Satcom band. The simulated active reflection coefficient of the central element is less than −10 dB over a 12.7% band for scanning up to 30° in both E and Diagonal plane, while is 8% in H-plane.

articleTitle: Progressive Phaseshifter Concept for Beam-Scanned Waveguide Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A Progressive phase shifter concept was proposed to address the challenges in beam-scanned waveguide array. For 1D scan, only one control is required, instead of controlling the individual phase shifter for each element. Simulation results on the preliminary design were included.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband Partially Reflective Surface Superstrate for mm-Wave Printed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband partially reflective surface (PRS) unit cell to improve mm-wave printed antennas' radiation performances. The proposed PRS unit cell is constructed by two different layers separated by an air-gap, with only the bottom face of each layer has a copper pattern printed on it. On the bottom and top layers of the PRS unit cell, a capacitive patch, and an inductive patch with a square-slot-loaded patch (SSLP) are printed, respectively. The unit cell exhibits a broadband positive phase gradient of the reflection coefficient with a high reflectivity around 62 GHz. As a superstrate above printed antennas, the PRS layers can be very useful in improving the radiation gain performance of mm-wave antennas in the considered band around 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Active RX-TX Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Some aspects of design of an Active RX-TX antenna were well discussed in previous works. It was noted the moving to the lower frequency band leads to decreasing of antennas additional gain. Further development of active antenna design is considered in the paper. The section of transmitting line was added to antenna design. This line of certain length was connected between the tap of microstrip antenna and the source of the FET. This connection result in increasing of antenna gain on more than 15 dB.

articleTitle: Deployable Miura-Ori Tightly Coupled Dipole Array for Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An origami-based Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) is proposed for small satellite applications. The proposed TCDA is the first to employ a rigid-flexible two-layered accordion structure. The array operates across 0.4-2.4 GHz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 3$</tex> at broadside and 0.5-2.4 GHz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} <3$</tex> when scanning down to 45° in the E-, D-, and H-planes, and without additional FSS superstrates. An <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> prototype was fabricated using Kapton and FR4 and tested to verify the bandwidth and gain of a finite array. The fabricated prototype was demonstrated to be packable, low-profile, and lightweight (only 1.1kg). Notably, when packed, the array has a one-dimensional size reduction of 75%. The packing compression is made possible by eliminating vertical PCB boards and incorporating the balun feeds within the dipole layer. This TCDA is one of the first foldable, low profile, and low-scanning ultra-wideband array in the literature.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Tunable Broadband Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A frequency-tunable broadband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with metasurface is proposed. The proposed antenna is comprised of a substrate with ground plane, a cylindrical dielectric resonator with two slots, a metasurface, a patch and a coaxial probe. The metasurface upon the substrate which consists of an array of “-” shaped units, the slots and the patch upon the cylindrical dielectric resonator (DR) have increased the working bandwidth of the antenna. The proposed DRA has realized the operating frequency band of 53.7% (3.5 GHz - 6.07 GHz). And according to the actual needs, the resonant frequency of the antenna can be adjusted by changing the length and height of the two slots. The tunable resonant frequency range is 4.7 GHz - 5.0 GHz. It has a good application in the communication systems which need more than one antenna.

articleTitle: Straightforward emulation of generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) in commercial solvers using electrically-thick Fabry-Perot metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In order to produce novel wave-control effects with metasurfaces, the fields must satisfy generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTC). The abstract zero-thickness of such penetrable sheets is generally incompatible with commercial full-wave solvers (FWSs), precluding the use of the latter to validate conceptual achievements related to GSTC. This is overcome by thick “Fabry-Perot” metasurfaces (FP-MS) which consist of parallel plate waveguides containing dielectric layers. Such GSTC-derived concepts as perfect anomalous reflection and beam-splitting have been verified thus far using the thick FP-MS structure in FWSs; herein, we extend the concept to accomplish perfect anomalous reflection. This seamless emulation of GSTCs in FWS, which includes intricate functionalities, can be instrumental for successful development of new MS capabilities in the future.

articleTitle: Capacity-Driven Optimization of Tiled Arrays for Multi-User MIMO Communication Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel methodology for the design of base stations antenna arrays for multi-user MIMO communications. The array has a simplified and modular architecture, composed by few sub-array tiles shapes, reducing the array control points. By combining a pre-coding technique for the setting of the excitations weights with an exhaustive search of exact tiling solutions, the communication channel capacity is maximized. The presented preliminary result shows that the optimized irregular tiling layout allows to reach higher capacity values with respect to a regular tiling configuration.

articleTitle: Wireless Charging of Ground-based Sensors from a UAV-carried Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses scenarios for wireless charging of a grid of ground-based sensors from a UAV carried wireless power transfer (WPT) transmitter. Towards that end a high efficiency 900 MHz rectenna is implemented with almost 70% peak efficiency and 4.8 dBi gain for the elliptical patch. The simulated scenarios indicate the necessity of circularly polarized antennas in order to limit the dominant losses factor which is the polarization mismatch.

articleTitle: One-Sided Leaky-Wave Antenna with TM Surface Wave Feeding and Open-Stopband Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A planar one-sided bull-eye leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is presented with suppressed open stopband (OSB). The antenna consists of a grounded dielectric slab (GDS) loaded on top with a periodic arrangement of double metallic strips, whilst a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> surface-wave launcher (SWL) feed system is adopted for cylindrical-wave excitation. The radial structure is also properly designed to suppress the OSB effect thus achieving reduced dispersion features when frequency scanning through broadside, as typically observed with 1-D periodic LWAs. A method-of-moments (MoM) dispersion analysis is also used to characterize the attenuation and phase propagation constants of the supported leaky-wave (LW) mode. The resulting single-layer LWA is lowcost and it is well-matched from about 18 GHz to 22 GHz. The planar 2-D design also radiates a directive pencil beam pattern with gain values reaching 15 dBi.

articleTitle: A Dual-Port Antenna With Reconfigurable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel dual-port antenna with reconfigurable meta-surface is proposed. When the antenna is excited through single-port, its pattern is end-fire. When the antenna is excited through dual-port with same phase, its pattern is bidirectional broadside. To achieve directional radiation, a reconfigurable metasurface is introduced to realize two states including equivalent PEC and PMC. With different excitation modes of dual-port antenna and different states of metasurface, the antenna with reflector can obtain five typical directional patterns. The main lobe can deflect to 49° with a hign gain over 9 dBi. In addition, the antenna has a small size of 0.23λ × 0.32λ. It can be predicted that the proposed antenna will have great potential on wide-angle scanning.

articleTitle: Robust Simulation-Driven Antenna Design using Parallel Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A parallel Bayesian robust optimization (PBRO) algorithm is proposed. In this work, multi-point acquisition function is used to add points, and Monte Carlo simulation is used to calculate the response mean and variance. The size of structure in the manufacturing of wideband antenna is described as an interval variable and a robust optimization model is established. The robust optimization of the broadband antenna is carried out by using the above algorithm, and the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by comparing the experimental results with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Maintaining an Active Learning Environment During a Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes methods for using the flipped classroom approach in a fully online, synchronous environment in order maintain active learning during the pandemic. The results are compared to previous efforts prior to the pandemic. Student evaluations are described and are consistent with in-person methods.
