articleTitle: Antenna Designs for Mobile Handsets With Consideration of 3GPP Requirements in FR2
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) specifications have supported spectrum from 24.25 GHz to 52.6 GHz as frequency range 2 (FR2) for the 5th generation mobile networks (5G), which brings some revolutionary change to antenna systems in mobile handsets. In this paper, the design challenges of mobile antennas in FR2 are discussed, and the state of art research works is also reviewed.

articleTitle: Fast Full-wave Microwave Imaging With Physics Embedded Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We design an explainable deep neural network for full-wave microwave imaging, which is assisted by a physics embedded neural network for forward modeling. Both forward and inverse problems can be largely accelerated, and the learning algorithms possess good generalization ability thanks to the embedded wave physics. Furthermore, the reconstruction can achieve super-resolution meanwhile keeping data consistency. By combining deep learning and physical simulation together, this method provides a new way for real-time full-wave imaging with good accuracy and reliability.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification for Pipeline Detection Using a 3-D Bistatic Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Pipeline detection is a problem of importance in water and oil transportation systems maintenance. Unlike localized targets, the scattering mechanism of extended targets such as a pipeline is unique in that the scattering phase center will change depending on the position of the receiver relative to the transmitter. This property renders traditional imaging techniques like back-projection algorithm impractical in detecting buried pipelines in Bistatic radar arrangements. To overcome this challenge, a new imaging algorithm for a multi-static subsurface imaging radar is developed that tracks the scattering phase centers as the receiver is moved around the transmitter in a way that is tailored to pipelines leading to a better performance in detecting them. Using a pair of antennas designed for GPR along with portable Vector-Network-Analyzer (VNA), the performance of the algorithm in detecting both metallic and dielectric PVC pipes filled with water is validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Compact Third-order Dual-band Bandpass Filter With High Selectivity and Independently Controllable Bandwidths
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact third-order dual-band bandpass filter (DBBPF) based on zero-degree feed structure is presented in this paper. The proposed filter employs a pair of electrically end-coupled open stub-loaded resonators (OSLRs), a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> stepped impedance resonator (SIR), and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> uniform impedance resonator (UIR). The two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> resonators are embedded within the OSLRs so that the filter is compact in size. The fundamental odd-and even-mode of the OSLRs couple with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> SIR and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> UIR to form the lower and higher passbands, respectively. The DBBPF exhibits high frequency selectivity and independently controllable bandwidths simultaneously. For experimental validation, a demonstration DBBPF centered at 2 GHz and 3.5 GHz is implemented, and the measurement results are given with good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Response of Laminated Composites to Guided Microwave Pulse
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The work of this paper is dedicated to characterizing the response of multi-layered composite material to incident microwave pulse. This serves as part of the forward modeling for our future work on applying microwave-induced thermal acoustic tomography (MITAT) on non-destructive testing of the defects in multi-layered composite materials. Microwave pulse has been used in MITAT for exciting the acoustic wave which is detected for imaging. Therefore, the response of the multi-layered composite material to a microwave pulse is studied in this paper, with some preliminary numerical results on the wave absorption and SAR distribution by different composites. It can be seen that SAR is not distributed uniformly and the difference in absorbed energy will cause different acoustic waves.

articleTitle: A High Gain Switchable Dual CP Wideband Rectangular Spiral Microstrip Antenna for mm Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Communication systems have been driven towards the new generations, such as fifth generation (5G), due to the demands of compact, high speed, and large bandwidth systems. This paper presents a high efficiency and low-profile dual CP Wideband rectangular spiral antenna microstrip antenna intended for use in 5G systems. The same antenna can be used Ka-band satellite communications. Stubs and slot are introduced to improve the impedance matching and mutual coupling of dual ports. The proposed antenna has a central operating frequency of 28 GHz. HFSS software was used for this design. The antenna has a compact structure with dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(5\times 5\times 0.508)}$</tex> mm. Rogers RO4003 material was used as a substrate for the antenna. The antenna has a low reflection coefficient of -22 dB, a high gain value of 5.3 dBi, a wide operating band, (24.97 -30.07) GHz, of 5.03 GHz (18.2%), and high efficiency.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Self-Complementary Frequency Selective Surface for GNSS Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper a miniaturized self-complementary frequency selective surface (SCFSS) for global navigation satellite system (GNSS) applications is proposed. Here, a spiral Jerusalem cross patch structure in conjunction with its complementary aperture are etched in the top side of the substrate. The obtained results show that the SCFSS achieves good angular stability for different incidence angles in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> for both TE and TM polarizations. Moreover, the proposed SCFSS structure proves to have a good polarization selective property, a low profile, an acceptable pass-band and stop-band symmetries.

articleTitle: A Four-Band Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna for Applications in S- and C-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the development and simulation of a circular polarized patch antenna for four-band operation in S- and C- band. The design of the antenna is based on the modal degeneration mechanism applied to a circular patch, which is perturbed by the means of the gap-coupling with parasitic reactive elements. In addition, the patch is also perturbed by etching four pair of slots. The combination of both the perturbation mechanisms results in a design capable of four frequency of operation, with a first pair of modes in the S-band, at 2.45 GHz and 2.75 GHz and two additional modes in the C-band, at 5.00 GHz and 5.20 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Mode propagation in glide-symmetric dielectric-filled corrugated waveguides
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Glide symmetry in periodic structures introduces several advantages such as low dispersion, wider stopbands, and higher levels of anisotropy. Here, we propose the use of glide symmetry in dielectric-filled corrugated rectangular waveguides. The operation of these filled waveguides is studied by means of a multimodal transfer-matrix approach that carries out a Bloch analysis of the corresponding unit cell to obtain the dispersion diagram of the structure (both the phase shift and the attenuation rate). In this specific configuration, glide symmetry is found to provide a wider backward passband below the cutoff of the non-corrugated housing waveguide.

articleTitle: Broadband Dual-Polarized Antenna Element for 5G Base Station Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A broadband dual-polarized antenna element is proposed for the 5G base station antenna application. The behaviors of the proposed antenna are investigated using the characteristic mode analysis. Characteristics mode 1 and 2 share the same resonant frequency, and their current distribution are orthogonal. The third mode, which is independent from the other modes, is utilized to achieve the desired resonant frequency. The dual-polarized antenna has the S11 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\leq-10\text{dB}}$</tex> bandwidth spans from 2.45 GHz to 4.1 GHz, and a gain of 8.5 dBi. The port to port isolation is more than 30 dB from 2.5 GHz to 4.1 GHz.

articleTitle: Ku-Band Dual Linear Polarized Flat Panel Phased Array Antenna with Very Low Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a flat panel phased array antenna by using the ADAR1000 chipset from Analog devices. The single radiating element is a stacked patch antenna with 2.5 GHz of impedance matching bandwidth. The 8x8 stacked patch antenna is capable of at least ±30° scan angles for both polarizations. This array utilizes a mirrored cell of 4 dual polarized antennas around a single chip. In turn, the mirrored configuration drastically lowers the cross-pol, resulting in a cross-polarization of 70+ dB down from the co-polarization. The fabricated array includes an integrated beam forming network and a suitable beam forming algorithm. Measured results will be presented during the symposium.

articleTitle: Use of UHF compact Circularly Polarized antenna for food analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Development of fast, accurate, mobile and low-cost tools for food analysis is an important topic to mitigate food-borne diseases. In this paper, a portable sensors based on S11 and S21 of compact circularly polarized antennas is proposed. A low-cost and portable VNA analyser is used to perform measurement and analysis. Fruits are used to assess the test-bed capability to classified different species. A raw of measurement using Orange, Tomato and Mango demonstrates that a signature for each species can be extracted. First results show the reflection coefficient is less sensitive than transmission coefficient to fruit position.

articleTitle: Remote Destruction of the Coronavirus by Dual-Polarized Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a remote sterilization technique through microwave radiation. The innovative approach requires the heating of a liquid water film layer, which can be sprayed onto the area of interest. Applications include the deactivation of the coronavirus and other pathogens by physically increasing the liquid film temperature achieving thermal sterilization. The proposed technique can be implemented by various antenna systems and retrodirective arrays. In this study, a dual-polarized antenna array is adopted and designed to increase the transmitted power levels without physically including more antenna elements. As reported in the paper, this dual-polarized approach has the benefit of reduced sterilization time when compared to a single-polarization system having the same number of antenna elements.

articleTitle: Ionospheric Equatorial Plasma Bubble effects on L1 single frequency code GPS positioning using precise ephemerides
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Amplitude and phase variations of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) radio signals used by the aeronautic community occur due to ionospheric irregularities (ionospheric scintillation), which may cause the degradation of service availability and performance, raising safety issues. This is particularly true in the Appleton Anomaly region, where the occurrence of ionospheric irregularities is known to be frequent. In this work, the results from an analysis of the impact of ionospheric irregularities on the single point positioning performance of GPS is presented and discussed. The results show that the developed model has a good positioning measurements and few discrepancies. However, in the presence of ionospheric scintillation, degradations of positioning quality are observed. These promising results can be applied to data from other stations and positioning system, with the objective of directly characterizing ionospheric scintillation effects.

articleTitle: Smart Cloaking Metasurfaces for Next-Generation Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we describe how advanced cloaking metasurfaces allows expanding the functionalities of wire antennas and make them suitable candidates for future wireless systems. In particular, we show that, by loading the cloaking device with proper electronic circuits, the antenna can be made sensitive to the characteristics of the surrounding environment and modify accordingly its transmitting/receiving properties. Several applications are discussed, showing that the behavior of conventional wire antennas coated with such advanced cloaking metasurfaces can be made dependent either on the power level or the temporal waveform of the incoming signal. The unprecedented functionalities here discussed may pave the way to a further boost in the quest of smart antennas for next-generation systems.

articleTitle: Glide-Symmetric Planar EBG Structure for Mutual Coupling Reduction Between Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a fully planar electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure exploiting glide symmetry is proposed for mutual coupling reduction between microstrip patch antennas. The proposed structure is studied in terms of dispersion diagrams and full-wave simulations showing a size reduction as well as an increased level of isolation when compared to its corresponding conventional structure without glide symmetry.

articleTitle: Elongated Object Orientation Estimation Based on Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The horizontal and vertical orientation angles of an elongated subsurface object are key parameters for object identification and imaging in ground-penetrating radar (GPR) applications. Conventional methods can only extract the horizontal orientation angle or estimate both angles in narrow ranges. To address these issues, we present a multi-polarization aggregation and selection neural network (MASNet) to estimate both angles of an elongated subsurface object in the entire spatial range. The network takes the multi-polarimetric radargrams as inputs, integrates their characteristics in the feature space, and selects discriminative features of reflected signal patterns for accurate orientation estimation. Numerical results show that the MASNet achieves high estimation accuracy with an angle estimation error of less than 5°. The promising results obtained in the study encourages new solutions for GPR-related tasks by integrating multi-polarization information with deep learning techniques.

articleTitle: Eight-Port Wideband MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz 5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An eight-port wide-band multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is presented for base stations applications. The antenna is composed by four unit cells <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(2\times 2)}$</tex> separated by a cross-shaped isolating block with a total size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{220\times 220\times 28}$</tex> mm ‘ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{2.42}\lambda\times \mathbf{2.42}\lambda\times \mathbf{0.3}\lambda$</tex>, at central frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{f}_{c}=3.3}$</tex> GHz). The unit cell is defined by a square cavity-backed antenna fed with two I-shaped crossed dipoles. The antenna provides 8 independent ports with 21.5 dB of minimum isolation and an impedance bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{S}_{11} < -10\mathbf{dB})$</tex> of 97% ranging at 1.8-5 GHz. Results show an efficiency higher than 87%, unidirectional radiation patterns and low envelope correlation coefficient. The geometry of the antenna is suitable for scaling this design to a massive MIMO system with the replication of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: A Compact UWB Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna with Enhanced Radiation Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized ultra-wideband antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) is proposed. By introducing a folded tapered transition, the low-frequency radiation performance is improved and reflection coefficient less than −10 dB over the whole working band is achieved. The measured results show that the antenna exhibits stable radiation patterns over a frequency range from 300 MHz-6 GHz.

articleTitle: Irregularly Clustered Antenna Array: A prototype for mmW 5G Base Station
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: NR 5G mmW networks require high performing base station systems capable to provide high capacity and wide coverage thanks to beam steering and high Equivalent Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP). The increment of radiated power imposes a limit in the generation of Grating Lobes toward sensitive places. In this article a PCB prototype for an irregularly clustered antenna is proposed. The main parameters for antenna synthesis, optimization and EM design are described. The validation of synthesis and implementation process is assessed with measurements results.

articleTitle: On the Gain Loss of Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Arrays with Narrow- and Wide-beam Element Patterns
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Gain loss and gain fluctuation are significant contributors to pattern degradation for wide-angle scanning phased arrays. To counter this, phased arrays can utilize various element types with large half-power beamwidths (HPBW) that increase the available scanning range. There are also a multitude of array structures that increase radiation in the endfire direction to extend the array scanning range. This paper attempts to address the gain loss and gain fluctuation for a scanning linear phased array for cases in which narrow- and wide-beam elements are utilized. Multiple scan angles are viewed for each element case, and the gain losses are determined.

articleTitle: Design of Rectangular Waveguide Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A waveguide array based on rectangular waveguide with high gain and low side-lobe is designed in this paper. Inclined slot cut in the narrow wall of rectangular waveguides is employed for horizontal polarization (HP) radiation. The realized gain of single rectangular waveguide slot antenna reaches 21.1dBi and the side-lobe is below -34.7dB at the center frequency of 9.4 GHz. The utilization of single rectangular waveguide slot antenna constructs a 4×59 waveguide antenna array, whose total volume of the structure is 1411mm×59mm×24.86m. For the designed array antenna, the realized gain achieves 28.6dBi and the side-lobe is less than 35.7dB. Due to the characteristics of high gain, low profile, compact, low side-lobe level, and ease of processing, this antenna is suitable for satellite communication stations.

articleTitle: Augmentation of Hybrid Integral Equations for Low-Frequency Analysis of Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) interaction with dielectric objects are formulated by hybrid field integral equations (HFIEs) which consist of electric field integral equation in the exterior and magnetic field integral equation in the interior of the objects, respectively. The method of moments is used to solve the equations where both electric and magnetic current densities are expanded by the Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis function. At low frequencies, the HFIEs are extended to the augmented HFIEs (AHFIEs) by additionally introducing the continuity equation of magnetic current and magnetic charge density as an extra unknown function. A numerical example for the low-frequency analysis of EM scattering by a dielectric sphere is provided to demonstrate the approach.

articleTitle: Advances in Bianisotropic GSTC-based Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present an overview of some of our recent advances on bianisotropic metasurfaces synthesized using susceptibility-based General Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs). Specifically, we discuss a series of related applications, which highlight the versatility and power of this method.

articleTitle: The Validity of Radiation Gauge
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Radiation gauge has been widely used in scattering problems to simplify the equations. However, radiation gauge may not always be correct. In this work, we demonstrate that in the case where polarization charges are present, radiation gauge may break down. We show two numerical examples in both time domain and frequency domain.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis based Optimized Vehicle Mounted Antenna Deployment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: One set antennas at three places on bus and car respectively, analyzed these two models via finite element analysis, derived the information of far fields of these antennas. After that, one discussed how the performances of antennas were affacted and eventually concluded some applicable suggestions on the promotion of omnidirectionality of far fields of antennas on vehicles.

articleTitle: Incorporation of Spatial Modulation in In VIVO Frequency Selective Nano Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Since Terahertz signals have proved their efficiency in ensuring safe human in-body based communications, future In-Vivo networks are envisioned to rely on them in order to ensure the forthcoming high-rate needs of the modern medicine. However, the propagation losses at these frequency bands are high. One viable solution for the quality of signal improvement is to enhance the spatial diversity through having recourse to multiple transmitting or/and receiving antenna elements. One undesirable, yet inherent, consequence of this is the generation of multi-channel interference (MCI). In this work, we propose to exploit the new spatial modulation technique with code division multiple access scheme to ensure a viable communication in In VIVO frequency selective Nano channels. The efficiency of the proposed scheme is highlighted through our simulation results.

articleTitle: A Meander Line UHF RFID Reader Antenna with Uniform Near-field Distribution
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel ultrahigh frequency (UFH) radio frequency identification (RFID) reader antenna is studied in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of multi microstrip meander line loop (MMLL) units, and each unit has an in-phase current along the loop. This antenna will provide a strong uniform magnetic field distribution in a larger interrogation range. The interrogation size can be adjusted by changing the number of units to meet the requirements of different RFID systems. To verify the correctness of this design, an antenna with 5 MMLL units is simulated. The simulated results show that the antenna achieves the good impedance matching over the frequency range from 900 to 964 MHz. And the proposed antenna achieves very uniform magnetic field distribution in the region of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{100}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \boldsymbol{240}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Measured-based channel capacity of multimode OAM system with dual-loop receiver
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: To solve the problem that the channel capacity is seriously affected by imperfect matching of transceiver array apertures, we propose a dual-loop receiver structure of multimode OAM communication based on uniform circular array (UCA) and investigate the channel capacity of OAM system on the basis of real measurements. Both measurement and simulation results show that the proposed OAM dual-loop receiver can effectively alleviate the power leakage caused by beam divergence, and then improve the channel capacity of multimode OAM communication.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Tapered Slot Antenna Array with Two-Decade (20:1) Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Realizing an antenna for ultra-wide bandwidth operation while maintaining a low profile are two necessary steps for many space-based antenna arrays. As the desire for more bandwidth increases, so does the complexity and engineering required to make such an element viable. Traditionally, to achieve bandwidths stretching from UHF to SHF require physically large elements with a half wavelength spacing in an array setting to get the desired performance. Some antennas even sacrifice performance (mismatch, loss) to achieve a wide bandwidth. The tapered slot antenna design presented in this paper achieves a 20:1 bandwidth, and is electrically small. The design takes advantage of a multiplexed matched feed method to get a good match across each band. The element is built utilizing 3D printing to aid the producibility of the unique structures associated with the design. The array aperture is dual linear with vertical and horizontal polarizations.

articleTitle: Application of Characteristic Modes on High Gain UWB Platform Integrated Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the cavity's influence on UWB (ultrawideband) monopole antenna structure using the theory of characteristic modes(TCM). An addition of square cavity converted the omnidirectional monopole to the unidirectional, high gain antenna. The cavity-backed antenna exhibits lesser impedance bandwidth and higher gain than monopole antenna. The change in antenna parameters due to platform or cavity has been analyzed using characteristic modes. The modal weighting coefficient gives the physical insight into the altered current modes due to cavity. It has been shown that identifying specific cavity modes can help in addressing performance deterioration of the antenna.

articleTitle: A Super Resolution Algorithms for Time Delay Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Time Delay Estimation (TDE) has been studied for a long time in the field of signal processing, sonar, radar, seismic waves, and radio waves. This paper uses the Matrix Pencil Method to restore super-resolution Time Delay Estimation (TDE) of signals in multi-path settings (MPM). To validate the proposed algorithm, errors were measured and compared to the traditional Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) and cross-correlation methods. TDE uses cross-correlation to develop calculations based on a single model called the optimal environment, but the accuracy of measurements continues to deteriorate as two or three signals are gradually entered at times shorter than the time period, necessitating super-resolution accurate time delay calculations such as MPM and MUSIC. Through correctly identifying and quantifying all components to their resolution limits and solving closely spaced frequencies, the proposed super-resolution MPM algorithm outperforms conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized End-fire and ±Broadside Millimeter-Wave Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A concept to realize a dual-polarized end-fire and ± broadside millimeter-wave (mmWave) antenna is devised and presented. The approach is based on a symmetrically stacked planar antenna (SSPA) topology. By utilizing the side radiation, which is perpendicular to the end-fire radiation, a dual-polarized quasi-spherical radiation is accomplished. This is achieved by controlling the phase difference between the top and bottom antenna elements. The extended design features dual-polarization with quasi-spherical radiation including end-fire and ± broadside directions. For one polarization, the phase difference between the top and bottom antenna elements is set to 180°. In addition, by exciting the antenna elements through another set of ports with in-phase signals, the other polarization is generated.

articleTitle: Single-layer Prephased 1-bit Metasurface Using True-time Delay for Symmetric Beam Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A single-layer prephased 1-blt metasurface for symmetric beam suppression under normally incident plane wave is proposed. By introducing true-time delay-based unit cells, the single-layer prephased metasurface is designed for millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless systems. Compared with conventional designs, the proposed design resolves the inherent problem of single-beam patterns on 1-bit reflective metasurfaces under normally incident plane waves based on a very simple single-layer design. The proposed metasurface exhibits excellent performance, including low sidelobe level and accurate beam direction from 38GHz to 42GHz, which stands an attractive candidate for 5G mmWave applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Dual-polarized Dual-passband Frequency Selective Rabsorber
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel miniaturized dual-polarized dual-passband frequency selective rabsorber (FSR) composed of a square loop resistive sheet loaded with double helix resonators (DHRs) and a dual-passband frequency selective surface (FSS). DHR have different band-pass frequency responses under two orthogonal polarized incident waves and increase the electric length of square loop, which improve space utilization and miniaturize the size of the FSR unit cell to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.115\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}}$</tex> and the overall thickness is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.097\lambda_{\mathrm{L}}}$</tex>. The simulation results indicate that the FSR has two transmission bands at 8.34 GHz and 11.7 GHz with low insertion loss, the bandwidth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{S}_{11}}$</tex> below -10 dB is up to 125.2% from 4.3 to 18.7 GHz, and the 80% absorption band are 4.6-6.3 GHz, 10.36-11.2 GHz and 13.3-19.1 GHz. The structure is of great significance to the study of multiband extension.

articleTitle: Ground Surface Clutter Suppression for GPR
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A sensor unit combining Ground penetrating radar (GPR) and EM Induction sensor for humanitarian demining activities was tested in the test lanes in Cambodia. Based on the acquired data, we found the difference of spectrum of the scattered wave from a buried land mines and other objects. We improved the signal processing algorithm used for image reconstruction to remove the ground surface clutter.

articleTitle: Co-Design of a Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line Filter-Antenna for Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work a design approach to synthesize a substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) based filter-antenna system is developed. The filter-antenna consists of a SICL based broadband filter and a rectangular slot antenna. Firstly, a SICL based fifth order bandpass filter operating with a center frequency of 28.3 GHz is developed utilizing parallel coupled half-wavelength resonators. The design and analysis of filter with fractional bandwidth of 12.01 % ranging from 26.6 GHz to 30 GHz to meet the needs of upcoming 5G band of communication is presented. Further, the proposed filter-antenna is realized by etching a rectangular slot on the top ground plane of the short-circuited parallel coupled SICL resonator. The proposed system with center frequency at 25.45 GHz exhibits a peak gain of 4.8 dBi with excellent filtering characteristics. Self-shielded and non-dispersive characteristics of SICL aids in design of a superior RF front-end with low noise figure.

articleTitle: Dispersion Relation Extraction of Periodic Leaky-Wave Antennas using Complex Eigenmodes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The problem of extracting the leakage factor and dispersion relation of a general periodic Leaky-Wave Antenna (LWA) is addressed using a complex eigenmode approach. The mapping between complex eigenmodes (ß,Ω) and the driven-mode dispersion relation (γ, ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) is used to extract the leakage factor of a radiating periodic LWA, and demonstrated using a slot array antenna as an example. The dispersion relation extracted from the unit cell mapping process shows an excellent agreement with an otherwise computationally intensive full-wave driven-mode simulation.

articleTitle: A Method for Sensing the Liquid in Infusion Bag
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a method for sensing the liquid in infusion bag. The dipole antenna combined with an AMC layer is attached to both sides of the infusion bag to sense the liquid. It operates at 2.4 GHz when the infusion bag is out of water/liquid. When the infusion bag is filled with water/liquid, its radiation is suppressed. The proposed scheme is flexible, compact and simple to provide a novel method for biomedical wireless sensors for infusion bag. It is practical to be used in the hospital.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized Aperture Fed Patch Antenna for LEO Satellite Constelations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The importance of satellite communications in the 5G and beyond 5G ecosystem has been widely recognized. Low orbits and the constant movement of satellites demand for adaptive antenna arrays in ground terminals. In this paper, a single patch element is designed for the K-band, broadly used in satellite communications. The antenna exhibits wide bandwidth and high switchable polarization performance (axial ratio < 3 dB over 2.2 GHz). All results sustain that this structure is a great candidate to implement in larger arrays used when broadcasting from space.

articleTitle: Combined Potential-Field Formulation for Densely Discretized Conductors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a novel combined potential-field formulation (CPFF) for rigorous analyses of electromagnetic problems involving closed conductors with various dimensions and arbitrarily dense discretizations. The formulation is based on the recently developed potential integral equations (PIEs) combined with the magnetic-field integral equation, as well as with another potential-based integral equation to reach resonance-free, low-frequency-stable, and iteratively efficient solutions using conventional discretization functions. Numerical examples demonstrate the superior performance of CPFF in comparison to other available formulations, particularly for challenging problems involving densely discretized structures and large numbers of unknowns.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Quadruplet Filtering-Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work a novel millimeter wave filtering antenna with two finite transmission zeros (TZ) using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is presented. The device employs a fourth-order quadruplet filtering topology having direct control over the TZ location. An equivalent slot antenna is used to maintain the filtering function, demonstrating a superior flat passband and roll-off compared to conventional cavity backed antennas. The device demonstrates a -10 dB bandwidth from 29.2 GHz to 30.4 GHz, with a peak realized gain of 5.2 dB and 4.9 dB and a low cross-polarization of -34 dB and -36 dB at boresight in the E- and H-plane respectively. The device is extremely compact at 0.77λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> x 2.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> x 0.17λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>.

articleTitle: Recently Revised IEEE Std 1502™-2020
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The recently revised and published IEEE standard, IEEE Std 1502™-2020 (Revision of IEEE Std 1502-2007) IEEE Recommended Practice for Radar Cross-Section Test Procedures, is briefly discussed. Topics include a short history of the standard, the definition of radar cross section (RCS), the major topics addressed by the standard, and a brief discussion of RCS test ranges.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Metadevice for Solving Equations and Inverting Matrices at RF Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Here, we describe some of the basic steps for solving mathematical equations with a metadevice, i.e., a subwavelength network that allows for the inversion of any desired matrix. The device consists of a connected network architecture of an elementary module. We examine possible RF implementations and provide simulated and experimentally measured preliminary results of this module, and demonstrate the case of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 2$</tex> matrix multiplication, paving the way towards the experimental implementation of metastructures with equation solving and matrix inversion capabilities.

articleTitle: Scalable Acceleration of Characteristic Mode Analysis Using Big Data Techniques
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present an approach to scale Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) using big data techniques over a wide range of Method of Moments (MoM) impedance matrices sizes. CMA is a computational toolbox that is used to decompose the electromagnetic response of a structure into a set of fundamental modes which provides physical insight into a target's electromagnetic response. CMA can potentially be time-consuming especially for large MoM matrices as well as when it is applied to a wide range of frequencies. Therefore, we propose a parallel processing approach to accelerate CMA using Apache Spark and Apache Hadoop, which are the most popular big data frameworks that support large-scale data processing in a commodity cluster. This paper describes our proposed approach and the scalability improvements that we achieved using Spark and Hadoop. Our approach improved the CMA processing time by 12X for 100 matrices of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{2\mathrm{K}\times 2\mathrm{K}}$</tex>) and by 10X for 51 matrices of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{14\mathrm{K}\times 14\mathrm{K}}$</tex>. Furthermore, our approach that builds atop big data techniques produced the same computational results as traditional tools for CMA.

articleTitle: Safety Metrics Investigation of an Electrically Coupled Patch Antenna for sub-6 GHz Portable Devices Serving 5G/6G Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we study the safety criteria of a capacitive coupled microstrip antenna operates at 5.4 GHz. We assess the safety of the antenna in terms of its Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) and Input Power Density (IPD). The antenna is placed close to a homogeneous dielectric cuboid of muscles to simplify the practical case. The values of the allowable fed power according to mass averaged SAR and area averaged IPD standards are compared. Both metrics are important to determine the safest limit that does not affect neither the body surface nor the internal organs.

articleTitle: Wave Manipulation through Advanced Smart Skins for Shaped Beam Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The possibility to design inexpensive artificial smart skins with advanced electromagnetic wave control capabilities is addressed with reference to their application in the Smart Electromagnetic Environment (SEE) framework. To this end, the complex multi-scale problem associated with the synthesis of the smart skin descriptors is firstly recast in terms of a phase-only inverse source one. The smart skin susceptibility tensor distribution and associated unit cell descriptors are then optimized through a System-by-Design (SbD) strategy. Preliminary numerical results are shown to assess the potentialities of the proposed design process in terms of both wave control and synthesis efficiency.

articleTitle: Ka-Band 3D Printed Wideband Dual-Polarized Antenna Array Fed by Differential Feeding Cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A millimeter-wave wideband dual-polarized 2 × 2 antenna array is investigated based on three-dimensional (3D) printing technology. A novel differential feeding cavity loaded with a short-ended cross-shaped waveguide and four shorting pins is designed to act as mode splitter and power divider for two polarizations. By combining with the modified cavity-backed self-supporting magneto-electric (ME) dipoles, good characteristics including wide bandwidths, stable gains and unidirectional radiation patterns for two polarizations can be obtained. It has been demonstrated that the proposed antenna array is suitable for millimeter-wave polarization diversity applications.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Range-Doppler Maps of Moving Targets in Traffic Scene
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper reports on unique signatures observed in Range-Doppler maps of various moving targets, including pedestrians, pets, bicycles, and vehicles, that can be found in typical complex traffic scenes. The radar data of these targets were collected using a newly developed fully-polarimetric high-resolution instrumentation radar operating at E-band frequencies.

articleTitle: Digitally Coded Metasurface Lens Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a millimetre wave band antenna set is designed using digitally coded metasurface lens for achieving gain enhancement and beam steering. An antipodal Vivaldi antenna with a two-bit digitally coded metalens operating at 28 GHz frequency with a gain enhancement of 3.5 dB, and total gain of 10.60 dBi is realized first. The designed two-bit coded metasurface placed at a distance of 24.5 mm from the antenna provides phase coherence for beam collimation. Furthermore, another transmit array antenna comprising four unit cells of varying transmission phases has been designed to steer the boresight beam of a microstrip patch antenna by 30° at 28 GHz frequency without employing any active elements.

articleTitle: PAF application on a large spherical reflector to survey 100 times faster than the FAST
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we describe an application of a Phased Array Feed (PAF) on a large spherical reflector, as a cost effective approach to realize a radio telescope with large collecting area and Field of View (FoV). Considering the neutral spherical reflector of the FAST telescope, calculations show that a PAF consisting of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$85 \times 85$</tex> elements with a spacing of 12cm could collect about 80% of the energy intercepted by a spherical aperture with a diameter of 300m at 1.4GHz, which is slightly higher than the efficiency of FAST telescope. And a FoV of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 2=4$</tex> square degree is achievable if a 20% gain reduction at the edge is acceptable. The fixed spherical surface makes the design and construction of the reflector much easier and less expensive than the active main reflector of FAST. The number of elements of the PAF is far beyond that of the current PAFs being developed for paraboloid reflector. Engineering challenges of and the prospective measures to cope with this large number may need to be investigated.

articleTitle: A Dual High-Order Mode Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present the design of a dual high-order mode leaky wave antenna. The antenna is designed to operate simultaneously at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{11}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{11}$</tex> modes, while typical leaky wave antennas (LWAs) operate at their fundamental mode, e.g., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{10}$</tex>. Utilizing the two orthogonal modes, our proposed design, not only doubles the channel capacity, but it also scans in both the elevation and azimuth planes. Broadwall slots are etched for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{11}$</tex> mode scanning from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-9^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24^{\circ}$</tex> in the elevation plane with a maximum gain of 14.77 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dBi$</tex>. By etching a second set of slots on the sidewall, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{11}$</tex> mode scans in the azimuth for a range of 29 degrees <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(65^{\circ}\ \mathbf{to}\ 94^{\circ})$</tex> achieving a maximum gain of 9.24 dBi.

articleTitle: Enhancement of THz Photoconductive Antenna Gain based on a Photonic Crystal Fiber Substrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents an index-guiding photonic crystal fiber (PCF) structure substrate to improve the gain for THz photoconductive antennas (PCAs). It is remarkable that the proposed substrate has the transverse single-mode and longitudinal multi-modes at 3.5308 THz. The directivity of the antenna in the case of the mode of the proposed substrate reaches 15.39dBi. In this mode, enhancement of the antenna gain can be achieved by increasing the number of longitudinal modes within limits.

articleTitle: Design of a Slotted Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna using a Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the use of a metasurface to improve the radiation properties of a Substrate Integrated Waveguide based slotted antenna is proposed. The design process of a 8 slot antenna covered by a metasurface and following a Chebyshev distribution is presented. We will compare the performance of this antenna and of a conventional one and demonstrate the improvement in the radiation performance that can be achieved without affecting its bandwidth.

articleTitle: On the Low-Frequency Scaling of Vector Potential Integral Equation Solutions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Vector potential integral equations (VPIEs) have recently been proposed as break-down free alternatives to field integral equations for analyzing low-frequency electromagnetic scattering problems. In this work, accuracy of VPIEs for perfect electrically conducting scatterers at low frequencies is investigated. Depending on the different representation of the vector potential formulation, four different integral equations in unknown electric current and normal component of the vector potential are obtained. To numerically solve these VPIEs, the electric current and the normal component of the vector potential are expanded using Rao-Wilton-Glisson and pulse basis functions, respectively. Inserting these expansions into two of the integral equations and using Galerkin testing yield a linear matrix system. Numerical results show that depending on the choice of VPIEs, the solution of this linear matrix system is inaccurate at low frequencies, similar to the magnetic field integral equation.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis for Active Manipulation of Electromagnetic Fields in Free Space
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a feasibility analysis of the active manipulation for electromagnetic (EM) fields is presented. The strategy of the EM fields control is to construct surface current sources that are able to control the EM fields in some near and far regions. We discuss the feasibility of the active scheme (with respect to power budget, control accuracy, and quality factor Q) as a function of the frequency and the distance between the control region and the source. The numerical simulations discuss the performance of the active field control scheme and illustrate some challenges and limitations.

articleTitle: A Shared NFC Antenna Using Metal Frame of Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a technology for operating the NFC antenna function by sharing the LTE (Long Term Evolution) metal frame antennas of a smartphone. It is to operate two functions of NFC and LTE with one antenna by connecting NFC circuit to the existing metal frame antenna through RF choke. By doing this, it is possible to remove the FPCB (Flexible Printed Circuits Board) NFC antenna, which can help to reduce costs and minimize smartphones. In the proposed structure that removes the FPCB NFC antenna and uses a metal frame, it was confirmed that it satisfies the EMV (Europay, Mastercard and Visa) certification standard, and there was no deterioration in the transmission and reception performance of the LTE antenna.

articleTitle: SAR Evaluation from High-intensity and Broadband Sources for Different Human Body Models
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes an intercomparison of the electromagnetic energy absorption by different gender and conformation human body models, when exposed to high-intensity broadband signals devices. In order to obtain the best estimation of the actual whole-body averaged (WBA) SAR values, a realistic configuration has been simulated. It consists of a typical scenario in which an adult is carrying a backpack device with antennas placed close to his neck and shoulders. This kind of instrumentation is commonly used in military equipment as backpack systems for communication purposes.

articleTitle: Fast Reduced Order Model of Low Frequency Integral Solver for Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A reduced order model of low frequency integral solver based on singular value decomposition is presented in this work. It can be easily utilized in analyzing the wireless power transfer system, even though the frequency as well as the distance between resonators and loops of WPT change simultaneously. The obtained numerical results show that the proposed reduced order model matches well with those results obtained by original low frequency integral solver.

articleTitle: A Wideband Concurrently Dual-Circularly Polarized Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dual-circularly polarized simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna is designed at ISM band. Four sequential rotated microstrip patch elements are excited by two sets of feeding networks: the feeding network of transmit (TX) antenna on the top side of the substrate for left hand circular polarization (LHCP), and the feeding network of receive (RX) antenna on the bottom side for right hand circular polarization (RHCP), or vice versa. The parasitic patches with an air gap are used to enlarge the gain bandwidth. The cancellation technique based on the phase cancellation and geometrical symmetry of antenna is employed. The simulation and measurement results show good agreement and demonstrate the good TX/RX isolation of greater than 35 dB across a wide bandwidth of 5–6 GHz. The TX/RX isolation reaches 48.5 dB @ 5.18 GHz, and the axial radio is better than 3 dB across the entire ISM band, which further proves the feasibility of this design methodology and the application in STAR and sensory integration.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Time-Delay Loss Quantification for High Symbol Rate Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A framework is proposed for quantifying signal degradation due to inter-symbol interference induced from the time-delay dispersion (also called group delay dispersion or pulse dispersion) of a non-timed array (e.g. phased array, reflectarray). A ray tracing technique is used to compute the element-by-element time delay and then summed and normalized in a corporate fashion to get an aggregate delayed response. This response is then quantified in a signal-level analysis in MATLAB to determine an upper bound on array size vs symbol rate.

articleTitle: Impact of Time-Bandwidth Product on Active Incoherent Millimeter-Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging uses transmission of random signals combined with an interferometric receiving array to generate images. Random signals are used to enforce spatio-temporal incoherence, a requirement for interferometric imaging that mimics the properties of thermal radiation. However, the finite bandwidth and duration of the transmitted signals limits the achievable incoherence. We investigate the impact of the transmitted waveform time-bandwidth product on image reconstruction. We evaluate the mutual coherence of the fields incident on the scene and the impact on relative target amplitude reconstruction and peak sidelobe levels (PSLLs).

articleTitle: Cloud Monitoring in Singapore Using GPS Residuals
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents cloud monitoring in Singapore using Global Navigation System (GPS) residuals. The GPS residuals are processed and shown in skyplots. For validation, the residuals in the skyplots are compared and analyzed against the sky images for cloud coverage. Results show that the residual values in the skyplots correlate well with the sky images in terms of cloud coverage. Thus, the effectiveness in cloud monitoring is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave PRGW ME Dipole Antenna with Surface Mounted Conical Horn for 5GB/6G applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband high gain printed ridge gap magneto-electric (ME) antenna with surface mounted conical horn for millimeter-wave applications is presented in this paper. Printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology is adopted to achieve a low-profile feeding structure to excite the dipole backed by a rectangular cavity. As a gain enhancing technique, a surface mounted conical horn, made from a very thin copper sheet is placed over the ME dipole antenna to achieve a realized gain of more than 15.3 dB. The proposed design exhibits a bandwidth of 7.5 GHz starting from 26.5 GHz up to 34 GHz. The proposed antenna is considered as a good candidate for millimeter-wave applications such as the future sixth generation (6G) of cellular communications.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Rampart Slotline Terminated With Patch for Low-Cost Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel wideband circularly polarized (CP) rampart slotline leaky-wave antenna (RSLWA) is proposed in this paper. The antenna is fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) in the middle of the antenna, and two chamfered CP patches are terminated at both ends. Compared with the terminating resistor, the terminating patch antenna turns the remaining energy at the end of the rampart slotline into radiation instead of being lost by heat. Compared with RSLWA with open or shorted terminals, the terminal patch reduces the reflected energy and increases the impedance bandwidth. The RSLWA is designed to operate at 5 GHz. Measured results show that the antenna has a peak gain of 7.6 dBic and more than −1dB radiation efficiency in the whole operating frequency band. The measured 3-dB AR bandwidth is 6.3% (4.8-5.14GHz) and −10 dB impedance bandwidth is 22.7% (4.52-5.68GHz). The proposed antenna features low cost, high radiation efficiency and wide bandwidth, which is suitable for various wireless applications.

articleTitle: Split-Field Domain Decomposition Algorithm with Fast Convergence for Electromagnetic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose a new split-field domain-decomposition (DD) algorithm, which can be readily parallelized in time domain. Different from conventional DD methods where interface fields are shared in common between adjacent domains, we split the field on the interface into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> components, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> is the number of domains sharing the interface. Each domain solves one component of the interface field. The resultant numerical system allows for each domain to be directly solved in a decoupled manner, and meanwhile the convergence of the interface solution can be achieved in a small number of iterations. Numerical experiments on a large integrated package structure demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed DD algorithm, and resulting parallel solver.

articleTitle: Adaptive Refinement for Scattered Field Quantities of Interest for the Coupled EFIE-MFIE
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We summarize the application of an adjoint-based adaptive mesh refinement strategy for surface integral equation (SIE) scattering problems. The approach enables targeting error in a user-defined functional and correcting the discretization accordingly. Moreover, the approach drives equilibration of the error contribution estimates, resulting in efficient and balanced meshes automatically. Finally, by leveraging an a priori error condition and the a posteriori adjoint-based error contribution estimates, the number of iterations required in the refinement process is not only drastically reduced, but consistent across chosen tolerances of the discretization error. We demonstrate the performance of the adaptive refinement strategy for enhancing the computation of scattered field quantities with p-refinement.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized mm-Wave Antenna Integrated within Microstrip PMC Packaging Cavity Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized cavity antenna is proposed within a back-to-back perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) packaging, created for two inverted microstrip feed lines with a common ground. For the x-polarized radiation (RF1), the cavity is excited via a slot etched in the ground, whereas a fork divider directly excites the cavity to generate orthogonal y-polarized radiation (RF2). The design and analysis are performed at 30 GHz. The antenna bandwidth is 3.5 GHz, covering 28.25 - 31.75 GHz with port-to-port isolation better than 40 dB. The broadside unidirectional radiation patterns are symmetrical for both polarizations. The antenna design is compactly restricted within the PMC packaging layers, without additional layers above the top radiating section.

articleTitle: From Tunable and Reconfigurable to Space-Time Modulated Multifunctional Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This abstract introduces a reconfigurable and multifunctional metasurface platform, that can adapt to various functional demands. It is shown that, by locally controlling parameters of each meta-atom, the metasurface can perform multiple reciprocal functions. In addition, by modulating the meta-atoms in both space and time, the same metasurface can provide nonreciprocal functionalities such as wave circulation and isolation. Switching between different electromagnetic functionalities is realized by setting different parameter values or different time modulation laws for tunable components embedded in each meta-atom, without the necessity of changing the metasurface body. We think that this technique is very promising for applications, especially in future adaptive and intelligent communication networks.

articleTitle: Receive Signal Strength- Based Human Activity Recognition
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel approach based on Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) used to discriminate Human Activities for biomedical applications, is presented in this paper. The proposed method use a machine-learning algorithm with discriminative features extracted from the slow fading component of the received signal. The impact of the demeaning window size used for the extraction of the slow fading is investigated and an overall accuracy of 94% is obtained with a window size of 50ms.

articleTitle: Design Of Reconfigurable Transmit-Reflect Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In order to realize the dynamic control of electromagnetic wave, a transmission and reflection type unit cell integrated with PIN diodes is proposed here. Based on the polarization isolation characteristics of grating, the transmission and reflection structures are designed separately. Under the premise of good reflection amplitude, the reflection phase difference within different diode states is around <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$180\pm 37^{\circ}$</tex> in the range of 5.3–11.8 GHz. By switching the four diodes' states, the unit possesses the perfectly transparent properties in the range of 7.3 to 8.6 GHz, and the transmission phase shift of 0° and 180° can be obtained simultaneously. To the end, perfectly transparent and reflective for orthogonal polarization within the same frequency band can be realized respectively, as the incident waves traveling from two different direction of the unit.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna for Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A low-profile, circularly polarized (CP) wideband antenna is a desirable component in any satellite communication system which requires high data transfer rate. Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna (MEDA) has emerged as an excellent candidate for such wideband application. However, the dimensions of a typical MEDA antenna restrict its practical use as an element for a rectangular array. Here we propose two techniques to miniaturize the printed MEDA to make it compatible with rectangular array configuration without significantly affecting its overall performance. For the proposed design, axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth and impedance bandwidth overlaps from 25.4 GHz to 31.5 GHz, with miniaturization of about 45% in one of the dimensions.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Antenna Using Annular Slots for 2.45 GHz ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized reconfigurable annular slot antenna with four PIN diodes for 2.45 ISM band applications is proposed. The proposed antenna has used a principle of slot antenna and has a parasitic element as a reflector. The proposed antenna which has a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.33\lambda_{0}\times 0.33\lambda_{0}\times 0.20\lambda_{0}$</tex> operates at 2.45 GHz, and forms ±45° polarizations. As a result of the simulation, a maximum gain and front-to-back ratio are approximately 6.28 dBi and 19.6 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of H-Plane Scanning Phased Array Antenna Using Huygens Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, Huygens metasurface is used to enhance the gain of an H-plane scanning phased array antenna. The Huygens meta-atom is realized by a pair of complementary rings with centrosymmetric structure and axisymmetric T-shape stubs, which are orthogonal to each other. The phased array is designed as a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> circular patch linear array. With the Huygens meta-lens loaded above the linear array, the fan beam radiated by the linear array is converted into the pencil beam, thus the gain of E-plane is improved. Fullwave simulation results show that the peak gain of the linear array is increased from 11.2dBi to 17.4dBi through loading Huygens lens. The gain fluctuation is less than 4.4dB in the ±26° scanning range.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Quarter-Wave Plate for Diffusion Bonded Slot Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A single-layered quarter-wave plate (QWP) is proposed and demonstrated for linear-to-circular polarization (LP-to-CP) conversion in the near-field of a slot array antenna. The QWP is based on a square unit cell with five elliptically shaped air holes - four on the edges and one in the center. The central ellipse is rotated by 45° which decomposes the incoming linear polarization into two orthogonally polarized components with 90° phase difference. The LP-to-CP conversion is demonstrated by simulating the proposed QWP in the near-field of an LP slot array antenna with a 3 dB axial ratio and −10 dB matching bandwidths of 5.1% and 8.9%, respectively, around 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation, and Measurement of Microwave Beam-Generating Structures With Near-Zero-Index Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present design, simulation, and measurement of microwave beam generators that consist of dielectric rods. The structures are based on near-zero-index (NZI) properties of rod arrays when they are designed and arranged in specific configurations to induce near-zero permittivity and/or permeability in the host media. Once NZI properties are achieved, directive beams can be generated by relatively simple shell structures that sur-round isotropic sources. In order to obtain customized patterns, we further use lattice irregularities to suppress undesired beams on selected directions. In addition to extensive simulations of both homogenized and actual models, the effectiveness of the designs is verified by measurements on prototypes that are fabricated via 3D printing. The results demonstrate the feasibility of efficient beam generation with well-designed arrangements of dielectric rods, thanks to their interesting NZI characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis of models to reduce complexity and simulation time of Multilayered Media for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the validation of mathematical equations which are used to derive effective dielectric constant and loss tangent of multilayered media is performed. The accuracy of the equations is verified using four models- a two-layer model based on same transmission and reflection coefficients, a two layer model based on parallel plate capacitors, a single layer model based on same transmission and reflection coefficients and a single layer model based on parallel plate capacitors. The EM simulations are performed on a multilayered media (a car bumper painted with four different dielectric paint layers) with a micro-strip array antenna resonating at 77GHz. The verification is done by comparing the antenna gain, the antenna phase and the Bidirectional losses in the four models. The models not only simplify the complexity of the structure but also reduce the EM simulation time.

articleTitle: Compact Slant $45^{\circ}$ Dual-Polarized Butler-based Omni-Directional MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of the compact ultra-wideband slant 45° dual-polarized Butler-based omni-directional MIMO antennas working at the frequency band of 1.69-2.69GHz. The proposed antenna consists of three panels of slant 45° dual-polarized dipole subarrays and two Butler-based azimuth beam formers. By replacing traditional T-splitter type azimuth beam formers of 2x2 MIMO antenna by the Butler matrix 3x3, the omni-directional 6x6 MIMO antenna can be realized without increasing the size of the antenna. A prototype of the proposed antenna is built and tested to validate the idea.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized SIW Cavity-Backed Patches Antenna with Air Cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel single feed wideband circularly polarized (CP) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed antenna with air cavity is presented in this paper. The proposed structure is mainly composed of two SIW cavities, aperture coupling slot, air cavity, and two patches. The CP operation is achieved by introducing a pair of L-shaped strips to the corners of the lower patch, and embedding a cross-slot on the upper patch. The proposed antenna exhibits a simulated impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 30.89% (13.96 to 19.06 GHz) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert \leq-10}$</tex> dB, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 14.67% (15.86 to 18.37 GHz) for axial ratio (AR) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\leq 3\text{dB}}$</tex>, and gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{6.86\pm 0.6\text{dBi}}$</tex> across the 3-dB ARBW. In addition, its AR can be kept below 3 dB over the entire 3-dB beam width. The proposed antenna also has a stable radiation pattern over the entire CP frequency band and exhibits good symmetry in all plane.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optical Beamforming using Horizontal Dielectric Wedges
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Quasi-Optical beamforming approach will be one of the most effective techniques in mmWave frequencies range to reduce the size, cost, power and improve efficiency of the entire process. This paper introduces a technique to form simultaneous minimally overlapping beams using horizontally oriented dielectric wedges. Beamsteering angle control can be obtained by varying the dielectric constant and thickness of the dielectric wedges. The design was simulated using Ansys HFSS and the results were validated using CST MWS.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study of a Low-frequency Wearable Device for Contactless Monitoring of Blood Glucose Level
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we propose a safe, wearable and contactless device for blood glucose level monitoring based on a low frequency RF radiating system. The innovative hardware arrangement is composed by two concentric RF spiral coils, inductively coupled and able to produce a focused magnetic field distribution; hence, the monitoring sensitivity can be significantly enhanced. First, we describe the hardware system and then, we perform full-wave simulations in order to validate the feasibility of the method.
