The obtained results support the proposed approach and suggest the possibility to integrate the radiating system in a wearable non-invasive device for the blood glucose real-time monitoring, encouraging further analyses.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Meta-Resonator Based Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for Sub 6 GHz Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized meta-resonator based pattern reconfigurable antenna is proposed for sub 6 GHz application. By exploring a novel dual-mode ring-shaped meta-resonator structure with in-phase and out-of-phase modes, a pattern diversity antenna with one omnidirectional pattern and one broadside pattern is researched and designed. A prototype of the proposed antenna with a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{0.005\ \lambda 0\times 0.34\ \lambda_{0}\times}$</tex> 0.17 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda_{0}}$</tex> is fabricated and measured. The measured overlapped - 10 dB bandwidth for two modes, port isolation, and peak radiation efficiency are 3.39-3.67 GHz (7.9 %, well covering LTE B42 band), -18 dB, and 84.4 %, respectively. Therefore, the proposed pattern reconfigurable antenna is suitable for sub 6 GHz 5G microcell or router applications.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Metasurface Polarization Convertor with Controllable Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Deep learning not only brings great changes to the field of image processing and voice recognition, but it also gradually affects the design of electromagnetic devices. Here, we propose an inverse design method based on neural networks to automatically output metasurface structure with controllable working bandwidth for linear polarization-conversion. As a result, relative bandwidth can be flexibly selected from 0 to 76% in the range of 7–20 GHz. The proposed method provides a platform to accelerate the on-demand design of meta-polarizer and other versatile devices for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Reception Optimization Strategies for UHF Mobile Beacons
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Reception optimization strategies seek to improve performance of directional signals to a receiver location. When performance improves, transmitters may operate with a lower power requirement and significantly reduce detectability through direction-finding attempts. Combined with Direction-of-Arrival estimation, a uniform linear array is used to optimize reception of mobile telemetry signals in the 466 MHz range. A time-delay beamsteering algorithm is implemented on a dipole antenna array to receive in the direction of an estimated signal with an overall gain of 3 dBi. A similar approach is simulated using diversity analysis with a signal-to-noise improvement of 7dBi. This study validates the aforementioned methods for directional selectivity using commercial-off-the-shelf configurations with the popular RTL-SDR dongle.

articleTitle: Synthetic Ultra-Wideband Phased-Array Transceiver for Millimeter-Wave Imaging Applications With On-Chip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of a synthetic ultra-wideband phased-array transceiver front-end in SiGe BiCMOS that is capable of providing the largest bandwidth among all RF millimeter-wave imagers reported in the literature. An ultra-wide imaging bandwidth of 100 GHz (10–110 GHz) is achieved by the integration of three adjacent, disjointed frequency sub-bands. Each sub-band includes a fully-integrated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 2$</tex> array of transceivers. Each transceiver includes a low-power differential pulse generator, a delay generator, a transmit-receive (T/R) switch, a low-noise amplifier (LNA), a multiplier, and an on-chip slot bowtie antenna.

articleTitle: RF-Induced Heating for Active Implantable Medical Device with Dual Parallel Leads under MRI
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the radio frequency (RF)-induced heating of active implantable medical device (AIMD) with dual leads under the exposure of 1.5T MR system. Simulations and experiments were used in the study. It was observed that the coupling between closely spaced dual-leads systems has lower RF-induced heating compared to the same system with a single lead. The effect of lead spacing on the RF-induced heating was also studied.

articleTitle: A Novel Coaxial Balun for High Power Electromagnetic Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel type of coaxial balun for High Power Applications in L band is presented. The device shows a compact configuration, and ease of integration with radiating elements, making it suitable for numerous applications as combiner, balun, symmetrizer and differential impedance transformer with high power capability. A fractional bandwidth of 8.6% at 1.3 GHz is achieved when using the device as the feeding network of a differential patch antenna. A total gain of 11.7 dBi was obtained.

articleTitle: Highly Parallelized Hybrid FDTD Solver for Simulating Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in Dense Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we describe a hybrid parallel FDTD solver for simulation of large-scale urban propagation scenarios that utilizes both shared and distributed memory capabilities of modern processors. Simulation results are presented for an accurate real-world physical urban model (Downtown Los Angeles) at HF band (40 MHz).

articleTitle: Coplanar-fed Planar Inverted-L Antennas (PILAs) for Miniature On-Metal RFID Tag Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A new type of miniature tag antenna, which comprises of a pair of planar inverted-L antennas (PILAs), is proposed for designing an on-metal RFID tag. The PILAs are symmetrical to each other and they are simultaneously fed by a narrow coplanar feedline, which lies along the line of symmetry of the tag. Despite being electrically small (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\ \text{mm}\times 35\ \text{mm}\times 3.18\ \text{mm}$</tex>), the proposed tag antenna can achieve high radiation efficiency of 51%, which is much higher than most of the contemporary miniature tags. As a result, the tag can achieve maximum read distance of ∼24 m on metal. Two notches are etched on the PILAs for introducing additional capacitance and inductance to the antenna's impedance for achieving conjugate match with the chip's impedance.

articleTitle: A Planar Wide-angle Scanning Array Using Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a pattern-reconfigurable planar array antenna with wide-angle scanning capability. It achieves wide-angle scanning by suppressing the grating lobes of the array antenna using pattern-reconfigurable antenna.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna With Suppression of Parasitic High Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact dual-band microstrip patch antenna with suppression of parasitic high order modes is presented. Firstly, a microstrip rectangular patch antenna working at the fundamental TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode is designed to create the first radiation band. Then, a U-shaped slot is utilized to create the second radiation band. The center frequencies of the first and second radiation bands can be adjusted independently. At last, each corner of the rectangular patch is chamfered and each non-radiation edge is cut by a rectangular region to suppress the radiation bands of parasitic high order modes. The proposed dual-band microstrip patch antenna has center frequencies of 2.4 and 3.5 GHz. The proposed antenna has merits of low profile, consistent radiation pattern, and suppression of parasitic high order modes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning: A Powerful Framework for the Real-Time Solution of Inverse Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work deals with the real-time retrieval of the electromagnetic (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$EM$</tex>) properties of an inaccessible domain starting from non-invasive measurements. Within this context, deep learning (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$DL$</tex>) is rapidly emerging as a powerful paradigm to solve inverse scattering (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$IS$</tex>) and imaging problems on a pixel-basis with unprecedented computational efficiency and accuracy. Accordingly, the main principles and fundamental aspects of the most diffused deep neural network (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$DNN$</tex>) architectures [i.e., convolutional neural networks (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$CNN\mathrm{s}$</tex>)] are briefly summarized, and an overview of the most recent works in this promising field of research is given. Paramount unsolved challenges are finally discussed to indicate some possible lines-of-research to overcome current limitations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$DL$</tex> strategies as applied to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$IS$</tex> and imaging.

articleTitle: Optimized Design of a Dual-Band PIFA Antenna Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The genetic algorithm (GA) is applied to optimally design a dual-band planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA). The slot mode of PIFA is determined by the encoding form of pixels and the optimal solution is achieved by improving the initialization of population in the GA. Also, the joint use of MATLAB-coded GA and high frequency structure simulator (HFSS) can more efficiently optimize the design. As a demonstration, the PIFA operating at the 3.4 GHz and 5.2 GHz frequency bands is designed, and its <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> parameters in the two bands are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-14\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-17.9\mathbf{dB}$</tex>, respectively. The simulation results validates the design.

articleTitle: A Very Low Profile Wideband Patch Array with Wide Scan Ability
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel planar cavity backed wideband wide scan microstrip patch antenna array. In order to obtain wide bandwidth capability without increasing the antenna profile, a cavity is placed on the ground plane. A very low profile linearly polarized antenna array is designed at the center frequency of 10 GHz with conical scanning ability up to 60°. The array has 21.5% bandwidth with active VSWR below 2. Proximity coupling is employed in order to achieve a low cross polarization level down to −70 dB. Connectors (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\ \Omega\ \text{SMA}$</tex>) and substrate (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}= 3$</tex>) have been chosen in accordance with convenient measurement setup and printed circuit board fabrication process, respectively. The dimensions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{a_{y}},\widehat{a_{z}},\widehat{a_{x}}$</tex>) of the unit cell of the array are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5\lambda_{0}\times 0.5\lambda_{0}\times 0.14\lambda_{0}$</tex>, with respect to the highest operating frequency (11.13 GHz).

articleTitle: Direction Finding with Cyclostationarity for multiple signals based on Time-modulated array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A direction finding method with cyclostationarity aiming to improve the performance for multiple signals based on time-modulated array (TMA) is proposed in this paper. By using the cyclic conjugate autocorrelation function (CCAF), the direction information of different signals can be effectively extracted after eliminating the interference of frequency spectrum aliasing caused by time modulation. With multiple binary phase shift keying (BPSK) signals, the simulation is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Compact Holographic Antenna using Pillbox Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact holographic antenna with a pillbox feeding structure. The pillbox feeding structure can illuminate the uniform field distribution in a large aperture. However, the pillbox feeding structure has large transmission losses. The miniaturized and high gain antenna is proposed with high aperture efficiency to compensate for this drawback. The proposed antenna operates at 24 GHz, and the maximum gain of the holographic antenna is measured with 21.2 dBi towards −11°.

articleTitle: A Hybrid RFID/Localization Antenna with HIS and 3D-Printed Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The need for tracking and localizing items/people through energy autonomous devices suggests the combined exploitation of Ultra High frequency (UHF) to supply power and Ultra-Wideband (UWB) signals for communication. This paper proposes the design and implementation of a versatile antenna to fulfil those requirements. The one-port spiral-dipole combination achieves the insensitivity to the background scenario through the presence of a High Impedance Surface (HIS) able to simultaneously guarantee unique performance, still maintaining a low-profile stack-up: no back-radiation in the entire frequency range, circular polarization in the UWB band, and high efficiency in the UHF one. The use of 3D printing reveals to be strategic for the robustness of the structure and for the adopted feeding mechanism.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized Wide-Angle Scanning Array With Low Sidelobe Levels and Low Cross-Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized phased array antenna is proposed for wide-angle scan with high-merit features of high port isolation and low cross-polarization in all the azimuth planes. The array element is comprised of stacked circular patches, parasitic cambered strips and a cylindrical hollow cavity fed by microstrip feeding networks in a substrate integrated waveguide cavity. Due to the array configuration in staggered lattice, the active array maintains acceptable wide-angle impedance matching and low sidelobe levels as the beams scan over a wide scanning volume within the frequency range from 3.3 to 4.0 GHz.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband and High-Efficiency Single-Sideband Time-Modulator With 2-bit Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) single-sideband (SSB) time-modulator (TM) with high efficiency is proposed and verified. The proposed TM with one decade (10:1) operation band-width is achieved by utilizing an UWB 2-bit all-pass networks (APN) phase shifter. Four phase states of the proposed 2-bit phase shifter with maximum phase error of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm7.8^{\circ}$</tex> over the entire bandwidth are switched in turn during each modulation period. Simulation results show that the power loss of the proposed TM is only 0.91 dB at maximum output power harmonic (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+1$</tex> harmonic) with less undesired harmonics at the center frequency from 300 MHz to 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of an Electrically Small, Low-profile, Parasitic Array for Wireless Electrocardiograph System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An electrically small and thin parasitic array is proposed for use in a wireless electrocardiograph system. Top loading and conformal element spacing allows the antenna to achieve an electrical size, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kr$</tex>, of 0.8. T-matching is used to counteract the drop in radiation resistance due to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.02\lambda$</tex> spacing between the driver and director. The two-element array achieves a peak realized gain of 5.1 dBi in the forward direction, with a front-to-back ratio of 14.3 dB. The simulated antenna is shown to produce a steady gain greater than 4 dBi when located at a distance greater than 4 mm away from human muscle tissue.

articleTitle: Finite State Markov Frequency Domain Channel Model for Vehicular Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A frequency-domain packet-level channel model for multipath fading channel is established in this paper. Based on the vehicular channel measurement, the channel state transition probability are analyzed to show the characteristics of rapid changing of high mobility channel in frequency-domain. The research on the frequency-domain packet-level channel model is a powerful tool to reveal the characteristics of frequency-domain channel of vehicular communications.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Pair Design for a Scan-angle Enhancement System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A physical two-Huygens' metasurface (HMS) lens system which doubles the scan angle of phased arrays is presented. For a highly efficient two-HMS lens system, we utilize the wire-loop unit cell design approach. Full-wave simulation results reveal that the proposed two-lens system improves the scan angle nearly by a factor of two, as designed, when the angle of incidence is below 15°. This approach enables a low-profile solution. Moreover, the results show that the directivities of the refracted beams by the two-HMS lens system are in good agreement with theory.

articleTitle: On the Effect of Variable Thickness of Conductive Trace for 3D Printed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Conductive filament such as Electrifi can be used for additive manufacturing of planar and non-planar geometries of microstrip antennas. The incorporation of variable thickness through a stair-step geometry of the top conductive trace of a planar microstrip patch antenna was presented here along with simulation and far-field measurements on the effects of such variability.

articleTitle: A Novel Miura-Ori Origami Reflectarray Antenna for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel high-gain Reflectarray Antenna (RA) design on a foldable structure, which is based on the Miura-Ori origami pattern. The antenna was designed to operate at 8.425 GHz for deep space communication. The origami RA was excited by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 2$</tex> circular polarized truncated corner patch array, positioned at a distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14\lambda$</tex> with a 10° offset angle. The proposed reflectarray can be efficiently stowed onto a 6U CubeSat, and in its deployed state it provides a large surface area of 459,566mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Therefore, it is well suited for small satellites and terrestrial tactical applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of Photoconductive Antenna Electrodes on Terahertz Signal Generation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of terahertz (THz) signals generated using photoconductive antennas (PCAs) based on different electrode geometries. The geometry of the electrodes influences the shape of the THz pulse and its frequency spectrum. The geometry can be used to provide improvements to the bandwidth of the PCA. We used the transient solution of the RF module of COMSOL Multiphysics to simulate the radiated electric field based on using the photoconductive current as a time domain source in the gap of the antenna. The dimensions of a previously published bowtie H-dipole antenna were used as reference that was modified to three new configurations. The results show that the bowtie-H-dipole antenna provided broader bandwidth compared with the fractal, slot, and/or circular shape electrodes PCAs.

articleTitle: Design of a Metasurface for a Circularly Polarized Antenna by Using Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A comparison between the properties of a metasurface composed by patch elements or loops is carried out by using the Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA). The final goal of achieving a metasurface able to radiate a circularly polarized field is obtained by using stubs that allows to fulfill the necessary conditions on amplitude and phase of the excited currents.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of a MIMO Antenna with DGS
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-isolation MIMO antenna based on the characteristic mode analysis. The antenna design uses monopoles as array elements, and the theory of characteristic mode (TCM) is used to determine the placement of DGS in the MIMO antenna design to improve the isolation between the element ports. To improve the isolation, the DGS should be placed in a specific position to attenuate the coupled mode without affecting the uncoupled mode. If there is no such specific location, the isolation cannot be further improved. The simulation results show that the designed antenna operates in the frequency band of 2.9~ 4.2 GHz, which covering the 5G communication band of 3.3 ~ 3.6 GHz, and the minimum isolation is improved from 13 dB to 25 dB.

articleTitle: Ripple suppression in 300GHz band cylindrical lens
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A 4 sectoral horn E-plane phased array fed cylindrical lens was designed for 280GHz 28dBi E-plane fan beam. Mechanical H-plane scan across <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 12^{\circ}}$</tex> by sliding was satisfactory, but E-plane phased array scan was affected by 2.5dB ripple from standing waves within the lens. In simulation, both serrating and curving the E-plane ends of the lens were found to suppress the ripple without affecting H-plane scan.

articleTitle: Real-Time CSI-Based Wireless Imaging for Human-Machine Interaction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In human-machine interaction systems, device-free and privacy-aware activity monitoring and gesture recognition is of great interest. In this framework, this work introduces a multi-step wireless imaging approach based on channel state information (CSI) and machine learning for the user's presence detection, localization, identification, and gesture recognition by using commodity Wi-Fi signals. The preliminary experimental validation in a real environment shows an excellent classification accuracy of 98%.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Metamaterial Microwave Absorber with Quasi-full-angle Stability
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel miniaturized metamaterial microwave absorber with quasi-full-angle stability is proposed in this paper, where the meander line and the strong coupling between the patches are applied to increase the angular stability and decrease the structure size. The results show that the absorption peaks are always maintained at 5.2 GHz for TE mode from 0° to 80°, and TM mode from 0° to 40°, while the absorption rate of more than 80% is maintained at 5.2 GHz for both TE and TM mode from 0° to 60°. The miniaturized structure is only 3 mm (about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.06\lambda$</tex>) in size while only about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.03\lambda$</tex> in thickness. The proposed metamaterial microwave absorber can be widely applied to electromagnetic interference shielding especially in narrow space application.

articleTitle: Design of A Broadband Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna With Differential Feeding
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband differentially fed circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna is designed. Combined with the field distribution of patch antenna, a double-layer differential microstrip feeding structure is proposed to form a circular polarization. The differential CP antenna works around 28.0 GHz, with a −10 dB impedance bandwidth and 3-dB impedance bandwidth of 13.2% and 7.0%, respectively. Within the achieved bandwidth, the radiation pattern has excellent conformality and symmetry. The height of the antenna is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.049\lambda_{0}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the operating wavelength at 29.0 GHz in the free space), achieving a low-profile design.

articleTitle: Solving 4,000 Wavelengths 2-D TM Scatterer Using Entire-Domain High-Precision MoM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present results for entire-domain analysis, based on method of moments, of 2D strips with cross-section length of 4,000 wavelengths. The strips are made of perfect electric conductor and are considered to be infinitely thin. The encountered singular integrals are calculated using a singularity cancellation scheme that ensures high precision results. Due to the high precision of integration and the usage of Legendre polynomials (basis functions) with the maximal order of 14,000, the strip with the cross-section length of 4,000 wavelengths is solved. The surface current density, obtained from the proposed approach, is compared to the current approximation obtained from commercial software. The results show that if high-precision integration is provided in conjunction with Legendre basis functions then a strip of the cross-section length up to 4,000 wavelengths can be analyzed as a single mesh element.

articleTitle: A New Curvature Based Shaped Reflector Antenna Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel curvature-based shaped reflector antenna design technique using the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) algorithm is presented. An approach based on optimizing the profile of a curve representing a rotationally symmetric reflector is proposed. In this method, the reflector shape is optimized with few design variables and an ideal design is found within a very small number of iterations. The validity of this method is verified by an application example and its advantages are compared with a reflector surface represented using the modified Jacobi polynomials.

articleTitle: DeeptDCS: Real-Time Estimation of Currents Induced During Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation via Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes DeeptDCS, a deep learning-based real-time emulator to estimate the currents induced during the transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS). The DeeptDCS takes the volume conductor model of a human head and the excitation parameters as inputs and provides the tDCS-induced three-dimensional current density across the whole head as output. The DeeptDCS obtains the current density more than 112x faster than the finite element-based open-source SimNIBS simulator while achieving a mean absolute error less than 0.1%.

articleTitle: Wideband and Wide Beam-Scanning Phased Array Antenna Design for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \times 5$</tex> stacked patch rectangular phased array, along with its feeding network, is designed and fabricated in a multilayered low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) substrate. The single element of the phased array is a dual linear polarized stacked patch microstrip antenna which has improved impedance as well as 3-dB gain bandwidth due to the stacked patch approach. Based on the field distributions, the single element's orientation is optimized to reduce the mutual couplings between the adjacent elements for a wide beam scanning range over a wide frequency band. The features of multilayered implementation, low dielectric loss, and excellent packaging properties ensure a compact and high-efficiency phased array design and qualify this design as an antenna-in-packaging (AiP) design.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Antenna with Isoflux pattern for Space IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a circularly polarized iso-flux antenna for IoT from space application at 868MHz. The structure is based on a tri-fillar helix configuration. Compare with classical solution, this new configuration can provide up to 2dB more gain at 30° of elevation.

articleTitle: Multipoles THz Metamaterial Biosensor for Low-Density Biomarker Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a highly sensitive multipole THz metamaterial biosensor on a High Resistivity Silicon (HR-Si) substrate is proposed to detect low-density biomarkers. The presented full-wave simulation demonstrated asymmetric, high-Q, and line-shape resonance modes at the frequencies between 870–890 GHz. The results show the metamaterial biosensor's ability to detect an ultra-thin layer of the analyte with a low-density biomarker.

articleTitle: A Wideband Phased Array Antenna with Grating Lobe Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of wideband phased array antenna, which allows for greater than 0.5λ inter-elemental spacing, while cancelling and mitigating the effects of the grating lobes. This method utilizes the concept of a multiple mode antenna element, leveraging the common mode and differential mode to synthesize two orthogonal radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Circular Arrays in Elevation and Azimuth Planes for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Circular antenna arrays offer unique beam steering advantages over linear arrays which may be utilized in adaptive beam steered radar applications. Due to their inherent symmetry, circular arrays may be steered in the elevation plane as well as 360-degrees in azimuth. In this paper, two prototype passively phased circular arrays and corresponding feed systems are presented. The first array is designed for a narrow beam with small physical footprint to scan a conical broadside region. This array is a microstrip patch array designed at 10 GHz using HFSS and three prototypes are manufactured with distinct phase excitations to demonstrate the conical beam steering capability. The second array is designed at 2.45 GHz to scan a 360-degree azimuth region and is an 8-element circular array of CPW-fed dipole-like radiating elements. The microstrip array is fabricated and the experimental results show excellent correspondence to simulation. The second array is under fabrication.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Surface Mountable Chip Antenna for 5G WiMAX / WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an electrically small chip antenna is presented for 5G WiMAX and WLAN applications. In this work, multiple vias and virtual ground (VG) are used to design a multiband miniaturized antenna. The feeding pad for the antenna is mounted on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50-\Omega$</tex> microstrip feed line. The proposed antenna offers −10dB impedance bandwidth of 130 MHz and 440MHz in WiMAX and 5GHz WLAN band respectively. The surface area of the chip antenna is approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.09\lambda\times 0.04\lambda\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> correspond to the wavelength at 3.5GHz. Due to its compact surface area, the proposed antenna can be mounted onto the circuit board of any wireless devices such as a dongle, Wi-Fi receiver, laptops smartphone etc.

articleTitle: Gradient Metasurface Dome implements a Matrix Beamforming Network for 2D Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we present a metasurface-based dome to be placed above a bidimensional antenna array able to synthesize a radiation beam pointing towards the specific direction in elevation and azimuth defined by the antenna that is radiating. The metasurface is designed for acting similarly to the beamforming network, allowing controlling the beam direction by switching power to the desired beam port. The metasurface consists of a dense array of Huygens unit-cells, each of which exhibits an extremely low insertion loss and the desired phase shift. The profile of the transmission coefficient across the surface is engineered to transform the spherical phase fronts radiated by the antennas into a plane wave propagating towards a specific direction. Here, the operativity of the proposed metasurface is verified by illuminating it with a set of antennas arranged into a 6×6 array, enabling its capability to radiate towards 36 possible different directions. The metasurface dome reduces the complexity of the antenna system, avoiding the need for a beamforming network, and enables the activation of more than one beam, or even all of them, simultaneously.

articleTitle: A Multiband Dual-Polarized Shared-Aperture Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact triple-band dual-polarized shared-aperture antenna array is developed and proposed. By flexibly applying the bandstop and bandpass frequency selective surface, a low band antenna operating in the 0.69-0.96 GHz band (LB), a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> mid band antenna array operating in the 1.8-2.7 GHz band (MB), and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4$</tex> high band antenna array operating in the 3.3-3.8 GHz band (HB) are successfully integrated within a compact volume of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.69\lambda \mathbf{L}\times 0.69\lambda \mathbf{L}\times 0.177\lambda \mathbf{L}(\lambda \mathbf{L}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at 0.69 GHz). Simulated results show that the excellent impedance matching and stable radiation performance are achieved all over the whole band.

articleTitle: Multichannel Metagrating Diffusers for Broad-Angle Radar Cross Section (RCS) Reduction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present an analytical scheme for the design of wide-angle metagrating (MG) diffusers, featuring a sparse periodic arrangement of polarizable particles (meta-atoms) embedded in a realistic fabrication-ready printed circuit board (PCB) configuration. Based on the Floquet-Bloch theorem, we model the MG as a multiport network, and design the meta-atom constellation and geometry to evenly spread the impinging power among numerous scattered waves in different directions, while specifically suppressing retroreflection. By enforcing multiple constraints simultaneously, we show that as little as three meta-atoms per period are sufficient to obtain this response over a broad angular range, thus offering an innovative solution to monostatic and bistatic radar cross section (RCS) reduction.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Base Station Antenna Array with Suppressed Cross-Band Mutual Scattering
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, new solutions to address the cross-band mutual scattering issue that causes the distortion of radiation patterns in dual-band antenna arrays are presented. A capacitance-loaded high-band (HB) element is innovated to mitigate the influence of HB elements on low-band (LB) radiation. A choking technique is implemented in LB antenna design to minimize the influence of the LB elements on HB radiation. A dual-band array section with the capacitance-loaded HB elements and double-arm choked LB element is fabricated and tested. The experimental results demonstrate that the cross-band scattering in the dual-band array is largely eliminated, and the array achieves stable radiation performance across well-matched bands.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line Fed Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna for 5G
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna employing substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) feed is proposed. The antenna utilizes four via-wall shorted patches on the top ground plane of SICL structure to obtain magneto-electric operation. Further, the bottom ground plane and SICL via-wall are used as cavity to improve the gain and front to back ratio (FBR). Full-wave simulations show that the antenna exhibits a fractional impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 28.7% with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{f_{0}=29.84}$</tex> GHz with peak realized gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6.83\pm 0.5\text{dBi}}$</tex> and FBR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{> 16\text{dB}}$</tex>. The radiation antenna efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 95\%$</tex>. It is designed on Rogers 5870 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\epsilon_{r}$</tex> = 2.33, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tan\delta=\boldsymbol{0.0012})$</tex> and measures <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.515\lambda_{0}^{2}}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{f_{0}=29.84}$</tex> GHz.

articleTitle: A Metal-Only Partially Reflective Surface for Metallic Resonant-Cavity Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A lightweight metal-only partially reflective surface (PRS) is proposed to realize a fully metallic resonant cavity antenna (MRCA). This PRS comprises a 2D array of dual-layer unit cells where each layer is made from a thin metal sheet. The top metal sheet of the unit cell has narrow slots, while the bottom layer has crossed metal stripes. The cell provides a positive gradient in the phase of the reflection coefficient. An MRCA designed with a PRS made of this unit cell has a much wider directivity bandwidth. The numerical simulations predict that the MRCA has a peak directivity of 18.3 dB and a directivity bandwidth of 1.33 GHz. The overall design structure of MRCA simplified the fabrication process by eliminating the isolating dielectric layers typically used between metal layers, which consequently help to reduce the weight and cost of the antenna.

articleTitle: A Bidirectional Pattern of DRA by Employing Cylindrical Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile bidirectional pattern cylindrical DRA antenna with single and double cylindrical spoof surface plasmon polariton (CSSPP) structures. The resonant structures are placed over a dielectric substrate. The omnidirectional pattern of cylindrical DRA in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ</inf>mode gets converted into a bidirectional pattern with the proximity placement of even mode resonating cylindrical SSPP structures. Moreover, the proposed antenna has single CSSPP, and double CSSPP resonator resonates at 2.4 GHz and 2.48 GHz, respec-tively. It exhibits a lower value of cross-polarization in the desired direction.

articleTitle: A 3-State Broadband Circularly-Polarized Unit Cell Enabling Steerable Reflectarrays for CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The growing applications of CubeSats have necessitated the innovation in low-profile CubeSat antennas that can achieve demanding performance. This work presents the design of a reconfigurable unit cell for reflectarrays to achieve broadband circular polarization (CP) beam steering on CubeSats. The element contains three Archimedean spiral arms, and the connections among the arms can be switched by p-i-n diodes to produce three states of phase shift. The simulated unit cell demonstrates promising broadband performance in terms of CP reflection magnitude and phase stability. A 14 x 14 elements reflectarray based on this unit cell is simulated, and has achieved RHCP beam scan up to 60°, with a directivity variation of 1 dB and axial ratio less than 3 dB in the range of 17.8 – 20.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Combination for Phased Array and ESPAR Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: a low-cost antenna system with high directivity is presented, with possibility of shaped beam in the vertical plane and beam switching in the horizontal plane, ensuring full 360 degrees coverage. The proposed antenna provides a higher directivity than the pattern of a regular Electronically Steerable Parasitic Antenna Radiators (ESPAR) while remaining much simpler than a phased array. The antenna system is made of two concentric rings, each consisting of 6 elements. Only three elements are active at a given time, the others are terminated with the reactive loads. The feeding and command structures are particularly simple. The proposed antenna is fabricated and measured for its performance.

articleTitle: A Wide-Band Metasurface for Asymmetric Microwave Transmission with Circular Polarization Conversion for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The polarization state control and manipulation of electromagnetic waves using chiral metasurfaces have various applications in satellite communications. The aspect of asymmetric transmission (AT) that allows a medium to pass the EM waves in one direction while having restriction in the opposite direction, adds an additional degree of freedom in order to facilitate one-way communication functionality. The proposed metasurface achieves linear to circular (LTC) polarization conversion with wideband AT functionality. This is accomplished for frequencies below 18 GHz using a bi-layered metasurface structure consisting of mutually twisted split ring resonators (SRRs). To achieve chirality, the proposed metasurface's top and bottom layers have a 90° rotation angle. For the frequency band of 13.34-13.83 GHz, the transmission goes up to − 4.3 dB. The maximum polarization extinction ratio (PER) of 45 dB has been achieved for the 490 MHz bandwidth at 13.5 GHz. The relatively simple structure, and the wide bandwidth enabled by using a bilayer metasurface, makes the proposed structure a promising design as a polarization controlling device that can be used in satellite communications.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a 77 GHz Time-Modulated Transmitter Array for Enhanced Backoff Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a time-modulated array architecture for enhanced power backoff efficiency. This technique can be combined with conventional power backoff enhancement methods such as Doherty amplifiers. With the proposed time-modulated array PBO technique, we demonstrate in simulation a power drain efficiency enhancement of 70% times larger compared with a typical class A/B amplifier operating at 77 GHz at −3dB backoff region and 90% times larger at −6dB backoff region.

articleTitle: EIRP Enhancement of Multi-Facet Phased Antenna Arrays for Full-Azimuth Radio Coverage
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An approach to the compensation of scan loss at large scan angles in multi-facet active phased antenna arrays for full-azimuth radio coverage is discussed. The proposed methodology is based on the coordinated management of the insertion phase shifts along the beamforming network of array panel pairs in equilateral triangle and square arrangements. The achieved enhancement of equivalent isotropically radiated power compensates for the scan losses experienced at about ±60° and ±45° in triangular and square panel array configurations, respectively. The presented results are based on full-wave simulations, and demonstrate effectively the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Improvement of Rectangular Microstrip Antenna by Mode Specific Meta Element Concept
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A unique idea of controlling of specific mode (s) of microstrip patch antenna is proposed here. It follows a simple technique using an external pin of length λ/4 attached to the radiating element. The overall structure becomes sensitive to different modes based on their field and current distribution. We specifically aim to suppress the XP generating TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode here. The strategic patch-pin configuration, therefore, perturbs modal property of the orthogonal TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode and leaves TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> unaffected. Thus the traditional nature of the radiating element is converted to a different kind of ‘meta’ nature. Here the concept and design insight have been explained based on our very recent investigation. Exclusive features of this meta-element should find potential scopes by exploring other different variations for future uses.

articleTitle: Application of Dielectric Resonator Antenna in Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Wireles biomedical telemetry through Implantable Medical Devices (IMD) has been one of the major interest of human kind in present times due to life supporting advantages. As sensors, actuators, battery and antenna comprises the IMD and role of efficient radiator describes the quality of implantable device. However, Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRA) have been proved more efficient in comparison to their contemporaries in different applications due to its inherent properties, but application of DRA in implantable devices is not proposed yet. In this paper, a rectangular DRA resonating at 2.45 GHz excited by coplanar waveguide feed has been proposed for in depth implantable applications.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Millimeter-Wave Digital Beamformer : Design and Experimental Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel receiver architecture for Millimeter-Wave (mm-Wave) digital beamforming (DBF) applications. The receiver employs On-Site Code Division Mul-tiplexing (OS-CDM) scheme to receive and uniquely encode signals from multiple antenna elements using orthogonal Walsh-Hadamard (WH) codes. Subsequently, the signals are combined and passed through a single analog-to-digital converter (ADC). This approach eliminates the need for multiple power hungry ADCs, thus significantly reducing the size, weight, cost and power (SWaP-C) requirements. Further, the digital hardware complexity of the receiver is reduced by more than 95%. A major challenge is the possible degradation in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) due to inter-channel interference (ICI). In this paper, we introduce new schemes to achieve greater than 30 dB inter-channel interference ratio reduction across a bandwidth of 400 MHz.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Fully Digital UWB Antenna for Direction Finding Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a new generation of ultra-wideband (UWB) radio frequency direction-finding system. The architecture of such a system is based on phase interferometry and exploits all leading-edge technology solutions such as the direct sampling of the entire analog band or the introduction of Artificial Intelligence for the processing of incoming RF signals. Thanks to these new solutions, a minimum number of antennas is needed to cover a multi-octave band capable to operate in the so-called folded mode. The presented solution is based on four full-band EM interferometer antenna array. The same signal collected from each antenna, after a first analog treatment, is then digitized with different sampling frequencies to get the diversity required for solving the frequency ambiguity problem. The Machine Learning approach is then adopted to realize the direction of arrival estimation. Comparisons between standard processing techniques and ML approach confirm the effectiveness of the presented solution.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Direction Finding Based on Time-modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An omnidirectional direction-finding method with three-element time-modulated array (TMA) is proposed to realize direction finding within 360°. By extending the linear array to a planar array, a new spatial degree of freedom can be provided to solve the front-to-back ambiguity of conventional direction finding with TMA. Meanwhile, the shape of the planar array is discussed to improve the direction-finding performance. Numerical simulations and experiments are performed to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Arbitrary Pulse Shaping using Nonuniform Spacetime Modulation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces and demonstrates a pulse shaping technique based on nonuniform spacetime modulation. This technique allows arbitrary pulse shaping and is in this regard unique, to the knowledge of the authors. Although we restrict here our attention to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+1\mathrm{D}$</tex> (1 dimension of time + 1 dimension of space) system, this idea can be extended to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+2\mathrm{D}$</tex> (and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1+3\mathrm{D}$</tex>) systems, which will feature richer scattering phenomenology given the simultaneous transformations of the temporal vectorial spatial spectra of pulses.

articleTitle: Scanning Reflectarray with Embedded Structural Grid for Deployable Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: a scanning reflectarray for applications demanding deployable, lightweight and power-efficient apertures is presented. The array's novel panel construction features a structural aluminum grid embedded within the antenna elements, allowing the assembly to be inherently rigid, yet lightweight and resistant to heat-induced warping. The array's reflective phase-shifting antenna elements are based on FET switches mated with variable-length transmission lines, allowing for very low DC power operation. Details on array design, prototype realization and experimental validation are presented.

articleTitle: Radar Antenna Gain Improvement Using an Integrated In-Package Dielectric Rod Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain microstrip antenna integrated with dielectric rod superstrate is paired with commercial off-the-shelf radar module. The hybrid mode theory is utilized to design the proposed superstrate providing gain improvement and range detection enhancement. Using a low-cost rapid manufacturing 3D printing technology, four 3D printed dielectric rods are designed and fabricated for pairing with the radar module transmitter and receiver antennas. Compared to a stand-alone radar module, a prototype of the proposed in-package dielectric rod superstrate integrated with the radar module provides 6.6 dB overall gain enhancement for both elevation and azimuth directions.

articleTitle: Radiative Performance of a Vivaldi Antenna Equipped with Petal-Shaped and Massive Lens
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The radiative performances of a high-gain wideband Vivaldi antenna equipped with petal-shaped and massive dielectric lenses are presented. A full-wave numerical technique was employed to include surface wave propagation effects in the dielectric substrates forming the antenna elements and the petal-shaped lenses, as well as diffraction occurring at substrate truncations. Information useful for choosing the most suited lens (massive or petal-shaped) to fulfill system design requirements in terms of weight, cost, and realized gain, are presented.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-band Decoupling Network for Two Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band decoupling network for two antennas. Design formulas are derived with systematic design procedures. Two benchmarks are presented to elaborate on the design procedure. Results show that the network offers impedance matching, high isolation, and high efficiency at both frequencies, verifying the proposed concept and theory.

articleTitle: A First Implementation of a Single-Layer 4×4 Butler Matrix on Flexible PET Using Printed Silver
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper shows the fruition of a first ever 4×4 12.5 GHz Butler Matrix built on 127 µm (5 mil) polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate; using conductive printed silver [Ag] on the top layer and plain copper (tape) on the bottom (back) ground layer. The beam(s) of the matrix had peak realized gain of −32 dBi due to the heavy loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> = −30dB to −40dB at 12.5 GHz) of the matrix. While thin PET is lossy (tanδ≈ 0.02) and printed silver has poor conductivity (σ = 2.6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>S/m), the thin PET's flexibility and silver ink's quick printing ability can be valuable to lots of practical applications in the mass production sector (and Ag can always be replaced by copper to improve loss). It is with hope that this work incites (and gives rise) to further progress and research in this field for the future development and improvement of such flexible and steerable antennas.

articleTitle: A Novel Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Electrochemically-Controlled Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel reconfigurable antenna that has three polarization modes: left-handed circular polarization (LHCP), right-handed circular polarization (RHCP), and linear polarization (LP). The reconfigurability of the antenna is based on electrochemically-controlled liquid metal. The basic structure is a probe-fed square patch antenna with four circular slots. 3-D printed containers are attached to the patch, in which NaOH solution and liquid metal are placed. By adding a positive DC voltage to the liquid metal and a negative one through ring-shaped copper wires surrounding the liquid metal, the radius of the liquid metal drop can change due to its electrochemical feature. The working mode of the antenna can thus be reconfigured. Simulation results by Ansys HFSS are presented.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Dual-Polarized 4×4 MIMO Multi-Beam RET Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of the ultra-wideband dual-polarized 4×4 MIMO remote control electrical down-tilt (RET) three-beam antennas for wireless communications at the frequency band of 1.69-2.69 GHz. Based on the required specifications such as gain, the range of the electrical down-tilt, the azimuth beam coverage, the cross-over point between beams, the side lobe level, and the grating lobe, ultra-wideband dual-polarized 4×4 MIMO three-beam RET antennas have been designed, implemented, and tested.

articleTitle: Complex-Impedance Dipole Antennas as RFID-Enabled Ice Monitors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: RFID tags can operate in a wide variety of environments enabling battery-free pervasive sensing. In this paper, time-varying impedance measurements are presented to evaluate the sensitivity of inductive-matched dipole antennas as ice thawing monitors. Relative Signal Strength (RSS) measurements of an encapsulated RFID tags based on a commercial IC are presented showing that the tags can be read for up to 45 minutes inside 9 mm-thick thawing ice. Furthermore, the relationship between the ice thickness and the RSS of the ice-loaded RFID tags. The experimental results show that inductive-fed dipole antennas are highly suited for RFID-based monitoring of ice formation and thawing for smart city and remote sensing applications.

articleTitle: On Evaluation of Incident Fields from Near Sources in Method of Moments Layered Media Solvers
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Unified methodology for evaluation of matrix and the excitation vector elements in Method of Moments discretization of Mixed-Potential Integral Equation with multilayered media kernel is proposed. It allows for evaluation of the reaction integrals of the incident electric field produced by sophisticated impressed current sources in the near vicinity of the objects embedded in layered media using the same functionality as that used for evaluation of the matrix elements. The method is demonstrated on the example of Hertzian electric dipole radiation in the close vicinity of dielectric capsule embedded into three layer stratified medium.

articleTitle: Ten Fundamental Antenna-Theory Puzzles Solved by the Antenna Equation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Describing antenna performance in the time domain has always been challenging, due to a lack of standardized definitions. In the frequency domain, gain and realized gain are commonly used, however, no analogous terms exist in the time domain. Without a common standard, the development of ultrawideband antennas is impeded. To address this, the antenna equation has recently been developed. It is shown how to combine gain with a meaningful phase, and what the time domain analog of gain is. It is shown how to relate antenna impulse response to realized gain. It is also shown how to use signal flow graphs to simplify and solve complicated antenna problems. With these examples, we should finally be ready to adopt as standards new terms that emerge from the antenna equation.

articleTitle: Multiple scan state using mechanically reconfigurable parasite antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper concern the use of cubesats to operate GNSS-R. It relates to the use of mechanically reconfigurable parasites to deviate a circularly polarized beam from its initial direction. More attention was paid to the ability to scan in all azimuthal directions than to increase the scanning range in elevation. Simulations show that a limited reconfiguration of a very simple system composed only of 4 dipoles and 4 parasites allows considerable scanning. Perspectives on how to improve the radiation system are given.

articleTitle: Link-Quality Measurement and Performance of WirelessHART in Industrial Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A practical and accurate link quality estimation mechanism is important for the upper protocols and algorithms to achieve better performance in wireless networks. This article analyzes the performance of WirelessHART in a harsh environment (i.e., Aluminum Smelter). Both RSSI and LQI decrease with the separation. In addition, Wi-Fi interference may degrade the performance significantly in industrial environments, and hence its use has to be monitored and controlled.

articleTitle: Analytical Analysis and Simulation of Structures of Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents an analytical analysis of the wireless power transmission system in comparison with the results of simulation. The system consists of two microstrip structures coiled into spirals. The calculations of the transmission coefficient are presented. The calculations were carried out in the MathCad environment. The graphs of the dependences of the energy transferring coefficient from frequency were obtained. Also the model of the system in AWR Design Environment was presented. Simulation results are also presented in this article. Calculated and simulated results are well agreed.

articleTitle: Reflector Backed Dipole Antenna Array Employing Side Reflectors for Null Depth Improvement
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates a method to make a deep null by adding side reflectors to a reflector-backed dipole antenna array. Parametric studies of radiation patterns reveal the side reflectors contribute to altering a beam pattern more flexibly than the conventional antenna. It makes element patterns in the array more identical, and the antenna scans a null greater than −30 dB constantly in the 5.8 GHz band. Compared to our previous work, which operates in the 2.4 GHz band, we confirm our method is a frequency-scalable approach and very easy to implement.

articleTitle: A Compact Beamsteering Metalens Array Antenna with Circularly Polarized Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a compact metasurface (MTS)-based lens (metalens) array antenna with a circularly-polarized (CP) phased array is proposed for low-cost beamsteering applications. The metalens array antenna is composed of three dual-polarized metalens elements each fed by a CP patch antenna. The transmission response of the designed unit cell for lens element under wide-angle oblique incidence with different polarization is detailly studied to transmit a CP wave efficiently. As a result, the proposed CP metalens array antenna achieves a 3-dB beamwidth coverage range of ±30° with the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of the CP feeding antenna well preserved.

articleTitle: Broadband E-plane Wide-angle Scanning Phased Array Base on V-shaped Structrure Above Cavity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This manuscript presents a E-plane wide-angle scanning phased array based on a V-shaped radiating element above a cavity with corrugated ground. Meanwhile, an extra stub is introduced halfway of the feeding structure to improve impedance matching. An 8-element array is constructed to demonstrate the scanning ability as well as impedance matching. The simulated results show that the antenna can achieve −10dB impedance band within 12.2-14GHz. The 8-element array can scan up to 68° with low gain fluctuation and low side lobe level. The simulated active reflection coefficients can still remain below −10dB when scanning up to 63°. The proposed antenna shows great potential in wide-angle phased array applications.

articleTitle: Capacitors-loaded Dipolar Patch Antenna for UHF Tag Miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A novel UHF RFID tag antenna, which has a compact physical size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\ \mathbf{mm}\ \times 30\ \mathbf{mm}\ \times 3.118\ \mathbf{mm} (0.107\lambda\times 0.092\lambda\times 0.0095\lambda)$</tex>, is proposed for metal mountable applications. The tag structure itself is designed using a pair of dipolar patches that are being fed by two T-shaped feedlines. Here, one pair of lumped capacitors are inserted across the narrow gap between the patches for introducing additional capacitance to bring down the resonant frequency and miniaturize the antenna size. Also, the tag resonant frequency can be easily tuned by adjusting the lumped capacitances. Experimental results show that the proposed tag antenna can achieve a far read distance of 11.1 m when it is placed on a metal plate, being tested with an effective isotropic radiated power of 3.28 W. Even though the tag size is small, it can still maintain good read performance.

articleTitle: Quantum Inverse Scattering – A Proof-of-Concept
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The potentialities offered by the Quantum Computing framework in the solution of microwave imaging problems are discussed and validated in a proof-of-concept fashion in this work. Towards this end, a tomographic inverse problem is firstly formulated within the first-order Born approximation under transverse-magnetic illumination. The resulting linear system of equations is solved by a customized version of the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) quantum algorithm. Preliminary numerical results are shown to illustrate the possibility to dramatically decrease the retrieval time by leveraging on the exponential computational improvement made possible by quantum algorithms.

articleTitle: Neural Network and Microwave Sensing for Food Contamination Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a technique covering the lacks in currently adopted food safety devices is presented, through a microwave-sensing prototype combined with a neural network. An antennas array, composed by 6 low-cost printed circuit boards, surrounds the product to analyze. Their positions and number have been chosen as a trade-off between an optimal coverage of the volume of interest and the physical constraints of an industrial device, i.e., the conveyor belt, moving at production speed. The signals are recorded and used to train a neural network, resulting in an overall 99.45% success rate in classification.

articleTitle: Frequency Tunability of a Low Profile, Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Frequency tunability is studied using a 2-element, low-profile, Yagi antenna. The antenna is comprised of a folded driven element and a straight director element with a low-profile approach using a 0.018λ spacing between the elements. In the antenna design, the potential tunable frequency is found by changing the director length to shift the frequency. By changing the director length, a total tunable bandwidth of 43.2% is achieved. This tunable frequency ranges from 1.98 GHz to 3.07 GHz with realized gain values above 4.71 dBi.

articleTitle: 3D Model of Terahertz Photoconductive Antenna using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a 3D model of a photoconductive antenna (PCA) on semiconductor substrate. The simulations were conducted using the COMSOL Multiphysics package. The model considers the laser excitation and the carrier generation acceleration in the semiconductor layer. The computational work was achieved using the frequency-domain RF module and the semiconductor module. The results demonstrate that simulating the active area alone produces sufficient accuracy ~0.01 % in the RF module solution (solution of the electric and magnetic fields) and ~ 0.23% in the semiconductor solution (photo current solution). The reduction in the simulated area helps minimizing the required CPU time and memory requirement in the 3D model. The largest case in this study was simulated at the National XSEDE Supercomputing with ~0.3 billion unknowns and memory requirement of ~3.2TB in the RF module.

articleTitle: Optimal Embroidered Wearable WPT Systems With Liquid Metal Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a study on the performance of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems embroidered onto denim using conductive threads is presented. A 30 mm radius transmitting (TX) element and an embroidered receiving (RX) element were fabricated on an FR-4 PCB and on textile using conductive threads, respectively. Different sewing layers (up to four) and angles were studied. The measured results show that a CSCMR system with four layers of embroidered elements achieves the optimal performance when sewing angles of 0° and 135° are layered on top of each other, providing a Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) of 58%. Furthermore, liquid metal nanoparticles were added between the four-layer design and this increased the PTE to 68%.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal-Beamsteering Reflective Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a reflective metasurface for full-duplex nonreciprocal-beam-steering and amplification. The metasurface is realized by leveraging the exotic characteristics of novel interconnected meta-atoms providing three main functions simultaneously, i.e., reception, non-reciprocal gradient-phase shifting, and transmission. Such a metasurface can provide directive and diverse radiation beams, and steerable beams by simply changing the bias of the gradient nonreciprocal phase shifters. The proposed structure provides large wave amplification, and is immune to undesired time harmonics, leading to a highly efficient beamsteering in the reflective state.

articleTitle: Prediction of 28 GHz Millimeter-wave Indoor Propagation Characteristics in a Residential House
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper predicts 28 GHz millimeter-wave indoor propagation characteristics in a two-story wooden residential house using numerical simulations based on the finite difference time domain technique. Numerical results of electromagnetic field distribution are utilized to derive 28 GHz parameters of path loss models such as path loss, shadow factor and cross-polarization discrimination. Especially, it is shown that the shadow fading in non-line-of-sight environment can be well characterized by the Gaussian-mix distribution model.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Paper-based Arabic RFID Letters for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design and analysis of newly developed reconfigurable, flexible and fully printable chipless Arabic alphabet-based radio frequency identification (RFID) tags for smart internet of things (IoT) and product marketing applications. The etching of the metallic copper tag strip is performed on a flexible simple thin paper substrate (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{r}=2.31$</tex>) backed by a metallic ground plane. The analysis of investigated tags is performed using CST MWS in the frequency range of 1–12 GHz for the determination of the unique signature resonance characteristics of each tag in terms of its back-scattered horizontal and vertical monostatic radar cross section (RCS). The analysis reflects that each tag have its own unique electromagnetic signature (EMS) due to the change of the current distribution of metallic resonator which could be used for the robust detection and recognition of all realized 28 Arabic alphabet tags.

articleTitle: Conformal Miniaturized Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth and Efficiency Using Periodic Magneto-Dielectric Anisotropic Meta-Substrate
