publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A conformal miniaturized patch antenna with enhanced bandwidth and efficiency is designed based on an artificial anisotropic meta-substrate composed of magneto-dielectric and dielectric materials. The antenna is designed to operate at 300 MHz band. For comparison purposes, different substrate combinations including dielectric, magneto-dielectric, two-layer magneto-dielectric and dielectric, and four-layer periodic magneto-dielectric and dielectric are investigated, and their performances are evaluated at the operating frequency. It is demonstrated that four-layer meta-substrate can effectively decrease the size and increase the bandwidth and efficiency of the antenna in comparison with the other studied host substrates. Numerical studies are performed on the performance of the designed antenna under structural deformation scenarios such as bending to corroborate for its potential use in conformal applications. It was observed that the wideband performance of the antenna is well preserved even after structural deformation while enhancing the efficiency significantly. The conformal magneto-dielectric meta-substrate antenna features a 5.9% matched bandwidth, 1.38 dBi gain, and 60 % efficiency at 300 MHz.

articleTitle: A Broadband Metasurface with Voltage-Controlled Transmission Phase
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an active four-layer metasurface using varactors is proposed which has 0° - 360° tunable transmission phase range and higher transmission magnitude than 0.8 with the large relative bandwidth about 12%. The capacitance of varactors is changed through the biased DC power, hence the transmission phase of the metasurface enables to shift continuously in an easier way, compared to the switch diode-based metasurface and digital metasurface. This work offers a valuable strategy to design broadband dynamically-tunable metasurface and has a good potential for high gain phased antennas and efficient beamforming.

articleTitle: Wideband Star-shaped mmWave Planar Array Antenna with Liquid Crystal
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a wideband star-shaped planar antenna with a liquid crystal (LC) material at Ka-band. The antenna array consists of the LC cavity and planar antenna elements with a microstrip feedline. Planar antenna array is designed with eight star-shaped patches. To check the LC dielectric constant at Ka-band, the designed antenna is fabricated and measured result of reflection coefficient(S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) ≤ −10 dB shows across the wideband (27 GHz – 40 GHz) without DC biasing with bean scanning from −62° to +5° and gain ≥ 8.15 dBi. The frequency range can be tuned with applied biasing voltage on the LC cavity.

articleTitle: A Low-Scattering Conformal Phased Array Based on Resistor-Loaded Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a resistor-loaded metasurface is proposed to control the in-band scattering of cylindrical conformal tightly coupled phased arrays. Loaded resistors of metasurface enable to adjust the phase and magnitude of scattered field. Therefore, the use of metasurface elements with random resistor values can provide random scattered field distribution. By optimizing resistor value of each metasurface element, the scattering pattern can be tuned to achieve a desired ultra-low scattering level. The designed array is able to achieve 3:1 impedance bandwidth for scanning up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pm 60^{\circ}}$</tex>. As compared to the reference array, the monostatic scattering of the proposed cylindrical conformal array is reduced about -30 dB throughout X band.

articleTitle: Study of Bondwire Interconnect for Antenna Applications in W-Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A self-compensated bondwire interconnect for a single-ended chip-to-antenna interface in W-band (75 to 110 GHz) is investigated. Simulation results demonstrate that a fractional bandwidth of 10% and a minimum insertion loss of almost 1 dB can be achieved for interconnects as long as 2 mm. The study of four-element patch antenna array show that the well-established and low-cost wire-bonding technique is feasible for antenna applications in millimeter-wave frequency range.

articleTitle: A 2×2 Dual-Polarized Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized millimeter wave magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna array is designed. The ME dipole element consists of four shorted patches, ground plane and differential feeding networks. A 2×2 array was fabricated and measured. The measured results show that the antenna achieves| S11| < −10 dB in band of 23.3 – 29.4 GHz (23%), in this band, the realized gain is up to 12.3 dBi and the isolation between the two ports is better than 23 dB.

articleTitle: Interface Field Optimization for Wide-Angle Metasurface Refractors in TM Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An interface field optimization technique is presented for designing planar, periodic refracting metasurfaces comprising three admittance sheets on dielectric substrates in TM polarization. To the propagating Floquet modes specified at the outer layers for a given refraction function, auxiliary Floquet modes are introduced to all three admittance layers. Their amplitudes are optimized such that all three surface admittances at material interfaces become passive and lossless everywhere. Full-wave simulations show perfect refraction without reflections.

articleTitle: A Wideband Millimeter-Wave 3-dB Hybrid Coupler Based on Printed-RGW Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband 3-dB coupler using printed ridge gap waveguide (Printed-RGW) technology for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications. The proposed printed-RGW 3-dB coupler can be considered as an excellent candidate for developing wideband feeding beam-forming antenna systems designated for future 5G and beyond wireless communications. The proposed 3-dB coupler structure has the isolation and matching level of less than -12 dB and acceptable insertion losses over the whole operating frequency band. The simulated results, carried out using full-wave CST Microwave Studio software, show a relatively wide bandwidth of about 26% at Ka-Band.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer to a Visual Prosthesis: 100 mW at 6.78 MHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An inductive wireless power transfer system for a neural implant is presented. The prototype can transfer 100 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mW}$</tex> at 6. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{78}$</tex> MHz transcutaneously for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.08\leq k\leq 0.31$</tex>, which corresponds to a distance of 8 to 15 mm, and a lateral misalignment of 0 to 15 mm. The achieved efficiency ranges from 55 to 77 %, depending on the relative distance between the coils. The transmitter coil outer diameter is 55 mm, the receiver coil outside diameter is 35 mm. The inverter is class-E, using a GaN MOSFET, and the receiver is class-DE.

articleTitle: Uniaxial Anisotropic Metamaterial Radome for 79 GHz Automotive Radars
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A uniaxial anisotropic sandwiched meta-radome is investigated for a 79 GHz automotive radar antenna array. The meta-radome uniaxial matching layers are divided into three angular sectors to provide the best matching of the oblique incoming waves to the radar. It is observed by simulation that the sectored meta-radome considerably improves the coupling of higher oblique angles from an illuminating far-field source to the antenna subarray thus becoming comparable to a uniformly designed meta-radome for a wide-angle matching.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Wide-Angle Scanning Waveguide Slot Filtenna Array for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A wide-angle scanning filtenna array for 5G millimeter wave (mmWave) applications is proposed in this paper. The filtenna consists of a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity, a dual-mode waveguide cavity and two slots. The dual-mode resonance in the waveguide cavity is tuned by the metal ridges. As a result, a four-order band-pass filtering response with a radiation null is achieved. The prototype filtenna covers the 5G NR n258 band (24.25 – 27.5 GHz) with a flat in-band broadside gain of 7.1 dBi. Finally, an 8×2 slot filtenna array is designed with a good wide-angle beam-scanning performance.

articleTitle: Fundamental Leapfrog ADI and CDI FDTD Methods
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the fundamental leapfrog alternating direction implicit finite-difference time-domain (LF ADI FDTD) method, which simplifies the right-hand sides (RHS) of implicit update procedures following the principle of fundamental schemes. The leapfrog complying-divergence implicit (CDI) FDTD method is also presented, which comprises implicit update procedures with operator-free RHS while featuring complying divergence. When formulated in fundamental forms, both fundamental LF ADI and CDI FDTD methods are seen to be related by shifting certain RHS operators and operands in the update procedures. While addressing several issues of the LF ADI FDTD method, the LF CDI FDTD method features many advantages including unconditional stability, complying divergence, simplicity and efficient leapfrog update procedures.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Beam Scanning Capability of Phased Arrays Using Quadratic-Gradient Metasurface Dome
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we propose a quadratic-gradient metasurface dome operating in the near-field region of a dual-polarized phased array able enhancing its grating-lobe-free scanning range without affecting its other characteristics. The dome consists of an array of Huygens unit-cells exhibiting an extremely low insertion loss and a proper phase shift in transmission. The main characteristic of the proposed dome is the quadratic-gradient phase profile, which minimizes the beam divergence in broadside direction, whereas linearly increases the scanning region in off-broadside pointing angles. A proper set of numerical simulations have been performed showing the capability of the proposed dome to enhance the grating lobe free scanning region from −58° to −83°.

articleTitle: Using Characteristic Modes for Determining the Incident Field in a Scattering Problem
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A procedure is derived to calculate an estimate of the incident field in a scattering scenario, based on the knowledge of the characteristic modes (CM) on the scatterer and their excitation coefficients. A visualization method of the estimated incident field is proposed, which does not only depend on the original incident field, but also on the structure of the scatterer. Therefore, it can provide intuitive insight into the behavior of the scatterer. It is shown by example that this procedure is suited to calculate the direction of arrival (DoA) of the original plane wave incident on the scatterer.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer on Human Arm for Future Body Area Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: With the fact that the wearble devices will be very common in the future, charging such devices becomes essential. We propose a wireless power transfer (WPT) system to transfer power to these wearable devices, in order to at least able to transmit the rescue signal in the case of no power or continuous charge. Here, the real arm model of a Chinese female is built, and one antenna is put on the elbow to charge the antenna on the upper arm close to the deltoid. The interaction between the arm and the antenna is investigated, including the matching, the channel characteristics, the pattern, the specific absorption rate (SAR), and the transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Vivaldi Array Antenna With Low In-band RCS and Low Cross-polarization Properties by Loading Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Absorber
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A Vivaldi antenna array with low in-band radar cross section (RCS) and low cross-polarization properties is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna array consists of 4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 4$</tex> Vivaldi antennas and an orthogonally oriented spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) absorber. Since the electromagnetic waves whose polarization direction is parallel to the SSPP absorber can be absorbed, the in-band cross-polarization RCS and the cross-polarization level of the antenna array can be reduced. The antenna array works in the frequency band of 3.7-15.0 GHz. Compared with the antenna array without SSPP absorber, the proposed antenna array can achieve a 10-dB RCS reduction from 6.2 to 13.5 GHz and a 10-dB in-band cross-polarization reduction from 6.2 to 11.5 GHz, while the radiation performance of co-polarization remains unchanged.

articleTitle: Pencil to Flat-Top Beampattern Transform and Its Application in Gaussian Array Design
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents an analytical transform of a pencil to the flat-top beampattern. The transform imposes maximal flatness at the beam peak by modifying the original excitation coefficients with a second-order polynomial. This transform is suitable for the synthesis of narrow flat-top beampatterns. As an example, a simple closed-form method for the synthesis of flat-top Gaussian beampatterns is provided.

articleTitle: Band Switchable Monopole Antenna for UWB, 5G and Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a printed monopole antenna with a novel band switching mechanism to switch between UWB, sub-6 GHz and 3–4 GHZ bands. The antenna uses a capacitively coupled parasitic line near the partial ground plane whose electrical length is controlled using two pin diodes. For the third band, a stub is added near the radiator. The VSWR < 2 bandwidth when the pin diodes are OFF is from 2.9 GHz to 10.2 GHz (UWB) and for ON case it gives sub-6 GHz band from 2.9 GHz to 5.7 GHz and the stub gives the third band from 3–4 GHz. The effect of adding a parasitic line in the partial ground plane is studied using surface current distribution. The proposed antenna is fabricated and tested for its VSWR and radiation characteristics. The measured results indicate that the antenna is suitable for UWB, sub 6-GHz <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathbf{G}$</tex> and cognitive radio applications.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis on Radio Coverage of 5G based Train Wireless Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: 5G based train wireless communication network is built in the Electric Multiple Units (EMU) train for investigating the radio coverage scheme with omnidirectional antenna and directional antenna at 4.9GHz. We investigate the influence of using different types of antennas on the radio coverage inside and outside of the EMU. Based on the measurement results, the propagation characteristics in train are analyzed, and then the antenna scheme of train wireless communication network in EMU is suggested. The directional antenna is found to be more suitable for radio coverage in EMU, since it has the characteristics of longer coverage in the train and less radio interference to adjacent trains.

articleTitle: A High-Order Mode Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a novel high-order mode leaky wave antenna. The antenna is designed to operate at the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{11}$</tex> mode, while typical leaky wave antennas (LWAs) operate on their fundamental mode, e.g., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{10}$</tex>. The proposed design is compared to the equivalent fundamental mode LWAs showing a significant increase of 5.64dB - 6.67 dB in gain.

articleTitle: Extreme Beam-forming with Metagrating-assisted Planar Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We present a highly efficient metagrating-assisted antenna (MGA) architecture with a simple integrated feed. Power from a localized line source is distributed optimally throughout the arbitrarily large antenna aperture with the help of a passive and lossless electromagnetic metagrating (MG). With appropriately designed meta-wire loading, the omnidirectional source field can be efficiently transformed into directive radiation. To aid the design process, a 2-dimensional volume-surface integral equation framework which accurately predicts the radiation pattern of the MGA is developed. Through constrained optimization, the directivity of the MGA in the desired direction is maximized. In this way, extreme-angle beam forming is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Two-Dimensional Beam Propagation Characteristics in Parallel Plate Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a small model experiment of microwave power transmission using the parallel plate waveguide. In the parallel plate waveguide, the electromagnetic wave can be regarded as two-dimensional. Therefore, we derived a two-dimensional theoretical equation by analogy with the Friis transmission formula. According to the theoretical equation, the electromagnetic wave attenuates in inverse proportion to the distance. The electromagnetic field simulation results were found to be close to the theoretical equations.

articleTitle: A GSG-Excited Ultra-Wideband 103–147 GHz Stacked Patch Antenna on Flexible Printed Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: An ultra-wideband aperture coupled stacked antenna operating in the WR08 band (90–140 GHz) is presented. The design consists of two rectangular stacked patches fed by a rectangular slot coupled to a stripline feed. A ground-signal-ground (GSG) probe pad configuration is included in the design to excite the antenna and perform wideband measurements. Ansys HFSS simulation tool is used for the simulation level design and the final layout is fabricated using the MFLEX modified polyimide (MPI) material. The simulated antenna achieves a −10 dB bandwidth of 44.9 GHz, with an average realized gain of 5.7 dBi and average efficiency of 73.9% across the bandwidth. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first antenna with more than 30% bandwidth fabricated on flexible printed circuit (FPC) technologies above 100 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of SICL fed Dual Polarized Dipole Antenna for Millimeter wave Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of dual polarized dipole antenna fed by Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line (SICL) is presented in Ka-band. Dual polarization is achieved using two orthogonal radiating dipole antennas. Two 45° tilted dipole antennas is devised by the top /bottom dipole arm printed on the two sides of the substrates and dipole arm in the middle layer. PIN diode is utilized in the feeding line to control the polarization of the antenna. Hence by switching the PIN diodes between dipole antennas, the dominant TEM mode of SICL is simultaneously excited in the antenna and dual linear polarization is obtained. The proposed antenna resonates at 28.1 GHz exhibiting gain of 4.9 dBi for the two polarizations and co-pol to cross-pol ratio better than 20 dB. This antenna is a suitable candidate for 5G millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Toward an End-to-End Metasurface Design Procedure for Power Pattern Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper extends an electromagnetic inversion algorithm for metasurface design which takes a desired (phase-less) power pattern and computes the required metasurface susceptibility profile. The proposed method incorporates a model of the metasurface unit cells that considers near-field coupling effects to allow for physically realizable unit cells. The developed end-to-end design method is summarized, and used to create a physically realizable omega-type bianisotropic metasurface.

articleTitle: Truncated Phase Reversal Fresnel lens Antenna for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: We propose a unique design perspective to truncate a phase reversal Fresnel lens. The proposed technique depends on utilizing the focusing of the feed antenna radiation in one plane using cascaded dielectric slabs, and eliminates the need for any feeding network. The proposed feed uses printed technology and possesses a very low cost feature.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Dual-Polarized Low-Profile Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized tightly coupled dipole array with ten-octave bandwidth and 60 degrees scanning is presented. A double-Y balun is employed to accomplish the transition of unbalanced microstrip line to balanced co-planar stripline. A frequency selective surface (FSS) resistive sheet is utilized to suppresses periodic ground plane interference and widen the operation bandwidth. Instead of bulky dielectric materials, a meta wide-angle impedance matching (meta-WAIM) layer with ellipse split rings is employed for a broader scan angle. A 10:1 bandwidth (0.2-2GHz) is observed with active <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < 3$</tex> when scanning up to ±60°. The radiation efficiency remains above 70% on average. Meanwhile, an extremely low overall profile less than 99mm (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.066 \lambda_{\text{low}}$</tex>) is achieved.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Radio Source Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture for radio event and source detection. The upper triangle of the auto-correlation matrix is extracted as the feature input to an uni-dimensional (1D) CNN and trained to detect the presence of a source in the sampled signal and estimate the number of signals. Since, the number of source signals present in the sampled waveform can vary between 0 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L-1$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is the number of sensors in the array, the network is modeled as a multi-class, multi-label classification problem. The proposed method is robust to a varying number of incoming signals to resolve and Signal to Interference Plus Noise Ratio (SINR). The CNN architecture is trained and tested with the number of sources varying between 0 and 4. The source detection architecture is introduced and its efficacy is validated using simulations closely replication real-time RF events.

articleTitle: VO2-Based Reconfigurable Meanderline Polarizer at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a reconfigurable dual-sense linear-to-circular polarization (LP-CP) conversion metasurface at Ka-band. The device operates in the satellite communication (SatCom) up-link portion of the Ka-band (27.5–31 GHz), which also includes the 28 GHz 5G mmWave band. Dual-sense LP-CP converters in the current literature do not have polarization diversity within a single band. The proposed metasurface employs vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) phase change material in two superimposed alternate meanderline geometries. The device consists of four of these layers and is constructed on Si substrates using micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) processes. The proposed metasurface has low insertion loss throughout the SatCom up-link band of <1.1 dB and excellent axial ratio <3 dB.

articleTitle: A Multiband Quasi-Yagi Antenna for WiFi/Bluetooth/WiMAX/Zigbee Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A multi-band quasi-Yagi antenna is proposed. The structure of the antenna has a simple feeding mechanism consists of a microstrip line and transmission line. Half of the driver and director is printed on the opposite side of the substrate to achieve a stable radiation pattern. In addition, the ground plane is modified, the upper slots were added for impedance matching, the middle slot to obtain additional resonances, the lower slots to improve the upper-frequency band radiation pattern. The antenna shows multi-band characteristic and has achieved |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < -10 dB in three different frequency bands (2.35-2.65 GHz, 3.8 - 4.3 GHz, 4.95 - 5.2 GHz). These frequency bands are suitable for WiFi, Bluetooth, WiMAX, and Zigbee applications. The antenna shows a relatively flat gain (4.2-5 dBi) and a very end-fire radiation pattern in all operating frequency bands.

articleTitle: Terahertz Imaging of ENU Injected Sprague Dawley Rat Breast Cancer Tumors
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we demonstrate the use of the reflection mode terahertz imaging technique for the margin assessment of breast cancer tumors developed in Sprague Dawley rats. The tumors in the rats were produced by injecting N-ethyl-N-nitrosourea chemical into their mammary pad. The pathology assessment results demonstrated the presence of fibro-fatty tissue adjacent to cancer in the excised tumor. THz imaging results show significant differentiation between these tissue types. Thus, the proposed rat breast tumor model demonstrated a potential to obtain cancerous tissues closely mimicking human breast tumors.

articleTitle: Microstrip Band-Stop Filter Design via Brick-Based Microwave Training Kit
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A brick-based passive microwave component design methodology is presented. Brick-formed metal cells and dielectric cells make it easy to iterate directly via hardware pieces. A rectangular open stub band-stop filter with a single and double stub are designed, built, and measured. The results are also compared with the free circuit simulator software, Qucs [1]. The study progresses with a single and double radial stub. The brick-based microstrip filter increases the quality of microwave education at the universities and lets the researchers design and prototype microwave structures easily.

articleTitle: Efficient Modelling of Antenna Measurements Including the Impact of the Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we introduce a fast analysis method for general antenna measurement evaluation in which the impact of the probe/range antenna coupling with the Antenna Under Test (AUT) and anechoic chamber can be evaluated. This method differs from the standard chamber evaluation techniques that aim at characterizing the anechoic chamber by its Quiet Zone (QZ). The proposed method is based on the antenna coupling equation, known from Spherical Near-Field (SNF) measurements, where the angular dependent absorber performance is included by image theory. The potential of this method is illustrated by evaluating both the QZ and a full antenna measurement scenario for a given antenna.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized HF/UHF Dual-Band RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized HF/UHF dual-band antenna fed by a dual-interface RFID chip. The main goal of the antenna design is to achieve a compact, cost-effective, multi-purpose, and high performance RFID transponder. The proposed antenna utilizes the HF coil as a ground for a meandered monopole antenna operating at UHF band. An inductive network is adopted to achieve a conjugate matching between the antenna and the UHF chip interface. Measurements of a transponder prototype show a power sensitivity of −16.5 dBm, which corresponds to a realized antenna gain of approximately −1 dBi at 860 MHz.

articleTitle: Design of Rectangular Waveguide Slot Antenna for Anti-interference Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a method to enhance the anti-interference ability of the rectangular waveguide slot antenna. By loading a set of metallic pillars in the rectangular waveguide, the out-of-band suppression capability of the waveguide slot antenna is effectively improved. In order to verify the idea, an anti-interference four-slot rectangular waveguide slot antenna is designed. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna achieves a flat realized gain of 12.5-12.8 dBi in operating band (6.75-7.25 GHz) and a radiation suppression of 33.9-64.7 dB in out-of-band (9.6-11.5 GHz). Compared with the traditional rectangular waveguide slot antenna, the corresponding out-of-band suppression is improved by 14.2-47.4 dB.

articleTitle: Proximity Feature Based Target Detection for Airborne Radar with Misaligned Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a novel target detection method is introduced for airborne radar with misaligned antenna array. The proximity feature of non-linear clutter ridge is extracted from the radar echo data via minimum variance (MV) method in the angle-Doppler domain. Subsequently, the feature is applied to distinguish target from the clutter. The proposed technique recognizes and detects target from ellipse shaped clutter due to velocity misalignment. The effectiveness of this approach has been proven with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Landmark Effects on RF-induced Heating for Patients with Artificial Shoulder at 1.5 T MRI
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The effect of imaging landmark on the RF-induced heating of an artificial shoulder at 1.5 T MRI is numerically investigated in this study. Imaging landmarks from the top of the head to the bottom of the leg are considered for the virtual adult male model. The incident field at the shoulder region is higher when the patient is being imaged for the lower body regions. Considering all these landmarks, the peak-spatial 1 g averaged specific absorption rate (SAR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1g</inf>) around the metallic artificial shoulder occurs when a lower back region is being imaged. The SAR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1g</inf> for the lower back imaging landmark is more than 1.5 times higher than that for the shoulder landmark. Additionally, the hotspot location around the artificial shoulder is also affected by the landmark.

articleTitle: Vertical-Wall Between Tightly Spaced Patch Antennas for Decoupling and Radiation Pattern Correction
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A pattern-corrected vertical loaded metal-wall decoupling technique is proposed for two patch antennas separated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}/20$</tex>. The wall is a back-to-back grounded dielectric substrate placed vertically parallel to the E-plane between two patch antennas. The middle of the wall is all metal, and both sides are three strips of the same width but at a different distance. The simulated results show that the structure realizes the decoupling, matching requirements, broaden the bandwidth, and corrected the 13° tilt angle of the H-plane radiation pattern to the broadside at 5.80 GHz.

articleTitle: Design Of A Compact Ultra-Wideband Microstrip Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a planar compact ultra-wideband microstrip antenna is proposed for millimeter-wave communication. The proposed single antenna element has 93.78% fractional bandwidth (covered band of 23.5 GHz to 65 GHz). The simulated radiation efficiency is greater than 93% and a peak gain of 5.6 dBi, with less than 3 dB variation in the whole band. The return loss of the single element antenna is well below −10 dB in the proposed band. The unique contribution of the proposed antenna design lies in its huge operation bandwidth (41.5 GHz) with a very simple structure. The proposed ultra-wideband antenna is suitable for many mmWave applications such as ISM band at 24 GHz, the upper region of K-band, Ka-band (27–40 GHz), mmWave 5G communication (26 GHz, 28 GHz, 38 GHz), as well as 60 GHz high-speed wireless communication (IEEE 802.11ad).

articleTitle: Miniaturized Angularly Stable Single and Dual Bands Bandpass Frequency Selective Surfaces with Transmission Zeros Near the Sidebands
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents two single-layer miniaturized bandpass frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) with single and dual-band resonances. Transmission zeros (TZs) are introduced near to the sidebands which in effect improve the filter selectivity at the resonance. The basic FSS prototype consists of a capacitive grid (CG) loaded cross-dipole aperture (CDA) which shows a passband center at 6.22 GHz with a 3 dB bandwidth (BW) of 20.3 %. Later the CG structure is modified by adding parallel slot lines (PSL) which are extended towards the center to realize the second FSS unit cell. The proposed FSS-2 exhibits closely spaced dual passbands center at 5.5 and 7.48 GHz with a frequency ratio of 1.36. Passband insertion losses at two frequencies are 0.19 and 0.46 dB with BWs of 31.7 and 13.5 %. The proposed single and dual-band FSSs show polarization insensitive filter response with oblique angle stability of 40° and 55° respectively.

articleTitle: On Propagation Graph Model for Industrial UWB Channels
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the suitability of a propagation graph (PG) model for ultra wideband (UWB) industrial wireless channels. Based on short range UWB channel sounding measurements in typical industrial scenarios, we estimate parameters of the model using a method of moments approach. The measurements are then compared with approximate expressions for the power delay spectrum (PDS) derived based on PG formalism. Results show reasonable agreement between the measured and approximate PDS.

articleTitle: Generalized Eigenvalue Problem for Spatially-Discrete Traveling-Wave-Modulated Circuit Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Traveling-wave modulation (TWM) is a simple form of space-time modulation which can enable electromagnetic effects such as non-reciprocity, frequency-conversion and amplification. TWM is often realized by applying a staggered modulation to a spatially-discrete array of unit cells known as stixels (space-time pixels). Currently available techniques for analyzing spatially-discrete traveling-wave modulation (SDTWM) require an entire spatial modulation period to be simulated simultaneously. Here, a generalized eigenvalue problem for SDTWM is derived which is independent of the number of stixels within the structure.

articleTitle: Study of low-profile broadband circularly polarized patch antenna-based on metasurface structure
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A simple broadband circularly polarized antenna based on metasurface(MS) structure is proposed. The antenna consists of a slotted floor and MS radiating patch, where the MS is placed above the slotted floor. The MS structure twists the polarization of linearly polarized(LP) wave into circularly polarized(CP) wave. The overall size of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$36\text{mm}^{\ast}36\text{mm}^{\ast}4.2\text{mm}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.6\lambda_{0}^{\ast}0.6\lambda_{0}^{\ast}0.07\lambda_{0}$</tex> at 5GHz). The impedance bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \mathrm{S}_{11} \vert < -10\text{dB},\ \text{IBW})$</tex> of the antenna is 44.16% (3.90–6.11GHz), and the axial ratio bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\vert \text{AR}\vert < - 3\text{dB}$</tex>, ARBW) is 20.35% (4.81–5.9GHz). In addition, the antenna has a symmetrical radiation pattern and low cross-polarization. Therefore, the antenna can be used in C-band satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Shaped Elevation Patterns for 5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the advantages and an example of using shaped elevation patterns for 5G base stations. A simple iterative power synthesis method involving the phase of shaped patterns, and suitable for both center- and end-fed sub-arrays, is used. Numerical simulations and some experimental results for an array of linear sub-arrays with cosecant squared patterns are presented to validate the concept.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Transmitarray for Wide-Angle Conical Scanning: Concept, Optimization and Validation
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Weather radar instruments have shown failure due to moving mechanical parts used to scan a directive beam conically. To eliminate the risk of mechanical rotation failure, we propose transmitarray (TA) antennas as an antenna alternative that can achieve the conical beam sweep electronically with no moving parts. Our approach to achieving such a design is a synthesis algorithm based on the circularly symmetric functional expansion of the TA element phase compensation and the optimization of the feed location. The circular symmetry of the TA element phase compensation functional expansion is enforced to take advantage of the azimuthal symmetry of the feeds placed along the ring focus that will ultimately produce the electronic conical scan. The optimal feed location that minimizes the phase error between the ideal and the circularly symmetric TA element phase compensation is obtained using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Full-wave simulation results of an 18 cm TA operating at 13.4 GHz are presented to validate the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Mantle Cloak Antenna with Rejection Band at Lower Frequency Side of Operating Frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a mantle cloak antenna with a rejection band at lower frequency side of operating frequency. By adjusting the surface reactance of the ideal metasurface sheet and the feeding part of the antenna, the mantle cloak antenna with the operating frequency of 750 MHz and the stopband frequency of 720 MHz is designed.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Wide Band, Wide Scanning Phased Array-Fed Reflector Architecture
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Phased Array Fed Reflectors (PAFRs) are desirable in RF antenna systems because of their high gain, however they require mechanical gimballing to compensate for the limited electronic scan volume that hinders swath. State of the art Electronically Scanned Array (ESA) solutions can address demanding link performance, capacity, and data rates using multiple agile analog beams, but they do so at a premium size, weight, power, and cost (SWaP-C). Especially for wide field of view (FOV) millimeter Wave (mmW) frequencies which require larger sized ESAs to close the links. This paper presents an innovative phased array architecture leveraging a ring-focused reflector that improves the scan performance of conventional PAFRs, denoted Wide Angle ESA Fed Reflector (WAEFR). This type of reflector architecture provides wide band performance with an electronic scan volume increase of up to 20x over traditional PAFRs and can reduce the size of an active ESA by over 40%.

articleTitle: VO2 based Ultra-Reconfigurable Ka-Band Reflectarrays for Next-Generation Communication and Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based ultra-reconfigurable reflectarray antenna for next generation communication and radar applications. Use of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, a phase change material, allows for ultra-reconfigurability by modifying the shape and size of the conducting reflective patches through an integrated heating matrix. The designed square patch unit-cell demonstrates a reflection phase shift in the order of 310°. Full-wave array analysis of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 \times 20$</tex> element reflectarray is performed. Simulations show a directivity between 22–26 dBi with good beam scanning performance within ±50° elevation angle at 32GHz. This data is also in good agreement with the theoretical calculations. The proposed VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based reflectarray unit-cells can be dynamically reconfigured electronically which enables the reflectarray to dynamically change its frequency of operation and steer its beam. The main advantage of this antenna is the versatility and quantity of reconfigurable states it can achieve in real-time.

articleTitle: Size Optimized Antenna-in-Package with Quasi-Isotropic Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: The Internet of Things applications require small wireless sensors with quasi-isotropic radiation, so that their communication is orientation insensitive. A method to realize quasi-isotropic antenna is by placing multiple radiators on the faces of a cube, which also acts as a package for the embedded electronics. In this work, we demonstrate quasi-isotropic radiation through a 3D Antenna-in-Package with multiple magnetic Hertzian dipole radiators. For quasi-isotropy, the dipoles on four faces of the cube must be in phase, while the dipoles orthogonal to the plane carrying the other four dipoles must be 60° out of phase. With this feeding arrangement, an isotropy of 7.3 dB has been achieved in the whole radiation sphere in simulations and 6.5 dB in a prototype where the ideal dipoles were replaced by practical microstrip patch antennas. The inner walls of the cube have been metallized to provide effective shielding between the antennas and the embedded electronics. We also optimized the size of the cube while maintaining a decent isolation between the adjacent patches so that the required quasi-isotropic radiation can be achieved. It is observed that the isotropy increases by reducing the size of the cube until the coupling between the multiple radiators starts to negatively affect it. As a trade-off between size, acceptable coupling and decent isotropy, a cube with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{\lambda_{o}}{2}$</tex> sides has been designed, prototyped and tested.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of 5G Radio Coverage with Inner End Door on Electric Multiple Units
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Internet of things (IoT) of 5G will be deployed at Electric Multiple Units (EMU) to reduce the number of cables. To ensure the coverage quality of the 5G in carriage, a measurement system, using omnidirectional and directional antenna respecticely, is built in the EMU. The measurement results of Reference Signal Receiving Power (RSRP) in the case of opening or closing inner end door scenario are analyzed for investigating the influence of inner end door. Based on the measurement results, we provide the suggsetions that Remote Radio Unit (RRU) should be deployed at each carriage and every two carriages in case of using omnidirectioanal and directional antenna respectively in closing inner end door scenario.

articleTitle: A Study of Human Body Shadowing at 300 GHz in a Scattering Indoor Corridor Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Presented in this paper are the premier results for human body shadowing at 300 GHz. The main-beam and partial blockage effects from a 3D physical model of human body in a typical indoor corridor environment for line-of-sight (LoS) conditions is analyzed. The analysis is based on ray-tracing simulations carried out for the manifold transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) locations. Results reveal that the proposed novel approach to study pedestrian blockage by means of beam spot size from high gain horns requires a different perspective from countermeasures to combat the likely severe shadowing losses.

articleTitle: Stealth Communication (SC) for 5G/6G Wireless to ensure spectral efficiency and privacy/cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a review on the state-of-the-art of “Stealth Communication” (SC), focused on potential applications in 5G/6G. SC is a new wireless system aimed at enhancing spectral efficiency and cybersecurity/privacy based on employing Ultra-Wide-Band (UWB) RF signals that mimic noises in wave form and below-noise-level at the receiver frontend. For 5G/6G applications, Same Frequency (SF) Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR) operating bandwidth covering 400 MHz to 11 GHz, and their Technology Readiness Level, are discussed. Implementation of SC in 5G/6G, held back so far by high costs and Covid-19, should be able to gain enough momentum under the thrusts of rising cyber attacks in 2021.

articleTitle: Improving the Efficiency of Parallel FFTs in Parallel Electromagnetic Solvers Based on the AIM
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Progress on a parallel boundary element method solver that targets structures embedded in layered media is presented. We compare the effectiveness of blocking and nonblocking communication methods in the propagation stage of the adaptive integral method (AIM). We demonstrate that the execution time of the proposed solver can be decreased with the nonblocking communication scheme. The proposed solver can compute the radar cross section of large multiscale structures, with up to 3.2 million unknowns, in under 15 seconds per frequency sample.

articleTitle: Investigation into Curvilinear Metasurfaces using IE-GSTCs with Normal Surface Polarizabilities
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Using an Integral Equation (IE) based electromagnetic field solver that is capable of modeling metasurfaces (MSs) using the generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs), we study the accuracy of surface susceptibilities for modeling curvilinear surfaces. The surface susceptibilities are first extracted for a simple practical unit cell with a metal loop exhibiting a strong normal magnetic polarization. Subsequently, a uniform MS in the shape of a semi-circle is modeled using the GSTCs, and compared to full-wave simulations. We demonstrate that the GSTCs can successfully model curved surfaces, with minor discrepancies occurring when the curvature becomes extreme.

articleTitle: Array Failure Diagnosis and Active Compensation for Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Aiming at the maintenance requirements of Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) in practical application, this paper proposes an element failure diagnosis and radiation pattern active compensation to ensure the IRS continues to operate in a certain standard. Specifically, the joint diagnosis process is realized based on the compressed sensing algorithm combined with the element reflection amplitude and reflection phase data. The compensation process uses the reconfigurable characteristics of the remaining working elements and utilizes the improved genetic algorithm for sparse optimization. Through analysis and simulation, a potential feasible implementation plan is provided for the failure diagnosis and active compensation of the IRS, which reduces the maintenance cost and improves its engineering application value.

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency Selective Surface for the RCS Reduction of Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective surface (FSS) with the characteristics of absorbing electromag-netic(EM) waves at around 14.1 GHz. The unit cell of the FSS is comprised of a back-to-back metal patch with a multi-ring structure in between. The multi-layer structure are generated to realize a bandpass response with a 3-dB bandwidth of 1.05 GHz. Specifically, the symmetrical structure of the unit cell of FSS results in the stable performance in different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex> direction of incident waves. A radome covered by the designed FSS is built to measure the RCS reduction ability of the FSS. The results show that the FSS can well reduce the RCS of the antenna and radome system in this frequency band.

articleTitle: Scattering from Random Rough Surfaces at X and Ku band for Global Remote Sensing of Terrestrial Snow
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Snow water equivalent (SWE) retrievals based on X and Ku band radar observations have been studying over several decades. The physical basis of such approach is that snow volume scattering at X and Ku tends to increase with SWE. However, for small to moderate SWE, radar signals at X and Ku band are affected by surface scattering from the underlying soil, which degrades the sensitivity. It is important to estimate the soil rough surface scattering and subtract out its contributions to enhance the correlation of radar observations and SWE. In this paper, we present results of soil surface scattering based on the numerical solutions of Maxwell's equations in 3D (NMM3D) full wave simulations. In the past, full wave simulations have been limited with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh < 1.5$</tex>. In plains, rms heights of rough soil surfaces are up to 3 cm, which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh= 10$</tex> at 17.2 GHz for Ku band. In this paper, we present NMM3D results for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh$</tex> up to 15. We simulated two types of rough surface: “constant ratio” which means the ratio of correlation length to rms height are between 5 to 20, and “limited correlation lengths” meaning correlation lengths limited to 10 cm, Simulation results show that that backscattering increase with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh$</tex> and then saturate at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh=2.5$</tex> for rough surfaces with constant ratio. However, for rough surfaces with correlation lengths limited to 10 cm, backscattering first increase with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kh$</tex> to reach the peak and then decrease.

articleTitle: Analysis of Angular Stability of FSS Based on Open Trapezoidal Rings Geometry
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the angular stability of a frequency selective surface (FSS) based on open trapezoidal rings geometry. This geometry presents interesting features, such as miniaturization and possibility of resonant frequencies independent control. This research is focused on the angular stability. The open trapezoidal rings geometry is described and initial design equation presented. A FSS prototype was fabricated and characterized, verifying a good agreement between numerical and measured results. The angular stability was confirmed for the incidence angle up to 30°, which is an encouraging result.

articleTitle: Unified Scattering Model for Modelling Electrically Large and Complex Object above Rough Surface
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: It is important to model electromagnetic (EM) scattering from complex object of electrically large size with considering the influence from surrounding environment. This paper presents a unified scattering model for efficient simulation of EM scattering from electrically large object above infinite rough surface. The proposed unified scattering model can be considered as an extension of existing scattering models for object above rough surface. It is very helpful to understand and implement different scattering models in a unified manner.

Author Keywords: complex object of electrically large size

articleTitle: Single-Feed Multi-beam Transmitarray Antenna Design Using Parallel Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a general design methodology for single-feed multi-beam transmitarray antennas by using a parallel particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The conventional PSO method is reviewed and a modified PSO algorithm is proposed which can be applied in parallel computing. Then the proposed method is implemented for a triple-beam transmitarray design. The numerical results show that the parallel PSO method contributes to a better radiation performance and reduces 87.6% of the computation time compared to the conventional PSO method.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Ultra-Wideband Planar Folded Dipole Antenna for Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A compact ultra-wideband (UWB) planar folded dipole antenna (PFDA) for mobile UWB terminal is presented in this paper. The proposed PFDA is mainly composed of two folded radiating elements and two pairs of parasitic elements. Each radiating element consists of two copper strips, and a rectangular slot is etched on the strip. The dimensions of the proposed PFDA are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$17\ \mathbf{mm}\ \times 5\ \mathbf{mm}\ \times 1.27\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex>. Optimizing the design parameters of the antenna results in an impedance bandwidth of 56.4%, covering a wide range from 5.6 GHz to 10 GHz. Particularly more than 89% total efficiency can be realized in the band of 6–9 GHz.

articleTitle: A Tri-band Highly Selective Passband Frequency Selective Surface Based on Multi-layer Coupling
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized and low-profile frequency selective surface (FSS) with three passbands is proposed. The FSS has a multi-layer combination structure, which consists of three metallic layers separated by two dielectric substrates. The top and bottom layers have the same pattern which is composed of a meandered cross slot and four edge slots. The middle layer is formed by metallic square ring. The strong coupling effect among the multiple layers generates three highly selective passbands. An equivalent circuit model (ECM) is proposed to verify its working mechanism, and the results of ECM agree well with full-wave simulation. Furthermore, the proposed FSS has high angular and polarization stability.

articleTitle: High Gain Tilted Beam SIW Horn Antenna for 5G Millimeter Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we have designed a very compact size planner tilted beam SIW H-plane horn antenna for 5G millimeter (mm) wave communication. In our proposed design, we extended the substrate as well as the upper-broad wall of the horn in the direction of the main beam. This tilted beam SIW horn antenna is one of the best solutions for the 5G mm-wave band. It has few attractive features namely high gain within a small dimension along with wide impedance bandwidth. The proposed antenna has got maximum gain of 10.3 dBi at 28 GHz. Its large radiating aperture also helps us to achieve wideband impedance matching. The proposed SIW horn antenna has 3 GHz -10 dB impedance bandwidth (27.8 GHz - 30.8 GHz) and also achieves very less E-plane beamwidth of 80° and 30° H-plane beamwidth.

articleTitle: Multi-Domain Learning Scheme for Full-Wave Nonlinear Inverse Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-domain learning scheme (MDLS) that combines frequency- and real-space features of contrast is proposed to solve full-wave nonlinear inverse scattering problems (ISPs). A noticeable characteristic of the proposed MDLS is that interlacer layers are added in traditional deep learning scheme, which serves as information-interchange layer to exchange the information in contrast space and its Fourier space. The main advantage of MDLS is to achieve a more robust and accurate nonlinear reconstruction by combining information from contrast and its Fourier domain. It is shown that the reconstructed results are robust to noise contamination and the reconstructed image quality is quantitatively better compared with the traditional architecture built in a single domain.

articleTitle: A Simple and Effective Method for Compressing Electrically Large Integral Operators
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new method to approx-imate electrically large Green's function by a reduced set of parameters. Using this new method, we can compress electrically large integral operators in a simple and effective manner. The compression has a reduced complexity of O(kn) for a dense matrix of size n and rank k, as compared to existing techniques that can cost O(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) or O(k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>n). Meanwhile, the accuracy is theo-retically guaranteed. Numerical experiments have demonstrated its accuracy and effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Method to Widen the Range of Direction Finding by Time Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method to enlarge the range of direction-finding in time modulated array. By improving the switching sequence, the distance between the harmonic main beams can be increased, and the direction-finding range is widened. In addition, a novel calibration method is proposed to improve the direction-finding accuracy when the incident direction reaches the main beam angle of harmonics. Simulation results verify the accuracy of the proposed method. In a seven-element time modulated linear array, the range of direction finding has been improved form ±59° to ±75°.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Using Liquid Metal Vias
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a moderately high directivity (~10 dBi) antenna having a reconfigurable radiation pattern. Specifically, the direction of the main beam can be altered. The radiation pattern control is achieved with the aid of a single-pole triple-through (SPTT) radio frequency (RF) switch. In turn the switch can be reconfigured with the aid of Gallium-based liquid metal. The proposed antenna operates at 5.8 GHz and it radiates in the End-fire direction with reconfigurable patterns in the azimuth plane. The proposed antenna and the SPTT switch are designed to operate on an RO4003 substrate and they are based around substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology.

articleTitle: Metal-Coated Flexible Dielectric Waveguides for Millimeter-Wave Multi-Lane Wireline Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Metal-coated flexible dielectric waveguides are implemented for potential deployment in millimeter-wave wireline communication applications. Although bare-dielectric waveguides show excellent loss performance (1~2 dB/meter) at millimeter-wavelengths, they are sensitive to the surrounding environment and not suitable for bundling multiple channels together. In order to solve the field confinement issue while ensuring the waveguide is still flexible, 3-microns of copper is coated onto the surface of a circular Polystyrene waveguide. The measured S-parameters of the implemented waveguide display less than 4 dB of discrepancy from theoretical study. Finally, the waveguide is paired with a 60 GHz transceiver module to demonstrate the feasibility of high-speed data communication.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Wideband Filtering Metasurface Antenna with Improved Frequency Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized wideband filtering antenna based on metasurface is presented. The proposed filtering antenna contains a 3 × 3 dual-layer metasurface with offset shorting vias, and a suspended dipole. Two radiation nulls are generated in the stopbands. The filtering antenna shows an impedance bandwidth of 19% and a compact size of 0.54λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.54λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free-space wavelength at center frequency). The stable in-band realized gain is about 7.3 dBi. This filtering antenna exhibits compact size, low profile, and improved frequency selectivity at band-edges. It can be used in compact multiband antenna array to reduce the mutual coupling.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Surface Wave Platform Using Fluidic Conductive Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Surface wave inherently has less propagation loss as it adheres to the surface and minimizes unwanted dissipation in space. Recently, they find applications in network-on-chip (NoC) communications and intelligent surface aided mobile networked communications. This paper puts forward a reconfigurable surface wave platform (RSWP) that utilizes liquid metal to produce highly energy-efficient and adaptive pathways for surface wave transmission. Our simulation results illustrate that the proposed RSWP using Galinstan can obtain a 25dB gain in the electric field for a propagation distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35\lambda$</tex> at 30G Hz where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> denotes the wavelength. Moreover, less than 1dB loss is observed even at a distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\lambda$</tex>, and a pathway with right-angled turns can also be created with only a 3. 5dB loss at the turn.

articleTitle: An Electrically Smaller Ultra-Wideband Monopole Antenna for Ground Penetrating Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the design and prototyping of an electrically smaller planar monopole antenna suitable for ultra-wideband radar application is presented. The antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14.3\ \mathbf{cm} (0.23\lambda_{0}) \times 12.5\ \text{cm}\ (0.2\lambda_{0})$</tex> in its lateral dimension. The antenna geometry is basically a multi-resonant structure consisting of a spiral arm and a wider rectangular arm embedded on the top layer of a low loss substrate. The designed antenna yields almost -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 0.5-6.5 GHz with an average boresight gain of 4.5-7.5 dB by using a reflector. While testing its imaging capabilities, we find that the antenna can accurately image subsurface buried targets.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Analysis and Implementation of a High Power Y-Junction Waveguide Circulator
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A design scheme for development of a high power Y junction circulator based on WR340 waveguide is implemented at 2.45 GHz. The proposed design is validated through multiphysics simulations assessing electromagnetic as well as thermal performance of ferrite disks when subjected to high RF power. Circulator was in-house fabricated in lines with proposed design. The so fabricated circulator was tested at 1 kW in Continuous Wave mode with promising results. The proposed design and development scheme can hence be implemented to develop circulators for RF circuits pertaining to industrial heating and space based wireless power transfer applications.

articleTitle: A Millimeter Wave Tri-Polarized Patch Antenna with a Bandwidth-Enhancing Parasitic Element
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a multi-polarized patch antenna operating at 28 GHz is presented covering two senses of circular polarizations (CP) and a single linear polarization (LP). Four loop slots are introduced in the ground plane under the corners of the square driven microstrip patch antenna. These loop slots can be shorted with the aid of 4 p-i-n diodes controlled via external DC biasing lines. Diagonal loop slots guide the formation of circularly rotating current on the driven patch activating one CP mode, while the other diagonal pair activates the opposite CP mode. Shorting all slots results in an almost plain ground plane making the antenna radiates LP waves. To enhance the bandwidth (BW), another square parasitic element on a thicker substrate is mounted on top. For the LP, a 10-dB impedance BW of 1.88 GHz is reported with a gain of 5.8 dB. While the CP's 10-dB BW is 2.07 GHz with a gain of 4 dB and axial ratio BW (ARBW) around 430 MHz. Radiation efficiency for all three modes is above %95.

articleTitle: CPW Resonators for Dielectric Characterization of Sheets at 77 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: A resonant-based dielectric measurement technique at W-band is presented in this paper. The sample holder makes use of two cascaded coplanar waveguide (CPW) resonators to improve the overall quality factor. The CPW resonator is fabricated over a single crystal quartz substrate to minimize the dielectric loss. The resonator acts as a very sensitive sensor to the material placed on top of it, in the form of a superstrate. The technique is capable of accurate characterization of the real and imaginary parts of the dielectric constants of planar dielectric sheets. The proposed technique is validated through fabrication and measurements.

articleTitle: Broadband Antenna-on-Display Applicable for WiFi
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband antenna-on-display (AoD) concept that can be integrated into the transparent region of the display panel. To enable broadband behavior while being in close proximity to the ground plane, the proposed AoD is designed as a leaky-wave antenna (LWA). The proposed transparent LWA consists of an array of composite right/left-handed (CRLH) structures. The transparency of the CRLH unit cell is realized using metal mesh conductive film. To improve the radiation efficiency, a CRLH unit cell that can reduce the shunt inductor by half is used. The fast wave region of the proposed unit cell obtained through the simulation is 3.4 to 6.5 GHz, which is consistent with the impedance bandwidth of the proposed broadband AoD. The measured realized gain of an LWA consisting of 13 unit cells is 1.83 dBi at 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurface for Dynamical Modulation of Reflection, Transmission, and Absorption
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable metasurface is proposed for dynamically modulating reflection, transmission, and absorption. The proposed metasurface is based on tri-layer structure, with varactors loaded on the top and bottom layers. By applying proper bias voltages to the varactors, this metasurface can achieve nearly full-range modulation of reflection, transmission, and absorption. This metasurface paves a new way for dynamic modulation of electromagnetic waves, and may find various applications in practice.

articleTitle: Robust Beamforming for Conformal Antenna Arrays using Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Robust beamforming for antenna arrays on conformal surfaces using software defined radio (SDR) is demonstrated. The beamforming is made robust against uncertainties in the angle of arrival of signals. Robust beamforming for conformal arrays is of interest for new applications in Internet of Things (IoT) and 5G/6G communications. The approach is demonstrated for a patch array on a cylindrical surface using the USRP-2955 SDR. Good agreement between theory and measurements is observed. Trade-offs between beamforming and array performance are discussed.

articleTitle: A Concept of Transparent Antenna Array on Touch Screen Panel for Sub-6 GHz Cellular Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a concept of the MIMO antenna array for sub-6 GHz 5G band mobile application. The antenna array is made of FTO(Fluorine doped tin oxide) for transparency of display, and consists of four fine notch antennas. The measured return loss is −22 dB, and obtained good agreement with the simulation result. All the coupling coefficients between each antenna are under −15 dB.

articleTitle: Hemispherical Luneburg Lens for Wide Angle Beam Scanning in the Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the results of a study that investigates a hemispherical Luneburg lens with a circular PEC base. The lens exhibits a wide-angle scan capability over a wide frequency band and can be mounted on conformal surfaces. The hemispherical lens has a smaller footprint and is easy to fabricate.

articleTitle: HIS Based Low-Profile Double-Negative Metastructure for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Double split High Impedance Surface (HIS) based low-profile metastructure is presented in this paper. The metasurface comprised of slotted rectangular-shaped ring patches experiences the peak current value near the ‘magnetic resonance’, causing the HIS to resonate at 28 GHz where it exhibits negative effective permittivity and effective permeability. The compact 8.7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>unit cell is placed over Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate and analyzed numerically. Nicolson-Ross-Wier approach has been used to observe the effective permittivity and permeability of the unit cell. The design has been further tested with 1x2, 2x2 and 4x4 array formation to verify the results. Having a compact design and double-negative characteristics, this structure can be considered for use in millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wave Propagation via Contextual Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (APS/URSI)
abstract: Beamforming is a cellular base station traffic-signaling system that determines the most effective data-delivery path for a specific user while reducing interference for neighboring users, and it has now become an integral technology in modern wireless communication systems. Contextual beamforming has evolved as an intelligent method in which the location information of a mobile user is predicted based on prior knowledge, and subsequently reconfigure the antenna arrays. Such a system relies heavily on a machine and deep learning applied on the data gathered to infer the context. This paper presents an antenna beamforming approach that exploits the location information of a moving mobile user in a mobile network.
